text: at least 50 people including an Afghan militant commander of Tehrik-i-Taliban, Sangeen, were killed in a series of suspected US missile attacks. The drones also targeted the vehilces in which militants were fleeing. Militants and tribesmen fired at the drones flying overhead. earlier an unmanned plane fired missiles at a bunker in Bekh Mary Langara, a predominantly Mehsud area. The attack left 6, including a commander Wali dead, while 7 others were injured.

Clashes between security forces and militants left 21 militants dead and 2 injured. 1 soldier was also killed while 5 were injured. Following the clashes, helicopter gunships attacked suspected militant positions.
A young man was gunned down when armd persons attacked him near Hussain hazara Goth, killing him on the spot.
11-year-old Muhammad Tariq was killed in a landmine blast. Tariq was returning home from a trip when the landmine blasted on the roadside.

During a search operation, Niaz Ali who was a 9th class student of Bagram Model School was shot and killed by security forces when he tried to resist arrest. Two of his brothers who were arrested were later released.
Body of an unidentified woman was found in the Badami Bagh aea.
Two picnickers were killed and one was injured by 3 personnel of Malakand Levies after an exchange of hot words which led to a quarrel. The levies personnel managed to escape after the incident.

In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, protesters attacked the property of a Hindu and burnt his car in Sargodha on Tuesday. Mob also burnt tyres and effigies of Indian leaders. Due fired tear gas to disperse them and hence 2 policemen and 3 protesters were injured.
Militants fired several mortar shells at an FC camp, injuring 2 security personnel. In retaliation, helicpoter gunships were used to target militant hideouts in Safi tehsil.

Pervaiz Mahmoodul Hasan, a resident of Nazimabad area in Karachi, was held at the airport for carrying a pistol in his handbag. He could neither produce a licence for the firearm, nor could he justify its posession.
Three persons were injured by Rangers' firing for violating the curfew set in the area.
an army captain and a soldier suffered injuries when their vehicle was hit by a landmine in the Shakai Valley.

An army man, Bacha Khan Khattak,  was shot and killed by two unknown assailants on a motorcycle in the main bazaar. According to Political Agent Mohammad Azam Khan, the victim-who was posted in the army canteen in Azam Warsak- was in plain clothes at the time. The authorities have started investigating the reason for the attack and for the assailants themselves. Last year, an official of ISI-Sher Nawaz- was also shot dead by unknown assailants in Wana Bazaar. Follow up: According to local admistration, the Yargul Khel and Ahmedzai tribes were responsible for the attack.

A bomb blast near a market killed 4 people and injured 25, among them 8 children playing near the site of the blast. Police reports claim that it was a time-bomb placed outside a music store but an FC convoy had passed through the area moments before the blast.
2 people were injured in a landmine explosion in Dera Allahyar area of Jaffarabad district.
A man was wounded in a shooting incident in the Preedy area.
One Abdul Waheed was shot and wounded by unknown men on Fida Mohammad Sheikha Road in Kaalri police station area.
Haqiqat Gul and Samin were injured when troops opened fire after the former failed to stop at a checkpost.
2 people were killed and 6 were injured when unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a shop at the Ghass Mandi Chowk. All shops were closed after the attack.

The army and police launched a joint operation after receiving information that Bakht Farzand, a wanted militant leader of TTP, was in the area. The operation led to Bakht Farzand and 4 other militans getting killed, while 3 others were injured.

a fresh wave of ethnic violence erupted across Karachi claimimg the lives of 25 people.  At least 40 others were also injured. Police say the trouble began when armed men who had taken position in the hills os of North Karachi, fired bullets upon Zarina Colony, resulting in the death of an MQM worker who came under fire. the police and Rangers returned gunfire forcing the gunmen to retreat. a Rangers' man was wounded. Vehichles were torched in Malir, North Karachi, Landhi and Al-Fallah.
The third day of the fresh wave of violence in Karachi.  Two men were killed in the main commercial area of PIB Colony as armed men on motorbikes opened indiscriminate fire in the market area.
Ummed Ali and his accomplice shot dead Ghulam Qadir. The cause could not be ascertained.
Unidentified youth intercepted a minibus and set it on fire in North Nazimabad.
In Mastung, a man was killed when some armed men opened fire on a van.

The founder president of SPSF working committee (Mir Murtaza Bhutto group) and the recently expelled Sindh council member of PPP (SB), Ghulam Mustafa Korai, alleged that Mir Murtaza Bhutto opened fire on a crowd of 150 protesters. It was said that he did so on a crowd of people who were protesting against Majeed Sial, who was responsible for expelling Ghulam Mustafa Korai, Ejaz Molai and Liaquat Nizamani from the party. The incident itself was not reported in the newspaper. Information about the incident is gathered from a news article of a news conference held at Hyderabad Press Club by Ghulam Mustafa Korai, in which Korai is accusing Murtaza Bhutto  of certain charges.
Unidentified group shot dead a doctor when he reached Hasan Clinic in Malir. The police termed it a sectarian killing.
Abdul Aziz, a Haveldar of Rangers, was killed and his driver was injured wen their vehicle came under attack.
there was an explosion at the railway tracks.

Baitullah Mehsud threatened to start killing soldiers that had been kidnapped weeks ago, if the military did not stop its operations in Tank. He also threatened to intensify attacks on security personnel in South Waziristan.

Dozens of Islami Jamiat Talaba students reportedly arrived at the PU campus and started thrashing students. According to faculty members, they attacked teachers upon intervention as well and threatened of dire consequences before fleeing upon intervention by the security guards. According to the IJT spokesman, the students did not belong to the IJT and claimed that the brawl was between the students of the Institute over some issue.

Over 100 armed men attacked the village, ransacked houses, ejected women from their houses and manhandled them. They later resorted to indiscriminate aerial firing. The incident took place when the male members of the village had gone to attend a Muharram Majlis. The reason behind the event is said to be a dispute between the Talpurs and the Pariyars. ; Follow-up: A followup report claims that the issue between the two groups is a land dispute.
Brick kiln worker, Abdul Ghafoor, was shot dead by two unidentified men on his way home. According ot his brother, Mansoor, he did not have any enmity.
Low intensity cracker bombs were planted under a car in front of Captain Inamul Haq's house and detonated by 'miscreants' to 'create unrest among citizens'.
A teenage rag picker lost his hand when a low intensity bomb exploded in Samanabad.
A man, along with his brother, threw acid on his former wife, critically injuring her.
A gas pipeline was blown in Loti gas field area resulting in suspension of supply to gas purification plant.

The protesters attacked almost all governmetn buildings and blocked the Quetta Taftan highway causing suspension of traffic.  Several buildings were set on fire in the protest against the killing Nawab Akbar Bugti in a military operation the previous day.
Helicopters shelled suspected militant positions and destroyed an FM radio station operated by militants.

JUI's Secretary-General Abdul Ghafoor Haideri led a demonstration in order to condemn the US for launching an attack on Afghanistan. The workers burnt an effigy of the US President on Circular Road and tyres on Multan Road. Maulana Haideri stated that jihad would be waged in Afghanistan and Pakistan if the Pakistani government stopped supporting the Taliban.
A man, Moosa, was shot dead in Kalakot
A 55 year old unidentified man was found dead in Gurimandar. The unidentified man was killed after he as hit by bullets. The circumstances in which he was killed could not be known.

Armed militants attacked security personnel who were conducting a search operation. In the clash that ensued, 15 militants were killed and 4 were arrested . A soldier was injured in the exchange. 4 beheaded bodies of militants were also found.
An Afghan national and his son were killed in Lawra Mandi in Miranshah on the charge that they were spying for the United States. They supplied goods to the Allied forces in Afghanistan.
The body of a young man, Liaquat Ali Khan, with his throat slit and abdomen ripped out was found inside his car. He was a dealer of electronic goods.

Police baton-charged and arrested activists of the PML-N who had gathered outside the Masjid Shuhada to offer funeral prayers for Pir Binyameen Rizvi. The police authorities, after talks, released around 100 activists who later staged a sit-in on The Mall.

JSSF leaders, speaking at a press conference alleged that police tortured a worker Abdul Khaliq Mehar during an illegal detention. They claim he was picked up and taken to an undisclosed location and interrogated about their leader Dr. Qadir Magsi. He later succumbed to his injuries in the hospital.

Two people Babar and his 5-year-old brother Waqar, of Gattha group, had left their house by a car driven by their driver when their allegedly their rivals from Khokar group opened fire at them injuring all three of them and a passerby. They were taken to the hospital where Babar and his driver succumbed to injuries. the condition of other two is also ssaid to be critical.
Police recovered a low-intensity bomb from a hotel in Rawalpindi.

According to DIG Makran Range, a remote controlled car bomb exploded as a van of Chinese Harbour Engineering Company carrying 14 people, including 11 Chinese engineers was passing. No group or organization had so far claimed responsibility for the attack.
militants fired a rocket at the Landi Kotal helipad which landed near the Hamza Baba shrine. It caused no damage but spread panic among the people.
An explosive device planted under a pipeline in Sui went off, damaging the pipeline severely. However, gas supply was noy suspended.
At Lund Khwar, unidentified people allegedly gunned down an aged person, Sadiq Baba. His son, Shah Wali, filed an FIR.
one soldier was injured when a bomb exploded near the Banda checkpost.
Two motorcyclists resorted to indiscriminate firing, causing injuries to one person.
militants' hideouts in Zaimdara,Shagai, Dabako, Babagam and other areas of Maidan came under shelling by security forces.
100s of traders blocked the main road, burnt tyres and chanted slogans against the political leadership to protest loadshedding that had lasted for upto 22 hours.
In Nishtarabad, voting had to be suspended ad women began to fight with fists and sticks. This occurred during the fourth phase of local body elections.
police defused an explosive device lying by a pylon near Baghbana.

Unidentified men opened fire on the house of Mansoor Chacha (a deceased MQM leader), killing two people inside, while injuring the son. A woman also got caught in the crossfire and was wounded. An eyewtiness stated that the armed men were wearing red caps.
India did shelling in Kotli Parmanand and Matianwala on Wednesday. However no casuality was reported.

The traffic constable, Muhammad Raffique, and the traffic inspector, Khalid Qureshi, saw a bomb lying on the roadside and imformed the Bomb Disposal Squad who defused the bomb. They said that the bomb weighed around 8 to 10 kgs and was made in Pakistan.
Two unidentified men were found dead.

An internet café and two CD shops were blown up in various areas of the provincial capital. Police were forced to ask the rest of the CD, video shops and internet cafes to close down businesses as this was not being tolerated by the Taliban.
A local tribesman was killed and four Taliban militants were injured when they clashes in Shakai area in South Waziristan.
The bodies of three young men were found from two places in Korangi. One was found lying in the Gawa factory while the other two found dumped next to a shrine nto far from the factory.

A religious leader of Dargah Shah Yaqiq, Khalifo Mohammed Ramzan Dars was shot dead by his rivals, while returning to his coastal town, Ladion, after attending a court hearing in Sujawal. The motive of the murder is stated to be old enmity over a land dispute.
A dispenser was shot dead by two unidentified men in Kahna on Sunday
a labourer, Mubashar, was killed in an explosion in a scrap godown in Samnabad.

Four outlaws and two tribal volunteers were killed and a military officer and five other people wounded in a clash between a lashkar and a gang of criminals. The criminal gang stopped the vehicle of Capt Faisal Islam of the Razmak Cadet College and his two guards, and snatched away their weapons and took the offiical away. The guard of Capt Faisal informed a local tribe of the incident, who traced the kidnappers and surrounded them. A clash then occured between the tribal volunteers and the criminal gang.

In a rare incident of its kind on the international border, the Indian forces opened fire from across the Wagah border after mistaking an unexplained explosion in a village in East Punjab for 'rocket fire from Pakistan'. New Delhi said it was a retaliatory fire in response to two rockets fired inside its territory from Pakistan side, but Islamabad dismissed the allegation.
According to Pir Binyamin Rizvi, the police is arresting PML activists before the arrival of party president, Shahbaz Sharif, in order to prevent a reception for him. 2 activists were arrested
Two brothers were killed and one was injured in an attack over a dispute involving karo kari. Details not available.
Sobho Oad and his son Saman Oad were seriously injured when some armed men attacked them at Johri Farm village.
three people including an alleged terrorist were injured in a bomb balst at a bus stand in Quetta. The blast occurred as the accused tried to enter the bus.
Haji Muhammad Hanif, who was a PPP member and also part of the area Zakat Committee, was killed when armed motorcyclists fired 7 shots at him and fled.
Rockets were fired on South Waziristan Scouts posted at Nawai Kot. However, no damage was done in the attack.
A person was killed by unknown assailants in Moinuddinpur on Wednesday.
A young man was shot and killed in his sleep when unknown persons broke into his room and opened fire before making their escape.

Fierce clashes erupted between local tribesmen and foreign militants when some people opened fire on a pro-government elder Malik Saadullah Darikhel, a local peace committee head, who had previously survived two more attacks on his life. This attack infuriated his relatives and a gunbattle between the foreginers and activists of the peace committee helped by the members of the Darikhel tribe ensued. It is worth mentioning that Malik Saadullah is considered a staunch opponent of foreign elements in the tribal area, and had been organizing fellow tribesmen against them, which is probably why there have been so many attempts on his life.
a doctor was shot dead at his clinic in sector 11-S of the New Karachia area by three attackers. The doctor had no political or religious affiliations.
One, Azmat Ali of Village Jalalpur was Bhattian along with his accomplices murdered his sister Shamim on suspicion of bad character.

A teacher at Habib Public school and a Pesh Imam of the Yasrab Masjid-o-Imambargah, Allama Razi Hyder, along with his sons was going to Habib Public School when 4 to 5 unknown assailants fired at their car. A senior police official stated that the attack seemed to be sectarian-motivated.

Unidentified assalants in a truck opened fire on the police party in Mehran Hotl Intersection on Friday injuring two cops and a pedestrian. Police cordoned off the areas leading to Cantt Railway Station where people wanted to go to receive PPI leader.
Two men were injured in a shooting incident near Al-Asif square in the jurisdiction of Gulzar-e-hijri.
Students of one BSO faction allegedly opened fire at a group of students from their rival faction, causing injuries to three students.
Nasar Khan axed to death his sister over suspicion of having illicit relations.
A villager was killed and another was injured in a heavy landmine blast in the Kot Nainan village in the Sialkot working boundary's Shakargarh sector.
A bus of route G-27 was set on fire by unknown arsonists.

The bullet-riddled bodies of Zahoor Baloch and Faqir Mohammad were found. The BSO-Azad claimed that Zahoor Baloch was an active member of the student party and that the two victims had been missing for a month.
A man was injured in indiscriminate firing by unidentified men.
A man and his two sons were wounded in 'sniper firing' at Disco Chowk in Orangi.
three personnel of Levies sustained injuries in a roadside explosion near Khar.

12 mortar shells were fired fron Afghanistan across the border. However no loss of life or property was reported as they landed in an open field. It may be noted that a joint army and FC camp is situated in the Alwari Mandi area.
During a raid, military helicopter gunships destroyed 2 militant hideouts and killed 6 militants.
A man and a woman were killed in Mawali Shar village on the pretext of karo-kari. Police registered a case against the woman's husband and his accomplices.
Railway Police foiled an subversive attempt and siezed five hand-grenades from the Rawalpindi-bound train. A suspect, Fayyaz Hussain, has also been arrested.

5 assailants shot dead PSF activist Liaquat Waraich outside his house. They showed up on a car and called him out of his house before opening fire on him. The victim's uncle has alleged that two IJT workers were among the assailants.

A correspondent of Mashriq, Amjad Ali Shah, was attacked by an armed group of timber mafia and seriouly injured. He had been receiving threats because he was drawing attention to the massive deforestation that was taking place. The police refused to register and FIR and seemed to be protecting the atackers.

Around 27 workers were arrested and several others received injuries when police baton-charged protestors in a bid to disperse them. Businesses remained shut during the strike called by the PADC to protest US strikes in Afghanistan. Protestors staged a sit-in on the road near Risalpur and public & private transport remained off the road throughout the day as the district administration called out the army as well to disperse the demonstrators.
A fierce gunbattle took place between two rival groups, Zargunkhel and Mulano Kallay, over a land dispute in Darra Adamkhel, which left four people dead and two others injured.

Thousands of people joined the Mma protest rally against the operation in Wana and against the pro-US policies of General Musharraf. They also burnt an effigy of General Musharraf. Qazi Hussain Ahmad addressed the protestors.
A bomb went off outside the college gate of Khyber Homoeopathic College Sharifabad on Tuesday. However no loss of life was reported.
The bullet ridden body of Naushad Ali was found. He was reported missing in the afternoon on the same day (i.e.: 16-May-04)

Two people were killed and eleven others were injured when a bomb exploded in the Venus Cinema in Okara. Management stated that two people had entered the cinema after the interval and left it shorty afterwards.
Supporters of the MQM-H set on fire shops owned by their rivals (MQM - Altaf). This came after 4 MQM-H had been killed during raid on the party office in Shah Faisal Colony.
In leepa sector, two people were killed in intense Indian firing/shelling from across the LoC in the Chunnian village.
Two people stepped on a land mine and were critically injured.
Indian commandos sneaked into the southern village of Azad Kashmir along LoC and massacred 14 people including women and children on Friday. 5 people got injuries while 3 succumbed to death
An 11 year old girl was injured when a stray bullet hit her in the arm during firing in Korangi between unruly youngsters and the police.

Two brothers, Rashid and Sajid, were shot dead when they were at the sessions court in relation to a blasphemy case they had been booked in. Both the victims belonged to the Christian faith. A police man was also injured in the firing that was done by a group of gunmen.
Militants blew up a primary school for boys.
A school boy was shot dead by unidentified people.
one person was killed and several others were injured in a clash between rival groups of Nomadics in Chak No. 313/HR (Faqirwala).
A young woman was found throttled to death in Kalri on Thursday
Taliban attacked a security check post in Wenai area in Swat injuring one security personnel.
A woman was killed when unidentified gunmen opened fire in the neighbourhood.
Armed motorcyclists opened fire on a tanker carrying fuel for Nato forces in Afghanistan. Following the firing, the driver stopped the tanker and the assailants proceeded to set it on fire.
Four people, including a nine year old vendor, were injured in a grenade attack on the Garrison cinema owned by army.

Unknown gunmen on a motorbike opened fire on Iran-bound pilgrims who were waiting for a bus to take them to the border. Three of the victims died on the spot while 4 others were injured. Police deemed the motives to be sectarian.
A minor boy was killed and two men seriously injured when two rival parties exchanged fire in village Ghadiala eastern. The rival parties were the Asghar and Ashraf groups.
A man was wounded in a 'sniping incident' at the Baloch Hotel in Liaquatabad.

angry protesters blocked the car of the federal minister, Syed Khursheed Ahmed, when he came out of the airport building. There were at least 400 sacked employees of the Sui Southern Gas Company along with 200 sacked employees of railway sleeper factory and hundreds of unemployed youths. the sacked SSGC employees said that they had been reinstated through presidential order with the assurance that thehy would get all monetary benefits, however no such thing had happened despite a lapse of 6 months. The minister assured them that they would receive their joining letters and monetary benefits soon. the police had to resort to baton-charge to disperse the protesters so that the minister could exit.
Hafizullah has a suspicion that his sister had relations with a man. He forbade her but she didn't listen. Then he shot her dead and fled.

Over 200 activists of the Jamat-i-Islami and Shahab-i-Milli disrupted a music show at Jinnah Stadium when they cut the power supply and threw crackers in the stadium. Armed with batons, they smashed the windscreens of cars, wagons and buses parked outside. POlice baton-charged the rioters and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd. Six people were injured in the baton-charge and four policemen sustained injuries when pelted with stones.
A road side remote-controlled bomb was used to target a security forces vehicle, killing 2 personnel and injuring another 4.
25 workers plucking peaches were injured in a mortar attack.
Gunship helicopters destroyed 3 militant hideouts in Madorhi area and killed 10 militants in Dabori area. 7 militants were also injured in the shelling.

Provincial Minister Sardar Sanaullah Zehri escaped an attempt on his life when a bomb was detonated by remote control when their vehicle was close to Surab in Kalat. The Baloch Liberation Front claimed responsibility for the attack.

Mr Julius Salik-MNA and eight other christians were arrested by the police after they were baton-charged as they were protesting on Shahrah Quaid-e-Azam on Thursday. Protesters also pelte stones to damage neon-signs, traffic signals and windscreens of private cars.

One person was killed and 14 others injured during a riot between activists of Anjuman-i-Sipah-i-Sahaba and Shia activists. The riot started after both sides raised slogans against eachother and later there as an exchange of gunfire.
Unknown gunmen intercepted and opened fire at a van that was taking labourers of Babri Cotton Mill to their homes. 2 labourers were killed and 4 were injured.
Tehrik-i-Nifaz-i-Fiqh-Jafaria staged a demonstration and blocked traffic by burning tyres as a protest against bailing out of Mr. Fazle Haq.
1 person was killed and his son was injured in a bomb blast occurred at Mohalla Sheranwala on Saturday.

Demonstrators, who were protesting against power outages, had planned to lead a rally to a WAPDA grid station in Kharrik locality. However, the police intercepted them and the mob retaliated by pelting them with stones. Police resorted to tear gas shelling and baton charge in order to disperse them. 3 policemen were among the 8 people injured.
A powerful explosion caused 7 injuries to guests at the Marriot hotel that included a US diplomat; Abdullah Mehsud, an Al-Qaeda linked commander, took responsibility for the blast on 31st October.

a protest demonstration against Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. As a result 62 political workers of different political parties were arrested. The People's Party, JKLF and the Four Party Democratic Alliance had gathered at the main chowk. The police resorted to lathi-charge to disperse the angry protesters and both sides pelted eachother with stones. several people were injured. the protesters also burnt tyres and blocked the road.
A police post in Tank was attacked in Tank when authorities imposed a curfew in the area after clashes between miscreants and security forces a day before. No other information was given.

A number of journalists were injured when police baton-charged a procession taken out to mark the International Press Freedom Day. The Punjab Union of Journalists had organised the rally and the participants wanted to march to the Governor’s House from the Dyal Singh Mansion.They were stopped by police at the Chairing Cross. Senior police officials told journalists they had orders to stop them from holding a march. This led to exchange of hot words between journalists and police who resorted to a baton-charge.
A watchman was shot dead by some unidentified men in a factory in Chuhng while he was on duty. The motive behind the murder could not be ascertained.
Salim Beg was injured when his pick-up was fired at in Shah Faisal Colony.
Tanvir Malik was standing ooutside his house when two armed motorcyslists fired at him. He survived with injuries. The reason behind the attack could not be ascertained.
Interior Minister Aitzaz Ahsan and former Punnjab Governor Ghulam Mustafa Khar were fired upon by unidentified gunmen during polling for by-elections in NA-99. They escaped unhurt.

The lahore bound chiltan express had a narrow escape when a powerful bomb went off on the railway tracks but the driver managed to apply the breaks in time and stop the train before it reached the damaged part of the railway line. It is also noteworthy that Pakistan railways has been using pilot trains since the begining of trouble in Balochistan.
A 47 year old man was gunned down when unidentified men opened fire on him while he was standing outside a mosque in the Khadda market area.

A man was killed in Lakhti Banda in Hangu district. He was accused of running a brothel. A note found on his body warned his family members that if they didn't stop the un-Islamic business, they would also be killed.
A police checkpost was blown up in Peshawar on the Frontier Road.
Seven houses were damaged when two bombs went off in the Makeen and Azdikhel areas of South Waziristan. No loss of life was reported.

An unruly mob stormed a phone centre damaging property when they were told that the free connections package deal they had been waiting for had been exshausted. Police were forced to used batons to disperse the crowd. Eye witnesses said two policemen were injured.

An explosive device planted near the house of the district nazim of Zhob exploded when the nazim was not present in his house. The explosion damaged the windowpanes of his house and adjacent houses. The nazim, Maulvi Habibur Rehman, belonged to the JUI (F).
At least 10 people were killed and 37 were injured when a powerful bomb exploded in a mosque in Akbarpura on Friday.

Militants planted bombs at a school and detonated them, destroying the entire building. The Nawagai Political Tehsildar, Arshad Ali Khan, claimed that 2 tribesmen had been arrested under the collective territorial responsibility act.
Four peope were killed and three others injured when their car was ambushed by unidentified gunmen, on their way to the court for a case hearing. The reason for the attack was not specified.
3 family members of the house of Jhando Chandio were killed by 10 bandits, led by Akbar Chandio, when they attacked his house over a land dispute.

A plot's owner, Muhammad Salim Memon, with 3 magistrates and some police officials asked the illegal occupants of his land to leave. The occupants refused and resisted it, resulting in a clash that left 11 wounded. The police arrested 18 people
Saifuddin, a servant at the residence of Rashid Hussain, was shot as an unidentified man rang the doorbell and shot him when he opened the door.
A man was found shot dead in the Railway Wireless Colony, Misri Shah.

Maulana Ghulam Hussain Naeemi, a religious scholar, was shot and killed outside his mosque. The assailants knocked at his door, which was answered by the scholar's son who led them to the mosque where his father was at the time. As soon as Naeemi came out the assailants opened fire and fled. ; Follow-up: The President of the TNFJ expressed his shock at the killing and condemned it. (See Note)
A doctor was killed by unidentified gunmen, who after killing him set his car ablaze and fled.

Activists of the Sipah-i-Sahaba Went on a rambage burning several buses , shops and an imambargah ( a Shia mosque). They clashed with the police  and several were later arrested. They were protesting against the killing of four SSP activists a day earlier, in Islamabad.

Police arrested 123 workers of the PML when they tried to reach the Punjab Assembly. The police baton charged and teargassed the protesters. They were protesting against removal of PML's Chief Minister Ghulam Haider Wyne.
A man shot dead a watchman and then blew up a video shop in Mardan.
1 person was killed and 2 were injured in Indian shelling along LoC in Keri Village on Sunday
Some MQM boys travelling in a car were attacked with stones by 12 teenagers, as  a result of which their car was damaged.

Najma Begum and her mother-in-law were sitting at home when Hafiz Mohammad Boota, Muhammad Yousaf, and Muhammad Aslam barged in and shot at them. As a result, Najma was killed and her mother-in-law was injured. According to the police, the victims were supporting the rivals of t accused in a property dispute.

A university student was knocked down by a minibus and killed. The accident sparked violence as an angry mob set the vehicle on fire and chanted slogans against the transport operators and traffic police. Police reached the spot to control the situation and were pelted with stones. Police resorted to tear gas shelling and baton-charging to take control of the situation. No casualties were reported.
A school teacher was killed and four policemen were injured when a bomb ripped the Uthal police station.
6 people were injured when a bomb fixed to a motorbike exploded in Chakar Chowk area. The attackers appeared to have targetted an FC vehicle passing through the area.
Unidentified men attacked and killed a shop owner at Dolly Video Centre in Block A of Nazimabad. The motive behind the murder could not be known.

Security forces claimed killing 18 militants in Charbagh area. Brigadier Tahir Hameed, who was leading the operation, said that troops had captured several wanted men an retrieved a large quantity of looted goods.
Sarai Alamgir police found an unidentified woman dead in Khumbi.
Youngsters pelted stones at and damaged a van.

Young protesters took to the streets, after a man was killed during a clash between two groups in Chandni Chowk, threw stones at vehicles and disrupted traffic. All shopping centres were closed throughout the day due to firing incidents; protesters also blocked the railway level crossing in Nazimabad, some youths even damaged a passenger bus and tried to set it on fire but the driver sped away.
Armed men, riding in a taxi, opened fire at and injured two guards of Nawab Aslam Raisani while they were sitting at a hotel. Another person present at the hotel was injured.
Two people were killed and four others injured in Indian shelling.

A religious leader and his student were killed while the cleric's son and another student were injured when two unidentified men on a motorcycle opened fire on them near the Bibi Nani Shrine. The Maulana belonged to the Ahl-i-Sunnat Wal Jamaat.

Demonstrators clashed with police outside the house of Murtaza Bhutto, Al-Murtaza, blocking a condolence call by President Farooq Leghari.  Groups of about 150 people also threw rocks at passing vehicles,  broke hotel windows and trashed a bank, government school and the reception area of hotels.  When the police tried to stop them, the protesters attack them sticks and stones. But no exchange of fire took place. The angry demonstrators were protesting against the killing of Mir Murtaza Bhutto.

a shutter-down strike was observed in many arts of Sukkur in protest against the Kalabagh dam. JSQM workers staged a demonstration at Sukkur Bypass, Garam Godi,Militray Road, Thermal Colony, Clock Tower, New Pindi and other areas. They burnt tyres and chanted slogans. the police arrested some activists. in Daharki the police arrested 10 activists of the JSQM for pelting stones at vehicles.

Syed Qamar Abbas, a former provincial minister and senior vice-president of the People's Party Parlimentarians NWFP was shot dead. He was on his way on a motorcycle with one Akhunzada Muhammad Ali when some people opened fire on them. Mr. Abbas was nominated in a case about the death in an election clash about 10 years ago of Shabbit Bilour, son of Awami National Party leader Ghulam Ahmed Bilour. Mohammad Ali was son of Fiqah-i-Jafariyah Pakistan leader Akhunzada Anwer Ali who was shot dead four years ago.
Unidentified gunmen opened fire at a roadside, injuring three passers-by.

Unknown men, waiting outside Abdul Rauf's house, chased Abdul Rauf and shot him when he was returning from work. The Afaq Ahmed-led faction of MQM-H claimed that he was a party worker associated with the Landhi area.

A man allegedly murdered his married sister and her paramour in Dollowana village. The woman had allegedly developed relations with Sher Muhammad of her native village, seperated from her husband and come back to her parents' house. Her brother shot her and her lover dead when he saw them together.
Several medical students were injured when police baton charged their protest rally. They wanted to secure admissions in the medical colleges. The police arrested 14 students.
Militants attacked three empty houses of IDPs in frontier region of Kohat on Wednesday. However no loss of life was reported.
A clash erupted between Dahani and Bijarani tribes in which one perosn was killed and ten were injured.
A body of a young man bearing torture marks was found in a graveyard.
District Nazim of Dera Bugti claims two Frontier Corps personnel were killed in a heavy gunbattle between security forces and tribesmen in Tegha area of Dera Bugti.

A large number of people blocked the Khokhar Road for over two hours in protest against the killing of a woman by a bus. The protesters burnt tyres and chanted slogans against the Transport company and the police. The protesters dispersed when some senior police officers assured them that legal action would be taken against the bus driver.
Four people were kiolled and three others injured hwne rival groups clashed over a land dispute
one mosque was destroyed and several houses were partially damaged during shelling.
A nine year old girl was injured by sniper bullets in the PECHS area.
A political rivalry had developed between two people, Anjum and Ashiq, during the previous general elections which led to the former attacking and killing the latter.
Security forces opened fire in Kharwanai area, killing a man in a shop.
a military convoy going from Miramshah to Bannu was hit by an explosive device detonated by remote control.
A constable was shot and killed when he stopped two unidentified men on the M. A. Jinnah Road.
According to MQM, Haqiqi men ransacked the offices of two of their activists' offices in Malir.
A young boy was injured in crossfire between rival groups near Jail Road. No information regarding the groups or the cause of firing Is reported.

Dr. Ishrat Hussain, a resident of Azizabad, was near his clinic when unidentified men intercepted his car and shot him dead. The family stated that a few days ago, some men had come to their home and inquired about their sect.
The body of an unidentified man was found in the fields in Raiwind area. He had been shot in the head.
40 people were injured in day long pitched battles between supporters of Mir Murtaza Bhutto and the police who barred the activists to reach the main terminal to receive him.

Militants blew up a government girls primary school in the Adezai area of Peshawar. According to sources, militants planted five explosive devices on the three-storey building and detonated them by remote.

Rival religious groups, Lashkar-i-Islam and Ansar-ul-Islam clashed in Landi Kotal after a jirga comprising of local Jamiat-Ulema-i-Islam failed to negotiate a ceasefire between the groups. Two people were killed and two others were injured in the clash.
A housewife was found dead in her bedroom under mysterious circumstances. The neighbours discovered the body.

12 militants were killed in a US drone fired missile on the suspected headquarters of the local Taliban chief in Khadezai area. 2 women were also killed in the attack. Thirteen people were injured. Hakimullah Mehsud, a Taliban commander loyal to Baitullah Mehsud said that 6 of his fighters had been killed in the missile attack and he vowed revenge.

As part of the MQM protest day against the victimisation and arrest of its women workers, a total strike was observed throughout the troubled localities in Karachi. Eleven persons were wounded in heavy shooting incidents in Saeedabad.
A checkpost of the Bajaur scouts and Levies force came under rocket attack and heavy gunfire. The security forces exchanged fire with the attackers who had laid siege.

Two persons were shot at and wounded near Nairang Cinema (Liaquatabad) by some unidentified persons who fired at them from a passing vehicle.According to an unofficial report, one of the injured later died.
6 persons were injured in election relatedd violence in Shahdadpur Taluka.
A head constable of the police, Mohammad Panha was gunned down inside his own house. The BLA claimed responsibility for the attack.

10 trucks of a convoy returning from Afghanistan were torched on the Peshawar-Torkham highway. Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Nabi, two wanted men had claimed responsibility for the attack. A fine of Rs. 20 million was placed on the Shinwari tribe for its failure to surrender them.
A man in his early 30's was found wounded by a bullet in his car. He was taken to the hospistal where he died. The police could not solve the murder.
The burnt body of a woman was found near the Punjab University New Campus.

Following an attack on the ANP Information Secretary, ethnic violence erupted in other parts of Orangi as the city police chief Saud Ahmed Mirza described it as \political and definitely ethnic\". Two passengers were killed and three others were wounded when a bus came under fire by unidentified men in Qasba Colony. "

Shuja, a ninth class student, was shot dead when a stray bullet hit him. Some student activists were released from Central Jail Bahawalpur. As they were coming out, some students belonging to a rival organization allegedly fired shots at them. Shuja, who happened to be passing by, was hit by a stray bullet and died.

Six air force personnel and seven other people were killed when a car bomb epxloded near a bridge on Peshawar-Kohat road. It was not clear whether the attack was a suicide mission or not. According to BBC, Taliban have claimed the responsibility for the attack.
a jeweller was shot dead in the Inayat Kallay area by unidentified motorcyclists.
Two people were killed and 32 others injured when a bomb went off in a cinema in Mingora. The cinema was packed to its full capacity and many were injured in the ensuing stampede.
CDG officials and the police were injured while carrying out an operation against the sale of porn CDs. The traders pelted them with stones injuring two of them.
Militants attacked two checkpost in Thall and Ghusha near Miramshah and injured four FC soldiers. Paramilitary retaliated and heavy exchange of fire started.
A push cart vendor was injured in a cracker explosion that took place at the Market Chowk, Tando Allahyar.
A motorcyclist was attacked and beaten up with sticks and his motorcycle was set ablaze.

3 friends, Tariq Aziz, Zubair Ahmed and Imran were shot dead on the Liaquatabad Flyover by people who first knocked them over with a car and then sprayed them with bullets using an AK-47. Zubair Ahmed had reportedly stated that some of the attackers were wearing police caps. The police denied having this information. All the victims did not have any political affiliations
An explosive device went off in an open drain near the cirty polic staion. No loss of life or property was reported.
A militant attack on a security post was followed by an exchange of fire that lasted for over an hour. A local militant commander was killed and 3 other militants were injured.
A minor girl was killed and several others were wounded when a mortar shell hit a house in Kabal tehsil during the security forces operation in the region.
In Bannu, four security personnel were injured in a roadside explosion when their vehicle ran over the landmine planted by suspected militants.
a man suffered serious injuries in an exchange of fire over election rivalry in Ferozewala. The groups led by Aslam Buttur and Iqbal traded fire. Aslam Buttur was injured.

2 peopl were shot dead and three were injured in a crossfire between two rival groups at Maraka village in Manga Mandi. Troops were called in when the situation deteriorated. The incident was a result of the second phase of local government elections.
The Chenab Rangers thwarted a major attempt by the Indian Security Forces to fence the Sialkot Working Boundary. They destroyed one big Indian defensive pillar.

The traffic Kiosk at Old Exhibition came under attack. Some unidentified gunmen took positions atop the Deaf and Dumb school from where they fired at the police post. Intermittend firing was also reported in some area at night.
CIA SI Muhammad Hussain Chang was gunned down by in an ambush by unidentified armed men near Sanjoro on Saturday.
A PPP activist, Shahid Narnoli, was shot allegedly by an MQM activist, Fareed, with whom he had previous unsettled disputes. However, both parties have launched FIRs against one another.

The administrator of South Waziristan, Mr. Asmatullah Gandapur, was traveling back to tank when his jeep was blown up with a remote controlled device, reportedly by militants. Both him and his driver sustained injuries.  Senior officials and Brig Mehmood Shah claim it to be a target killing and the handiwork of militants.

The body of Javed (23 years old, third year student of Government Degree College, Kohi) was found. His was tortured before being shot and many of his bones were fractured. He was abducted by three unidentified men three days prior to the recovery of the body.
2 people were killed and 5 were injured by unknown persons in Landhi Korangi Area on Friday.
A gang of dacoits killed 6 members of the same family as a 'punishment' to the people of the village for releasing information about the dacoits to the police.
A young man Bilal Ahmad was gunned down in Chak 108-SB
A bullet riddled body of a man was found.

Anwar Khatoon and her daughter, Nasima, were gunned down by armed men. The assailants threw their bodies in the Indus River. Raza Mohammad, Anwar Khatoon's husband, lodged a \case against seven men, but had been arrested till the filing of this report\". "

30 personnel of different agencies-primarily secret agencies, police and elite forces- arrested Dr. Inamullah Khan from his house without any search warrant. SHO of the city police station expressed ignorance concerning the matter. Sources said that he might have been arrested for his 'links' with a banned religious group. Dr. Ali Asghar expressed regret over the reluctance of the police to disclose the victim's whereabouts.
Gunmen of the Kosh tribe shot dead Rahim Bux Solangi in the Machka area, which led to an escalation of the ongoign war between the Kosh and Solangi tribes.
A woman, Nasim Akhtar, was shot dead when she was going home in the Topi area of Swabi district. The woman's son, Zahor Shah, has registered an FIR with the police.
Haleema was shot dead by her husband, Abdul Ghaffar Kandhro as he suspected that she had illicit relations with Bhoro Kandhro. He later surrendered himself to the Dubbar police.

Solangi tribesmen held a demonstration in protest over the arrest of one of their men. Policeman opened baton-charge and tear gas to disperse the angry crowd.  Protesters attacked the police in retaliation by pelting them with stones and sticks.
A bomb blast partially damaged two cell phone shops. The miscreants had planted indigenous explosives in a generator in the market.
Four people were killed and four others were injured in sporadic clashes between rival tribes in different areas of the Kurram agency.
A suicide bomber smashed his car into a checkpoint near GHQ as he was signalled to stop. 5 security personnel were injured in the incident.
In the after math of Benazir Bhutto's death, angry PPP protestersattacked a police station with stones, smashing windowpanes, signboards etc.
An unidentified man was gunned down in Nazimabad.

A violent protest by residents of Lyari over a complete power breakdown for 2 days left a 12-year-old child injured, who later succumbed to his injuries at the hospital. The protesters raised slogans against KESC authorities. Details of the violence are not given.
People from various parts of the city blocked the road and burnt tyres to protest against loadshedding. They also raised slogans against the government and FESCO.
Security forces claimed they defused a bomb placed on the side of the road in Kot village in Charbagh area.
One person was wounded in Indian shellin across LoC in neelum valley on Wednesday
One villager was injured in the Charwa sector in the firing by the Indian troops from across the LoC.
A clash between Pitafi and Mallah communities at the Tando Muhammad Khan police station left STP leader Raza Mohammad Khaskheli, Iqbal Hanjo and head constable Mohammad Juman injured.

A customs employee, Saleem Farooqui, who had been missing for two days was found dead in his official vehicle on Korangi Road in Defence Housing Authority. The body, reportedly, bore bullet wound marks.
A powerloom worker was shot dead by some unidentified persons when he was going home along with his brother.

The police officials arrested a boy and a girl for quarrelling. In the meantime, Union Council Nazim Irfan Haider Cheema and his elder brother, Sajjad Haider Cheema, both sons of Tehsil City Nazim, Mumtaz Ali Cheema, went to the police station and held dialogues with the SHO Muhammad Akmal. According to the SHO, the boys attacked him first and threw around office furniture. He denied allegations of torture of the Nazim's sons. According to the two sons, they were beaten up severely by the SHO after they asked him to resolve a petty issue. They said that the SHO became angry without any justification and started to beat them up in his room.

A Muharram procession that was headed to Imambargah Sahki Munawwar Shah was attacked by a hand grenade that was hurled from a nearby building. The blast killed a 2-year-old boy and left 31 others injured.

The Tehrik-i-Nifaz-i-Fiqah Jafaria took out a procession against the killers of Allama Arif Hussain Al-Hussaini. The protesters were protesting against the 'imperialist forces' behind the murder. They burnt an American flag.
A person was killed and his son was injured by armed men in Jacobabad on Sunday.
A married woman was strangled to death by her husband and two other accomplices on the pretext of Karo-kari
The Karachi bound Shah Rukn-i-alam escaped disaster when a bomb planted on the railway track exploded destroying safety plates and nuts of the track.
A teenager was injured while standing in a street in Taya Joiyaan village in Charwa sector across the LoC when some bullets fired by the Indian troops hit him.
An advocate of the High Court was gunned down when armed men intercepted him on Tariq Road and opened fire on him. He succumbed to his injuries at the hospital.
Baro Khan was killed an danother injured when their motorcycle hit a landmine in Bekar area.

Abdul Rauf Mohammad Naseem and Attaullah, both Afghan nationals, were killed by snipers. The motive of the murder is said to be an old enmity between two political groups of Afghan Mujahideen- Gulbadin Hikmat Yar and Mohammad Nabi groups.

A man was killed and his brother sustained injuries when a group of men opened fire on them while they were working in the fields of the Khingriwala village, allegedly because the man had developed illicit relations with the sister-in-law of one of the other men.
Three family members, including two women were shot dead by their rivals over a previous dispute when the rivals opened indiscriminate fire on them in their home.
A police patrol van was targeted by a remote controlled IED, killing 2 people and injuring 11. A police constable was among those killed. The BLA claimed responsibility for the attack

Following the assassination of senoir MQM member Farooq Baig that sparked anger among MQM workers, Karachi witnessed a number of arson attacks that the police claimed targeted mostly vehicles owned by 'people from a particular ethnic background'. Three buses and a hi-roof van were torched in Landhi Town

the army made inroads into Mehsud territory in South Waziristan. The Army claimed that 32 militants had been killed in the offensive. Helicopter gunships shelled suspected militant hideouts in Barond, Serwekai and Gul Serai areas.
The body of a local commander, Ihsanur Rehman, was found from the Kokarai area on the outskirts of Mingora during a search operation.
Farhan Saeed Butt of Bridge Colony, Cantonment was held by Airport Security Force after a pen pistol was recovered. He was handed over to the police for interrogation and legal action.

Five tribesmen, including two women were killed in a clash between two rival clans of Bugti and Domki tribes in the Sub-tehsil of Lehri about 250Km east of Quetta. According to reports both tribes used heavy weapons including rockets, and bombs againsteach other.

The dead bodies of Amir and Shakir, residents of Bakra Piri, Lyari were found and taken to the hospital. Police claim that the deceased were associated with Lyari Peace Committee. Background: Karachi has been gripped with fear after a week filled with incidents of targeted and indiscriminate killing which has strained the relationship between coalition parties MQM and PPP.

A senior advocate was targeted when two unidentified assailants entered his chamber on the District Court premises and opened fire on him. He was injured and rushed to the hospital. According to police, the assailants later fired on a constable posted at Choti Zarin police station.
Armed motorcyclists opened fire at a tea shop, killing 1 man and injuring another.

Police batoncharged male and female teacher who had gathered outside the Islamia College for Women on Cooper road in order to protest against the proposed privatisation of the educational institutions.

A girl was injured when suspected militants fired rockets and missiles on border areas of Manro Jangle and Speray in Mamund tehsil of Bajaur. Tribal lashkars retaliated which caused the militants to flee.
Police fired shells at the PPP demonstrators in Lyari on Saturday. PPP was demonstrating against the government and alleged that 100 PPP workers were arrested
A man was shot dead at A-area during the on-going violence in Khokhrapar and neighbourhood areas.

When the district labour office tried to resume possession of land that was encroached upon by a lady -Sharifan- she refused to vacate the plot and attacked the watchmen accompanying them. She also said that she would launch a rape case against them if they try to take the land from her. The team left after their police escort abandoned them when a group of ladies came out in Sharifan's support.

Two MQM activists were gunned down in an encounter in Sector A-1 on Orangi Town. The police claimed to have recovered submachineguns from their possession. MQM contradicted the police and claimed that three of their activists had been killed in cold blood.

According to witnesses some unidentified armed men brought a young man to Nadi Ali Pulia, shot him and set his body on fire. According to police, the man had been tortured beforehand as well. Follow up: the man was said to be an MQM leader.
Haji Fazal Kareem, a UN worker from Afghanistan, was injured when he was hit by rifle butts by some unidentified attackers after his vehicle came under fire. His two companions escaped unharmed.

At least 40 suspected militants were killed and 43 others captured in a new military offensive in the Bara area of Khyber tribal region. The local administration had imposed a curfew in Bara tehsil before the operation titled 'Biya Daraghlam' (Here I come again). It was the second operation aimed at enforcing the writ of the government in an area that was under the control of the outlawed Lashkar-i-Islam. Followup: In the continuation of the same operation in Bara tehsil, at least 16 suspected militants were killed and 35 others arrested in the second day of the military operation. Security forces had faced stiff resistance in Akkakhel and Kohi localities, but cleared the areas after a clash which left several militants dead.
a bomb was defused in a neighbouring area of Nizampur Ghaliyan near Kingra Road Bund, by the Bomb Disposal Squad.
When residents of different localities learnt of the police violence they staged a protest on the Peshawar Charsadda road and burnt tyres.

There was a protest against a raid by the police on the private residence of Chairman Khanqah Sharif UC- Mian Najeeb-uddin Owaisi conduted to arrest a person. Hundreds of youung blocked the National Highway and the police tried to disperse the crowd using teargas shells. The protesters retaliated with bricks. There were 10 people who sustained injuries.
Security forces launched an operation after militants had attacked two checkposts. In the clashes that ensued, at least 1 militant was killed and 4 were injured.
The former district general secretary of JUI-F-Maulana Saleemullah and another person were gunned down by his rivals in Latambar area on Tuesday. Three other persons were also injured.

a man and a woman were killed on the pre-text of karo-kari in Abdul Rehman Shar village. One Mubarak Shar opened fire on his sister-in-law and her relative when he found them in a compromising position.
An activist of the MQM was shot and killed in an encounter with a police party when they raided a terrorist hideout in Block N of Nazimabad.
Indian forces targeted border villages of the Norwal district by using machine guns. Sources said that the Pakistani forces responded effectively.
The body of a youth was found in the Orangi Town graveyard.

General Officer Commanding Swat Maj-Gen Javed Iqbal was injured when his helicopter came under attack near the Afghan border in Upper Dir. After the incident, the security personnel clashed with militants and shelled their hideouts.
at least 15 people were injured when a bomb placed on a push-cart parked at a taxi-stand in Dera Murad Jamali went off. Several vehicles were damaged in the blast.

2 students were injured in baton charge and 8 others were arrested when IJI students protested and started towards the city's most crowded cinema houses allegedly involved in screening of obscene movies.

A dispute over the occupation of a mosque between Tanzim Ahl-i-Sunnat-wal-Jamaat and a group of Tablighi Jamaat created high tension in the area. Each group claimed ownership of the mosque. An attempt by the Tablighi group to take possession of the mosque led to law and order situation at the Friday congregation. The police were called to restore peace and they used batons to disperse the violent contenders.
pipeline connecting Pir Koh gas field with sui plant was blown up. The Baloch Republican Army took responsibilitty for the incident.
Unknown persons hurled a hand grenade in the lawn of radio Pakistan building which exploded with a bang damaging some window panes and a pickup truck. However no casualty was reported.
Patani Bibi w/o Muhammad Nawaz was shot dead by her brother, Waris, over suspicion on her character.
Unidentified men opened fire on a former IGP and other policemen, killing him and four other police personnel on the spot while injuring 2 others.
Three people were wounded in Orangi Extension during the on-going violent shooting incidents.
Firing by Indian security forces prevented sowing of paddy fields in border villages. 2 cows were killed and some houses were damaged.
An old land dispute between the Mallah and jamali communities claimed a life when a man from the Jamali community was shot and killed by men from the Mallah community.
A man was killed in Buffer Zone.
Terrorists gunned down two snake-charmers and hanged a TNT employee in Malir. This was a continuation of violence in Karachi which had been going on for 2 days.
a policeman performing his duty as the guard of the DPO was shot dead and his daughter was injured when gunmen entered the Karachi-bound bus that they were sitting in.
Three members of a family were killed and five others were injured when a mortar shell hit a house in Gall Maidan area.
Two militants and one civilian were killed in a clash in Shinow Ghundai

Some PIA staffers were injured during a protest strike by a joint action committee of PIA employee's unions at the Karachi airport. The strike was being observed at veriosu airport across the country to protest against PIA's decision to hand over some routes to Turkish Airlines. According to Sohail Baloch, convener of the protesting employees, 'outsiders' had been sent by certain politicians to disturb the otherwise peaceful strike.

Benazir Bhutto of the PPP claimed that one of her party's MPA's received threatening phonecalls which warned him to join the \Patriots\" group or party renegades or he would suffer dire consequences. "
the beheaded body of an unidentified man was found near F-9 park.
Unidentified people killed a man and injured 2 others. No further details given.

Ramzan Jatoi, Allan Jatoi, and Sain Dino Jatoi suspected that their relative, Zubaida- wife of Koro Jatoi, had illicit relations with Elahi Bux Kharos. They strangled her and threw her body in the Dadu Canal.
Two armed 'bandits' killed former chairman of the Ushr and Zakat Committee, Jacobabad District.
In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, violent protesters burnt the effigies of various Indian leaders and attacked various temples. They also burnt tyres.
The body of a youth with its throat slit open was thrown down from the roof of a three-storeyed hotel in Naulakha area on Monday
Unknown persons did indiscriminate firing in Ashraf Colony on Monday night.

Thousands of women and hundreds of men protested the local administration's plan to acquire land to build a university. The women went out in the streets and men started firing from a hill top. The police stopped the marchers from going to a college run by an Ismaili community. And paramilitary troops were deployed there. The Agha Khan community is not building the university, but has been targeted in past demonstrations.

Eight oil tankers carrying fuel for US forces in Afghanistan were set on fire by four masked men near the Western Bypass on the outskirts of the provincial capital. This was the first time Nato tankers had been attacked on the outskirts of Quetta. Noone claimed responsibility for the attack.

suspected militants fired four rockets on the Miryan Police Station. However they missed the target and landed in a populous area. one of the missiles landed on a house killing a youth on the spot. The people of the area blocked the roads and held a demonstration

Two rival groups of sudents in Government Degree College exchanged hot words which led to a clash. They threw bricks and used batons on each other and shots were also fired. The police and Principal intervened and brought the situation under control.

A group of armed men barged into a house and opened indiscriminate fire, killing 2 sisters. The father of the victims, Allah Dita, had a land dispute with a family from Sharaqpur and it was his rivals that were responsible for the killings. This land dispute had climed 4 lives in the past.
Mohammad Soomar Dahani shot his wife and his three-year-old daughter in the name of karo-kari. According to him, he had no intention of killing his daughter.
a young man, Muhammad Yaseen, was shot dead near Jilani Centre, Merewether Tower. 2 men on a motorcycle intercepted him and opened fire, killling him and wounding a passerby.
in Bhana Mari area, the three sons of Ghulam Rasool opened fire on their rival Minhaj, and injured him, while a passerby was killed.

Twelve kidnapped people were shot one by one in a hijacked minibus that was parked near Allawala College on Orangi Town. According to reports, all twelve victims were kidnapped earlier from a market in the area while they were out shopping. Police found the bodies in the bus, all were blindfolded with hands tied behind their backs and a bullet wound at the back of the head. Police claimed that the act of terrorism was in retaliation to the death of four MQM workers in a police encounter the day before. All victims were either Sindhis or Punjabis. The dead included a constable, a Ranger and an advocate.

Four armed men on motorcycles gunned down Liaqat Ali Rind in the A-section police area. He was on his way to school in Mumtaz colony when the men opened fire on him. The motive behind the killing was said to be karo-kari.
Ahmed Khan and Rehman Khosh were gunned down over a land dispute. No further details were given.
Some unidentified men on a motorcycle opened fire on a FC vehicle killing three FC personnel and injuring the driver.

at least 10 lawyers were injured in a clash with police during a protest against General Musharraf taking oath as President of Pakistan.the protesters called upon the political parties to boycott the elections.hundreds of lawyers came out after a general body meeting of the Lahore Bar Association.they were pushed back repeatedly by a heavy contingent of police.LBA President wrangled the police as he tried to take the lawyers out on the road.when policemen dragged a couple of lawyers after a scuffle some lawyers started beating policemen in plain clothes who were rescued by other lawyers. a brawl also began.Advocate Shah and Azar Latif pleaded for clam and the police then allowed the lawyers to come out onto theh road.a case was registered against 150 lawyers.7 constables and 2 inspectors were injured.

Unidentified men on a motorbike pulled up to Wali Muhammad, a trader, and shot him from close range. He died on the spot. Later during the day, traders from the market staged a sit-in to demand protection from the police.
security forces backed by helicopter gunships attacked militant hideouts. 2 villagers were killed and several schools were damaged when security forcecs shelled the area.
Two workers of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement were killed in an armed attack.
Security forces on patrol came under fire from militants. 1 militant was killed when security personnel fired back.
A house and a tractor were partially damaged in a bomb blast in the house of a tribesman.

Mohammad Owais, a PPP activist affiliated with UC-1 of City Area-110, was shot and killed by armed motorcyclists outside his house. He was the nephew of Akram Baloch, a senior PPP leader in the Lyari area.
The body of an unidentified woman, approximately 25 years old, was found from Sattukalta. Police stated that strangulation marks were found around her neck.

Saud-ur-Rahman, a local leader of the ASWJ, was shot and killed and his two aides were injured when armed motorcyclists opened fire at them. An ASWJ spokesman claimed that this was a conspiracy against sectarian harmony. The victim was ASWJ's North Nazimabad town head.
2 brothers, Tanvir and Javaid, were shot dead by some unidentified assailants in Chak 4 on Shahkot Nankana Road. The motive behind the incident could not be ascertained.
The badly decomposed body of a person was found in Kot Lakhpat area on Saturday
Militants fired two rockets on the Head Quarters building of the Bajaur Scouts injuring two security personnel.

Unidentified people shot dead the principal of Government Monotechnical College, Syed Gul Imam Shah, as he was about to leave the college. His family stated that he had no personal enmity. He was from Attock area and had been living in Ancholi Society, Federal B Area.
Three people were killed and two were injured when a group of armed men, reportedly belonging to Lashkar I Islam, chased the vehicle of Malik Guli Shah Kukikhel, in order to kidnap him.

Residents living in Lahore near Multan Road staged a protest demonstration against the killing of a Shia religious leader, Allama Abdul Karim Mushtaq. The residents blocked the Multan Road and burnt tyres on the road, suspending traffic for almost two hours.

Scores of people blocked Ferozepur Road near GHQ Hospital in protest against a robber/murder incident. They burnt tyres and chanted slogans against the police for an hour and demanded early arrest of the culprits.
Two rockets were fired from an unknown location which exploded in the outskirts of Peshawar. No damage was reported.
Momin Ali Chandio killed his wife Zarina because when he came home, she was sitting with his cousin. His cousin escaped.

a number of peoplestaged a demonstration on Khadim Ali Road against an inordinate delay in the issuance of passports and alleged corruptionand by the regional passport office. On refusal to register a written complaint against them, they attacked the office braking the wondows and damaging furniture, the outer wall and the gate.
A powerful bomb ripped through a car parked outside a bank on a busy road in the cantonment area, causing minor injuries to 24 people. Eight vehicles and windowpanes of nearby buildings were damaged.
The Indian Security Forces continued firing on Charwa, Bajwat, Chaprar, Harpal, Sucheetgarh and Shakargarh sector. As a result, the firing damaged 4 houses. There were no casualties.
Violent clashes between two factions of MQM continued for the 3rd day when armed men ambushed a vehicle and shot dead the two unidentified people inside.
A man was injured in bhoor while several cattle were killed as the Indian firing continued from across the Sialkot working boundary.
The bullet-riddled body of Rab Nawaz, a resident of Shanti Nagar who hailed from Kashmir, was found by the police.
An SHO and three other police personnel were injured in a bomb explosion when their vehicle hit a roadside improvised device which was exploded by a remote control.

According to police, various religious parties and leaders set a circus on fire as part of their anti-obscenity campaign. Police claim they had set a deadline for the district administration and police to close down all vulgar and obscene places and halt all activities and had set fire to the circus after the deadline had passed. Some 200 people, including MMA's Qazi Hamidullah, Gujranwala MMA information secretary Babar Rizwan and Abdul Malik Shah were booked by the Sabzi Mandi police.
Militants launched a mortar attack on a telecommunications tower on the hilltop in Darra Adam Khel killing a subedar and 2 soldiers.

President Gen Pervez Musharraf warned the militants barricaded in Lal Masjid to surrender or be prepared to get killed. He stated \The government has the power and could do everything, including killing them, but it is demonstrating great patience to save human lives\". Followup: The authorities issues a 'last warning' on the 8th of July 2007 to the Lal Masjid cleric and his fighters, as speculation mounted security forces would launch a full scale assault."

Both PPP and PML-N had setup protest camps to express their respective views on an ongoing issue involving the leaders of both parties and CJP. The PPP workers marched towards Farid Gate where PML-N activists were already present. PPP workers allegedly ransacked the PML-N camp, uprooted their tents, burnt tyres and chanted anti PML-N slogans. The led to a clash between both sets of workers leading to 4 PML-N activists getting injured.
militants blew up a link bridge in Kla Dher, disrupting vehicular traffic.
A presiding officer was beaten up in Jambar Khurd village by a union council nazim and a acouncillor for refusing to accept certain rejected votes.

Shaukat Jut went to the police station to register an FIR against the murderers of his son. They refused to register the FIR and  told him to take it up with the Raja Jhang police station as the crime did not occur in their jurisdiction. Shaukat, 'having despaired of the officials coming to good', returned to his village, and gathered 35-40 people and set the Theh Shekhum police post on fire. Then the Kasur SSP and the Saddar Circle DSP assured the protesters of the registration of the case.
A student and resident of Azad Kashmir was shot dead in Orangi Town.
Two persons were injured in a clash between rivals inside a mosque during the election of Zakar and Ushr Committee.
A truck and utility store were set on fire.
Ali Bux and Ghanwar Marfani were gunned down, by 10 armed men, near Meero bridge. Area people said that the incident was an offshoot of a running dispute between Marfanis and Brohis.

Police clashed with students who were protesting under the banner of the IJT, who claimed that the police had registered a 'fake' case of attempted murder on some of its activists. The protesters blocked the main road and burnt tyres to press for the withdrawl of the case and the police responded by resorting to baton-charge and aerial firing. In response, the students pelted the police with stones. 2 policemen and 2 students were injured. A case has been registered against 150 students for the event.
Three people received bullet injuries due to shooting incidents in Korangi.
A man was wounded at Ayesha Manzil.
a man was killed and another was injured in an attack by three brothers on Karamuddin and Abdul Ghani Narejo with axes, over a land dispute.
Six persons were injured in a tribal clash between the Khokhars and the Malaks in Pano Aqil. The clash was over a property dispute. Both sides used sticks, lathis and fire arms freely.
Two Bugti tribesmen were killed in a landmine blast in Patokh area of Dera Bugti.
2 women were injured in Indian shelling along LoC in Nakyal Sector on Wednesday.

Students from Government College of Commerce, Commercial Institute and Polytechnic Institute protested against the murder of Mirza Taimur Beg. They burnt tyres in several places in the city and called for stern action against the murderers.
One militant was killed and seven others were arrested in a raid by security forces in the Michini area of the Yakghund tehsil.

4 people were killed and three were injured in a clash between Arain group and Dogar Group over the distribution of irrigation water in Sahiwal on Sunday; Follow Up: The Dogar group leader Allah Ditta succumbed to injuries on Thursday. The original incidence took place on 20th August whereas in the newspaper, reporting date is 27th August
Nasir Ahmed Butt, a member of the Ahmadi Communnity and a fruit vendor by profession, was gunned down by armed motorcyclists.

Students of different schools took to the streets and pelted passing vehicles with stones, disrupting vehicular traffice in Lyari protesting against the arrest of Mr. G.M. Syed. Glass panels of a local bank branch were also smashed during protesting. They dirupted traffic on ShahWaliullah Road and Atmaram Pretamdas Road where they burnt a Pakistan Steel van. They aslo resorted to aerial firing upon the refusal of shopkeepers to close down their shops. The crowd later dispersed when the police arrived on the scene.

militants simultaneously attacked a building in the police lines area, district police office and the city police station. a hand grenade hurled at the city police station fell on a house, killing Razia Bibi and injuring her husband and mother-in-law. this event sparked a heavy exchange of fire between the police and the militants. a local said the Taliban was responsible.

Dozens of people from Shahdara and its neighbouring areas blocked the GT Road and burned tyres to protest the shortage of electricity, water and gas. MPA Rana Iqbal and Shahdara police tried to passify the mob but when it didn't work riot police charged at them with batons. The protesters responded by pelting the police with stones to which the police resorted to aerial firing which eventually dispersed the mob. Sub-inspector Afzal Virk was beaten up by the protesters as well.
Unidentified activists hurled crackers  in different localities but no one was reported to be hurt.
One man was killed and two others were injured in an altercation between two groups of the Teevno clan in Banho Teevno village near Tharu Shah.  No other details were reported.
A bullet riddled body of a young man was found in a taxi. The reason behind the killing could not be ascertained.
Maqsood Khushal was passing through Millat Town when his vehicle was intercepted by unidentified youths who set him and his vehicle on fire.

Residents of Hassanabdal, frustrated by frequent power breakdowns, attacked three Wapda officials who had come to the area to fix a fault. They also damaged the vehicle and thrashed its driver. They then proceeded to the Wapda complaint office and thrashed two officials working there and ransacked the office. When the protesters proceeded to block the G.T.Road, police negotiated and convinced them to disperse.
Militants planted IEDs around a Basic Health Unit and detonated them, destroying the building.

The bodies of two teenagers were found stuffed in gunny bags near Timber market in an old city area. The bodies bore gunshot wounds and seemed like they had been killed a couple of hours earlier before being dumped.
A young girl was stabbed to death by her finacee on suspicion of her having illicit relations with another man.
Security forces and militants clashed near Jaler Post and Banda Post. Residential areas in Banda also came under attack, leaving a teenager injured.

A passer-by was killed and 5 others were injured in a clash between a group of milkmen and police during an operation to drive out cattle from the city limits. A squad of 11 LDA officials, a magistrate and four policemen reached Madina Market when they were intercepted by milkmen who attacked them with sticks. The police resorted to aerial firing to disperse the attackers and a stray bullet hit a passer-by, which proved fatal.
Paramilitary headquarters were targeted with missiles and rockets, leaving a soldier and a technician injured.
An old person was killed by unidentified persons in Modern Cold Storage on Sunday.

Imtiaz and Falah Sher were intercepted by armed men while they were travelling in their car. The assailants shot and killed them before fleeing the scene. A kin of the victim had gunned down a man over a sectarian issue some time ago but the police did not say anything about the motive behind this incident.
Ten shops were set on fire by activists of SNA who were protesting against the killing of Sindhis in Karachi and Hyderabad.
A school was blown up by militants in the Mohammad Jan Kallay area of Bara tehsil.

After a young man was targeted in the Hussain Hazara Goth area of Karachi, two groups exchanged heavy gunfire in the area. An office of a political party was also set on fire and was partially burnt. According to police, the incident seemed to be because of a dispute between two ethnic groups in the area.
Bashir Ahmad and his wife, Sahiban Bibi, were returning to Chuchak when Saleem Hasan and his two accomplices intercepted the couple and strangled them to death  over a residential plot dispute.

Vendors were blocking the Sabzi Mandi road and had spilled over to the main University Road. When the police tried to push them back, they opened pelted stones. The police retaliated by firing in the air to disperse the crowd. A spectator standing in his balcony, Naeem Siddiqi, was hit by a stray bullet and injured. Another person sustained minor injuries as well.
Amjad Imrani was killed. No further details given.
A special branch constable was shot dead while he was standing near Diwan Hotel in Lahi Gate, Shikarpur when an unidentified man opened fire on him, killing him on the spot.
A young man was found shot dead near Bhit Shah Mazar with visible signs of torture on his body. In the last 24 hours, 5 to 6 men were killed in Lyari due to a dispute within Baba Ladla gang.
ISPR spokesman, Major Mushtaw Ahmed, claimed that five militants were killed during operations in the Mangaltan area of the Charbagh tehsil.

After Mazhar Hussain allegedly set a manuscript of the Holy Quran on fire, angry people from the area demonstrated outside his house and attempted to set Mazhar, his family members and his house on fire. However, police and local ulema (religious scholars) intervened in time after realizing that the accused was mentally handicapped. Mazhar Hussain was later arrested on charges of Blasphemy.
Following a fresh wave of violence, a police constable was killed by unknown men in Sohrab Goth on Sunday.
Two people killed one Asif and injured three others over a land dispute. No further details were given.
A militant was killed and four FC troops were injured when militants attacked a security forces' convoy in Dera bugti.
A woman was shot dead by unidentified men in Kehror Pucca on Wednesday.

A curfew was imposed in Hangu bazaar after four people were killed and several other injured in clashes between two sectarian groups. The trouble started when sabotuers blew up four shops in the main bazaar which killed two people. The incident sparked clashes in the town and another two people, one of them an Afghan refugee, were killed. Helicopter gunships flew at low altitude to monitor the situation.

Four persons, including the Assistan Advocate-General, were hurt when two consecutive bombs went off on the Arts School road within half an hour of each other. Officials reported that they were locally made devices.
