Aslam strangled his sister, Nasreen Bibi, to death for 'honour' after the family suspected that she had 'loose morals'.

Helicopters hit several targets in the Mehsud area after a rocket attack on a paramilitary fort by militants. 10 militanst were killed and troops claimed to have destroyed several bunkers and seized two vehicles loaded with weapons.
Mian Liaq Ahmad was attacked by some unknown assailants in the People's Colony.

At least ten people were killed and twenty eight others were injured when a time-bomb, fitted in a motorcycle parked along the main gate, went off at Hussaini mosque in Malir when worshippers were coming out of the mosque after Friday prayers. A vehicle parked next to the motorcycle was severly damaged as well.

Armed riders on a motorcycle targeted a young man belonging to the Sunni Tehrik, when they opened fire on him in Sector 11-G. A spokesperson for the Sunni Tehrik claimed that the victim was their party activist and was targeted by the 'banned outfit' only for his association with the ST.
Two bullet-riddled bodies were found from the Pasni area of Khuzdar.

The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as a man was gunned down by armed men on a motorbike in Taiser Town. He was reportedly targeted due to his ethnic background as he did not belong to a political party.

a blast took place in the Kabari bazaar, dealing in second hand electronic items. 20 shops were gutted. A bomb planted in a bicycle outside an ice-cream shop in the same area went off 2 minutes later. Both blasts took place in the Qissa Khwani bazaar. 5 civilians were killed and over 70 injured. two militants who fled after the attack were killed in an exchange of fire with the police, while 2 other militants were arrsted.

2 journalists and about a dozen lawyers were injured when police tear-gased and baton-charged the long march caravan on Sheikhupura road, when the police tried to stop them and told them to go back. The lawyers retaliated by throwing stones and removing barricades. the police also hit vehicles carrying Jamaat-i-Islami activists and broke window panes.
A 16 inch diameter pipeline connecting a gas plant with Pir Koh gas field was blown up.
An unidentified man was killed in Pak Colony, however, his body could not be recovered due to intense firing in the area.
6 armed men ambushed the vehicle of the chief of the Mamond Lashkar, Malik Muneer Khan, and killed him. The deceased had raised a lashkar of Mamond tribes and destroyed several militant hideouts.

A Taliban group raided shops in Wana and burnt hundreds of metres of cloth saying it was too thin to be made into suitably modest garments which would not cover the human body properly and that was un-islamic.

Eight people were injured when activists of Pakistan People's Party and Muslim League (Nawaz) clashed. The clash started fater both the parties' candidates were returning after filing their nomination papers for the upcoming elections. They raised slogans against eachother which led to the clash.
7 people were injured in a clash at Chak 96/9-R polling station, over local government elections.
Jamali and Bhutta tribes clashed over an old feud killing two people.
A Datsun pick-up was set ablaze.
The same militants that had destroyed 2 school buildings earlier, proceeded to the a basic health unit building and blew it up in a similar fasion.
Indian shelling along sialkot working boundary in Suchectgarh sector injured a person on Monday
A cinema owner was kidnapped in peshawar along with his body guard and chauffeur.

The Indian Security Forces continued firing on Zafarwal, Charwa, Bajwat, Chaprar, Harpal, Sucheetgarh, Bajragarhi and Shakargarh sectors. As a result, two villagers- Shams Ahmed of Mundarwal and Muhammad Boota of Thathi Gujran village- were seriously injured as they were hit by stray bullets fired by the Indian Forces. The firing also killed 2 animals in Thathi Kalan village, badly damaged nine houses as well as the paddy crop. The Chenab Rangers returned the fire.
12 armed men attacked the house of Salabat Chider and killed one person, identified as Muhammad Nawaz, while two other people were injured.

Violence between two rival tribal factions erupted for a second time in recent days. The Hamidzai and Ghabizai factions used heavy weapons against each other on Friday and continued to do so till the publication of this report. However, no casualties were reported.

When Levies personnel stopped a car for checking, the occupants hurled grenades at the checkpost, killing a Levies man, Itbar Gul, on the spot. The security personnel chased the assailants and opened fire which casued the explosives on one of them to explode, killing him on the spot and making it possible for the other two to be arrested.
Militants fired two missiles on a Scouts camp in Wana, but failed to cause any damage. Security forces retalitated by firing mortars and artillery on suspected hideouts.

Two persons were killed and another was serious injured in an armed clash between two rival groups over a property dispute, when the Gharsaney faction of the Storikhel tribe exchanged fire with their rivals in a remote village in Tirah valley. Later a casefire was negotiated between the groups by a decision of a jirga.
Two rockets hit houses in Musa Colony and Braganza area respectively. Three people were injured and the houses were damaged.
Mohammad Arshad, a labourer, was shot dead by Mohammad Rafique in Misri Shah area.
Two FC men were injured when their vehicle was blown up by a bomb explosion.

Students of a local girls college staged a demonstration to protest against the recent increase in fees and also against the arrest of 22 protesting students the day before. A contingent of female police officers was called to control the situation. When a police contingent put up barricades to block the way of the procession, the students hurled stones and bricks at them, injuring 2 constables and a magistrate. The police responded by resorting to baton charge and tear gas and also gave a severe beating to boys of primray school who were on their way home. The protesting students burnt an effigy of Punjab Education Minister Usman Ibrahim and chanted anti-government slogans. They also blocked the road by burning tyres.

6 persons from a rival group killed  one, Khan Mohammad Anwar Khan, a Muslim Leaguer and former District Councillor and ex-Chairman of Gojarke Union Council in Daska tehsil. 2 of the assailants, Tahir and Sikandar, have been arrested.
Indian shelling in chattar bazaar and balakot village injured 6 people on wednsday
A rocket was fired on the house of Inayat kaley tribal chief Muhammad Ibrahim Khan. No one was hurt in the attack.
Two men were kidnapped and shot in Korangi. One of them died instantly and the other survived the attack.

27 people were killed and more than 80 injured when two suicide bombers struck two localities in the high security  zone in the garrison city of Rawalpindi. The first bomb exploded in a packed bus carrying defence employees near the Qasim market, followed by an equally powerful explosion about three kilometers away and close to the GHQ in RA bazaar area. Authorities described the two blasts as a coordinated move to hit high-profile targets in the military garrison. It was claimed that both the bombings were carried out by al-Qaeda militants.

Pro Baitullah Mehsud militants killed 22 tribesmen of the Niamatkhel clan of the Bhittani tribe. Tehrik I Taliban Pakistan claimed the responsibility of the killings. On the other hand, Niamatkhel spokesperson stated that their struggle against murderers, robbers and kidnappers (i.e. Taliban) would continue.
The residents of Basil and Sesko villages have been fighting over a pasture land for 45 days. Two people were shot and eleven were injured in a recent clash between the two tribes.
Powerful bomb exploded near officials house causing damage to nearby property
3 persons were killed and 3 others were injured in an armed clash between two rival groups at Chak No 15/GB.
Indian shelling continued on villages on the Working Boundary of AJK. Details are not available.

Suspected pro-Taliban militants shot dead an alleged leader of a gang after he ignored warnings to stop criminal activities in tribal areas.  Ameer Sayed was driving his car when he was ambushed in Darra Adamkhel by armed men.
A man and a woman were killed by the latter's family in the name of honour when three men shot them both.

At least one student was injured in a clash between supporters of the APMSO and the Pakistan Students Federation (PSF) at the Urdu Science College when one group tried to manhandle the supporters of the other group, shots were fired in the air which was followed by a free for all using blunt weapons. According to sources, the trouble began a day before when some students were stopped from interfering with the intermediate supplementary examinations.
At least three civilians were injured and a house was destroyed in unprovoked Indian firing from across the Line of Control in Ghaipura village, Leepa valley.
Two persons were killed and ten were injured in a gun battle between the Chachar and the Jagirani tribesmen over a land dispute in Kutcho Bindi village.
Activists of the Muslim Students' Federation marched trhough the city centre and burnt tyres and broke windows of shops to protest against the killing of MSF Additional Secretary and his son.
Two student groups, IJT and MSF, exchange fire in MAO College. No one was injured.
During a general strike called by the JSMM against the assassination of Shaheed Benazir Bhutto, 'activists' and 'Sindhi people' set ablaze 127 vehicles including 76 trailers.
power supply to several areas of Kalat was suspended after a pyon of a transmission line was blown up in Quetta's outskirts.

Supreme Court's additional registrar, Syed Amjad Raza was shot dead by four armed men who barged into his house at 4:15 am. The police claim that the murder was done by robbers, but the widow of the officer said that it was a clear case of target killing, as the 'robbers' did not take anything from the house, and shot the officer from a point blank range as he opened the door. She also suspected some involvement of the government and other agencies in the murder, because a police patrol WAS present outside their house when the murder took place, and it did not take any action to catch the fleeing culprits.
Factional fighting between rival groups of MQM caused firing in Nasir Colony in which 4 people were injured.
Noor Bajkani shot dead his sister in law, M, on the pretext of karo-kari
unidentified people planted a bomb near a hairdresser's shop in Mal Adda Nushki Bazaar. The bomb went off injuring 2 people as a result.
Two people were killed and eight others injured in a bomb explosion aboard a passenger bus.
A woman, identified as Samina, was found stabbed to death at her house. SHO Muzamil Husain suspected that it might have been for 'honour'.
Militants used remote controlled bombs to blow up a government primary school in the suburbs of Peshawar.
Four people including two police officers were injured when a polling station in Killi Qambrani was attcked by unknown assailants with a hand grenade.
According to the police, Ghulam Rasool, was stabbed several times and then thrown into the canal (where it was recovered from). The motive behind the incident could not be ascertained.

a large number of men on motorbikes emerged from Faizabad and moved onto Garden Avenue when they set fire to a police post and damaged traffic signals. This was in reaction to the Suprem Court's decision.
The police had arrested a large number of Sipah-i-Sahaba activists from a mosque during Moharram procession. Thus the SSP protested against the arrests by distrupting traffic and burning tyres.

100s of residents from Peshawar, led by businessmen, organized a protest procession against excessive loadshedding of electricity and natural gas. Even though most of the protesters had dispersed peacefully, the police arrested a few and beat them up. Upon hearing about this, the protesters returned and threatened to block the main road. They later dispersed when they were assured that the matter would be resolved.
A man was shot dead and another injured when 3 armed men on a motorcycle opened fire on a sweet shop.
troops backed by helicopter gunships attacked militant hideouts in Chinna, Ammay Kamay and Garh areas of Kohat, Khyber and Orakzai agencies.
A dispenser was shot dead by unknown assailants in Saroki village on Wednesday
A youth was killed and two women were injured in Korangi No. 2 when plainclothes commandos opened fire on some youngsters who came to the area to collect protection money.
A mutilated corpse of a man was found dumped in an apartment.
2 brothers were shot and killed In their sleep by 2 unidentified men.

Residents of various areas of Union Council Khalisa-I blocked the main road to protest against suspension of electricity supply for over 16 hours. The protesters were dispersed by the police who used batons and tear gas.
troops carried out search operations around Kandao near Biha, Waliabad, Sambat, Baidarra, Gulibgah and Shakardara. During an exchange of fire one soldier was injured in Gulibgah

Activists of several religious parties held a protest in front of the Masjid-i-Shuhada to condemn sactions on Afghanistan placed bu the US and UN. They burnt the American flag and threw bricks and shoes at plainclothes policemen who were trying to push them back into the mosque.

30 people were injured when PDA rally was teargassed and baton-charged by police as the procession entered Clock Tower Chowk on Friday. The rally was against the corruption, goondaism and lawlessness in the country.
One Saifullah was gunned down by four armed men. The motive behind the murder is not clear.

The Najeeb Pathan group had a land dispute with Farooq group, upon which the two traded fire with each other. When the police arrived at the scene, a constable got hit by a bullet, and died on the way to the hospital.
During a military search operation, some militants opened fire at security convoy. The soldiers retaliated and killed 5 militants and injured 3 others who were then arrested.
A hand grenade was hurled into a barbar's house, causing injury to 5 people. Damage to the building was also reported.

four people, including an ASI and a police constable were injured police resorted to firing while confronting with violent protestors. Hundreds of Gujjo town residents were protesting against alleged confinement and torture of one Khamiso Mirbahar, brother of a local PPP leader, Urs Mirbahar. ; Forty activists of People's Party Parliamentarian were booked by police for creating a law and order situation while protesting.
Shaukat Ali, a cloth trader by profession, was found shot dead at a desolate place near Tohid mosque.
Two security personnel were injured when a landmine exploded in the Kharoti area near a checkpost in Tari Mangal.

Syed Raza Haider, a senior member of the MQM and a member of the Sindh Assembly was shot dead while he was attending funeral prayers at a mosque. The assailants first shot his guard and then went inside and shot Raza Haider. The MQM leadership insinuated that the ANP was responsible while Interior Minister Rehman Malik has explicitly stated that the Sipah-i-Sahaba was responsible as Mr. Haider was on their 'hit-list'. Follow-up: Initial investigations hint at sectarian motives behind the killing.
Reportedly, there was an incident at another ANP stronghold in Bacha Khan Chowk.  The public stoned a passing vehicle and, in retailation, the police fired teargas shells at the protesters.

A Pakistan Air Force (PAF) transport aircraft and a VIP chopper aborted their missions for Chitral after a rocket was fired on one of them near Dir. It is not known who fired the rocket and for what purpose.
A heavy exchange of fire took place between the security forces and the militants when militants attacked a security checkpost situated in a government school in Dheri area.
A man was killed in Orangi.
A woman was killed when the Indian security forces heavily shelled the villages in Hajira sector, Poonch.
Five pesonnel of security forces were injured in landmine blast in Lehri area.
Sharif Khalid allegedly shot dead one Akhtar Ali in Ballaywala Police Station area.
Protesters allegedly opened fire on a police mobile van near Al-Karam Square, Liaquatabad.
A US drone fired missiles at a house, killing 9 people and injuring 3. The identities and nationalities of the victims could not be established.
At least five tribesmen were killed while another three were injured in a clash between the Masayzai and Imranzai tribes in the mazai Adha area of Qilla Abdullah.
A remote control bomb was detonated by terrorists, damaging the Kalparti Bridge.
Ten people were injured during a clash between the supporters of two rival groups, the PPP and Arbab Ittehad, on the occasion of election of Usher/Zakat Committee.
an exchange of fire between militants and security forces took place following an attack on a checkpost on the RCD Highway. No casulaty was reported as the rockets fired missed the checkpost.
A trussed up body of a young man, bearing torture marks, was found dumped in the Lyari river.
A watchman, Fazal Ghani was injured in an explosive device blast in Malik Nawab market, outside a shop for video games, VCRs and CDs etc.

enraged people forces shoop keepers to pull down their shutters after the death of a boy in a road accident on Umerkot road. Enraged Baloch community people gathered at the civil hospital and broke glasses of the gates in protest and raised slogans against the police.

Two persons were killed and another one suffered injuries when Odho and Ansari tribesmen exchanged fire in Memon Mohalla in Khairpur after a bitter argument arose during tea. Both groups used firearms to shoot at each other. Another report stated that due to an olde dispute, one of the Ansari tribesmen followed the other party to settle a score and an exchange of fire ensued.

A former press secretary of the Shia Ulema Council and a Nikah Registrar was killed when armed men targeted him near Pakistan Chowk. No eyewitnesses could confirm the mode of transport etc. Police termed it a sectarian attack.
Two children were seriously injured when a mortar shell hit a house in Sultankhel area.
Gul Mohammed Barohi was shot and killed by unidentified attackers.Police said it was the result of a tribal dispute between Marfanis and Barohis.

The Director of Research Laboratories in the Ministry of Defence, Syed Zafar Hussain Zaidi, was shot dead by two motorcyclists who intercepted his car on and sprayed bullets at it. The driver managed to survive without any injuries. According to the SSP Central, Shaukat Hussain, it was a targetted killing with sectarian motives. Follow-up: The Lashkar-i-Jhangvi claimed responsibility for the murder. They stated that any government functionary that abuses power would face the same fate. The also stated that they had urged President General Musharraf not to implement the death sentence awarded to Sheikh Haq Nawaz.

clashes between the Shahlyani and the Mengal tribes began when a land owner, Mir Shahlyani and Abdul Nabi Mengal's own brother who worked on Mir Manthar Khan Shahlyani's farm were killed by him on 3-jul-05.  following thiis Mir Shahlyani's brother and other tribesmen attacked the Chakar Khan Mengal village. tribesmein from both sides took poitions and exchanged fire.5 people were killed and 2 others were injured. police cordoned off the area and forced the tribesmen to cease fire.
Four missiles were fired on a paramilitary camp in razmak.
Rival political activists attacked the procession taken out by ANP, Madeji, to protest against the Hyderabad killings.

A man killed his daughter over 'honour' in the Civil Lines area. Reports said that Arshad's daughter 'S' had developed relations with a youth in the neighbourhood and he was taunted by some people over the affair. Arshad then injured his daughter with a knife, and she later succumbed to her wounds.

Five civilians and a policeman were killed, and 30 others injured when a suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the main gate of a police parade ground. Officials and eyewitnesses said the attacker ploughed his Suzuki car into the gate of the police compound on the main Hangu-Kohat Road, where a large number of recruits were busy in their morning drill. They said the bomber detonated the explosives when the security guards stopped him at the gate of the Mazhar Parade Ground.
Local police, headed by Sub-inspector Shaukat Gujjar, raided a theatre, arrested 2 actresses and tortured spectators during the havoc that ensued.
Gojra police found the headless body of an unidentified woman from the canal.
Militants kidnapped 6 tribesmen. Security forces have started a search operation and have arrested 3 suspects and seized 2 vehicles.
A rocket was fired on a hospital in Landi Kotal. The armed depot is situated at the back of the hospital could have been the target. This is the third attack on the hospital in two weeks.

People gathered in the Orangi township area and pelted passing vehicles with stones. They set a water tanker and two Pakistan Steel buses on fire. Police had to resort to tear gas shelling to disperse the crowd.
A cloth trader was shot dead by unidentified persons in Township. He was not known to have any enmity or montary dispute with anyone.
A person was found dead in his Multan Road quarter on Friday. His body was hanging up with a rope.

Some people of the Hazeena village hurled hand grenades at their rivals house over a land dispute, causing injuries to a few people there. Later, the two parties exchanged heavy gunfire which resulted in the death of five people.
Seveal people were injured in Ward No 13, Multan during LB elections on Saturday.
Two policemen were injured.
Police sources say that an ex-MQM political activist who joined the ruling PML after the 1992 cleanup operation was shot dead along with his son by unidentified men while a passerby was injured.
A body stuffed in a sack was found near Siddiq Goth in the Al Falah area.
Muhammad Muneer was murdered at Bussu Wali, near Shorkot.

Two children were killed and 5 others wounded when two land mines exploded in Shinkot Gang of the Bajaur tribal region. The landmines were planted at the main gate of a residential compound of a tribesman, Noor Jamal, which exploded in quick succession. His two sons died on the spot, and Noor Jamal himself lost his legs.

Two passengers, including an army man, were killed and 9 others were injured when a powerful bomb ripped through a Jhelum-bound passenger bus near Kharian. This was the fifth bomb blast in a passenger bus during the last 2 months.

Three Chachar tribesmen were killed in the Dreho village, Kandhkot town when a rival party opened fire on a man, killing him on the spot. The relatives of the deceased chased the killers and managed to gun down two of them. All belonged to the Chachar tribe.

4 rockets were fired from the mountains of Shahpur village, causing damage to a house and an orchard. The owners of the house have no enmity and according to the report the site of the blast is close to the private residence of a police head constable, Riaz, who had been charged with killing two brother's in custody a month ago but were not arrested.
One Rafiq was shot dead. No further details were given.
A teenage girl was hanged to death by 4 assailants. The motive behind this incident could not be ascertained.

A peaceful procession by teachers, while moving towards the Secretariat campus to present the AJK Prime Minister with their grievances, was baton-charged and tear gassed. This provoked a violent clash when protesters began pelting vehicles, police and shops with stones. Many policemen were injured during a free for all scuffle. Traffic came to a standstill while the police tried to disperse the crowd.
Five people cut a woman's ear and nose over a match issue at Zafarkay village. They tried to strangle her with a cord first, and later chopped her nose off when villagers came to rescue her.
Lance Naik Tariq Mehmood, constable Sifatullah and an unidentified person were injured in a landmine blast when their vehicle hit it in Chatar Khaleji area.
On the fourth day of the on-going violence in Karachi, more than half a dozen shops were burnt in Aligarh Colony.
A first year college student was on his way home when an unidentified motorcyclist shot and killed him. The motive behind the killing was not known.
two militants were killed and 6 soldiers were injured in clashes in Aligrama, Guljaba, Fizaghat.

The death of Farooq Dada, an alleged MQM terrorist, and his three companions sparked off violence in the city areas of Gulbahar, Nazimabad, Malir and Badia Town. Protesters burnt a KTC bus and two other vehicles in the Gulbahar and Federal B area. Incidents of heavy shooting were mostly reported from Baldia Town. A number of witnesses claimed that Police and Rangers resorted to indiscriminate firing and did not even spare women and children.

there was an alleged attack on the office and party workers of Sindh Taraqqi Pasand Party in Nawabshah by a particular group. They warned that if such activities are not stopped the consequences will be disasterous. The STP condemned the attack.
Unidentified men attacked a house of a police constable in the Gulbahar area and killed him in front of his family.

some people were taking a small Alam procession to Bakhshi park Imam Bargah when people from a different sect stopped them on the pretext that they did not have permission to use that route. People from both sides exchanged words, fire, and stones.
Militants opened fire on a vehicle injuring two men of the security forces.
Security forces demolished a seminary in Bachkan Ahmadzai area. The religious seminary, Jamia Miftahul  Uloom, was believed to be used as a sanctuary by militants.

During the fourth phase of local body elections, there were several clashes between supporters of candidates and security personnel. In Nawabshah district, a candidate for Nazim and dozens of his supporters were arrested for attacking a police party.
Unknown assailants entered Abdul Wahid's house and shot the inmates and fled. They killed 4 members of a family. The police have arrested 1 individual.
A paramilitary convoy came under attack in kaniguram and three passers-by were injuried.
The body of an old man was found in Mehmoodabad on Thursday.

A joint team of the Capital Police and an intelligence agency captured a suspect who is alleged to be the Deputy leader of the TTP when they intercepted an explosive-laden car. The suspect is said to be a car-bomb expert and was supposedly on his way to hand over the car to a would be suicide bomber for an attack.
Two bodies stuffed in gunny bags were found from the Federal B area.
Two people were killed and another injured when they were targetted by unidentified gunmen.
Three people were shot dead and four others were injured in a clash between two groups when they opened fire on each other at the Swati Gate.
Security forces continued artillery firing on the Militant hideouts in Mingora while local villagers set a militant vehicle on fire.

Five students were allegedly shot and injured in Jamshoro university when police resorted to firing in order to disperse an unruly crowd . According to reports, the students had barged into the vice chancelor's office demanding that the exams be postponed. Upon refusal they damaged a university car, tv set and fax machine along with torching a police checkpost. The members of the Taraqi Pasand Students Federation and Jeay Sindh Students Federation claimed that the police had opened indiscriminate fire on the students. Hwoever, the police denied all claims and said they had only resorted to aerial firing and that several policemen were injured when students pelted them with stones.
A 30-year old man was shot dead by unidentified gunmen who came in a care and fired at him.
IJI chief , Mian Nawaz Sharif was passing through the village of a rival PDA cadidate when his supporters clashed with PDA member PPP. IJI activists fired at the PPP workers but no one was injured.
A cloth seller, Abdul Rashid of Gojra, went to a mosque to pray and was shot dead by the prayer leader.
a Pakistani paramilitary soldier was shot dead by suspected militants.

Jet fighters, helicopters and gunships attacked some villages in Khwaizai and Baizai tehsils along the Afghan border and in Michinai area of Mohmand agency. Troops destroyed 20 houses including that of Taliban spokesperson Ikramulla Mohmand, in Kong and Sheikhan villages. a Taliban Markaz in Sheikhano Kallay was also destroyed. helicopter gunships also targetted militant positions in Bhaikor, Speeray and Mullaghani villages. at least 18 militants were killed.
9 soldiers, 2 militants and 1 civilian were killed in roadside explosions and exchange of fire in different parts of Malakand.

According to Frontier Corps sources, unidentified people fired 20 to 25 rockets at the Saeed checkpoint. The assailants fled when FC men returned fire, they said and added that no casualty had been reported.
A woman was injured by \sniper's firing\"."
A bomb weighing one kg was found on the Chunaywali Bhatti Chowk and taken into custody by the Civil Defence officials.

Two tribesmen were adminsitered 99 and 70 lashes in public in Bara, Khyber Agency, for a 'proved charge' of committing unnatural offence against a minor boy. The administered punishment was witnessed by 5000 people in a local goods market.

Two bomb blasts took place in quick succession near the seminary. The first exploded just outside a restaurant and the second exploded after a delay of 10-15 minutes; Follow up: Compensation for the blast victims was announced the same day; Follow up: Funeral prayers of eight victims were held in the Madressah.
Amir Khan and a woman were shot dead at the Ajab Khan Killy allegedly on suspicion of hng illicit relations with each other.
Three people were killed and four others were injured in the intermittent exchanges of fire between the militants and the security forces.

Four rockets were fired at the Sui Colony from the direction where the Bugti House was located.  After the rocket attack, an exchange of fire continued for 10 minutes between two rival groups. However, no loss of life or property was reported. It was not clear from the report who the rival groups were, or whether the attack was an act of terrorism or a targetted attack.

Former chairman of Qila Soba Singh town committee Abdul Hameed was shot dead in his house by two armed men. The two accused shot him dead when they entered his house and resorted to firing. The victim's adopted son was also seriously injured in the shooting.
A group of Afghan refugees and some people of the locality opened fire on each other, resulting in the death of 1 person and the injury of 3 people.
Hundreds of Gwadar Town residents demonstrated against Wapda. The protesters also burnt 3 out of 5 Wapda generators in protest against shortage of electricity and long hours of loadshedding.

Troops killed 15 militants in Swat in a search-and-cordon operation. A large cache of arms, ammunition and explosives was seized during the raids. Followup: The area where the operation took place was Banjot and Jamet areas, which was mentioned in another report.
A woman was killed by her husband on the pretext of karo-kari in Jakhrani village, Jacobabad.
Militants attacked a security checkpost with weapons and rockets in the halakhel and Mulla Syed areas of Cheenar. The troops retaliated and destroyed three bunkers in the area.
The bullet-riddled body of Muhammad Tahir, who was a labourer at an industrial unit, was found a day after he had gone missing. The victim hailed from Multan in Punjab.
Unidentified miscreants planted a remote controlled expplosive device on a road near sadiqabad. However no loss was reported.
Salim was brought dead to the hospital.
In Qazi Ahmed, Mrs Kamoot was gunned down on suspicion of illicit relations by her husband Rano Khan.

15 people of two rival groups were kidmapped after the police arrested a member of the sudrani clan. Members of the Sudrani clan attacked the village of the rival clan and kidnapped 4 hostages. The police despite several negotiations with the sudrani clan failed to recover the hostages. The rival gang heavily armed then attacked the villages of the sudrani gang looted shops, houses and kidnapped several members. The sudrani gang then forced upon the police to release the arrested member and negotiations were underway for the release of all hostages. The TPO when contacted by the news men said that negotiations were underway and all hostages will be released shortly.

An attempt on the life of Balochistan's CM, Jan Mohammad Yousaf, was made by armed assailants opening fire at his motorcade. Spokesman for the provincial government stated that the ATF vehicle had come under fire of a paramilitary force due to a misunderstanding.
Alam Zeb was targeted by armed motorcyclists within the remit of Pakistan Bazaar police station
A mother of seven was axed to death by her brother when he suspected her of 'immoral' behavior. The killer later surrendered himself to the police.
The President of Tehrik-i-Minhaj-ul-Quran, Azad Kashmir Branch, Prof. Mohammad Rafique, was seriously injured when attacked while sitting in 'Aitikaf'.

The Lal Masjid and its surrounding areas witnessed pitched battles between security forces and supporters of Maulana Abdul Aziz, former chief cleric of the mosque, after worshipers refused to offer Friday prayers behind a government-appointed imam. The protesters, many of them students of Jamia Fareedia, slipped into the mosque, reoccupied it and repainted the walls of the mosque red, which had been turned beige on the orders of the authorities.  The act came as a direct protest against the government's acting on Lal Masjid, which had killed a number of people.
an activist of MQM, Umar Din, was shot dead by on Nishtar road.
A shell fired by the Indian troops landed in house in Goi village injuring four persons of a family.
Waris Ali, along with his sons Riaz and Farhad, shot dead Amjad Ali over a petty property dispute.
The bullet riddled body of Yasin Awan, who was kidnapped two weeks back was found.

At least 15 people were killed when a lashkar attacked Jilamai and Chardewal villages. The police arrived at the scene and opened fire at the rioters. Residents alleged that the assailants were trained militants from North Waziristan. An official in Alizai confirmed five dead and six wounded in the attack while an eye witness said that 15 bodies were counted on the outskirts of the village.

Firing erupted all over Hyderabad city and Latifabad areas of Shahi Bazaar, Chotti Ghitti, Churri Gali, Gari Khatta areas and several parts of Latifabad. A policeman was injured in firing at Bhattai Chowk.
The body of a local trader, who had been kidnapped near his hometown in Khungi, was found in Arang area of Bajaur Agency. The body bore five bullet wounds.
The Banda post was attacked, in which one soldier was injured.
A  young man was shot and injured in 'sniper firing' by unidentified persons in the Arambagh area.
An unidentified body was found in the Raees Amrohi Colony.
Three brothers who were MQM workers were shot dead by unidentified gunmen.
A grenade was thrown into the courtyard of ASI Noor Mohammad Bugti's house, injuring his guest Amanullah.
FC soldier Muhammad Nasir was killed when he was hit by a landmine while defusing it.
A woman, B, was shot dead by her husband, Mehrab, in the name of karo-kari as he suspected that she was maintaining illicit relations with Hakim.

The Lal Masjid moral brigade descended on the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences on hearing of alleged descecration of Quranic verses in its nursing hostel. But they left mysteriously after a while without taking any action. The police figured that they probably got a message from their higher ups to not take any action at the moment. But the show of strength reminded people of the possible action the Lal Masjid brigade could take in any show case of moral disintegrity.
A suicide bomber blew himself up at the house of Federal minister for Political Affairs, Mr. Amir Muqam, killing three people including a former provincial minister and injuring two others.

Ten people were killed and 11 others injured in armed clashes between Sunni and Shia groups. The clah started after a children's squabble. The police arrested 25 people. A curfew was also imposed to avert further clashes.
An activist of Imamia Jirga was shot dead by unknown persons at Jahangir Pura Road on Tuesday.
There were three explosions in Karachi. The second explosion was when a firecracker exploded near Saddar Dawakhana. Three people were injured- namely Imran, Nadeem Ahmed and Mohammad Riaz.

an explosion in Nawabshah occurred near the National Bank's main branch on the Sakrand road causing damage to a part of the building. No casualty was reported. Intelligence sources said that the explosions were caused by bombs whereas DPO Gayasuddin Rashdi sadi that the blasts were caused by crackers. The Sindh National Liberation Movement claimed responsibility for the blasts in a pamphlet found by intelligence personnel near the building.
A man was shot dead and another injured when armed men belonging to Brohi and Qambrani tribes opened fire on them. The motive behind the incident was said to be an ongoing tribal dispute.
A soldier suffered injuries when he stepped on a landmine and was rushed to the hospital in the Meshti Mela area.
Some unidentified motorcyclists put bombs outside CD and barber shops at midnight. Seven shops were destroyed and over 13 shops were partially damaged.
A former candidate for the slot of Bahadur Khan Union Council was sht dead at Syedan village.
A clash took palce between MQM and PPP workers. The MQM claimed that it was attacked by PPP activists. At least four people were injured.
In kotli Rau Abu Bahar, a man allegedly shot and killed his sister in law who had an affair with a young man in the village.
Indian firing continued alla day and Pakistani forces retaliated.

Bahawalnagar tehsil Tehrik-i-Jafaria Pakistan (TTP) President Syed Fayyaz Bukhari and his friend Wasim Ahmad was shot dead near the Stadium Road. Both the deceased were going on an auto-riskshaw when they came under fire from unidentified people.

A barage of artillery and missiles fired from Afghanistan hit residential compounds and a hotel in Mangrotai, killing 11 people and injuring 10. It is said that that NATO forces had launched an operation in Barmal, Afghanistan, against insurgents near the Pakistan border, and several artillery shells landed in the Mangrotai area, Shawal, which was covered with thick forests.  An official said that 18 artillery shells and six missiles landed in the Pakistani side and hit a hotel and seven houses in the border area. Followup: A Pakistan military official confirmed that at least 9 civilians had lost their lives in the recent incident where some rockets and missiles were accidently fired from across the border by the NATO led forces in Afghanistan. The NATO officials too confirmed the incident.
Security forces defused an improvised explsoive device planted on the roadside.
A man was killed in the Sharda sector in the upper Neelum valley when he was hit by a splinter of a mortar shell duriing unprovoked shelling by the Indian forces.
4 people were killed and two were injured when a bomb exploded in Killi Sad Muhammad on saturday
Three people were killed when unidentified gunmen sprayed a passenger bus with bullets and fled.
A young man Intizar was shot dead by three unknown assailants in Chak 1/1 AL on Sunday
Four armed persons murdered one Ms Sadori in the jurisdiction of Kandh Kot police station. No other detail was given.

A Nato trailer, that was on its way back from Kandhar after delivering supplies, was attack by armed motorcyclists. The three people on board were injured and one of them, who was the driver, later succumbed to his injuries.
Two missiles fired by a US drone on a suspected militant training compound killed four. It is not clear if there were any high-profile targets present at the time.

Protestors held a demonstration rally against publication of blasphemous caricatures in European newspapers, ransacked and set on fire a no. of buildings, including the Punjab Assembly, and hundreds of cars and motor cycles. The shooting which claimed two lives occured on Egerton Road where a bank security guard opened fire on approaching rioters. three youngsters suffered bullet injuries and two them succumbed to wounds. Police used tear-gas shells and resorted to baton-charge to diperse the crowd which left around 19 injured.
Militants attacked a security convoy, injuring 3 personnel. Security forces retaliated, killing 10 militants and injuring 3.

a policeman and another person, Mohammad Ramazan and Yaseen, were killed by unknown assailants. The incident occurred near Ghas Mandi. Yaseen was said to be an activist of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement, but the police said his political affiliation could not be confirmed. it is not known which one of the two was being targeted.
A woman and her two daughters were injured in the Chilyana village when they came under the fire of the Indian security forces from across the LoC.

Tubewell owners and farmers blocked the main road, chanted slogans against the government and burnt tyres to protest against MEPCO for sending them inflated electricity bills. The protesters dispersed peacefully after police and Mepco officials assured them that the matter would be taken up.

3 family members of a leader of the ANP were shot dead by suspected Taliban in their village, Malikpur, in Buner. It may be mentioned that the security forces had recently destroyed the house of a local Taliban leader Misbahuddin.

Ten people were killed and several others injured in an armed clash between two rival clans of the Tiri Mengal area of Parachinar. The Paiwar and Geedu clans of Kurram Agency clashed following a failure of a jirga held to negotiate a minor tribal dispute between the two. The clash intensified  when tribesmen of Geedu clan launched an offensive against their opponent tribe and the two sides used sophisticated arms and weapons against each other freely.

The 'accomplices' of PML-N MPA Ehsan Raza Khan thrashed Mirza Qadeer Ahmad for filing a writ petition to the Lahore High Court that challenged the 'fake' degree of the MPA. The victim was a former union council nazim who had won a seat against the MPA's brother twice in the past. However, MPA Ehsan Raza Khan claimed that Ashfaq, who was one of the assailants, had a family dispute with the victim and that the High Court litigation had nothing to do with incident.
The dead body of Ashraf was found.

Rana Kalimullah Khan, son of a former councillor- Rana Muhammad Ahsan- and his six gunmen were sleeping when an assailant fired at them, killing all of them. This was over an election rivalry between two relatives.
A Quetta-bound car coming from Noshki was attacked by armed gunmen on motorbikes. 3 people, all from the Sasoli community, were killed.

According to the report the Khadim of the Qadianis Masjid, a man was burning papers outside the mosque when he was spotted doing so by a youth. Hearing about the incident, villagers gathered and started raising slogans against the Qadianis. The Qadianis allegedly opened fire on the mob, injuring 10 people.

4 people were killed and another 3 injured when an explosived device went off in a garage. ; Follow-up: Nawabzada Gazen Marri, Home Minister of Balochistan, claimed that the blast was the result of a fuel tank exploding and not an act of terrorism. (\Quetta blast not a sabotage, says minister\", Dawn, 02-Apr-94, Page 12)"
A mortar shell hit a vehicle killing two civilians in Umrai area.

At least one dozen vehicles were damaged by activists of religious parties in different parts of the city, during a complete strike observed there. Police arrested 24 protestors on charges of damaging public property and trying to bring out a procession.
Muhammad Amir was stabbed to death by his rivals- Ghulam Mohammad Yar, Ahmed Yar and Muhammad Anwar- over a land dispute. Police have arrested all of the accused.
Two workrs of the Sipah-i-Sahaaba Pakistan were gunned down by unidentified motrcyclists while returning from Juma prayers.
Voting had to be stopped for 40 minutes when supporters of the PPP clashed with supporters of PDP. However, Rangers intervened and got the polling resumed.
A Frontier Corps personnel was killed in a landmine explosion in Dera Bugti area. The FC soldier, Nazim Shah, was killed when he stepped on the landmine on a road.

Following the assassination of Syed Raza Haider in Karachi, violent backlash was seen in various parts of Sindh. Aerial firing was used to force shopkeepers to close their shops in various areas of Nawabshah.
Jet fighters bombed militant hideouts in Upper Orakzai. 3 militant training camps were destroyed while at least 12 militants were killed and 6 injured.
Militants blew up a government-run health centre in Mamozai.
One person was killed and six others injured when MQM party office was attacked by unidentified gunmen.; Follow-up : One of the injured died of his wounds in the hospital.
Munir Ahmed, a resident of Aziz Town in Ferozekhel, was found dead with gunshot wounds.

A boy was killed by Indian firing during overnight skirmishes between Pakistani and Indian troops on the ceasefire line in disputed Kashmir. The boy, Shabir Yasin, was killed in the village of Danjer, around 3 km from the town of Athmuqam in the norhtern sector of the UN-monitored Line of Control. Tension had been running high between India and Pakistan following a rocket attack by Indian troops on a Pakistani civilian mosque that killed 20 people.

A clash took place between two groups of the Khambay village over a piece of land in the area. The Naseer group reportedly attacked the Jatt group to take possession of the land but they were over powered and one of them was taken to the police. The police then arrived at the spot and tried to arrest the rest of the group members but came under fire which resulted in the death of a police constable. Police later gunned down three members of the Naseer group.

Students of PSF staged a protest at Faisal Chowk against the Federal Ministers for their incapacity to solve common man's problem and also demanded the release of their detained colleagues. They also burnt old tyres and blocked the traffic.
The bullet-riddled body of a man in his early 30s was found lying in some bushes alond the main road. The body had 5 bullet wounds and bore torture marks.

Explosive material was hurled at a gas pipeline that supplied gas to Karachi. The blast caused minor damage. Larkana DPO Mazhar Nawaz Shaikh accused Abdul Fatah Janveri of the JSMM of being behind the blast and arrested him.

The police barred the SSP from holding a religious conference. The SSP activists protested and this lead to a clash between them and the police. 2 SSP activitsts were killed. ; Follow-up: A later report about the incident claims that three people were killed and several were injured. The SSP activists set multiple vehicles on fire. No arrests were made.

In the after math of a raid by Rangers on an Mohajir Qaumi Movement office in Korangi, enraged youths set three vehicles on fire in Nasir Colony and attacked an Edhi ambulance that arrived in the area to pick up an injured person from the area where the gunbattles had taken place.

Security forces and militants exchanged fire in the Kandoor areain Pir Koh gasfield area, after a group of militants opened fire on a camp of the Frontier Corps. FC troops returned fire, causing the attackers to escape. No casulty was reported in the firing.
One person was shot dead  by unknown assailants in Township area on Thursday

An altercation between Jamil Hashmi, former president of Tehsil Bar Association, Shujabad, and Amir Bakhsh, a local leader of PPP, led to the latter attacking the former leaving him in critical condition.

As part of the violence on the second day of a two-day strike called by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM), a man was found injured in a car in Liaquatabad, with his hands and feet tied. He later succumbed to his injuries at the hospital.

Kamran Rizvi, spokesman for the MQM (Haqiqi) and a cadidate for the N-182 and PS-79, alleged that 70 to 80 workers of the MQM 'Altaf Group' attacked his election office and beat up his workers, injuring five of them. He claimed they used clubs and kicks and also took away cash and valuables. He further alleged that Nazmabad SHO was among the attacking party. A sub-inspector of the Sharifabad police station stated that only one Haqiqi worker had been beaten up and that no one received any bullet injuries.

Three music centres were blown up in Swari bazaar. The improvised explosive devices exploded at intervals between 10.30pm and 11.00pm which created panic in the area. The targeted centres included Mian Yousaf Music Centre, Malik Cassette House and Ismail Music Centre. The blasts partially damaged dozens of nearby shops. Shopping centres had been receiving warnings to wind up thier 'un-Islamic' businesses and to refrain from entertaining female customers.

Residents of Sumundri blocked the road leading to the Sumundri Police Station and besieged the police station after the police had allegedly tortured an electrician. The police tried to disperse the mob 'forcebly' but to no avail. SHO Mehmood Haroon said that the police official involved in the raid had been suspended and that the PML-N leader would be arrested. The victim, Faisal Butt, was also a complainant in a case against PML-N leader Yameen. The police, along with the PML-N leader had raided Mr. Butt's house and tortured him publicly, before local residents rescued him and took him to the hospital.
Armed men attacked two trailers carrying Nato supplies to Afghanistan and torched one of them.
Security forces' operation in the Shakai-Kaniguram axis along the Sherwangei-Laddah road resulted in the killing of seven militants.
Two people were injured in the Datot village as the Indian firing continued from across the LoC.

A worker of Tablighi Jamaat was seriously injured when a home-made explosive device went off in the main mosque of Khanka Dogran known as 'Eik Minar Wali Masjid' half an hour before Jumma prayers. The local office of Sipah-e-Sahaba was also situated in the same mosque. The motive behind the attack was not mentioned in the report.

a boy was injured when one of 2 rockets exploded near a small house on Major Tufail Road in the Quetta Cantonment area. The other rocket exploded inside a security officials bungalow causing some damage. Security forces launched a search operation.
The Assistant Supritendent of District Jail Lahore, Ikramullah was gunned down by unidentified assailants in Jail Road on Wednesday.
Militants executed two people in North Waziristan for their alleged involvement in assassination on Al Qaeda cammander Abu Laith Al Libi
Two people were killed and two were wounded when their rivals opened fire over a land dispute in Jalalpur Pirwala on Monday

Peshawar University students launched, what they called, a 'new phase' of struggle for their rights by opening fire on campus and detonating explosive devices in the lawns of various departments. The students of three universities have recently formed a united front to pressurize the government into accepting their demands, which include subsidised electricity supply, reinstatement of rusticated students, release of detained students and change in the 'top administration' of the University of Peshawar.
An unidentified man was found death at the tomb of Jehangir.
Five people were injured in Nakyal sector as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.

a clash between ANP workers and levy force took place at the Tor Ghundi checkpost when the party's president Asfandyar Wali Khan leading a big procession was refused entry into the tribal agency. The levy force resorted to aerial firing and tear-gas shelling as the protesters moved across the barriers erected.
Wazeer Ali shot dead his wife Ms. Gohar Khatoon in Raees Mir Gadhi village, declaring her a Kari and escaped.

According to a military official, security forces repulsed a attack on a checkpost by militants in the Ghutai Sar area. He claimed ten militants were injured in the exchange of fire that continued for two hours.

Six members of a family were gunned down in Lanishan Village when a group of Dhanwar tribesmen attacked a house and opened fire on the inmates, killing six of them. According to police, there was an old feud between the two groups of the Dhanwar tribe.
Armed men of Patafi tribe attacked a village and opened indiscriminate fire, killing 3 people including a 5-year-old girl and injuring several others. The reason for the attack was a tribal feud.
Ten armed men barged intot he courtyard of the courtyard of Jalbani tribesmen in the Sono Jalbani village, killing two and injuring another when they opened indiscriminate fire with klashnikovs.
Two unknown men opened fire at a police station in Kotwali gate on Thursday.
Unidentified men kidnapped two labourers, tortured them and later sprayed them with bullets in Chochna Depot in Liaquatabad.

A coalition of ulema belonging to the Barelvi sect, under the leadership of the Sunni Ittehad Council, had planned to march from Bari Imam shrine in Islamabad to Data Darbar in Lahore to protest against the recent attacks on shrines across Pakistan. However, the police thwarted the march by placing containers on the G.T.Road. It was claimed that militants had plotted to attack the rally and it was being stopped for security reasons. The SIC activists tried to move the barricades and the police retaliated by using tear gas and batons. The protesters responded by damaging public and private property and pelting the police with stones. Sunni Tehrik chief Sarwat Ijaz Qadri claimed that the Punjab government had arrested 8000 workers.

After TMA officials got some shops vacated following the completion of contracts, angry traders of Lorry Adda market went on a strike, burnt tyres, blocked the road and later marched up to the TMA offices where they staged a sit-in. The shopkeepers claimed that they wanted to renew the contracts but the TMA officials threw them out, whereas the TMA claims that the shopkeepers were evicted because they were neither depositing their outstanding dues nor filing applications for renewal of contracts.
two militants were injured when security forces opened fire on a truck loaded with weapons near Banda checkpost,  when the driver did not stop for checking.

4 persons allegedly shot dead one Mohammad Siddique and seriously injured his wife Zulaikhan, near Masood Akhtar railway station's quarters. It is reported that some gypsies had setup tents near the railway station.
A girl was shot dead by her two brothers on suspicion of a loose character.
A woman was killed in Indian shelling on the neelum valley on satuday
Two clans of the Chachar tribe clashed with automatic weapons on a dispute piece of land.Two people were killed.
Two army officers were wounded when their vehicle was struck by a remote controlled bomb near Esha checkpost in Miramshah.
Eight Indian soldiers were killed and Six Pakistani soldiers were injured whne the armies clashed due to the erection of a permanent fence by the Indian Army.
In the on-going wave of violence in the city, target killings and body dumpings continued. A body with a bullet wound to the head was found in a gunny bag nea Ibrahim Ali Bhai school in Orangi.

The care-taker of the Lawari Sharif Shrine, Badin was shot and killed in his home in Defence Housing Authority. The police stated that a tussle between the groups of Mohammad Sadiq Qureshi and Pir Hasan Qadir had been going on for years for the control of the Shrine, which had taken many lives since the 1980s.
A Nazim of the Union Council No 266 was shot at and injured seriously by a youth on the Faisalabad-Jhang road.

An exchange of fire took place across the Pak-Afghan border between Nato and Afghan forces on one side and Pakistani forces on the other. The exchange took place after at least 5 mortar shells were fired into Pakistani territory, prompting Pakistani security forces to respond with light artillery. No casualties were reported.

3 masked men fired at a local People's Party Parliamentarians leader, Najamuddain Abro. He was the brother of Naib Nazim Taluka. Najamuddain Abro's nephew, Imran, was seriously injured. The assailants escaped after committing the crime.

a bomb planted in Noor Restaurant in Rakhni bazaar went off when the restaurant was closed for Friday prayers. The restaurant and two nearby shops were destroyed. Windowpanes of other shops and buildings were also smashed. No casualty was reported in the incident.
former Chairman of Bolan District council Sardar Sher Mohammad Khan Rind said that the Baloch nation would strongly react if drone attacks are conducted by the US in Balochistan.
Teekam Das slaughtered his three daughters and then slit his thoat as a mark of sacrifice to Kali Mata.

The recent wave of political killings continued as gunbattles raged in Landhi and surrounding areas. Two activists of the MQM-H, who had recently joined MQM, were gunned down near Hussaini Chowrangi when armed men opened fire. Two minor boys sustained injuries in the gunbattle that took place in the area.
Two men were killed while seven others were injured in a clash between the members of the Khaskheli and Khoso tribes in Ali Nawaz Shah village.
The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as a passenger coach was set on fire within the remit of the Mominabad police station.
A youth was wounded in Saeedabad.

Former Nagrianwala union council nazim, Chaudhry Zulfiqar Warraich, and his accomplices thrached some children who were taking out a procession for Eid Miladun Nabi. The children were chanting religious slogans that annoyed the Ex-Nazim who belonged to another sect. The assailants later entered houses of members of the other sect and tore down flags and banners displayed to celebrate the occasion. A case was registered against the assailants by Kunjah police.
militants fired 6 rockets at a police station and an airport. Five rockets landed in a field and 1 damaged a seminary in Kotka Khan Zaman injuring a youth.
Two activists of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement were killed, two were arrested and four escaped after a shootout with the police in Korangi.
A convoy was hit by a landmine in the Ghiljo area of Orakzai and three security personnel were injured.
the police recovered the body of an unidentified youth from a minor canal near Chak 710-GB.
Body of a 36 year old man was found from Korangi Sector F-6. Torture marks were found all over his body.
Two men were injured in a clash between the two groups of Arain and Chang in Pakka Chang.

Ad hoc doctors whose services were terminated by the government joined the students of King Edward Medical College. The doctors were demanding reinstatment while the students were protesting againsted biased examination marking. They burnt tyres and blocked trafic.
Two Wapda employees were found dead in their rented house in Karimpura, Lalamusa. The motive behind the killing could not be ascertained.
Rockets were fired at FC Fort in Kohlu. BLA has claimed the responsibility of the attacks.
A man was killed and another injured when an explosion occurred in a scrap yard while the men were unloading scrap from a truck. The police sealed off the warehouse and arrested its owner.
Two missiles fired by a US drone killed 5 people, including 3 Arabs and injured 2 when they hit a house.
A clash between gun totting groups occurred in Baloch Colony flyover and many people suffered injuries and deaths.
A man, Mohammad Bugti, was gunned down on Sariab Road by unidentified assaialants.
a group of protesters turned violent during their protest against the disqualification of the Sharif brothers and damaged the offices of 2 banks.
Police ASI Sher Zaman was injured and his mother-in-law was killed when armed men opened fire at the former's house.
A shopkeepers was injured when he was hit by a stray bullet. Sporadic firing had taken place after a strike call given by the MQM coordination committee.

According to the police, Mirza Irshad Beg, who was the MQM unit chief of New Karachi, was riding in a black car along with his companions when he was ordered to stop by the police. Mirza Irshad Beg reportedly opened fire on the police and fled. The police then chased them, and in the subsquent exchange of fire, Beg was killed while his accomplices managed to escape. The relatives of the deceased, however, claimed that Beg was in illegal police custody, and was killed in a fake encounter.
FC troops destroyed several hideouts of militants during an operation.
Neelam, a 22 year old woman who had recently been married, was shot dead by her uncle, Zulfikar, for allegeldy having an affair with her neighbour.
Unidentified assailants on motorcycles shot dead a former activist of the banned outfit, Sipah-i-Sahaba near his house in Rehan Colony. The police did not rule out a terrorist attack.
a leader of the Sipah-i-Sahaba and his driver were shot dead infront of his house in Model Colony by three attackers.

Workers of MSF and the police clashed against each other following the Punjab  (PML-N) Youth Wing general-secretary Khwaja Saad Raffique's  challenge to the police of arresting him. He said he would hold a demo in front of Lohari Gate, and that he'd see if the police dared to arrest him. The challenge was made in view of the recent arrests made by the police of the youth wing workers, including Saad Raffique's younger brother, Khwaja Salman Raffique. The MSF workers pelted stones at the police and fired shots in the air, prompting the police to teargassing and also firing shots in the air. However, no one was killed or injured in the clashes. In another report in the same newspaper, it was mentioned that the demostrations were held in response to police raids on the houses of MSF leaders at Crowd Adda, Shah Alam Market and Muslim Mosque. MSF workers alleged that one of their activists was injured in the police firing. They also staged a sit in and blocked traffic on Circular Road. Followup: A followup report claimed that three people received burn injuries during the protests at Lohari Gate when a political worker set fire to some discarded cardboard boxes next to a chemical factory. The fire caught on other inflammable material, and three factory workers were injured. One of them later succumbed to his injuries.
Four workers of PSF were kidnapped and tortured by unidentified assailants. They were later released.
A dead body of a 50 year old man was found in a snooker club in Altaf town in the Korangi area. The man was said to be a member of an elder's committee of the MQM.

A soldier and a militant were killed in an exchange of fire between security forces and militants. It was said that security forces acting on information that militants were hiding in the area were raiding houses when they came under attack. The forces retaliated and an exchange of fire ensued. However, other reports said that the exchange of fire started when a military convoy was ambushed by militants.
2 students were injured during a clash between two student groups in Jinnah College Nazimabad on Wednesday.
A hand grenade was lobbed at a police post in the Tajazai area on Monday night.
3 people were shot at and injured by unidentified men in Mumtazabad on Friday.

Police resorted to firing and teargassing as angry protesters took to the streets, torched a truck, pelted stones at vehicles and ransacked banks to mour the killing of Murtaza Bhutto. Eight PPP (SB) activists were allegedly injured in the firing, along with two constables when the police opened fire on a procession at Lahore Regulator coming from Mirokhan Chowk to Al-Murtaza.
A bomb exploded on the railway line casuing 1.5 ft portion of the track to be blown up. Sources said that a local made device had been used to blow up the railway tracks.

A candidate for Nazim, Ramzan Mastana, along with dozens of supporters stormed into a polling station and picked up 5 ballot boxes. They allegedly beat up men and women voters of their opponent group and attempted to put the boxes on fire. Officials of various agencies arrested the candidate and six others.
A bomb exploded in a hotel room. No casualties were reported. The room was rented by an Afghan national who is absconding.
Two groups of students from the computer science department had an armed clash but fled when the police showed up. No further details given.
A shepherd was injured when a US-made device exploded when he touched it. Around four dozen unexploded devices were further recovered from the mountain area.
A husband and wife were killed at their Datta Nagri residence.
2 proclaimed offenders, Mohammad Jaffar and Ahmed Shah -residents of Bagatu, Hangu District- were found dead in the mountains by locals, who informed the police.
Yasin, a milkman by profession, was shot and killed by armed men while he was on his way home on his bicycle.
A school girl was killed when a suicide bomber blew himself up near a security vehicle not far from a military police checkpost. 23 people including 15 security personnel were also injured.
Six persons shot dead Mohammad Aslam over a land dispute and escaped. No other detail was given.
the Sarband police found the decomposed bullet-riddled body of a man, Abdullah Jan, in a local graveyard.
Two hand grenades were hurled at the courtyard of a mosque during Asr prayers. 25 people were hurt in the attack but no one was severely injured.

Unidentified militants blew up a government-run high school for girls at Sulemankhel village in Badbher area. A rocket was also fired at the building. Bazidkhel union council nazim Fahimur Rehman blamed a bara-based religious group for the blast.

PPP workers attacked the Taimuria police station to set their companion, Suhalin Zaman, free. Police had registered FIR against Suhalin but the party workers ransacked the police station, tore the FIR, took away the locker keys and set Suhalin free.
Haji Muhammad Sadique, owner of a hardware shop in Jinnah Market, was stabbed to death in his house by 3 assailants. The police could not ascertain the motive for the murder.
A man was killed and at least four others were injured in the Khuraitta sector as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.

Hundreds of unemployed post-graduates, graduates and matriculates thronged the police lines for jobs of drivers, constable or wireless operators. Several of them fell unconscious due to the heat and baton-charge by the police to disperse the crowd..
A bullet riddled body of a man was found in an abandoned taxi.
A man belonging to the Mahar tribe was killed in the Dingro Mahar village as part of the on-going dispute between the Mahar and Jatoi tribes.

Some anti-encroachment staff members of the Metropolitan Corporation Lahore were injured when encroachers resisted the former's attempt to remove encroachments. However, the MCL team was successful in removing the encroachments.
An army officer, who was on leave in his village was killed by unidentified men.
A woman was injured in the Indian firing on Bhedi sector in Bagh district.

Six persons were injured as two rival groups clashed over a property dispute in Kamoki when one of the groups was restrained from constructing on the piece of land and both opened indiscrminate fire on the other.
a woman Mst. Dhayani was killed by her son as he suspected her of having illicit relations.
A man was wounded in a shooting incident in Site industrial area.
Several people were hurt during a clash between PPP and PML workers during filing of papers of PPP candidate Abbas Ali Ansari. Both the groups raised slogans against eachother which led to clash.
A woman, Phairo Mai, was axed to death by her husband. Her husband suspected her of having illicit relations with another man from the village.
A bullet riddled body of a young man was found in a bag.

Bloodshed made its way back into Karachi when MQM Haqiqi attempted to stage a comeback in the strongholds of the MQM in Malir and Landhi. The killing spree moved to the areas of Landhi where two men, belonging to the MQM, were killed in an attack on a bus near Hussaini Chowrangi.

Labour Party Pakistan workers were baton charged when they were marching towards the Governor's house to hand over a 'dissenting note' against the government for following the policies dictated by the World Bank and IMF. Many protesters were injured.
a man, Raja, was shot dead by armed men on the way to his village.
A man shot dead his wifer and her alleged paramour along with another villager (who came under fire) on suspicion of illicit relations.

Some unknown assailants opened fire on Muhammad Shafi Bhutta, the President of AH, Khairpur Tameywali when he was going to offer Fajr prayers. The police arrested 12 activists of SSP and AH to prevent any untoward incident from occuring.

People's Democratic Allinace's Federal Minister Haji Zafar Leghari and MPA Manzoor Wassan alleged that there motorcade was attacked by unidentified assailants in which three people were injured and 15 vehicles were damaged.
Militants attacked a security post with heavy weapons which led to an exchange of fire in which 2 soldiers were killed and another 6 were injured.
An Afghan national was shot dead and another injured when some masked men raided the Afghan Refugee camp of Maula Dad. The motive behind the raid could not be ascertained.

A man was killed and a bus was set on fire during a strike called by the Sunni Ittehad Council in protest over the conviction of the self-confessed killer of Salman Taseer. There were reports of firing and arson incidents from the FB area and an activist of the ST was killed in firing as well. A minibus was set on fire in the Korangi area.
In Darai and Danda areas, troops killed two terrorists and captured seven in the ongoing military operation against militants.

A hand-grenade blast neat the Rainbow Centre in Saddar left an Intelligence Bureau inspecter dead and nineteen others injured. The blast was said to have occurred next to a milk shop; Follow up: Investigators probing into the incident claimed that it was carried out on eithnic lines. It was ruled out that the Rainbow Centre itself was the target or that it was an assassination attempt on the IB official.
Militants blew up the government girls high school Ali Grama
On the fourth day of the on-going violence in Karachi, arsonists set fire to a truck in New Karachi.

A woman, Ms Zeenat Khatoon Lashari, was killed by a close relative in a village on the outskirts of Ratodero. According to the police she was shot by the relative when she delayed in preparing food for him. However the news report claims that other sources suggest that she was killed on the pretext of Karo-Kari.
2 groups clashed over the occupation of a 'Panchayat Ghar', leaving 1 person dead and 3 others injured.
A dead body of a youth was found bearing torture marks.
A man was wounded in Saeedabad.

An explosion in the reading room of the Dyal Singh College Library led to a blaze which gutted  almost the entire ground floor of the library, injuring 23 people and consuming thousands of books.Police said the blast seemed to be the work of terrorists. Muslim Students Federation (MSF) said it was either terrorism or an act by the People's Student Federation (PSF) to gain control over the college. PSF denied the charge. Followup: It was claimed in a meeting that a group headed by PML(N) Youth Wing secretary-general Khwaja Saad Raffique was responsible from the bomb blast.
A three year old boy was found dead, wrapped in a shopping bag, in Green Town. The police say the exact cause of death would be ascertained after he autopsy.
A tea stall owner was shot dead for refusing to close down his tea stall.

Abdul Jabbar Yousafzai, Deputy Director, Water Resources Management was on his way to the Airport Road when unidentified men opened fire on his jeep. He died on his way to the hospital. The motive behind the murder could not be ascertained.

Following the arrest of 7 young men, acccused of attacking a boy and later attacking the police party that was taking the victim to the hospital for medico-legal examination, more than a 100 supporters of the arrested men gathered outside the police station and pelted it with stones. They also damaged vehicles parked outside. The supporters also blocked Benazir Bhutto Road, uprooted the traffic police pedestal, damaged traffic lights, burnt tyres and staged a sit-in. The protest had not ended when this report was filed.
Two brothers shot their three sisters over a property dispute.

at least 8 people were killed and 10 others injured in clashes between two groups, the people of Balishkhel and Sadda in Kurram Agency. Assistant Political Agent Ayaz Mandukhel said that the groups were attacking residential areas with mortars and rockets.
Militants attacked the Jagani security check post in Sangsilla, Dera Bugti. However, the security presonnel killed two militants and injured 4 others in the ensuing shootout.
Five people were killed and several others injured in indiscriminate firing by unidentified gunmen.
clashes and incidents of firing related to the local government elections were also reported from Matiari, Tando Muhammad Khan, Dadu and Jamshoro districts.
Two people were killed in Pathar village in Kotli as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.
a lawyer, Mirza Qaiser Sohail, was found stabbed to death in his house where he lived alone in Mehmoodabad. The police have found no leads.

Security personnel's vehicle hit a landmine as they were trying to clean up the area of land mines planted by militants. Three security personnel were killed and three others were injured in the incident.

Allama Talab Hussain, Chairman of Ilmi Council of Seerat un-Nabi and chairman of supreme Council of Islami Darul Umoon was shot dead by two unidentified motorcyclists in Judicial Colony, Sattokala while he was on the way to the Bank. Police attributed the killing to be a part of the on-going sectarian violence and that the scholar had been receiving death threats in the past.
A spokesman for the Taliban, who claimed responsibility for a school bombing earlier in the day also claimed that two houses of Khasadar personnel were also destroyed.

One person was shot dead and a woman was injured by their rivals. Ashraf of Roshanpura had a land dispute with Salim of the same locality. They were holding talks to resolve the issue when Salim opened fire on Ashraf, killing him and injuring his wife.

Shahid, an MQM activist was gunned down allegedly by members of rival faction MQM-H. Shoaib Bokhari claimed that it was an attempt to prevent MQM supporters from attending the funeral of fellow party workers that had been killed the day before. Follow-up from Section 2: The real name of the victim was Rizwan Ali while 'Shahid' was his alias. He was killed when his house was attacked allegedly by MQM-H workers.

Ali Hassan Mugheri, a businessman, was shot dead by armed motorcyclists while he was on his way back from mosque. Sipah-e-Sahaba leaders condemned the incident and demanded immediate arrest of the killers.
a Haqiqi worker was gunned down near his house near Chandni Chowk in Paposhnagar by unidentifed motorcyclists

Dacoits armed with automatic weapons attacked the OGDC Qadirpur gas field and opened indiscriminate fire damaging the machinery installed by Coporate Marethan Company. The motive behind the firing and damaging machinery could not be known immediately.
Helicopter gunships destroyed a training camp of suicide bombers in Charbagh. Six militants were killed and several others wounded in the attack.
An armed clash between two local groups - Humayun Butt group and Bobi Gujjar group - left a bystander, 10-year-old Shahab-ud-Din, dead.
A young person was found dead in Kahna on Sunday. He had torture marks on his body

The Youth Force of the Jamiat Ahle Hadith (JAH) organized a rally to protest against the government's failure to arrest the killers of Maulana Ehsan Elahi Zaheer and other JAH leaders. The police had erected barricades to prevent the protesters from reaching Governor's House and when the demonstrators tried to remove them, the police pushed them back. The protesters responded by resorting to stoning and tyre burning after which the police used teargas shells and batons to disperse them. 12 protesters were injured while 6 were arrested by the police.
An unidentified young man was kidnapped, tortured and killed in Khokhrapur, Malir. A note was found on the victim's body which said 'Fate of an informer'.

A watchman of Madrassah Darul Uloom Minhajushariah, Muhammad Wakeel, was shot once in the chest as he was running his errands. He died and the assailant fled the scene. A senior police official did not believe that the killings could be sectarian, however, he did not rule out terrorism.
At least 37 people were injured when a bomb exploded at a public meeting of Jamhoori Watan Party at Dera Allahyar on the second death anniversary of Nawab Akbar Bugti.
Qari Muhammad belonging to the Jamat Ahle Sunnat Pakistan and a member of the Darul Uloom was shot dead on his motorcycle by unidentified persons.
Two unidentified bodies of young men were found. One of the bodies had 25 bullet wounds.
A checkpoint in the Dangeen area and another in the Razmak area came under rocket attacks in which two paramilitary soldiers were wounded.
As two MQM(Haqiqi) activists were killed, people staged a protest against that incidence and torched two buses and a car

The chief of a peace committee of Mohman Agency was killed while another elder, belonging to the Khyber Agency was critically injured in an attack outside a mosque in Peshawar when militants attacked both the tribal elders with  sophisticated weapons. Both elders were reportedly anti-Taliban workers.

Over 150 villagers, including traders, blocked the Daska-Glotiyan-Gujranwala road to protest against dacoity in their area by burning tyres and chanting slogans against the police. The police arrived at the spot and reassured them that the culprits would be arrested.
A clash took place between militants and security forces after the former attacked a checkpoint. 3 militants were killed when security forces retaliated.
Three people were killed and seven were injured when a pickup going from Biliameen to Sadda hit a landmine near Arawali village.
in an enmity that stemmed from the elopement of a woman, three of a family were murdered and one injured. A fourth member of the family is missing, it is believed that he might have been killed.
Prayer leader, Hafiz Mohammad Jamil, was shot dead in his house in Farid Kot village, Deepalpur by unidentified persons.
3 people were killed and several others were injured in a clash between two tribes near Gulistan on Sunday.

A Dali (caravan) of worshippers was proceeding to Urs of Bari Imam when people inside a mosque got infuriated over the beating of drums at prayer time and consequently attacked the procession. The clash that followed left 6 people injured.
