three people fired on the security officials near the checkpost in spinwam area. Troops returned fired, killing two on the spot while the third suspect escape. Residents of the area said the tribesmen were unarmed and not involved in the miitancy. Troops arrested five people at the checkpost and found 14 hand-grenades in their possession.

Kabir Wasti, a senior politician, was beaten up by a group of people and received multiple injuries. Mr Wasti was on his way to Rawalpindi from Islamabad when a Prado, bearing a government registration plate, hit his vehicle. Following the collision some men got of from the Prado, pulled Mr Wasti out of his car and thrashed him before escaping.
11 people were injured when two rival groups attacked eachother woth bricks and clubs during an election campaign.
There were reports of violence across malir following the arrest of MQM (Afaq) 's leader. The protesters burnt atleast three vehicles and blocked the main road.

Nasirul Raza, brother-in-law of MQM MPA Afzal Anwar was shot and killed in Nazimabad after he had been kidnapped on Thursday. The MQM alleged that MQM-H activists had kidnapped him and tortured him before killing him.
unidentified saboteurs attempted to blow up two pylons near Abdullah Dakhan and Gul Mohammad Khoso village. Sindh Liberation Movement claimed responsibility for the attack.
Vendors and encroachers attacked a team of Municiapal Corporation Multan (MCM) were beaten up by vendors when they tried to remove their stalls.The police played the role of a silent spectator.
Kashif and Naveed, Tableeghi Jamat members were gunned down by unidentified men.

Following the death of an MQM-H worker, armed protesters took to the streets and resorted to violence. Masked men opened fire at a Pakistan Steel bus, injuring Essa Khan who was an employee of Pakistan Steel.

Two brother, Saleem Khan and Anar Khan, were targeted at their workplace - a clay oven - by unidentified motorcyclists who fired shots at the brothers and fled. Saleem Khan died on the spot while his brother was injured.

Militants blew up a house of a pro-government tribal elder in the Zafar town area of Miramshah. Malik Khan Asghar Khan was accused by militants of supporting government policies. Relatives of the tribal elder said he had reveived the threats from the militants, warning him not to support the political administration. Malik Asghar and his family had already shifted to Peshawar.
According to MQM, Haqiqi men kidnapped two of their party activists and tortured them in Khokhrapur.

JUI-F attacked a Ahl-i-Hadith mosque that was under construction and took away the doors, windows and zinc sheets. They did this as the Ahl-i-Hadith party published a controvertial pamphlet that outraged te JUI-F. The JUI-F also blocked the Karakoram highway and burnt old tires on the Batagram bridge. According to eyewitnesses, the police reached the location in half an hour but merely watched the JUI-F destroy the building.
A blast occurred when a truck loaded with coal blasted when a landmine went off in Ramsayzai area on Wednesday in which a truck driver was injured seriously

A policeman was killed while his companions managed to escaped after occupants of a car opened fire on them. A police spokesman accused the MQM of the killing, saying that its leaders had warned the district central police that party workers would opened fire at policemen if they tried to stop them from collecting hides and skins of sacrificial animals.
A public call office in Angor Adda was blown up.
a man alias Wit along with Sardar and Abdul Sattar killed Mohammad Ali and injured Mohammad Irshad  and Akram.

In the midst of a strike called by the MQM to protest against the 'extra judicial killing' of its workers in police custody, protesters went on a rampage while trying to stop traffic and set fire to a car in New Karachi.
Some people pelted stones on the buses in Gari Khata on Sunday in a clash between two student groups.

Two members of a family, Shahbaz and Salma Bibi- were shot at and injured when they entered their house. It was stated that they had not supported the accused in the local body elections (held on 21-3-01) and the accused hurled threats concerning this over the last few days.
10 militants were killed when they attacked a secuirty forces convoy in Warza.

Agitation began when protesters blocked ferozpur road and burnt tyres, pelted stones at vehicles etc. Police had to use baton charge and aerial firing to disperse the crowd. The people were protesting against WASA for not providing water.
A US drone targeted a militant compound, killing at least 6 militants.
Four persons were injured due to Indian shelling in different sectors of Azad Kashmir on Tuesday
Two men were shot at by unidentified gunmen. The reason behind the shooting is not known.
Anlar Abro was shot dead by her father for establishing illicit relations.

A father and his son, both TJP supporters were gunned down, allegedly by SSP men, while they were exiting their printing press. Both Mohammad Ashraf Naqvi and Jaffer Hussain Naqvi died on the spot. Both victims had been implicated in a case for burning copies of the Holy Quran but later investigation showed that the case was 'cooked up' by the SSP.
The bomb disposal squad defused two powerful bombs planted on railway tracks.
Three villagers were hurt when Indian Troops fired across the LoC
As a continuation of the unrest caused by the murder of a local builder earlier in the day, there was indiscriminate firing which injured one person, Haseeb and killed another, Atif.
3 people including a Constable were killed in a violent protest when the police raided a house to to recover an abducted woman in Shah Wali Village on Wednesday.
Security forces backed by gunship helicopters attacked the militants in Siddiqabad area of Bajaur. 11 militants were killed while another 15 were injured.

The body of an alleged US spy was found in the Shakai area. The victim, Bashir Ahmad, belonged to Kunar, and his family resided in Kotki village in Chaharmand area. Bashir had been kidnapped by unidentified men on charges of spying for the US forces, and was later killed.
Anjum Akbar, who was a practicing lawyer at the sessions court and a mother of 2, was shot and killed by unidentified assailants while she was travelling in her car.
Heavy exchange of gunfire ensued between two rival religious factions because of disputes over religious matters

2 people were killed and 3 were injured when a Zamindar arrived at adisputed land along with Revenue Officer to get his land demarcated when the rival party of Lashari tribe opened fire on them at Dadko Mori on Wednesday.
A bullet-riddled body was found from KMC park in sector 1-C of Orangi Town. He bore two bullet wounds that proved fatal and was also believed to be mentally handicapped.

Six members of a family including two children were killed and three other injured allegedly by their relatives. The dispute was trigered by alleged illicit relations Azam with Khan daughter, Aasia. Khan along with his accomplices barged into Azam house and killed six of his family members.
Ali Murad Muhammad gunned down his sister-in-law, Mst. Irshad, and injured her alleged paramour, Mehboob.
Kakrar, was hsot dead by two men who invited him to a dinner at their house. Th reason behind the murder is not known.
Four people of a family were found slaughtered in their house. The reason behind the gruesome act is not known.
Syed Zafirul Hassan, an accountant of Quaid-i-Azam Academy, was shot and killed in the jurisdiction of the Sharea Faisal police station.
Militants attacked a checkpost in Bara and the security forces attacked militant positions in Ghandao Locality using artillery weapons and managed to killed eight militants.
A man, Mohammad Shoqeen, died in a village after a 'dud' shell he brought home went off.

Police constablies Muhammad Ishaq and Musa were killed when armed men intercepted their motorbike and opened fire. 3 other people, including an sub-inspector of the CID, were injured. The Lashkar-i-Jhangvi claimed responsibility for the attack. The policemen killed belonged to the Shia sect.
A man and a woman were shot dead on the pretext of karo-kari. Police were conducting raids to arrest the killers.
A clash occurred between the Muttahida and Sunni Tehrik. Hamidullah suffered injuries as he was beaten up with clubs.
An alleged MQM activist, wanted in robbery cases, was killed in an encounter with the police in the SITE area.
An unidentified body with the hands and feet tied was found from the Khaji Ground in the Gulbahar Police precints.

Muttahida Qaumi Movement and Jeay Sindh Qaumi Mahaz gave a strike call for 13 June 01 throughout the province in protest against police action and against water shortage in Sindh. Several vehicles were set on fire throughout the city. A vehicle was set on fire near the SSP South office in the Arillery Maidan police limits.

Clashes started in Islamabad between the police and lawyers and political activists when the police baton-charged lawyers who wanted to go inside the Election Commission building. Lawyers and political activists were unhappy at the allowance given to President Pervaiz Musharraf to contest in the elections again. The Supreme Court bench had dismissed challenges to Gen Musharraf’s dual position as president and army chief, giving him a big legal boost against his political opponents. Scores of lawyers, journalists and political activists were injured as the police baton charged them and fired tear gas shells when they tried entering the Election Comission building. The police was seen thrashing people, after which the people too began to fight back. Over 20 journalists were wounded in the clash. The number of injured lawyers and political activists remained unknown.
5 armed men broke in to a house and opened fire on and killing a woman and her sister in law on the pretext of karo-kari.
In the on-going wave of violence in the city, target killings and body dumpings continued. The body of a young man was found under the bridge of Teen Hatti within the remit of Jamshed Quarters.
A woman was hit and wounded by a stray bullet in Risala.
A young man was shot and killed outside a clinic in Shah Faisal Colony by two armed men on a motorcycle. The police termed it a target killing.
An unidentified man was found killed in fields by unknown assailants in the sattokatla area on Sunday. Sources said that there were marks of torture on his body.

Fayyaz Hussain Rizvi was on his way to work when he was intercepted by two men on a motorbike who shot and killed him. Police suggested that the motive was sectarian and the Jafria Alliance Pakistan \criticized the government over its failure to stop sectarian killings\"."
A person was injured in the Indian shelling on the Mandhol village in Hajira sector.

The bodies of an MQM(Altaf) activist, Anwar Iqbal, and his son were found near the Malir River bed, blindfolded and their hands tied behind their back. It was reported that they had received at least 15 bullets each and the police claimed that it seemed that they had been executed by a firing squad.
Nawab of Kalabagh's son Nawabzada Malik Muzaffar Khan was gunned down along with his two bodyguards in Daud Khel on Monday.

As a result of the verdict of supreme court annulling the appointment of Justice (Retd) Deedar Shah as NAB chairman, strike was observed in  Thatta, Sajawal, Mirpur Bathoro, Gharo, Dharo and other towns and PPP activists burnt old tyres and blocked traffic on friday.
Two police constables were injured in an exchange of fire between law enforcement agencies personnel and miscreants in Unit No. 12, Latifabad.
Armed persons shot and killed Tajoo, alias Gulzar, and a woman in an agricultural field on the pretext of karo-kari
Gulsher shot dead Asif on the suspicion that he had an affair with his sister. He saw Asif wandering near his house, at which he got infuriated and shot him dead with the help of accomplices.
3 people including 2 minor girls were stabbed to death while asleep in their home near bus stand Phalia by unidentified assassins; Mohammad Arif killed his wife and 2 daughters.

Security agencies found a bag full of explosives outside the Army Officers Mess in Rawalpindi. It was found on the same day when two suicide blasts occurred in Rawalpindi which targetted security personnel.
3 people were gunned down by unidentified men in Jinnah Town on Friday.

The police scuffled with jounalists and human rights activists as the police did not allow them to enter the airport despite previous promises by the Lahore police chief DIG Tariq Saleem and Operations police chief Aftab Cheema that they would not be barred from entering the airport. The police allegedly injured a journalist from an English-language daily and a plain clothes man slapped a woman reporter from an Urdu daily.
An ASI-Riasat Ali- was shot dead by unknown assailants in People's Colony on Thursday.
A person killed his sister over karo-kari in Nawabshah Town on Saturday
A 50 year old man was on his way home when unidentified men opened fire on him.
A leader of the PPP (Shaheed Bhutto Group), Ali Mohammad Sonara and an associate were shot dead by unidentified motercyclists.
A vehicle of the Khwaizai peace committee hit a landmine causing damage to the vehicle. However, no casualties were reported.

Armed tribesmen of Wazir Dand area of Khyber Agency blocked the main road of Jamrud for an hour to protest against the joint operation of the Khasadar force of the political administration and Khyber Rifles in their area. They exchanged fire with personnel of the Kyber Riffle when they tried to clear the road for traffic. No one was injured.
Imam Bux Palal and Abdul Sattar Palal were killed in a clash between two groups over a land dispute.
The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as a policeman was killed in the Sharafi Goth area of Landhi.
the body of an unidentified man was recovered from the property of the Water and Sanitation Department.
Militants attempted to blow up the Chamatalai Bridge in Khawazakhela. The bridge was partially damaged.
A former union council nazim was shot dead while his two associates suffered injuries when his rivals of Cheema group sprayed their vehicle with bullets over a property dispute.
Angry protesters ransacked the PTCL office and cut 400 phone lines. They were protesting against flour shortage as well as continued loadshedding.
Gunmen shot and killed three men in a late night attack in Baldia Town. According to reports, the men were between the ages of 25 and 30.
Zulfiqar-ul-Hasan, a worker of the MQM's Unit 112, was standing near his friend's house when two men on a motorbike pulled up and fired shot at him.
A rocket fired by militants his the wall of old Commissioners house located near Kohat police's deputy inspector general's office.

Armed clashes between two rival ethnic groups left at least 16 people dead and over 78 injured. The groups fought pitched battles and used firearms and sharp edged weapons. Shops, vehicles and public property were also damaged. A police party that tried to intervene came under heavy fire, leaving 3 policemen dead. Another policeman, who was passing through the area was also shot and killed.

A UC-7 Naib Nazim,Mohammad Fahim, of Korangi town and his associates were fired upon by unidentified men who fled in a taxi. The Naib Nazim and one associate died on the spot while the third was injured.
A man, approximately 40 years old, was found dead on the Circular Road, in the Yakki Gate police limits.
A Hindu Temple at Thatta was reduced to ashes as some unidentified miscreants set it ablaze.
A vehicle belonging to a bread company was set on fire

During a session of Thatta District Council two groups had a heated exchange of words on the issue of collection of octroi taxes following which one group took out arms and resorted to firing in the hall. As a result Syed Abdul Sattar Shah Shirazi and Syed Sikandar Ali Shah were killed while 2 others were injured.
Two people, Khan Muhammad and Sharif, of opposite groups were seriously injured in a clash over a land dispute.

A complete strike was held on the call of an all-parties conference. A peaceful procession was taken out and at the culmination, several political and religious party leaders addressed the participants in which they said that if America tried to impose a war on Afghanistan, the people of Pakistan would stand by their Afghan brothers and wage jihad.

Protesters from the Mohamnd tribe marched towards the WAPDA office to protest against the removal of electricity connection.The protest turned violent and there was an exchange of fire between the tribesmen and paramilitary forces for three hours.;Follow-up:Another person died of his injuries in the hospital.the situation remains tense in the area.

a tribal elder, Malak Hoshyar Khan, and 2 militants were killed and 4 others were injured in a clash between the Taliban and a tribal lashkar when 200 armed militants attacked the village of Tali in Salarzai area. They fired rockets and missiles at the houses of tribal elders and checkpost of volunteers of the Salarzai tribe. Secuirty forces also shelled militant position in support of Lashkar forces.
24 people were killed and 40 others injured when a bomb exploded on a passenger train. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Three dead bodies were found in different areas of Swat. Details are not available.

SSP activists burnt tyres and pelted stones at passing traffic during a rally staged to protest the burning an SSP flag by another organization. The police resorted baton charge and use of tear gas to disperse the mob. 11 SSP activists were arrested as well.
the beheaded body of a soldier was found outside a destroyed police station in Pir Baba. He was identified as Qaisar Ali, of Sapal Bandi in Swat.
2 boys, Faizullah and Azeem Jan, were hurt in Chaman as a result of some explosive material planted there by some saboteurs.
a lineman of Pesco, Mohammad Rehman, was killed and 4 others were injured when a bomb exploded while they were repairing a pylon which had been blown up earlier.

Taliban militants beheaded a Polish geologist after negotiating his swap with the government failed. The Taliban spokesperson said that the Poitr Stancza was killed because authorities failed to free four militants of the Lashkar-i-Jhangvi before the given deadline.
A rocket hit a house, injuring two people and damaging the house and a vehicle.
A prayer leader was offering prayers in the limists of Band Korai police station when unidentified persons opened fire, killing him on the spot.
4 people were injured when a group of 10 Jafri clansmen attacked the Mohammad Yaqoob Brohi village.
Some youths fired a rocket at an armoured personnel carrier, however, it missed the target. No damage was reported.

The renewed wave of targetted killings that began a couple of days ago with gun attacks in Malir and Landhi continued as an MQM activist was killed while his aide was injured when armed men opened fire outside Murghi Khana Stop in Landhi.

Following an attack on the ANP Information Secretary, ethnic violence erupted in other parts of Orangi as the city police chief Saud Ahmed Mirza described it as \political and definitely ethnic\". Sources at the Abbasi Shahhed hospital said that man was found dead at Qasba No. 2-1/2 with a gunshot wound."
Fida Hussain and Shaaban Ali were standing near an Imambargah and Jamia Masjid Imamia when two unidentified men on motorcycles shot and killed them.
A leader of the Muslim Students' Federation,which is a student group backed by PML , was injured when unidentified men opened fire on him and fled.
a blast was reported from Dera Bugti town. A house was damaged in the Bugti Colony after a homemade explosive device went off. No casualty was reported.
Some people threw explosive material at the house of Municipal Councillor Iqbal Baboo but no loss of any kind was reported.

After receiving intelligence reports that Taliban commanders were meeting to regroup scattered militant groups, security forces moved into Orakzai. The soldiers, backed by artillery, tanks and helicopters clashed with militants. 38 militants were killed while 11 were injured and 23 were arrested. 10 security personnel, including FC and army men, were killed. According to AFP, 50 security personnel went missing after the clashes but local officials refused to comment on that claim.

Two low-intensity blasts in a crowded CD market, that took place 10 minutes apart, left 7 people injured. Police believe that the perpetrators were 'extremists who earlier targeted some cultural events in the city'.
The burnt body of an unknown man was recovered, by a forest department official while on duty, from a forest near Fatehpur in Layyah district.

Police discovered the tortured and bullet-ridden bodies of three MQM (Altaf group) activists in Shah Faisal Colony.  The three men, aged 15 to 25, were kidnapped from their homes Monday morning, allegedly by MQM-H activists.  Later in the article, the reporter states that police officials believe the motive to be \a sequel\" to the killing of two activists of MQM Haqiqi shot dead in Korangi on Sunday.  Police say the victims were blindfolded and believed to be shot by firing squad."

City PML-N leader Mian Babar and his driver were killed near the Tibbi Police station when two unidentified motorcyclists opened fire on their vehicle, killing them on the spot. According to officials, the PML-N leader had been receiving threats for the past few days not to pursue a murder case.
The bullet-riddled body of an unidentified man was found near the Bridge in Orangi Town no. 7.
Two policemen on duty were shot and killed by 3 armed assailants. The victims were identified as Muhammad Anwar Niazi and Ali Akbar Niazi.

unidentified tribesmen partially destroyed a picket established by the Khyber Rifles in Charwazgai on the grounds that the place is frequently visited by their women. The personnel of the paramilitary started rebuliding the demolished part of the picket.
A girl was injured due to Indian shelling along LoCin Southern Kotli District on Monday
a youth, along woth 2 accomplices, killed his grandmother over a property dispute in Abid Colony at Kot Farid Khan.
Four people were killed in a gunbattle between two groups in the Eastern Bypass area of Quetta. Two of the four bodies were identified as Bugti tribesmen.
Two armed motorcyclists killed a man, Mohammad Asif, and injured his wife, Shakeela, while they were on their way home on their motorbike. Police claim it was a target killing.
unidentified militants tried to blow up a bridge by planting three bombs under it. The bridge was partially damaged.
11 people were injured when youngsters of Kachhi community attacked Christian and Hindus of Machhar Colony with firearms and stones. The reason for the attack is not known.
Militants attacked two girls schools in Balambat area of Lower Dir. They first blew up the building of a community school and then set on fire a  high school building in the area.
A bank branch was ransacked by unidentified persons near Liaqatabad Post Office on Wednesday.

Maulana Hasan Jan, a leader of the JUI (Fazl group) and vice president of the Wafaqul Madaris, was assassinated when he was going in a car with three other men. When the car reached a deserted spot the unknown assailants sprayed the car with bullets. Maulana Hassan shot to political prominence in 1990 after defeating the late Khan Abdul Wali Khan of the Awami National Party in a National Assembly election for Charsadda, prompting the latter to announce retirement and end a career spanning 50 years. On a number of occasions, he had condemned suicide bombings as anti-Islamic. Security officials said it would be premature to attribute sectarian motives to the murder.
Shoukat Labano killed his mother while she was sleeping on the pretext of karo-kari and then fled. He suspected his mother was maintaining illicit relations with Liaqat Labano.
The body of Malik Haroon Ahmed, who was a local lawyer, was found floating in a canal. He had been missing since 13-Apr-94
Faiz Mohammad was killed in firing by unidentified gunmen.

In the midst of a strike called by the MQM to protest against the 'extra judicial killing' of its workers in police custody, protesters went on a rampage while trying to stop traffic and set fire to a minibus, a coach and a car in Azizabad.
The charred bodies of two young girls were discovered in a ditch in the Karala jungle some 40 km from Mansehra. The Nazim said that the girls might have been killed over Karo-Kari.
A man was brutally murdered in the jurisdiction of Par Hoti police station.
Power supply to Sui and Dera Bugti was also suspended after three pylons on Sui-Kashmore road were blown up powerful explosives.
Terrorists blew up the building of a private school.
India did shelling across LoC in Chakothi sector on Wednesday. No damage was reported
2 people were killed and 5 wounded by unknown assailants in Qasba Colony on Tuesday. Police claimed that violence was executed on ethnic grounds.

The police baton charged and tear gassed a procession of the Pakistan Awami tehrik (PAT) workers on the Mall which was held to demand that investigations into the killing of 100 children be carried out by the army rather than the police. According to the police, they reacted only after being attacked by the processionists.
A former councillor and his gunman were killed while another gunman was injured when unidentified men opened fire on them in Rakh Jhok village.

Saida, a girl of the Shar tribe, had been declared 'Kari' (\Disgrace to the family or to the tribe\") by a jirga after she married a man of the Phulpoto tribe. Her brothers visited her at the Darul Aman, where she had been admitted on the orders of a court, and threatened to kill her if and when she left the Darul Aman. "

In reaction to the misbehaviour of the area councillor by the police who went to Malir Extension Police Station seeking release of two detainees on Monday, thousands of protesters started protesting due to which police lathicharged them and later opened fire on them wounding 5 persons in Malir Extension Colony on tuesday.

40 people were arrested due to a clash between angry christian mob and police at Mall Road on Sunday. The protest was done against the addition of religious column in National Identity Card. The windowpanes and signboards of a large number of shops as well as vehicles were among the targets. Two police kiosks, one set up in Regal Chowk and other near Tollinton Market were set ablaze by the violent group.

Hundreds of enraged Mamond tribesmen barged into the Nadra office and thrashed the staff and damaged records and other documents. They alleged that the Nadra staff and levies were charges in excess to the fixed rate in order to issue the computerized identity card forms. They said that the Nadra staff only issues those forms to those people who pay more than the fixed charges. Later a big contingent of levies came and arrested 20 people. 10 people were seriously injured.
Indian shelling on the border villages of the Working boundary kills three and injures 21 others.
A bomb destroyed at least eight oil tankers in Sheikhwal area .

Five armed people shot dead a young man as they were suspecting that the deceased had illicit relations with their sister. The accused also seriously injured their sister, who was admitted to the hospital.

A clash between the Jatoi and Jagirani tribes took place when both tribes used different kinds of weapons in the exchange of fire in Kalar Goth. After which the highway near Sukkur was closed down. No loss of life was reported.
A Kalhoro man was kidnapped from the Ishaque Mashi village in Larkana and was shot dead some distance from the village.
A constable and a pedestrian were wounded in a drive-by shooting incident in Golimaar area near Husainiya Imambargah.

A suicide bomber tried to ram an explosive-laden vehicle into a police van. The vehicle exploded about 5 feet away from the police van, injuring 10 policemen. The van was transporting prisoners, including the sons of a TNSM (Tehrik-e-Nifaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi) leader, to an anti-terrorism court when the attack took place.

Eight people were killed when around twenty unidentified armed men entered Moosa Colony, dragged eleven people and huddled them in one room in a house belonging to a KMC employee and opened fire, killing eight of them on the spot. All were said to be Pushto and Hindko-speaking. According to officials, the room had some Urdu couplets inscribed on two papers and pasted on the walls. One read, \hum hain mata-i-koocha-o-bazaar-ki tarhan\". Awami National Party's provincial chief, Amin Khattak, alleged that the killings were carried out to spark ethnic riots. "

a truck engaged in carrying supplies for Nato forces in Afghanistan was burnt and a crane was damaged when rockets fired from nearby farms hit them at a terminal on Ring Road. The assailants also deflated the tyres of some trucks at the terminal. Police reached the spot and an exchange of fire took place which forced the attackers to flee.

Sajid Ali was intercepted and killed by armed motorcyclists moments after he had left his house. Intermittent firing was witnessed while the victim's body was being shifted to the hospital. After the funeral, mourners staged a sit-in and the Jafria Alliance of Pakistn condemned the 'targeted killings on sectarian grounds'.
Three brothers shot dead their sister and a man on suspicion of illicit relations in Chak Chandia, Rajanpur District.

protests continued for the fourth consecutive day in Punjab against the disqualification of the Sharif brothers. Many markets were closed down as a result. They chanted slogans and set up protest stands. PML-N workers also destroyed a bus at Clock Tower Chowk.
Dr. Javed Asghar, owner of Doctor's Hospital and husband of PML-Q MPA Faiza Asghar, was fired at by unknown assailants. He was in his car at the time and managed to escape unhurt.

Two persons were killed and four were injuerd when misfired rockets fell on the houses on local people in Meri Khel and Tandi Kalley area during the ongoing fight between security forces and militants.

In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, violent mob two places of Hindu worship in Khuzdar on Tuesday. 5 people were injured as they attacked a Hindu locality, looted and ransacked 17 shops owned by Hindus in various parts of the town.
The APMSO alleged that Mohajir students wer being tortured in Nara Jail. It was also alleged that the police had registered false cases against Mohajirs.

The Pakistan Army captured the Shinkay area from the Al-Qaeda linked militants in the Mehsud dominated area of South Waziristan. An army general was unable to report on the number of casualties both on the army side and the militant's side. A huge cache of arms, ammunitions and bomb-making devices were recovered from six caves in the area.
Muhammad Anwar, a soup vendor, was shot and killed by occupants of a yellow cab in Korangi.

After the news of another dead body being found spread, enraged residents took to the streets in protest, blocked the main road, pelted cars with stones and set a rickshaw, a motorcycle and a shop on fire.
Zubaidah Bibi was murdered by her real son and her brother for allegedly having illicit relations.

A man, Jamil, was shot dead by his brother over a land dispute. The victim was ploughing the fields when the accused him not to. On resistance, the accused, Ishaq, fired at his brother, killing him on the spot.
The SPSF President of Mehran University-Mr Niaz Hussain was allegedly tortured by the Tarraqi Pasand in Mehran University on Saturday.

A woman was killed and her son-in-law was injured along with a passerby when Amin alias Bhola Chor, a tough of the area, opened fire on them with the help of his accomplices. The accused had snatched a house from the woman, who went up to the court for the matter. The court decided to award her the house, prompting Amin to kill her.
A pipeline was blown up using a home-made explosive device near the Gahi Khan chowk in Shalkot area. Gas supply to many areas of the city was disrupted after the balst.
An 18 year old boy was killed by a stray bullet while standing outside the election office of PP-195 candidate.
3 people including 1 woman were kille don the pre-text of karo-kari in the Ali Mohammad Khoso village.
2 different tribal battles left 4 people dead and several others injured. The first clash was between two rival Pashtun tribes while the second was between rival Baloch factions. (See Note)
Two groups of Lashari tribe exchanged fire over a land dispute, leaving 3 people dead and 1 injured.

a co-driver of a cotton loaded trailer identified as Nur Mohammad was burnt alive when some students of Shah Latif University set it on fire while protesting against the death sentences given to their collegues by a Karachi court

Two rockets were fired from a place in Quetta and rocked the city when one landed and exploded on the roof of the FC headquarters, smashing windowpanes and causing damage to the building. The second rockets target was unknown. Police patrolling the area rushed to the graveyard of Ibrahimzai and seized an unexploded rocket.  No loss of life was reported.
As part of the on-going violence due to violent demonstrations by protesters mourning the death of their leader Chaudhry Altaf Hussain of MQM, a man was killed in Chakra Goth.

activists of Shahbab-i-Milli, an offshoot of Jamaat-i-Islami attacked a local marriage hall in sabzi mandi area where a competition of brides was being held. They ransacked the furniture and threatened the participants and organizers with dire consequences. they had previously asked the manager to close the 'vulgarity show' but he had refused to do so. Shabab-i-Milli president, Furqan Butt, said that they would not allow anyone to promote 'obscenity' in the city at any cost.
following the killing of the baloch nationalist leaders violence erupted in Balochistan. Government offices were attacked, a PTV booster was damaged and 2 fire tenders were set ablaze.
Five people were injured in a clash between two clans of the Jatoi tribe over a land dispute.

87 students who had started a hunger strike to demand admission to medical college after having passed their pre-medical examinations, were baton charged by the police. The police allegedly beat up the students, some female students among them.

An angry mob attacked the police post Bhown and threw its record in a nearby pond besides smashing its windowpanes. According to reports, some policemen asked local drivers for a vehicle for fatigue duty but the drivers refused. This infuriated the police staff then allegedly abused the drivers. The episode spread a wave of anger at the area residents who then attacked the police.The police retaliated and fired in the air to disperse the protesters.
Unidentified tribesmen killed a Taliban commander in Rabia Khel area of Orakzai Agency.
During a strike against the desecration of 10 copies of the Holy Quran and a number of \Seeparas\", some miscreants attacked the jeep of the DSP. "
Members of the Shar and Mehar tribes clashed over a dispute over relations between a Shar girl and a Mehar youth.

Police found the tortured body of a man in Landhi.  His religious affiliation could not be known.  A senior police official stated that the fresh sectarian violence was sparked by the Thursday morning murder of two TJP supporters.
one person was killed and 8 were injured in a shootout between rival tribal groups at Hub. The clash was between the Rind and Jamote tribes over a land dispute. The police also arrested 3 people.
A woman , who had gone to collect firewood in the forest was murdered by unidentified attackers. No further details given.

Unprovoked Indian shelling on civilian population in Chorbat valley, Shyoke sector near the Line of Control resulted in destruction of two houses along with the death of a few animals. However, no casualties were reported as villagers had alreay evacuated and had taken shelter in bunkers.
Police recovered a body of an unidentified man from the Mirwah Canal. According to the police, he had been killed elsewhere and his body was dumped in the canal.
A man who was found seriously injured with bullet wounds diedin the hospital.
A group of armed Maher tribesemen attacked a Jaoit village and killed one Jatoi tribesman and injured two othes. The reason is reported to be a land dipsute.
A body of a 15-year old boy was found with torture marks.
An unidentified man was murdered by unknown assailants who later threw his body into some bushes.

Chaudhry Transporters and Masood Al-Zafar Transporters had a long feud over the seizure of each other's bus stands. Twenty armed men of the Masood group attacked the bus stop of the Chaudhry group and took it over. They used batons and firearms to sieze the bus stop and thyey hurt 3 during the clash. The police arrested 2 people, while the rest are absconding.
Three people clubbed a man to death over a land dispute
The body of 35-year-old woman was found.
Six people were injured in Chuprial in the attack by security forces.

Police backed by army demolished a religious seminary believed to be used as a safe haven by militants in Lakki Marwat. No one was present in the seminary at the time of the incident, so no casualties or arrests were reported.
A man was killed and another was injured in a shooting by motorcyclists.
Five militants were killed and two others were injured when their vehicle hit a landmine in the Mamozai area of Orakzai. They were suspected members of the Taliban.
A youth was found murdered in an alley.

a peaceful rally was staged by the Rawalpindi/Islamabad Union of Journalists to condemn the kidnapping of Royal TV reporter Najam, Express' Hafiz Shahid Munir and Karimullah Gondal from Gujranwala. The rally started from the National Press Club, when the rally reached near D-chowk the Islamabad police baton-charged the participants  jounalists. they chanted slogans infront of the Parliament House. as a result more than 6 people were injured.

Khosa tribesmen chased 4 Gorchani tribesmen when the latter were attempting to flee after killing Shabbir Khosa for allegedly having an affair with a woman from their tribe. The two groups exchanged fire in which one member from each tribe was killed. 3 of the assailants managed to escape.
In a protest against the ethnic clashes in Quetta on Thursday, violent mob attacked and looted shops in Gwader on Saturday.
local police station attacked by locals for failure to arrest an Afghan refugee who fled after killing 2 locals and wounding 2 others. Elders intervened and stopped the situation from getting worse.

A volunteer of the Pakistan Qaumi Razakar was found dead in Baldia No 2. The victim was identified as Talib, son of Hashim, of Saeedabad. Police said the victim belonged to the Kutchi community, and was believed to have been killed somewhere else and dumped at a desolated place.
Two brothers were shot dead over a land dispute in the Raib village when their rivals opened fire on them in the fields.

2 goats and a cow were killed in Indian firing near the Sialkot border. Indian security forces continued intensive firing on Pakistani border villages of Zafarwal, Sucheetgarh, Chaprar, Harpal, Bajwat, Bajragarhi, Charwa and Shakargarh sectors. Some houses and 4 tractors were also badly damaged.
A young man was found murdered in Kharadar. The victim was found wrapped in a blanket in a narrow street behind Allahrakha Park with his hand and legs tied. His abdomen had been stabbed repeatedly.
4 officials of the Punjab Constabulary were injured as a bomb was hurled at them by some unknown people.
A Hiace was forced to stop in the journalists society, Gulshan-i-Iqbal, and set on fire.
A young watchman, Irfan, was found dead inside his rented quarter with two bullet wounds.
As security forces advanced to Upper Orakzai tehsil they were attacked by militants. In the clash that ensued, 8 militants were killed and 4 injured while 2 security personnel were also injured.

Two policemen sustained bullet injuries in a bid to stop a gunbattle between groups of two rival sects in village Taqipur. According to area people, imam of Masjid Haq Char Char Yar in Taqipur had arranged a conference on Khulfa-i-Rashideen during which he and other speakers allegedly made remarks which were found objectionable by the people of the other sect.  A group led by one Tanvir Shah approached the area police and made imam of the mosque to wind up the conference. Some people then allegedly opened fire on the son of Tanvir Shah, which sparked a clash between the two groups.  Some people alleged that the clash started when Tanvir Shah and others beat up Maulana Shams of the rival sect.

Armed men opened indiscriminate fire on the house of one, Abdullah, and shot and killed a man that was present at the house. He was a relative of Abdullah. This incident followed an assassination of a father and son, with whom Abdullah allegedly had a previous dispute. Police believe this may have been revenge killing.

Afghan-based militants attacked Pakistani security checkposts in the Khairkai Maskini Dara areas, killing a volunteer of a lashkar and injuring a few others. Lashkars and troops repulsed the attack in a joint effort.
A bomb exploded in a small hotel in the Rakhni bazaar. The Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility of the attack.

A man was killed while a dozen sustained injuries in an exchange of fire between two rival groups in Baghbanpura. One of the group leaders, the General Councillor of ward 37, was having a meeting in his office with around 20 other people when the rival group stormed the building and started firing. A fire started when a stray bullet hit a gas pipeline. One person dies while a dozen sustained injuries. The accused who were later arrested claim that the Councillor and his group had committed a blasphemy and that they were responsible for drug-peddling as well ; Follow-up: A man who had sustained injuries in the firing incident in Baghbanpura died in the Mayo Hospital on Dec 6 raising the death toll to 2.
A person shot dead his wife and a school teacher on the pretext of karo-kari in Mirpur Mathelo on Tuesday
A mortar shell house fell on the house of one Kaki, killing 5 family members and injuring 5 others.
a Pakistani soldier was killed and 11 others were injured when a bomb blast hit their truck in a tribal area near the Afghan border.
An unidentified body was found in Nazimabad. Police believed the murder was the result of factional fighting between rival groups.

Highly charged PML activists stoned the district police lines, set afire old tyres, damaged the official jeep of a Punjab minister and smashed windowpanes of different shops at various places in the city during the funeral of their Lahore additional secretary general Javed Ashraf. Police had to resort to teargassing to disperse PML activists throwing stones at the police lines on Empress Road following the burial of Javed Ashraf.
During the strike called by religious parties against the US-led attack on Afghanistan, a person was injured in Kalri when miscreants opened fire.
Sehwan town police found the body fo a 60 year old man in front of Mazar of Lal Shahbaz Qalandar. The body had marks of torture on it.
Some armed members of MSF attacked the office of People's Programme, run under the PPP. They ransacked the premises and caused damage to the property. No arrests were made.
An Afghan national was found dead in his rented room by unknown person/s.

An engraged mob consisting of MSF, PSF, SQM and other associations stoned and damaged the Pajero Jeep of MPA-Seth Muhammad Aslam while it was parked at Assistant Comissioner's Office in Khanpur on Tuesday
A young man was killed while his brother was injured by rivals in Shadbagh area on Saturday

A number of students were injured when a group of Sindh Peoples Students Federation (SPSF) came under attack, allegedly from a rival group, at the Islamia College. Leaders of two SPSF groups, led by Yar Muhammad Mallah and Haji Hamza Chandio, were at loggerheads with each other on several issues and a meeting had been called to negotiate the differences between then. When Yar Muhammad and his supporters entered the building premises to start negotiations, they came under fire from unknown people. Several people of SPSF were injured in the attack.
tribesmen fired rockets at checkpost in Ghori Nullah area in Dera Bugti claiming to have killed one personnel and injuring three others.
Tariq Memon was gunned down at Doctor's Colony.
The bullet-ridden body of an unidentified boy was found dumped in a pond.
The report mentions that 12 people were killed but the above mentioned incidents only account for 9 vicitims.

A Pasban leader was shot dead by his rivals in the suburban village of Nasirpur on G.T Road. Abdul Haseeb was an advocate and president of Pasban Peshawar district. Police said the murder was a result of old enmity.
A man was injured in a shooting incident in Saeedabad.

Five people were killed and five others injured after a US drone fired missiles into a house used as a hideout by militants in Machikhel area. Local people said that two of the missiles ripped through the house adjoining a madressah, killing five people suspected to be linked with the Taliban. The house reportedly belonged to a man named Shah Mehmood Khan, who was not there at the time of the attack.
A 35 year old man was found dead in the North Cantonment area.
An activist of the MQM and his friend were both shot dead when unidentified persons opened fire on them while they were sitting in Chamba Gali.
Security forces killed five militants in fresh attacks on suspected locations in Salarzai tehsil of bajaur Agency.

Some people in a car hurled a grenade towards the Bugti House. The grenade exploded in near the JWP office in front of the Bugti House. Guards fired shots at the vehicle but it managed to excape. Nawabzada Talal Akbar Bugti blamed 'government agencies' for the attack.
On the second day of a renewed wave of violence that police saw blended with 'ethnic colour', as intense firing left a man dead while at least a dozen others were injured in Sherpao Colony of Landhi.

A suicide bomber who was driving an explosive-laden vehicle, apparently on his way his target, was asked to stop at a checkpost. When he tried to speed away the police fired shots causing the pick-up to explode. 14 people were injured in the explosion.
Jahangir Marzai shot his wife, Sothi when she was home alone and fled
Zohra was shot dead by her brother on the pretext of Karo-Kari. He has been arrested and a case has been registered against him.

Manzooran Bibi, a mother of six, was killed by her brother, Nazar Abbas. The victim had developed 'illicit' relations with a man from the same village and the two had been caught by the Burewala police after which her husband her asked her to leave his house.
Zarina was murdered by her brother, Mehdi Hassan, who suspected that his sister had developed 'illitict' relations with a man.
miscreants in a car fired at a checkpost near Sultanwas. Troops returned fire killing 6 militants.
PPP workers became furious when their candidate was disallowed from the polling station by IJI workers. In the clash that ensued 6 people, including 2 policemen, were injured.

Twelve persons were injured when an explosive device planted in a car blew up near Wazir Dhand checkpost. The attack was suspected to target a tribal elder who was to pass through the checkpost. He was among the injured and many cars parked in the area were also damaged.
A bullet-riddled body was found at Nishan-i-Haider Chowk in Orangi Extension.
A watchman of a cargo firm was found dead in his office at Zafar Ali Road under mysterious circumstances. His body was found tied with ropes.

A woman and her two alleged 'paramours' were killed by the woman's husband's nephew when he found the three together at her house. The victims were identified as Sharifan Babi, Aziz Ahmed  and Amir Alam Khan.
A man was injured in Taroti village of Abbaspur sector as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.
Two tribesmen were killed and three others were injured when a vehicle going from Sadda to Arawali hit a landmine.

Two armed men on a motorbike intercepted a water tanker and fired at the driver. The driver lost control of the tanker and rammed into a rickshaw, killing a little boy inside and injuring his brother. The water tanker driver also lost his life.

A scuffle between shopkeepers and personnel of anti-encroachment staff of Muzzafarabad Development Authority was followed by a baton-charge by the police which left 5 shopkeepers injured. Earlier, the shopkeepers had shown the MDA staff a court stay order but the latter had torn up the document which caused the scuffle. The chairman of the MDA, Zahid Amin, claimed that his aim was to 'liberate the town from influential politicians' who he described as a \Qabza Group\" that had obtained illegal land allotments. "
militants hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Shapur on the Dalazak road. No one was hurt.

Four people, including a policeman and a prayer leader of a police station mosque, were injured when a blast occurred in a bicycle workshop, which injured the shop owner Sharifullah and his son Aamir too. According to officials, the device was a time bomb.
A school was blown up by militants.
A farmer was injured when the Indian forces shelled the Charwa sector across LoC.
Armed men opened fire at a car, killing one person and injuring 2 others. The deceased was identified as Obaid.

Hakim Ali and Sher Muhammad alias Sheri have a long fued. Sher Muhammad and Mukhtiar Ahmad went to Hakim's house and fired at the inmates. Two people died while one sustained major injuries. Police registered a case.
Helicopter gunships targeted suspected militant hideouts. No further details are given.
A man was shot dead in 36-B area of Landhi. His political affiliation was not known.
Two rockets were fired at a police team chasing a vehicle. However, both rockets missed their targets.

Two sisters were shot at by their husbands in village Nat Kalan near Ghakkhar.The sisters had returned to their parents place after being unhappy at their in-laws. The men had asked them many a times to come with them, but the sisters refused. So the accused reached their place and opened fire on both the women while they were asleep. One of them died while the other was stated to be in a serious condition.
Four militants were killed in an exchange of fire with security forces when thei car was stopped for a a security search.

The students of a local degree college ransacked the Wapda office in protest over the unscheduled and prolonged spells of loadshedding in the area. They smashed windopanes and damaged the furniture of the Executive Engineer's office. District Nazim, Pir Haider Ali Shah, reached the spot and assured them that the load-shedding would be brought to an end.

140 people from the Bugti and Marri tribes had been killed in the opeation in Karmo-Wadh area of Kahan Town, the headquarters of Khair Bux Marri tribe. It was a major operation in which both sides suffered losses. Some of the injured security personnel had been airlifted to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Multan.
Mashaal Khan and his three accomplices shot dead a man and his son over a land dispute. The victims were identified as Sher Ahmad Jan and Mir Ahmad Jan.

Four people were killed and several others were injured in Rehri Goth in a clash between two groups over a piece of land when 20-25 persons attacked a house with firearms, batons, and sharp edged weapons.

Two people were killed and another critically wounded in a dispute over three-marla piece of land. Mozzam Ali with his accomplices attacked Mohammad Ali and Safdar, killing them on the spot. The police had booked nine people in relation to the incident and were conducting raids to capture them.
Jinsar Kharos fired at his wife, Munwar Khatoonm, and Ghazi Kharos on the pre-text of karo kari and escaped.
local police have recovered a decomposed body of an unknown girl from Mandipur canal Hydel works.
The deputy director, Balochistan Public Relations department, was gunned down by unknown assailants near Dhadar. Police suspected that a land dispute could be behind the killing.
Two Afghan planes violated Pakistani airspace and dropped several bombs on an Afghan refugee camp, killing 8 refugees and destroying several slum houses.
One militant was killed and two others were injured in exchange of fire with the security forces after they attacked a security post in Barkhlozo.

A PPP worker and a passer-by were injured when two PML activists opened fire near the Chistia High School in Islampura. According to officials, the PPP and PML activists had argued the day before when the PPP worker was putting up PPP flags near his party's office.

Hundred of militants attacked security posts in Tang Khata, Kausar, Rashakai and Khazaza in Bajaur. The security forces backed by gunship helicopters and fighter jets retaliated killing 16 militants and injuring 22 others.
Constable Azhar was hit by a bullet and was seriously injured.
A landowner was gunned down and his brother was wounded by some armed men in Adilpur Village on Tuesday.
armed men killed Shakeel, son of Major (retired) Farhad, at a market in Hayatabad locality.
Several PPP workers were injured and about 250 were arrested as they were protesting against the government in Parliament Square on Tuesday.
security forces and armed tribesmen exchange gunfires in Bugti area. However, no casualties were reported.
A constable was injured when protesters pelted a police mobile with stones.
A rickshaw driver was stabbed at night and succumbed to his injuries in hospital.
Armed men attacked 2 Kohat University of Science and Technology students. They killed one while the other managed to escape.
Edhi volunteers found two bullet-riddled bodies in a park.
There were reports of a bomb blast but no casualties occurred.
2 people were killed in a clash between Ujjan and Kaleri tribes in Khairpur on Saturday. Tribes had 15 years old rivalry
A shopkeeper was shot dead by unidentified men in Rajgarh on Saturday.
Two motorcyclists gunned down one person in Sahin locality on Saturday, while motive behind this killing could not be ascertained
At least five people were killed and four were injured in Indian shelling along LoC in Pando Area on Friday

Three members of a Sindhi family were gunned down when unidentified armed men stormed into their house and opened fire, killing them on the spot, while two others were injured in the attack. Police claimed that the Mohajir Qaumi Movement carried out the attack.

An Imambargah caretaker was shot at and injured by two unidentified men on motorcycles when he was on his way back from a general store in Mian Mir Market. He was the president of Anjuman-i-Husnainia and had been receiving threats but nothing was done about it.

Two MQM workers were gunned down in their Turk Mohallah residence when it was raided by law enforcement agencies. The police changed their claim later and said their bodies were dumped here by unidentified men. The MQM accused the PPP (backed by Punjabi-Pukhtoon Ittehad) to be behind the killings along with the law enforcement agencies.
Local militants killed 6 alleged criminals as revenge for the death of their associates killed in Pandialai tehsil.
Unkown assialaints fired rockets at a frontier corps checkpoint blowing up a powerline but no casualties were reported.
Hafiz Javed Ahmed was found murdered mysteriously in his bedroom in Shahdara Town. He was stabbed to death.

Activists of the SNGPL union staged a demonstration to protest against the police for not arresting the factory owners who shot at a company official during a raid on 25-Dec-10. The protesters raised slogans against the police and set tyres ablaze.
Unkown people fired 5 rockets damaging a microwave tower and several telephone towers disrupting telephone communication in the area.

During the general strike called by the main Opposition alliance, led by the PML-N, party workers took out a rally during which they traded bricks and bottles with PPP activists. However, no injuries were reported.

People threw traffic out of gear and burned used tyres on roads leading to the General Bus stand and Raiwind in protest over the administration allowing factories to be built in residential areas and the killing of a minor boy and four others in a blast of a factory boiler outside Kot Rukan din Khanon. They demanded the immediate arrest of the factory owner. The crowd dispersed upon assurance by police that the owner would be arrested.

Commission agents, labourers, vendors and transporters staged a rally to protest agains the imposition of withholding tax. After marching on streets, they arrived at Deepalpur Chowk and set tyres on fire.
A clash between two rival sectarian groups took place over the taking out of a religious procession. The police intervened and tear gassed to rioters. Several people were injured.
Indian shelling in Kahuta sector caused partial damage to two houses on Friday

Seven people were killed and eight others injured when a bomb placed in a vehicle exploded at a filling station in Shabqadar area. The bomb was said to be in a carton of 'medicines', and was handed to the driver to be delievered to a person in Anbar bazaar. Local Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack, and said that the explosion was a warning to the people of Anbar who had raised an anti-Taliban Lashkar. They warned that more attacks would follow if if the Lashkar was not disbanded.
A person shot dead his wife and his neighbour on the pretext of karo-kari in Yaro Lund on Sunday
Three minibuses, two buses, and an Ilyas coach were set on fire in Korangi.
Two rival groups clashed over a piece of disputed land. There was an exchange of gunfire. The police reached the scene and dispersed them by firing aerial rounds. One passer-by was killed.
A girls government school was partially damamged when militants tried to blow it up in the Kalanga Akakhel area by planting an IED.
Six unidentified armed persons attacked a police party near Kot Nawab
Rocket shells were fired in Cantonment area from the Koh-Murdar on Monday. No casuality was reported
The four-room building and all the records of a government primary school were destroyed when militants planted explosives and detonated them.

A Moharram procession was taken out from Mohalla Phool Shah and was heading for Mohalla Thala in Town of Tank, a device exploded in nearby graveyard when the procession was passing near it. The blast triggered a stampede as the processionist ran about in different directions. the IGP said police had not found any sharpnel near the site and could not determine the nature of explosive device.
One Girdari Lal was shot and injured by nuidentified gunmen in a moving car.
Official of the PGMI and SIMS clashed over occupation of rooms in the office building. Furniture was thrown out and damaged.
Seven militants and one soldier was killed and several others were injured when military attacked the militant positions in Swat.
Militants attacked a security checkpost with mortars but security personnel managed to repulse the attack. 1 soldier was injured while 5 militants were killed.

A man was killed by his own collegues and a watchman injured when five armed men tried to kidnap a school principle. Upon resistance by the watchman, one of the kidnappers was killed by his collegues' firing, while the watchman himself was injured.

Following the assassination of Syed Raza Haider, the MQM announced a 3-day mourning period. Two official vehicles of government departments were torched while miscreants also tried to set on fire a truck on Ring Road.
A young son of a 'peshiman' of a mosque and his friend were killed when unidentified men opened fire on them from a moving vehicle while they were at a club near Masjid-i-Ahbab.

2 car bombs exploded with a 30 min. interval. The first explosion was of a mild intensity and the car used was not stolen. Police believed that a time-bomb with magnet was planted in it after it was parked. The second car which blew up, a golden Honda city, was parked a few feet away. Follow-up: According to the Infromation Minister, Al Qaeda may have a hand in the explosions as such an organised attack could not be done by just locals. However, the police suspect supporters of Harkatul Mujahideen Alaami, a gang of militants, who unsuccessfully tried to blow up President Pervez Musharraf's motorcade in Karachi in April 2002 and detonated a car bomb outside the US consulate two months later, killing 12 Pakistanis.
Blasts, caused by some explosives, occurred in different parts of Larkana. The blasts occurred at Railway Station, Municipal committee building and bus stand. No loss of life was reported.
a man and his wife were shot dead in their house in Rawalpindi. Mahommad Hanif, deceased, had come to Pakistan from England 15 days ago. The reason behind the killings is still undetermined.
Mohammad Hussain, a young man, axed his sister, Hamidaan Bibi, to death for allegedly having 'illicit' relations with a man.
militants shelled a paramilitary base, the security forces returned fire in retaliation.
Militants blew up the Government Girls Primary School in Sheraki area.
Security forces raided a house in Bhai Korona area and killed two militants when an exchange of fire ensued.

Jet fighters targeted Nari Baba which is a base of Lashkar-i-Islami, killing eight LI members. Some people kidnapped by the LI were also reported to have been killed. LI spokesman, Haji Zar Khan denied the killing of any LI members.
The body of a boy was found from canal in Lahore on Friday.
Ijaz Ahmed shot at and injured his aunt allegedly for developing illicit relations with a man.

The worsening power crisis, triggered violent demonstrations across Punjab. In Bahawalnagar, protesters stormed the office of an MPA and caused damage. They burned tyres, pelted stones and raised slogans against the government in various localities.
Three armed men attacked people coming out of a mosque after Friday prayers in Orangi Town, killing one and injuring another.
Two policemen were shot dead in M.A Jinnah road by unknown assailants on Saturday. The victims were sub-inspectors Muhammad Rehan and Muhammad Nisar

At least 20 dock workers were injured in a clash between rival labour groups at the Karachi Port Trust after a dispute over the loading of rice cargo.  The violence erupted after a KPT union opposed the deployment of outside workers for the loading of the rice.  The injured were taken to the hospital and police arrested nine workers from both groups.
The Rangers' post at Fakir Ka Pir was attacked with crackers twice, however, no one was reportedly injured.
A girl was killed while an infant was injured as the Indian shelling continued from across the LoC in to the Chakothi sector.
A person lost one of his legs in a landmine blast on Friday
Two people were injured in Dharra village in Kotli as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.
Three worshippers were injured when masked men opened indiscriminate firing on Taraweeh prayers in a local mosque. The firing created a stampede at the place, and the accused managed to escape.
An Assistant Commissioner , his daughet and his guard were shot dead by unidentified gunmen. The killings spread panic in the city and Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan announced a strike.
The activists of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM), sustained bullet injuries when unknown persons opened fire on them after polling was closed.
a bomb went off near schoool building in Mir Ali injuring one  soldier.

A few hours after the murder of a local builder in Gulistan-i-Jauher, some unidentified people took to the streets, fired into the air, forced shops to close, suspended traffic and set six cars on fire. The police claimed the the original murder was due to personal enmity .
The police intercepted three people, Asif, Asif and Irfan, allegedly as they were about to open fire on a police contingent.

A former head of district bar association, along with the help of some 25 armed accomplices, beat up a rickshaw driver for daring to ask him to park elsewhere. When the shopkeepers tried to intervene in the matter, they were subjected to torture too.
Shahud-ul-Hasan was shot dead and three others were seriously injured when miscreants fired a volley of bullets at a local hotel in Unit No. 10 in Liaquatabad. No other detail was given.

Five armed men opened fire at their rivals near a filling station. Reacting quickly, the men returned fire and killed all the five attackers and a passerby. The shootout also resulted to three injured seriously. Two cars and filling station of one of the rival groups was also torched. police have registered a case against the groups.
Amir Razzaq, an MQM activist, was shot dead by armed motorcyclists outside a barbecue shop.

Around sixty to seventy armed Bugti tribesmen stormed Bugti Colony police station. They killed one cop, injured 2 and kidnapped 4. They also took huge quantities of ammunition. After fleeing from the police station, they let the kidnapped policemen go. The police and Bugti tribe have clashed previously as well.
Hazara bridge linking Mingora with Kabal tehsil was blown up by unknown miscreants. The bridge was blown up three times last year.

Some 20 to 25 young adults attacked a PRTC bus full of passengers that was coming from the Civil Secretariat. They attacked it with bricks and stones and injured two children. The Police Emergency Squad arrested one person.
Following the attack on ANP activists in Gullistan-i-Jauhar, some unidentified people set ablaze a bus on Monday in Pehalwan Goth.

Assailants, in a Suzuki hi-roof bearing official number plate, opened fire at the participants of a MMA-led funeral prayer. This resulted in the participants panicking and throwing stones at the car. The assailants left the vehicle behind and ran awary. 2 Rangers rushed to the area, however as they were approaching, they were also pelted with stones. This resulted in shooting and Abu Aala got injured.

The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as unidentified miscreants set fire to five roadside tea stalls and food outlets and half a dozen pushcarts in Surjani Town's sector 4-A, 4-B and 7-A.
Two brothers with the help of two companions shot dead a tea stall owner, Akram, on the Railway Road.  The people of the area protested against the incident and blocked the G.T Road by burning tyres.
Two persons were shot dead by unknown assailants, when they were fired upon while sleeping. Motive behind the killings was not ascertained and the villagers claimed they had no enmity.

Allegedly, the SHO and his subordinate unlawfully picked up a lecturer of the Faisalabad  Government College University, his father and brother and tortured them. The lecturer claimed that they were tortured to please their political rivals. In an inquiry the accused policemen stated that they had aided the lecturer in a timber theft case. A case was registered against both the SHO and his subordinate.
A prayer leader, maulvi Qaimul Zaman, was killed by eight armed assailants at his house in kabal tehsil, Swat.

Two armed men gunned down Jamilur Rehman Abbasi, a former unit in-charge of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement in the Phulleli area. He had been recently released from prison regarding a murder case charged against him
Militants attacked a security checkpost. No further details given

A police party, headed by Sub-inspector Liaquat, reached Pipal house to record a statement of Javaid Warraich, brother of MPA Khalid Warraich who's body guard had just been shot. Jawaid Warraich had brought the injured body guard to Pipal House as well.  As they (it is not clear who) were arguing, someone opened fire, killing a constable, and injuring an ASI and an SHO.
Two men were injured in Kotli Khumbah village as a result of intense Indian shelling from across the Line of Control.
In an exchange of fire between two groups of the Brohi clan in Sabaz Ali Brohi village as a result of a dispute over sharing of irrigation water caused injuries to 13 people.
Unidentified men opened fire on a helicopter in the Akakhel area as it was returning from Orakzai. The helicopter also returned fire and targeted militant hideouts.

The students of Islamia College under the banner of Muttahida Talaba Mahaz, smashed window panes of three hostels, damaged a college bus and pelted the police with stones while protesting anti student policies by the administration. The police resorted to the use of tear gas and baton-charged the students to batter down the protest. No injuries were reported. Three student leaders were also arrested.
Unidentified assailants have killed four people, including three women, of a family after entering their house in the guise of women. The reason behind the killing is unknown.

Suspected militants attempted to blow up a bridge in North Waziristan. According to the police, a local boy informed them of the remote controlled device planted underneath the Kachkot bridge. The bomb disposal squad defused the bomb. Military convoys frequuently use that bridge.
A bomb blast in the Gaddai market suspended the inter-provicial traffic. The bomb however, did not cause any casualty
Two people- Sadiq and Munir- were injured when their opponent group attacked them outside a polling station in Gulberg.

A young unidentified man was killed in an encounter with the police. The police reached Shadman Town on a tip off that some youngsters were resorting to firing in the area. When the police arrived there, they had an exchange of fire in which one youngster was killed.
Polling was suspended at polling stations in Taj Muhammad Abbasi village due to clashes between the supporters of rival candidates.

Following multiple murders in quick succession in the city, angry residents demonstrated against the local administration for their inability to curb the rising crime wave in the city. The protesters damaged public property including street lights and sign boards and chanted anti-government slogans.
Mohammad Sharif and his father, Sikandar were killed by their rivals when they were working in their fields. The reason behind the attack is stated to be an old land dispute between the two baradris

a bomb attacked to a motorcycle exploded in the Defence Officer's Colony, killing one person.it is unclear if the man that died was a suicide bomber or someone else. A car and some windows were also damaged.
two men who had been kidnapped from the Kohat-Parachinar road were found near Alizai. The two men had been kidnapped when they were going to the Kurram Agency.
A Datsun pick-up was torched.
An armed clash between mebers of the Shar and Jagirani tribes took the lives of three people.
A man was wounded in Sniper firing in Orangi Town.
There were several scuffles during polling and some injured had to be hospitalized. There were also reports of arrests of some miscreants.
Zulfiqar Hussain was shot at and injured by undentified gunmen.

Balochistan Minister for Labour and Manpower, Maulana Mohammad Sarwar, allegedly attacked Mohammad Ilyas Lashari with a knife and kept him in captivitiy for several hours at the former's residence. Lashari, a senior government official at the Communication and Works department, claimed that the minister invited him to his house and asked him to not take up the position he had been transfered to by his department. When Lashari refused, the minister attacked him. The accused has denied the allegations

two armed motorcyclist gunned down three people, Roshan Ali, Shaib Dina and Fida Hussain, and injured five other when they opened fire on a tractor-trolley which was headed to Fatehpur.the injured were taken to the hospital where two of the injured were said to be in critical condition. old enmity is said to be cause behind the attack.

a shootout between two rival sectarian groups during a Tazai procession left 13 people including a police constable injured. The clash began when members of one sect attacked the other. The police arrested a number of people after the incident. 4 shops were set on fire and 2 others were damaged.

An SSG commander was killed and three others injured in an attempt to enter the mosque and put an end to the Lal Masjid controversy. Scores of militants had taken over a mosque and held many students hostage. The Pakistani government was making efforts to to crack-down on the militants of the Lal Masjid during these days.
The decomposed body of an unidentified man, around 35 years old, was found lying on garbage.

Suspected militants launched 2 simultaneous attacks on two military checkposts. According to Brig Mehmood Shah, the militants launched the attack with mortars, rockets and machine-guns. The soldiers called for reinforcements. At least 9 FC soldiers, 6 Pakistan Army soldiers, 20 suspected militants, 3 civilians, and 1 Khasadar were killed. At least 10 paramilitary soldiers were injured. 1 militant was captured.; Follow-up: The government has claimed to have retrieved four more bodies of foreign militants, taking their overall death toll to 22.

Students of local institutions blocked traffic to protest against the 'attitude' of transporters that operated on Hakkar Road. The protest turned violent whent he police tried to intervene and open the  road for traffic. The students attacked the police with stones and clubs, leaving 5 policemen injured.

A spiritual leader and his son were gunned down in broad daylight when unidentified assaialants opened fire on them while they were sitting outside their house in Iqbal Colony. SSP, Malik Ahmed Raza claimed the slayings may have been the result of the 'Gaddi' dispute.

Two bombs planted in a drain near Taj Chowk by militants were defused by bomb disposal personnel. The timely action of the police averted a sabotage attempt which might have caused huge losses to life and property.

Another gunman of the PML-J MNA Chaudhry Amjad Ali Warraich was murdered when 5 assailants opened fire on him in Kaleki. Two months ago, another gunman of the MNA was killed in a similar attack and the case was registered against the PPP MNA, Chaudhry Muhammad Ilyas Jat for abetment.
Sialkot's Peoples Youth Organization vice president, Khadim Husain, was murdered in his house by some unidentified people. The motives behind the murder were not mentioned in the report.
Three PPP workers were attacked by a local PML councillor and his accomplices. The workers were beaten up and taken to PML office  but were released later. No arrests were made.
protesters resorted to blocking roads, tyre burning and aerial firing in protest to the killing of the three Baloch leaders in Turbat.
A suicide bomber rammed his explosive ladden jeep into a check post near Thall, killing himself and three other paramilitary soldiers and injuring 16.

2 women and 2 children were killed when a mortar shell hit a house in an Afghan refugee camp in Ghamkol area as security forces intensified attacks on militants' hideouts in Darra Adamkhel. 4 other members of the family were injured.
An exchange of fire between rival groups in Malir left at least 2 people injured. Sporadic incidents of firing were reported from the area amid high tension.

Frontier Corps backed by warplanes, helicopter gunships, tanks and artillery pounded suspected hideouts of militants in 5 villages of Lakaro and Pandyali tehsil, sadi to be the strong hold of Tehrik-i-Taliban's Mohmand chapter.3 civilians were killed while 12 civilians were injured.

It was alleged that police beatup a student of the Chemistry Departement when he was discussing the problems and the demands of the students with the Vice-Chancellor. Following the incident the students boycotted classes in protest.
A Tehreek-i-Jafria Pakistan leader was shot dead in Haroonabad by two motorcyclists. The attack occurred when the deceased was about to enter a mosque to offer Maghrib prayers.
Agha Mahmood Ahmadzai-a local leader of BNP-M was gunned down by unidentified men in Kalat on Monday. After firing, his vehicle got out of control, hitting and injuring two men.
2 security personnel were injured in firing by miscreants at the circuit house in Mingora.
nine people, 5 policemen among them, were injured when a suicide attacker rammed an explosive-laden motorcycle into a police van.
militants attacked a cargo terminal of Nato and damaged four containers as well as the office at the terminal.

An attempt to attack an Imambargah in Hazara Town failed as the explosives being carried by the suspected bomber exploded prematurely. The suspect was identified as Pervez Noor of Dera Allahyar town in Jaffarabad.
A home made blast at Habib Bank Shershah branch caused extensive damage to the bank. There was, however, no casualty. Police was investigating.

police baton-charged protesters of Baloch-Para who were protesting against shortage of water in their area. They ransacked the office of the taluka nazim, personal assistant of the taluka nazim, naib nazim, taluka municipal officer, meeting hall and other offices. three people were injured while breaking the glass of the offices. the protesters burnt tyres on the M.A Jinnah road. police reached the spot and baton-charged the protestersat the Mirza Mansoor Baig Chowk. 13 protesters were arrested.
A gwadar police official was killed and two others were injured in grenade attack on a police officers house when two motorcyclists threw a grenade and fled.
A man was shot and wounded in the Phuleli area.
A doctor, his wife and their two month-old baby were found dead at their residence in Mayo Hospital.

Following the targeted killing of ST worker Islamuddin, intense gunfire took place in the area which forced shopkeepers to pull down their shutters. The report claims that a police van came across the 'armed riders' and in the exchange of fire that followed, injured and arrested one of them. It is not clear if the armed riders were the assassins or the the people that resorted to gunfire after the assassination. An bystander was also injured in the exchange.

The office of a student group at Adamjee College was ransacked by rival students. Furniture was broken and slogans scribbled on the walls against the 'leader' of the group. The APMSO condemned the incident and blamed its rivals for the incident.
Two people died when an explosive device went off. It could not be ascertained whether they were tried to plant the device or carrying it but they were almost certainly militants.

Former activists of PSF shot and killed the father of Shah Zeb, an IJT worker who they had kidnapped but who had managed to escape. Following Zeb's escape, the former PSF men - Yahyah Gujjar and his accomplices - went to the former's house and upon being told that he was not there they shot dead his father Raja Aurangzeb. The victim was a worker of the Al-Hamd Textile Mils.
Security forces attacked militant hideouts, destroying 4 hideouts and kiling 11 militants. 6 militants were also injured. Independent sources however put the death toll at 3.

Two men on a motorbike opened fire on Naimatullah alias Mohan Bengali while he was travelling in his car. Naimatullah, a PPP worker, was killed while his female companion was injured. It was reported that the cause could either have been a property dispute the victim had or his political affiliation.
