A hawker of the general bus stand, Nazir Husain, was stabbed to death by three people. Police claimed to have arrested the three killers, Muhammad Aslam alias Kala, Shafaat and Rana Iftikhar Ahmad.
The bullet-riddled body of a Haqiqi activist was found in a car in Shamsi Society.
The body of a 35-year old man was found lying in a field near Nishtar Colony police station. Police said it was almost decomposed.
Communites affected and displaced by the Pehur canal demonstrated to get jobs and compensation. The police baton charged them and arrested six people.

Following a clash between two BSO factions the day before, another clash erupted when supporters of one faction who were 'outsiders' entered the college premises and resorted to aerial firing before installing themselves in strategic positions. Students of the other faction, who were in classrooms on the first and second floors, returned fire and the exchange continued for about 30 minutes before the police moved in and used tear gas shells to disperse the groups. BSO (Yasin Baluch) accused their rival faction, BSO (Soheb) of initiating the clash and claimed that one of its members had been injured while the BSO (Soheb) claimed that 3 of its supporters had been injured.
Traders of Local Timber market observed strike and staged a demonstration against the growing theft incidents in the area by burning tyres and chanting slogans against the police.
Three security personnel were injured when their vehicle hit an IED on the road near Gora Qabristan in Miramshah.
The Chenab Rangers thwarted two major attempts by the Indian Security Forces to fence the Sialkot Working Boundary in the Bajwat and Jammu sectors. They destroyed two big Indian defensive pillars.
There were several incidents of violence on the eve of the union council polls. A gang of miscreants intercepted and set a passenger coach on fire.
A man was injured in a shooting incident in North Nazimabad.
A villager was killed in a landmine explosion in Dera Murad Jamali.
an unidentified man was killed in a blast on the Ghulam Khan road. Officials said the man was planting a remote controlled device when it exploded and killed him on the spot.

A People's Party activist was kidnapped, tortured and killed and his body was found from a graveyard in the Orangi. His family claimed that ten armed men had raided the house and kidnapped him the day before.
One private vehicle was set ablaze by unknown men in Saddar on Friday.
Two students were hurt when students with two different political viewpoints took out a procession. Both the groups clashed with stones, knives and clubs. The police, reprortedly did not intervene.

A senior government official and his friend were injured when an explosive device resembling a hand grenade was hurled into his house. The official, Junaid Shah, who was a deputy director-general in the communications department was haing tea with his friend Malik Shaukar Ali, a Pakistani origin British national, when the event occured.

12 people were injured when supporters of Legislative Assembly Speaker, Mumtaz Hussain, belonging to the Muslim Conference turned violent. They pelted the police with stones and the police tear gassed them. They were protesting gainst the filing of a no-confidence motion against the Speaker.
2 auto richshaws, a truck, a minibus and a small van were set on fire by unknown men in Nazimabad Area on Sunday.
Protesters clashed with police and pelted the police vans with stones. They were protesting against the alleged kidnapping and torture of a maid and her husband by their employers.
Walls of the local social welfare department office and the women's Pardah Club were damaged when a bomb exploded in the area.
the guest house of one Hameedullah Takhtbhai was set on fire.

Over hundred suspected militants attacked a police check post in the Badabher area and set the two room building on fire. However, the police was allowed to leave the post. On the other hand, the Superintendent of Police stated that the police post was attacked by criminals impersonating as militants.
Armed clashes between two rival student groups took place in Government Post-Graduate College Bannu as a result of which one student was injured on Wednesday.
Paramilitary troops stopped a suspected car. The two suspects in the car opened fire but were shot in the retaliatory fire by the troops.
Ali Raza, a resident of Frontier Colony, was shot dead by two men on a motorbike.
At least 7 people were brought to the LMC Hospital with bullet or knife injuries as firing in the air continued through the night.
two vehicles were partially damaged when miscreants set them on fire.

On the call of Jeay Sindh, the students of Sukkur, Ghotki and Pani Akil boycotted classes. In Sukkur the Jeay Sindh students blocked roads and burnt tyres . However, the police dispersed them. They also resorted to firing in old Sukkur area. Many vehicles were also stoned. The reasons behind the strike call were not mentioned in the report.
An unidentified body was found stuffed in a gunny bag.
The chopped body of a shopkeeper was found from a bag in River Ravi in Bashira Village on Friday.
election to 113 union councils of Kasur district were held amid reports of of violence which left scores of people including Ganda Singh SHO injured.
Two groups of Sabzoi and Sawand clansmen clashed over a land dispute , killing 3 people.

A suicide bomber exploded a vehicles near a highly-guarded checkpoint, killing 10 people, 2 of which were children and 3 policemen, after being stopped for checking at the post on Matta road, which was a militant stronghold. Major Amjad Iqbal stated that it was a desperate act by the defeated militants.
Fire crackers exploded in various areas of the town causing panic.
The body of a new born baby girl was found in a polythene bag thrown in a plot.
An unknown man came to Asghar's General Store and opened fire on Asghar and fled. Asghar was injured and the motive behind the incident could not be ascertained.
A prayer leader of the Masjid Al Banat, was shot and killed when unidentified persons opened fire on him in Tetley, killing him on the spot. The Qari was said to have taught girls at a moque.
Two blasts were reported in the Mastung town. A tower of a private cellphone company was damaged in one of the explosions. The exact location of the second blast could not be ascertained
Irshar Patwari was killed by unknown assailants over a land dispute.

An army man was found strangled outside the Lahore Fort. Lance Naik Tariq Hussain of 8th Azad Kashmir Regiment was posted at Head Sulemanki in Okara district and had come to Lahore to visit his brother-in-law.  Police suspected he was strangled by a cloth.

The TJP took out a rally to protest against alleged government excesses against TJP supporters. They claimed that ever since Mr Watoo had taken over as Punjab Chief Minister, excesses against the Shia communnity had increased. They also demanded certain measure to be taken against the SSP and urged the Federal Government to take notice of the 'partisan attitude' of the Punjab Government. The processionists 'gave a sound beating to three suspected persons' and handed over to the police.

Armed motorcyclists opened fire at Asad and Farooq, who were working at a shop, killing them on the spot. One person was injured in the attack. The police claimed that it was a case of targeted killing.
A man killed his sister and her alleged parampour for having illicit relations. The headline mentions three people being killed but the report mentions just two.
The Chenab Rangers thwarted a major attempt by the Indian Security Forces to fence the Sialkot Working Boundary. They destroyed the two pillars erected by the Indians.
The MQM coordination committee alleged that Muhammad Aslam, the brother-in-law of MQM chief Altaf Hussain was arrested and subjected to torture in Adiyala Jail.
Three rockets were fired on a camp in Makin area bordering the two waziristan agencies.
Soliders attacked a police station after two army men were arrested and questioned by the police.The soldiers attacked the policemen injuring atleast three.
Masked men shot dead Mohammad Jamal and fled. No further details given.

Police killed two militants after they opened indiscriminate fire and injured two policemen when their car was asked to stop for search on the Hassah Bridge in Balakot. DIG Syed Imtiaz Altaf claimed police had information that terrorists planned to target Friday  congregation at the main mosque in Balakot. Police encountered more gunfire from the mountains by militants placed there to give support to the suicide mission, however, it died soon. Suicide jackets and explosives were recovered from the car.

The house of Dr Mahmooda Sultana, wife of MQM supporter Shaikh Liaquat Hussain, was attacked my armed assailants who opened fire at it. Dr Sultana claimed that the attack as aimed at killing Amir Liaquat, editor of the daily Parcham, who was not home at the time of the incident. In the firing incident at the Parcham office 2 days ago, where a manager was killed, it was also claimed that the target was the editor.
A 22 year old man was shot dead at his doorstep by two unidentified assailants.
A man killed his daughter for marrying out of her own choice. The police arrested the man.
2 people were killed and 3 were injured in a clash between two rival groups in Shahbazkhel on Sunday.
Talib Hussain was killed by his 4 armed relatives in village Lakho, Kahna, over a property dispute.

Enraged activists of the JSQM took to the streets in various areas of Sukkur, barricaded highways, burnt tyres to vent anger against the arrest of their leader by the law enforcement, demanding his release. A complete shutter-down strike was observed.
The decomposed body of Amanullah- son of Juma Khan, of Jhok Qureshian- was recovered from a forest by the Gomal University police.

5 bullet-ridden bodies were found with a note attached claiming that they were US spies and that any other person caught spying would meet the same fate.  2 other bodies were found in Qutabkhel area and Mirali Bazar which are assumed to have suffered a similar fate.
the Mehsud Scouts impounded a vehicle and arrested a militant after an exchange of fire with militants fleeing from the Chapari area.
A man killed his wife outside his residence. He claimed that his wife was trying to flee the residence which Is why he opened fire on her. He later surrendered himself to the police.

Three minor sisters were found murdered on the second storey of their house by their grandmother. Their father was a proclaimed offender and mother was absent. The motive behind the killing could not be ascertained.

Military spokesman Major General Atthar Abbas claimed that 21 terrorists had been killed during the succesful take-over operation in Kotkai over the span of two days while three security personnel laid down their lives with another eight wounded.
A 10 year old girl was in the field with her cattle along the LoC in Mandhar village when picked up a \mine-like\" device hiding in the bushes. This device exploded, blowing her hands off."
the civil lines police found the body of a man, Fahim Anjum, lying in a nullah at Gulistan Colony.
A worker of MQM, Azeem, was shot dead while passing through Sector 36-B in Landhi.
A Pesh Imam of a mosque was found murdered in his Hujra in Mosque in Liaqatabad on Saturday.

A low-intensity blast, presumably caused by a cracker, partially damaged a shrine and injured two 'devotees'. It not be determined if the explosive device was flung from outside the shrine or if it was planted inside.
A head constable was killed in Khuzdar by unidentified gunmen. Later, a man identifying himself as the spokesperson of Baloch Liberation Army claimed the responsibility for the attack.
Mohammad Ashraf, a PPP, a leader of IJI was stabbed to death and his son injured allegedly by PPP workers in a dispute over pitching of an election camp. Six PPP workers were arrested.

3 people were killed and 4 others were injured when a shell exploded inside a house in the Janet Shah village. The explosion occurred in the house of a scrap dealer. As the defused shells were collected from the conflict zone, the acrap dealer may have stored the shell.
Tribal volunteers backed by gunship helicopters attacked the militant hideouts killing 10 militants an injuring 8 others.

Five people, including two policemen, were injured when two persons riding a motorcycle hurled a hand grenade near a small road side restaurant. The police added that the imam of the BMC mosque was amongst the injured, and that the attackers had used a home-made device.
A blast occurred in a fruit vendors push-cart in front of the Old Kotiwali. The local Bomb Disposal Squad said it a was a home-made low intensity bomb.
Two tribes exchanged a fresh wave of violence on an on going clash lasting 11 years.
8 militants were killed and 3 soldiers were injured as militants attacked a checkpost in Ghelju Area, Upper Tehsil on Saturday. A vehicle was also destroyed in the exchange of fire.

Protesters blocked the Sialkot Daska Road for many hours to demand action against the failure of the police to protect them from ruffians. They burnt tyres and pelted stones.The deputy commissioner and the SSP rushed to the scene and assured of a timely action.

A grenade was thrown at Faqirabad mosque during Isha prayers, killing 1 and injuring at least a dozen others. Soon after the incident, Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan workers blocked a road to protest the attack. They also anounced a shutter down strike.
An unidentified bullet riddled body of a young woman was found at Islam Chowk in Orangi Extension Area.

Two people were killed and several injured in a bloody clash between two rival tribes in Jamrud. The clash broke out over the privileges granted by the political authorities to two clans of Zakakhel, one led by Malik Darya Khan and the other by Malik Mahmood Khan. Heavy weapons, including mortar guns and rocket launchers were used by the clashing groups.

Two motorcyclists opened fire at a car carrying Dawat-i-Islami chief,Maulana Muhammad Qadri. One of his companions was killed on the spot while another was injured and rushed to the hospital where he succumbed to his injuries the next day. The Dawat-i-Islami chief, who was on his way to the airport to catch a flight to attend a meeting of the Milli Yakjehti Council.
A blast in the Court premises killed an elderly man.

militants fired 12 missiles on Khar. Two landed near the Bajaur Scouts Camp, two outside the officers' colony, one near a higher secondary school and the others hit civilian areas. One woman and two children were killed.
Amanat stabbed his younger brother, Karamat, and his wife and two children to death over a property dispute. The bodies were thrown in Upper Chenab Canal and had not been retrieved.
An unidentified young woman was shot dead by unknown men in Bahadarabad. The motive behind the murder was not known.

a suicide bomber on a motorcycle hit a bus carrying employees of the Kahuta Research laboratories at Choor Chowk on Peshawar Road, injuring more than 40 people. Windowpanes of several nearby buildings were smashed. At least 10 vehicles were damaged. The attack was described by the people as a grave breach in secuirty in the garrison city.
fierce clashes between the security forces and the taliban militants loyal to Maulana Fazlullah. Helicopter gunships also shelled the area as well as targetting militant positions in Charbagh tehsil.
A bomb went off outside an auto workshop of the International Committee of Red Cross (ICRC) in Sufaid Dheri area, which damaged the wall of the building a bit.
In a clash between two groups of the Junejo tribe over irrigation water, one person was killed and another injured.
miscreants blew up 4 transmission towers in Barkhan by planting explosive material around the structures.
A man killed his teenaged sister in Wah village over suspicion of illicit relations.
A bullet-riddle body was found. Police suspected that the victim was kidnapped from somewhere and killed before being thrown in the area.

Between 400 and 500 people of a particular sect blocked the main road and tried to set tyres on fire at Chandani Chowk to protest the registration of a case against them under the Blasphemy and Anti-Terrorism Laws. The police used batons to disperse the crowd and also arrested over 30 people, who were released later in the evening. The case was registered in the aftermath of rally held recently where their rival sect attacked them after alleging that blasphemous sectarian slogans had been raised.
A man was killed and two others were injured in a blast in Kohlu bazaar.
A partially decomposed body of a young man was found dumped in a well in Millat Gardens in Malir. The hands and feet of the deceased were tied, and the body bore marks of torture.

Following the assassination of Syed Raza Haider, the MQM announced a 3-day mourning period. Armed men patrolled the streets to make sure that no one defied the morning call. Miscreants set ablaze a medical store in Islamabad Mohallah.
One girl was killed while another was injured when they picked up a toy bomb which exploded.

A primary school teacher, who was to serve as an assistant presiding officer at the Arbab Bhai Khan polling station, was shot dead and two people were injured when a police constable (or a person wearing police uniform) fired on them.
A 40 year old Mohajir Qaumi Movement activist was shot dead in Korangi after being kidnapped from Landhi a few hours earlier.
Maqsood Hussain was shot and killed. Nor further details given.

Shopkeepers protested the arrest of their collegues by blocking the road and burning tyres. Their collegues were arrested by the traffic police as they were displaying merchandise on the footpath. The protest ended peacefully as the MNA Shabbir Ahmed Khan assured the protesters that the shopkeepers would be released. They later were released.
The body of a labourer, Haq Nawaz, was found with injuries to the head.

Protesters blocked National Highway at different points from Quetta to Karachi against the killing of Nawab Akbar Bugti. Protesters blocked the road between Gwadar and Karachi burnt tyresand pelted stones at vehicles. Balochistan National Party-Mengal Secretary General, Habib Jalib, said the protests will continue til the government decide to halt the military operation and resolve the issues politically.
Security forces killed two militants and arrested three suspects during operations in the teligram area of the Charbagh tehsil.
Five militants were killed when security forces pounded militant hideouts in the Gurguri hilltop in the Bara tehsil, retaliation to an earlier attack.
Troops on routine patrol were attacked with a roadside IED. 2 personnel, including a Major in the army, were killed while one other person was injured.
A doctor was found shot dead in his clinic. The police says it was a targetted killing.
A constable was killed and three others were wounded when unidentified occupants of a yellow cab opened fire on the Model Colony police station.

Prominent poet Mohsin Naqvi was gunned down by an unidentified assailant in Allama Iqbal Town. A worker of a nearby shop was also injured in the firing. The motive behind the murder could not be known, but sectarian motives could not be ruled out. The assailant had waited outside a shop to target the poet.
a labourer, Gul Mohammad, was found tortured to death in Mehran Town in Korangi. The ANP said that the victim was its worker.

District president of Tehrik-i-Jafria and a friend were killed while another was injured when two unidentified motorcyclists opened fire on them at a medical store in Khanewal. Later, police arrested seven suspects and workers of the Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan.
several armed men opened firing and killed a girl and injured 7 others in Church Colony near Kot Salim.

Two rival groups, led by Rana Aizad and Shahbaz, of the Government College University Faisalabad resorted to aerial firing on campus. Police registered a case against more than two dozen members of both groups while took thirteen students into custody.

The Indian Security Forces continued firing on Zafarwal, Charwa, Bajwat, Chaprar, Harpal, Sucheetgarh, Bajragarhi and Shakargarh, Jammu, Oovi, Chhumb sectors. As a result, the firing killed 2 animals, badly damaged 6 houses. The Chenab Rangers returned the fire.
The bomb disposal squad defused an IED that had been planted along a road.
a school girl and another were killed and 3 sustained injuries when unidentified persons sprayed bulltes on a passenger bus near an FC checkpost.

During the strike called by the MQM Youngsters burnt tyres on the road and pelted police vans with stones. Police resorted to firing and tear gas shelling at various places including Kazi Abdul Qayyum Road and Sakhi Abdul wahab Complex. An exchange of fire between police and protesters also took place in New Cloth market area and a rickshaw was set ablaze on Jacob Road.
An activist of MQM was shot at and injured by unknown assailants in Korangi on Friday.
Syed Nasim Shah, a landlord, was chatting with his friends outside his house when unidentified men fired at him killing him on the spot.
A person killed his wife in Kando Hingorjo Village over karo-kari on Monday. His brother was also involved with him in killing.
A young resident of Touheed Colony was shot dead by a rival group in retaliation for another murder the day before.  The boy's relative was accused of committing the previous murder.
A shop keeper was shot dead in Gulshan-i-Iqbal.
Two bullet riddled bodies of unidentified men were found. The bodies bore severe torture marks.
One person was killed and another injured when unidentified gunmen raised anti-MQM slogans and fired at a procession going to attend a Quran Khwani for slain PSF leader Najib Ahmed.
In Kokrai area of Saidu Sharif, three miiltants were killed in a clash after an attack on a police vehicle. Six grenades, a Kalashnikov, a rifle and a pistol were seized.

Following the assassination of Khalid Malik earlier during the day, employees of the SSGC gathered and tried to proceed to the Balochistan Assembly with the body of the victim. The police put up barricades to stop them. The mob pelted the police with stones and tried to remove the barricades, to which the police responded by firing tear gas shells. Witnesses also claim that the police fired at the crowd, injuring one protester.
Security forces carried out operations in the Razmak-Makin axis, killing four terrorists and arresting one from the areas of Tauda China Khula and Fort Knoll.
Protesters blocked the road by burning tyres.
Another bomb exploded in the city but no loss of life or property occurred.
A man and a woman were killed in the the Haji Ubedullah village on the pretext of Karo-kari by the woman's husband.

Zakir Hussain was targeted by two men on a motorbike who stopped infront of shop and fired at him, killing him on the spot. This was the second sectarian killing in as many days. The Jafria Alliance Pakistan criticised the government for not taking any action to stop targeted killings in Karachi.
The Bomb disposal squad defused an explosive device planted outside a mosque. According to officials, MNA Usman Tarakai and MPA Javed Tarakai were the target of the sabotage attempt.

A congregation of Zikrees, a small sect Muslims, was attacked with a bomb. The assailants tossed the bomb at the congregation and the explosion left at least 8 people, including 3 policemen, injured. Tension regarding the activites of this sect had increased recently with some groups calling for a ban on the former's congregations.
The JUI-F rally started form Chowk Bazaar's Masjid Wali Muhammad and ended near Ghanta Ghar Chowk. The participants chanted anti-US slogans and burnt US flags as well as an effigy of President Bush.
the Taliban killed a junior officer of the Khasadar force after his abduction earlier this month. A chit was found on the body that stated that he was killed for spying on Taliban for the US forces.
Police opened fire at a tribesman who 'aroused suspicion of the police' and then did not stop when the latter signaled him to. Three people were injured.
A watchman shot dead the alleged paramour of his wife and injured his wife for having illicit relations.

Three people were injured in a bomb blast in the parking lot of the Lady Reading Hospital. The bomb also damaged three vehicles and shattered the windowpanes of cardiology ward. Police claimed it was a gas cylinder that caused the balst but failed to show the remains of the cylinder.

Enraged protesters took to the streets after the assassination of two religious scholars. They protested violently heading towards Soldier bazaar, Jamshed Road, Liaquatabad, and Nazimabad and blocked roads by burning tyres and pelting vehicles with stones. Two shops, a bank and a bakery were set on fire and looted located near the place where the killings took place. A man was shot and injured on Lasbela roundabout; and the protesters attacked press photographers near Guru mandir, smashing their cameras. A heavy contingent of police was deployed in the surrounding areas.
According to reports, 6 people were killed and 5 others were injured in Tiarza.
In bareech Market area on Sirki Road, two people were killed and another injured. A police officer termed it a case of target killing.
A bomb was hurled at a police vehicle in Essa Nagri, but the explosion did not cause any damage. No other information was given.
The bullet-riddled body of a young man was found outside Ali Imambargah.

Security forces arrested nine suspected militants during a search operation in Darra Adam Khel. The forces seized weapons in a raid from arms factory, which had allegedly been supplying weapons to militants. The factory owner's nephew was killed in the raid when he tried to flee from being arrested.

A teacher of Baddomalhi School, Master Mohammad Asif, was shot dead outside his house while his father, who was also a teacher, received bullet injuries. The victims had woken up when they heard intruders and were shot at when they came out to investigate.

A rally held by the All Pakistan Clerks Association (APCA) was stopped from reaching the Chief Ministers House by the police who used teargas to disperse the protesters. The APCA, which was demanding the payment of one month's salaries to government officials of Balochistan amongst other demands, had been warned against demonstrating in front of the CM House. The police claimed that the protesters hurled stones at the police, forcing them to retaliate with tear gas shelling.
a soldier of the Mohmand Rifles was killed and 2 others were wounded in an attack by militants on the Derwazgai checkpost.
Five persons were injured when two groups of the Phulpoto clan clashed.

a former Nazim of Peshtakhara union council Riaz Khan was shot dead outside Peshawar Central Prison while he was going home. The killing was over some old dispute between 2 parties led by Ghani and Sandal Khan. He was killed when the rival group opened fire on them.
The Jihad Defence Forum comprising of wight Jihadi organisations announced that they will join the Jihad in Afghanistan in case of an American attack on it.

A group of unruly youths set a bus on fire on Mohammad Bin Qasim Road in the Arambagh area during  a strike in the areas of Liaquatabad and Orangi, in protest of the killings carried out in the areas.

Bahawal Sher and Shahmand murdered their sister Ghulam Fatima with spades in a bid to grab her 72 canals agricultural land. The accused threw her body in a well and made it look like an accident, but post-mortem results showed she was murdered, after which the accused were arrested.

Following the death of an MQM worker, firing contunied during the day and 3 vehicles were set on fire. The MQM worker, Imran Qazi, was killed after a scuffle in a cricket match between two groups of young men where some people opened fire.

Fifteen militants were killed and seventeen others were injured when security forces launched an offensive operation in the Zangi, Dogar Tarali and Marghan areas of Kurram. Security forces faced stuff resistance from militants and four soldiers were killed while 12 others were injured.

The Local District Bar Association burnt an effigy of MQM chief Altaf Hussain for using foul language against the legal fraternity. The lawyers gathered outside the bar premises where they had setup a hunger strike campagain against the government for not establishing a High Court bench in the district. The bar members insisted that they register a case against Altaf Hussain.
security forces targeted a suspected suicide car in the Gagra area.
following the killing of the baloch nationalist leaders violence erupted in Balochistan. a mob entered the office of the district nazim and ransacked it.

Violent protesters burnt the Gulistan Cinema, They also blocked National Highway by burning tyres at several places on the Highway. Protesters attacked the Quaidabad police station and Police and Rangers fired teargas shells to disperse the mob. There were several people injured, one police van, two petrol stations and a cinema were damaged.

During the strike called by Muttahida Qaumi Movement and Jiye Sindh Qaumi Mahaz, there were certain incidents of firecrackers exploding in some areas. However, the majority of the strike was peaceful. The strike was called to protest against police action and against the water shortage in the province.
As part of the violence on the second day of a two-day strike called by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM), unidentified pedestrian was killed in a crossfire near Farooq Masjid.

The Alliance for the Restoration of Democracy tried to gather and protest on May Day, however most efforts were foiled by the police. In Lyari, PPP workers clashed with the police. The police baton charged them and resorted to aerial firing.

A 40 year old workers of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement, the father of two, was gunned down. Shahaab Raza Haider, a former unit-in-charge of Unit 179 and worker of Unit 173 , was sitting in a chair outside his car wash service station near Anjuman Islamia Market when two unidentified motorcyclists opened fire on him. Witnesses said that victim, who was also a former assistant sub-inspector of the Sindh police, died on the spot.
troops attacked suspected militant hideouts in Tiligram and killed 14 terrorists.
Protesters, that included traders that had closed their shops, burnt tyres and raised slogans against Hesco for prolonged power outages.

Three people were killed in a clash between two rival groups in a village near Hasilpur, Bahawalpur when men armed with guns and clubs, belonging to the Bud clan, attacked the other clan's house in the Khairo Deh village. Sources said that that both clans had developed a feud and this violence was in continuation of that.
An ex-armyman was tortured by the police during a raid.He was taken to the police station and tortured again till he died.
Edhi Highway Centre, Gujrat, in-charge Mubarak Husain Gulshad had a narrow escape when some unidentified men fired at him while he was asleep in his house. The motive behind the attack in not known.
The decomposed body of a youth was recovered from a field near Rachna Town. The victim was identified as Khalid, and there were several stab wounds on his body.

Ismatullah Sharif, the elder brother of PML MPA Muhamad Afzal Sahi, was killed by some unidentifed armed people when he was asleep in his Haveli. Police sources said the Sahi family had rivalries with some other parties of the area.
at least 19 rockets were fired on FC checkpost in Chashma, Loti, Pir Koh and Sangsilla areas of Dera Bugti. However no casualties were reported in the attack.
A powerful explosive device that was planted on the wall of a police post went off, damaging property. However, no loss of life or injury was reported.
Roshan Ali Shaikh and Razul, wife of Abdul Hakeem Shaikh, were stabbed to death by their cousin, Waheed Ahmed Shaikh, in the name of karo-kari. He then surrendered himself to the area police.
According to reports, militants attacked the checkpost in Ormegi area, a gunbattle ensued leaving eleven militants and one soldier dead while four soldiers and six militants were injured.
At least five policemen were injured when a home made bomb went off on the Sawal Dher road. It may also be noted that the area is notorious for attacks on the security forces.

As part of the protest against the police raid on Khidmat-i-Khalq of MQM, some protesters burnt the post office near Raja ki kothi, Shaheed Umaid Ali Kaimkhani office in Unit 4, two hilux-pick-ups and the sub division Wapda office in Affandi town.

Thousands of villagers of Gangapur set on fire Buchiana police post and reduced it to ashes  to protest against the inefficiency of police in arresting the four dacoits responsible for killing a retired havaldar.

Bomb disposal squad defused a time bomb that was otherwise due to exlode at a time when the area is normally occupied by women shoppers. A watchman had spotted the suspicious shopping bag and alerted the police.
the police recovered the body of a PML-N women wing's Sahiwal President, Mrs. Gulzar Qamar, from the bank of the canal near Kinaan Park. She had gone missing 2 days ago.
two rival groups of the Bugti tribe exchanged fire in the area over a land dispute. There were no casualties
Eight mortar and rocket shells were fired from the Afghanistan side into Angor Adda tribal region. One of the shells hit a bunker, which resulted in injuries to a soldier.
Vehicles carrying activists of MQM to a public meeting organised by MQM were pelted with stones and at Patel Para and Orangi Town. Several workers were injured.
A girl 'K' was allegedly strangled by her brother for her bad character. She had eloped with a youth and later recovered through a panchayat. Her brother then killed her.
A young man shot dead in his house by four unidentified men,after they barged into the house.The attackers managed to escape.
Another device went off at the fish harbour causing panic among sleeping fishermen however no loss of life or injury was reported.

Police resorted to teargassing to disperse some demonstrators on The Mall following a funeral prayer of the people killed in an early violent demonstration. The police had killed a few people in connection to an earlier demonstration. The demonstrators chanted slogans against the government for killing 'innocent and peaceful' protesters.
7 unidentified armd men opened fire at a factory staff bus carrying about 50 factory employees, killing the driver and injuring 11 others. Soucres claimed that the attackers were Afghan refugess.
On 15-Oct-10, several activists of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF) attacked and opened fire on members of the rival Islami Jamiat-i-Tulaba (IJT), injuring two IJT activists.

Indian and Pakistani paramilitary troops traded heavy fire along the LoC after a 48 hour lul, but no casualty was reported. Indian and Pakistani authorities blamed each other for the fighting. Indian officials claimed the Pakistani Rangers began shooting after suspecting Indian authorities of laying a fence along the winding border of occupied Kashmir. The Pakistani officials said that the BSF (Border Security Force) opened unprovoked firing , and that the Indians also tried to violate the status of the working boundary in Kashmir.
4 men fired on Allah Noor.
One person was killed by four villagers over a land dispute.
Security forces continued to pound militants hideouts in Matta tehsil.
Unknown gunmen targeted construction workers, killing two and injuring 1. All the victims belonged to the Hazara tribe.
An elderly man was found butchered at his green town house on Saturday. He was alone in house and his family went to Khanewal to celebrate eid

Militants continued attacks on the cantonement and city areas of Kohat for the second consecutive day. Militants fired rockets at an ammunition depot of the security forces from the Bezote area but the rocket missed its target and exploded in a pond in Sheikhan.
3 people were killed and 3 were injured due to Indian shelling across LoC in Neelum valley on Sunday
One Mazhar Hussain along with his friend Nazar Husain of village Chuttan, murdered his wife suspecting her chastity.
A Shia leader, Syed Asad Ali Raza Abidi, was shot dead by 4 gunmen at an Imambargah Gulistan-i-Marfat on College road. The killing was the outcome of a rivalrty between two shia groups.
A Lashkar-i-Islami supporters was killed and another injured near Anjari Khwar in Bara, in an attack by supporters of the rival, Ansar ul Islam, group.

2 groups of student of the Karakoram International University clashed over a petty dispute promting administration to call the police and control the situation. The police had to fire tear-gas shells to disperse the students.

more than 2000 prisoners of the district jail burnt the official record and demolished mud walls of the wards and climed on top of the barracks, in protest against the alleged torture of 4 prisoners by the jail staff. The prisoners also tortured a few constables. the police shelled tear gas, but it intensified the protest.

At least 5 passengers were injured when a bomb planted on Indus Highway exploded. The passengers were travelling to Kohat from Peshawar. Militants also fired 14 rockets at different areas in Darra Adamkhel but no losses were reported.

3 people were killed and 18 others were injured, 8 of whom were policemen, in a clash between the Bengali Para residents and the police. The residents had assembled outside the Ibrahim Hyderi police station to protest against the arrest of some members of the locality and demand their release. around 400 people ransacked the police office and broke the windscreen of the parked police van. the police lobbed tear-gas and both sides clashed. the police said that no clash had taken place. police said the Bengalis had kidnapped three people and when they received this information they went to the colony they found the bodies.
Armed men on a pick-up shot at children playing outside their school, wounding 4 of them, and drove off. The wounded children belonged to the Turi Alizai tribesmen.
A murder accused was tortured to death by the police .

A top militant leader and his seven accomplices were captured after an exchange of fire between the security forces and militants in the Spin Thall area of Hangu after militants opened fire on a convoy patrolling the area.

During a protest demosntration the Iranian Cultural Centre on the Mall was set ablaze by activists of the SSP who had gathered for the funeral prayers of their chief Maulana Ziaur Rehman Farooqi who was killed in a bomb blast the day before. An MCL fire fighting squad was turned back after they were pelted with stones. Law firms situated in the same building were also gutted.
One student was injured when MSF members attacked a group of ATI students and a clash ensued. The police arrested several activists.
Residents of Taxila and businessmen burnt tyres and placed heavy stones to block the road to protest against prolonged power outages.

Unidentified people opened fire at a car, killing one person and wounding the other. The injured victim was Dawood Khan Wazir, who was a provincial council member of the ANP, and the deceased was his brother Irfan Khan Wazir.

Mureed Khan Bugti, a close aide too Brahamdagh Bugti, a member of the central executive committee of Balocj Republican Party was shot dead in Mari Jalbani village, when they were attacked by three men while in the latters house. The police said the incident seemed to be linked to an old enmity.

An organization of the Sheikhmalkhel tribe in Bara, thrashed and jailed a journalist for misreporting the activities of the organization. The journalist who belongs to the same tribe was on official duty when he was picked up and severly beaten before being put in a private jail.

Shahzad Raza was intercepted by two men on a motorbike and shot dead. The victim's elder brother had been targeted in a similar fashion earlier in the month and the Jafaria Alliance Pakistan claimed that both incidents were part of a new series of sectarian target killings.
Unidentified men shot dead Haji Nawab in T & T Colony. Haji Nawab was a resident of Bilal Colony.
a taxi driver, Mohammad Nasir, was killed by unidentified people in in Patana.
A woman was killed by her brother and husband for on suspicion of loose morals.
A police officer's bullet-riddled body was found from the Saeedabad police area.
Five more civilians were killed and sixteen were injured in the Indian firing along various sectors across LoC.

The bullet-riddled body of a young man was found from the Mowach Goth area. According to officials, the body may have been lying there for two days. The victim was blindfolded and received a single bullet-wound to the head.

Violence, which erupted after the killing of two MQM-H activists, continued with rival political groups trading fire and property being damaged. A Pakistan Steel bus was set on fire, while another bus was later set ablaze as well. A 15-year-old boy received bullet injuries due to gunfire in Korangi's Labour Square area.

A rocket fired from the West of Quetta landed on the White Road behind Governor's House, causing panic in the area. It was a 107mm rocket. No loss of life oroperty was however reported. No one claimed responsibility for the attack.
Chief of Jogezai tribe and a leader of PAMP was injured along with his driver in an armed attack on his vehicle by unidentified men.

Six rockets were fired on the Larkana Sugar Mills, damaging its boiler and other structures. The heavy exchange of fire between the attackers and the guards on duty was followed by the attack which created panic in the mill and its residential colony. A bullet also hit the vehicle of Resident Director of the mill, during the exchange of fire, but he escaped the attack.
a bomb exploded in Gwadar, smashing window-panes of houses on the hospital road. No casualties were however reported.
Hafiz Syed Hassan, who was an SSP activist was shot dead by assailants who entered his house/clinic, posing as patients, and opened fire at him.
A tehsil coucillor died of injuries sustained in an acid attack by her husband

following the kidnapping and murder of an ANP activist, Shahrukh, violence erupted in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. 8 cars and an NLC water tanker were set on fire by enraged protesters who smashed the windows of cars parked outside the apartments. The police did nothing. other activists of the ANP took to the streets pelting stones at passing vehicles and setting fire to them. Shahrukh's body was eventually found on Sunday morning.
At least one person was killed and five others were injured in the Indian shelling on the Abbaspur sector of Poonch district.
The body of an unidentified man was found stuffed in a sack in Saeedabad. The victim was reportedly tortured and 'throttled' and his hands and feet were tied when his body was found.
Four security personnel were killed and one was injured when a landmine exploded in Pir Koh gas field area in Dera bugti.

Agha Abid Shirazee was shot and killed by an armed man on a motorcycle while he was travelling in his car. Jafria Alliance Pakistan (JAP) condemned the killing and the police suspected that it was done on sectarian grounds.
Two rockets were fired on the couts camp by militants. Residents reported that the rockets missed the target and hit two houses near the camp.

Two landowners, Ali Muhammad Kamoka and Ali Ahmed Chadder, were killed and their driver was injured when unidentified men ambushed their car and opened fire at them. The victims were on their way back after appearing in court.
A person named Kamran Khan was gunned down by unknown men in Nasirpur on Tuesday.
Three Jagiranis were traveling by motorcycle when some people traveling in a car opened fire, killing them. Reportedly due to ongoing clashes between the Jagiranis and Solangis.

activists belonging to the student wing of a political organization SPSF barged into the office of the Ghulam Mohammad Maher Medical College principal and vandalized the place, on the plea that Professor Hafeezullah had adopted a discriminatory attitude with their comrade to fail him in examinations. the situation was brought under control after negotiations with the students.

Nasirabad police station came under attack when people of the Kalhora community got irked by the police handling of some people they arrested. The police had  summoned a certain Nawaz Ali Kalhoro who was the vice president of Sindh National Alliance, and Ayaz Ali of Wadho Kalhoro village on the complaint of a certain Dr. Bhemandas who alleged that Nawaz Ali Kalhoro wasn't handing over the produce of 72 acres of land to him. The accused argued with the police, at which the police beat up the arrested. This angered the residents of Kalhoro village, who pelted the police station with stones. The police had to resort to baton charge and tear gas shelling to disperse the crowd.

A local leader of the ANP and of the Badhber Qaumi Lashkar narrowly escaped when a roadside bomb exploded along the side of the road. However, another vehicle passing through the areas was damaged and the driver received minor injuries.
A blast derailed three bogies and the engine of the train near Tangwani on Tuesday. 15 people were injured.

Protestors damaged six buses and injured two drivers to protest agaisnt the death of a man who was run over by a bus belonging to a local transport company. They blocked the road for three hours and intercepted every bus that passed through the area. The police baton charged the crowd to bring the situation under control.
The body of an unidentified person was found in Shafiqabad area on Monday

Suspected militants fired rockets on an army post. Senior government officials said it was too early to draw any link between the rocket attack in the Kurram Agency and the ongoing operation in South Waziristan.
A constable was killed in North Nazimabad while he was on his motorcycle.
An expatriate was found murdered in his house with multiple stab wounds and head injuries. Police could not determine whether any valuables were missing or not.
During exchange of fire between the security forces and militants while a search operation was underway, a taliban leader and four other accomplices were killed.

Clashes erupted between tribes from Balishkhel and Sadda. This happened after a funeral ceremony was attacked. Rockets were also fired at Shalozan, Bughdai and Luqmankhel areas near the Afghan Border. Local people claimed that militants that had relocated from Waziristan and other militancy-hit areas were behind the initial attacks. (See Note)
A young man was shot and killed in Ittehad town in Baldia when gunmen targetted him on a motorcycle.

Four people, including two MQM (Haqiqi) activists, one MQM (Altaf) and one pedestrian, were killed during in a clash between the two Mohajir Qaumi Movement groups in Asif Colony, when Haqiqi workers were fired upon in Asif Colony who in turn retaliated.
The Afghan army fired several rockets on a border post of the Pakistani army. The attack triggered skirmishes and the two sides exchanged fire.

Three PPP activists, Usman, Younis and Babu, were shot at by unidentified men on a motorcycle. Two of them died on the spot while the third was taken to a hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. Dozens of PPP workers took the bodies with them and staged a sit-in in front of the Chief Minister's house. they demanded a case a to be registered against the 'provincial goverment's coalition partner' .

Punjab Professors and Lecturers Association, FC College arranged a protest meeting and flayed the government's move to returnt he college to the Presbyterian Church. Some of the protesting students clashed with the police deployed at the gate leaving eight injured. The students claimed that the police had stopped them from entering the college and had resorted to baton-charge. However, the police stated that the students had broken a windshield and had to be stopped.
An eighty year old woman was hit by a stray bullet and killed while she was cleaning her veranda in Kalakot.

A truck carrying 150-180 Kg of explosives blew up outside a police station. Tehrik-i-Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack saying the group had decided to resume attacks after laying low since their amir's (Baitullah Mehsud) killing last month. Followup: The death toll of the blast rose to 15 as five more bodies were retrieved from the debris.
Twin pipelines of the Sui Southern Gas Comapny were damaged by an explosion.  The blast was similar to ones that have taken place recently for which the SLA claimed responsibilty.
An angry mob attacked houses in Christian Town, on rumors that Christian's living there had desecrated the Kalma. The police intervened and arrested three people.
Militants used IEDs to blow up a school in Mohmand Agency
A boy was killed and two others were wounded in Indian shelling in the Hajira sector, Poonch from across the LoC.

security forces have launched a ground offensive in the towns and cities of Swat. security personnel were engaging militants in Kanju town. An operation was under way in Takhtaband, where seven combatants had been killed in a clash and the body of militant `commander` Malanga was lying with the security forces.

The relatives of a victim of a \fake encounter\" staged a protest against the Khudian police. They were accompanied by a large number of villagers who blocked Allahabad Road for 6 hours, burnt tyres and raised slogans against the police. The police resorted to teargas shelling, baton-charge and aerial firing but the demonstrators only dispersed when SP Waqas Hussain assured them that a case would be registered against the accused policemen. "
Arsonists set on fire seven public and private vehicles and the Allied Bank's Frere Road branch while sporadic gunfire also took place.
Scattered incidents of firing continued in the strife-hit areas of Karachi as two bodies were found stuffed in gunny bags off the Northern Bypass. Both men had been shot in the head.

Thousands of teachers protested against the denationalization of government schools. They blocked the main road ans as a result were baton-charged by the police. Several teachers were injured and over 250 were arrested.

unidentified men attacked a jirga that was going on between the Wazir and the Khuidadkhel tribes in Kurram, killing 1 and injuring 5 others while an elder, Sher Khan, was kidnapped. The reason for the attack could not be ascertained.
A resident of Kandhar allegedly strangled his wife suspecting that his wife had been maintaining illicit relations with a man of the area.
Militants attacked Mamokhawara checkpost. The security forces also fired at the militants. The military also came to the help of te FC personnel and opened artillery fire on the militants.
A bomb was discovered at the Lahore residence of Gujranawala Deputy Inspector General. The bomb disposal squad was able to defuse it in time.
Two people were killed and two others were injured in a clash between two groups over a piece of land in Deepalpur on Monday
A woman was injured in a bomb blast took place in the train when it reached near Chughalpura on Thursday.
A powerful blast took place close to a tile factory owned by Mohammad Manzoor. It was a home-made time bomb. No one claimed responsibility for the attack.
Two US drones fired 4 missiles that targeted a house used by militants. 6 militants were killed.
A boy shot dead his married sister whom he suspected had illicit relations with another man. He opened fire on her for her bad character and she died on the way to the hospital.
Two armed motorcyclists opened fire at 2 SSP workers who were on their way back from a conference. The SSP men were injured but managed to overpower the assailants and hand them over to the police.
An unidentified body was found near Nairang Cinema in the jurisdiction of the Liaquatabad police station.
Three people were injured in firing by unidentified gunmen.
The headles body of young man was found from Ibrahim haideri.
A minor girl was killed in the shelling by Indian armymen on villages in the Shakargarh-Narowal sectors.
Two groups of Chandio tribe clashed over a land dispute in Karimdad Chandio village. 3 were killed and 8 injured during the clash.
A man shot his sister because she wanted to remarry. The accused later shot himself and died on the spot.

Malik Tariq, a former member of Khidmat Committee, was supporting the candidates of Aashiq Dayal group in the local polls. According to Afzal (a Dayal group candidate for councilor) the rival Jat group sought Tariq's help but he refused. Then as Tariq and a few others were returning after canvassing, 5 armed men targeted him and opened fire on him and killed him.
A woman and her child were brutally slaughtered by unknown men near Salar Village on Thursday

Ms Gulzadi, who was declared 'kari' by a local jirga after she left her home to marry a man of her choice. She had returned home after her parents agreed to 'solemnize' her marriage. However when she returned they organized a jirga that declared her 'kari' and proceeded to 'sign her death warrant'. The order was carried out and her body was burried at an unknown location. Since the incident, male members of the Khoso community have gone into hiding.

Demonstrators from different political parties attacked two trains because they felt they were not obseving a complete wheel-jam strike to express solidarity with the Kashmiris. The police came to intervene but was pelted with stones.
a car was set ablaze in Landhi

According to sources, over a dozen militants fired nine rockets and mortar shells at the Saro Killi police station in Shabqadar area of Charsadda causing damage to the boundary wall. The exchange of fire between militants and troops continued for a few hours.

Some unidentified outlaws threw explosive material on the residence of Haji Munawar Ali Abbasi, former Sindh minister for local bodies. No casualties were caused, but the explosives damaged the windows of the house and created panic at the site. The miscreants escaped on a motorcyle.
Ten people of a family were gunned down and 12 others injured when their relatives opened fire on them to avenge an old enmity. Both the families belonged to the Baloch tribe.
Two people were gunned down in, what was termed by the police, an incident of target killing. The BLA claimed responsibility for the attack.
Abdul Sattar, a welfare officer in Quetta, was shot dead by 6 armed men while he was waiting for the Bolan Mail.

Inreaction to the attempted assassination of the Shia leader earlier that day a Mob mobilized and burnt several government offices and private buildings including the house of the forest officer with the officer and other five members of the family trapped inside and burnt alive. The local health department chief was also shot and random shooting by the mob killed another man aswell.
Two people were killed and at least 16 were injured in the Indian shelling on Leepa valley from across the LoC.
a scavenger was injured when a toy bomb exploded near the Satellite Town in Quetta.

Muhammad Naeem Kakar was killed and six other injured in an exchange of fire between two rival groups in district courts Quetta where the two groups had come for a case hearing. Both the groups had old enmity which aprked the incident.

Ali Mardan, an employee of Pakistan Railway was shot dead by unidentified people on a motocycle in a high security zone where the US Consulate and the Chief Minister House are located. Police say that the motive behind the murder cannot be ascertained immediately.

Militants opened fire a security personnel during a search operation. Security personnel fired back, killing 3 militants. The search operation was started after security forces received a tip-off regarding the presence of militants in the area.
A powerful explosion rocked Pasni  when some unknown people planted a home-made bomb near the building of a TV booster.
A man and his neice were wounded in a shooting incident in the Gulberg area.
One Abdul Majid with five accomplices entered the house of Asghar Ali and shot his daughter dead. The former had an ongoing land dispute with the latter. The accused managed to escape.
A civilian was killed when Indian forces fired across the LoC at a political meeting called by a member of the Legislative Assembly.
Soon after the targeted killing of an MQM man, arson attacks took place in the Nazimabad area. A bus of 2-K route was set on fire at Habib Chowrangi.
an explosion took place in Cavalry Ground killing 1 boy. The bomb had been planted in a heap of garbage in an unoccupied residential plot. 3 people were injured.

The additional secretary of Muslim Students' Federation and his minor son were gunned down by two unidentified motorcyslists. The reason is stated to be the pursuance of a murder case by the vicitm against a political figure.
An MQM activist was shot dead by unidentified men in Oangi Town on Thursday.
Seven shops were damaged when a bomb went off in a hair-cutting salon in Darra Adam Khel.
Two brothers stabbed their sister to death because they had doubts about her modesty.
Villagers attacked a police party to get a villager freed from police custody. They beat up the policemen and fleed with the accused.

500 farmers staged a demonstration when a fertilizer dealer dispatched 600 urea bags for black marketing after his refusal to sell them to the farmers. Farmers in protest blocked the Raiwand road and also burnt tyres. The accused was arrested.
zahid Hussain was allegedly shot dead by five men over a trifle in Bahawalpur.
Unidentified men entered a mosque in the buffer zone area and opened fire at a Muezzin. One man was killed and 2 others suffered injuries.
A bomb exploded in the cinema. Injuring four people.

Enraged students gathered in Faisal Town set a Pakistan Telecommunication Limited van on fire in protest soon after it crushed and killed a student in Faisal Town. Some senior police officers negotiated with the protesters and assured them the culprit would be found, to which they dispersed without any further incident.
one person was killed and 2 others sustained injuries in a roadside landmine.
One person, Sher Muhammad, shot dead his sister Nooran alias Noori as she had allegedly eloped with her paramore Jafar Husain from Chak No 457 GB. Police registered a case against the accused.

A 40 year old factory watchman was found murdered in the factory. Preliminary investigations suggested tha he could have been strangled. It could not be determined who was behind the murder or what their reasons were.
A mother and her daughter were found dead in the fields of Ganghudher village.

A suspected woman suicide bomber blew herself up at a checkpoint in the high-security military cantonment area on Babar road. The police claim she may have been holding the bomb inher hand to plant it somewhere and it went off prematurely; Follow up: Police claim that the woman suspected to be a suicide bomber was not in fact so and that it was a remote controlled explosive device that was used in the attack.

Activists of PPP-SB took out a rally to demand the arrest of the killers of their leader Murtaza Bhutto. They marched through many roads before demonstrating in front of the Karachi Press Club, where they burnt an effigy of Asif Ali Zardari.
Armed men on a motorbike opened fire at a trailer carrying supplies to Nato forces in Afghanistan. The driver of the trailer was killed while another person on the trailer was injured.
three gas pipelines in Loti gas field area were blown up by explosives.

Maulana Azam Tariq, Chief of Millat-i-Islam and MNA, was assassinated and four others were killed when three unidentified gunmen intercepted them at the Golra toll plaza in the outskirts of the city and sprayed their car with bullets, killing them on the spot. Police officials termed the killing to be sectarian as the Maulana had received threats of sectarian nature previously and had also escaped attempts on his life before.
Some unknown people blocked the Panj Hatti Road of the town and burnt tyres in protest of the bombing of the Imambargah Ali Raza on 1-June-04
Ashraf and his wife Mehnaz was shot dead by unknown assailants in their house in Shahi Bazaar's Qadirpura Mohallah.
Some unidentified men attacked a Church and burnt copies of the Bible.

A jail official and seven prisoners were injured in a clash that erupted in Adiala jail when the jail staff tried to force feed the under-trial prisoners who had been on hunger strike for a day. Unrest had been brewing in the overcrowded jail for months over the allegations of torture and drug trafficking by the prisoners.
Two studnets were injured in a clash between two rival student groups over the hanging of banners in Sahiwal.
Some unidentified opened fire on a former coucillor outside his house.The attackers managed to escape.

missiles from a drone killed at least 3 people in Laddha subdivision when it hit a car iin Mudori area, dominated by the Mehsud tribe. Unofficial sources put the number of people killed at 5. Amir Mohammad Khan, an official of the Laddha administration said there was a training camp close to the area attacked.
The blood-stained body of a widow was found in her house in Kot Chutta. No other detail of the motive behind the murder or the party responsible was given.

Syed Tahir Nadeem, son of JUI (F) central leader (Allama Syed Abdul Majeed Nadeem) was found unconscious in Habib Colony. His head had been hit by a blunt weapon. No motive behind the incident was ascertained.
Police baton charged and arrested 24 people from two religious groups when they clashed over the possession of a mosque.
The body of a youn man was found with a bullet hole in Samnabad, Gulberg on Thursday.
Six Siyal tribespeople were injured in a clash between two groups of the tribe over a petty issue in village Jurial Siyal near Saghiyoon.
Two people were killed and four others were injured in unprovoked Indian firiing from across the LoC in Neelum Valley.
The security forces set the house of militant commander Tariq on fire. His house was used as a headquarter for Taliban during the Darra operation.
Six persons armed with rifles and guns opened fire in Goth Kero near the Indus Highway, killing one person and injuring another.
Six rockets fired by militants, that were apparently aimed at an army checkpoint, hit houses in a nearby vilage, killing 2 women and 2 children in addition to injuring 7 people.
A tribal elder and his son survived a road-side explosion when they were on their way to Khaar on their car. Malik Juma Gul was a prominent elder of the Mamond tribe

A pick up van with 4 militants fired kalashnikov shots in the air. The army troops tried to intercept the vehicle. The vehicle managed to pass through but passenger vehicles coming towards the checkpost were also hit, in which 11 civilians were killed and 6 injured. However, according to the ISPR spokesperson, 2-3 vehicles came towards a FC checkpost and started firing, the FC retaliated, in which there may have been a few civilian casualities who may possibly have been terrorists.

Two pro-government tribal elders were killed and another was injured when a bomb exploded in the Chaharmang area. Earlier this year, some unidentified people had attack one of the victims', Malik Hakeems', house, killing his close relative. The police speculated that the present attack was due to personal enemity too.
three children were wounded when a rocket fired by militants hit a residential area in Jadeedabad.
37 people were injured in a clash between Mandokhel and Abdullahzai tribe over a piece of land in Zhob area on Wednesday

Four people were killed and two others were injured in a clash between two rival groups in Kaaleyki-Phalora in Pasrur tehsil. There had been an old political enmity between the Ansari group and Patwari group. On Tuesday some people fron the Ansari group went to the haveli of Patwari group for reconciliation. Suddenly bothe groups infuriated on some isseu and Patwari group opened fire at their rivals killed four and injuring two others. The accused fled firing in the air.
A warehouse in Soldier Bazaar came under a hand-grenade attack that left two people wounded after, according to the police, its owner refused to agree with the terms of the extortionists.
3 people were injured in a bomb blast took place near Gambella Police Post on Friday.
2 sisters were killed and their brother was injured in Mohalla Sarbanan on Thursday when a hand grenade concealed in a bottle given to one of the girls by an anonymous person went off.

A clash occurred between farmers and irrigation officials as the farmers were protesting over the shortage of water supply to the Kobri Shakh as was promised by the officials. The police registered a case against 15 people.
A young man was injured in a firing incident.

Due to massive loadshedding, power riots erupted in the Rawalpindi region when farmers, traders and mechanics from nearby villages blocked the G.T. Road in Gujar Khan by burning tyres and chanting slogans against the PPP regime and President Asif Ai Zardari. Later, the mob, equipped with clubs, ransacked a nearby complaint office of Lesco and burnt it wooden furniture and destroyed gadgets by heaping them on the burning tyres. The office of SDO located in the vicinity of the grid station was also ransacked by a mob of over 300 youths. The SHO of Gujar Khan tried to negotiate with the protesters but they had no leader.
Six people were killed and four others injured in an armed clash over a disputed land between villagers belonging Nadrak and Mian Isa villages.

A clash between two groups at Shah Faisal Colony left at least 17 people wounded in incidents of sporadic firing. Witnesses said that the trouble started when a group of a political party returned to the locality with party workers who had allegedly been tortured by their rivals three days ago. They said the group opened fire when they saw their rivals, who returned fire. Later the armed groups took to the streets and resorted to heavy firing in the locality. Some vehicles and shops were also burnt down in the violence.
unidentified assailants murdered Noor Husain,the father of a prayer leader, Qari Fiaz Ahmed, in Dinga. The motive behind the kiling is unknown.
An Afghan national was killed when he struck a landmine in Gabrial, Bajaur. Details are not available.

Tehrik-i-Jafaria Pakistan workers took out a procession to protest against the killing of Fayyaz Haideri in police custody. Fayyaz was an activist of the TJP. The protestors marched towards the Mall, where they asked people to remove their vehicles from the road. They then pelted stones on some cars and smashed their windowpanes. The TJP workers also attacked some police jeeps at the GPO crossing and damaged a police car and an SGA&ID car.The police tried to stop the crowd by firing teargas shells. The crowd then resorted to aerial firing, and the police responded in kind.

According to official sources, the Chenab Rangers thwarted a major attempt to build a fence by the Indian Security Forces near the Sialkot working boundary. A pillar erected was also badly damaged in the exchange of fire.

Two oil tankers carrying jet fuel for US-led coalition forces in afghanistan caught fire and caused explosions causing damage to nearby property. Taliban have taken responsibility for blowing up the tankers as a warning to Pakistani drivers carrying fuel for US led forces.
An unidentified bullet-riddled body was found. Doctors claimed that the victim was 'brutally tortured'.

A bomb exploded near the residence of the provincial livestock minister in the railway housing society in Quetta. The bomb was planted on the wall of the Quaid public school, which was 15 yards away from the Provincial Livestock Minister Abdul Qadoos Bizenjo's residence.  Another bomb was found in the same locality but was defused. It is not known whether this was a terrorist attack, or an assassination attempt on the minister.
Abbas was shot dead by Irfan Chandia as Irfan suspected that Abbas had relations with his sister.
A watchman was shot dead outside a factory in Malir.
Security forces were patrolling the Bosaq area of Batkhela when militants attacked them. Four militants were killed in the exchange of fire that ensued.
Three members of a family including a teenage girl were shot dead in Kot Mubarak in Dera ghazi khan on Wednesday by the rival group
a man, Ajmal, was shot dead.
Two persons suffered injuries as a time device fitted in a Nato oil container blew up in Torkham, Khyber. There were other containers parked there, however, none were damaged in the attack.
Two tribal elders, Malak Shaheen and Syed Mohammad, were injured when a bomb exploded.

According to reports, the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Hyderabad was on his way to Hyderabad when his jeep was fired on by dacoits on the Bulri Shah Karim Road.  The guards returned fire and the dacoits retreated.  They had allegedly looted the passengers of a van on the same road earlier that day.
the people took out processions to express solidarity with Iraqi people and President Saddam. They burnt effigies of President Bush and demanded that the government support Saddam.
2 people were killed and one was injured when 5 armed persons opened indiscriminate fire in Karampur Village on Thursday.
Unidentified armed men shot and injured a lawyer, Mohammad Anwer, near Lalpur village.

At least fifteen people were killed and more than Thirty injured in a bomb blast in a gambling den of a densely populated area in Ghaas Mandi. There was blood and human flesh on the main road along the club and windscreens of vehicles parked outside were shattered. SP of the Special Investigations Unit was of the opinion that the way the blast was carried out and the kind of material used, it seemed like the work of militants. However, he claimed it premature to reach a conclusion immediately; Follow up: A suspect, belonging to the \Al Mukhtar Group\", an unknown militant outfit, was arrested in connection to the club bombing."
Terrorists reportedly kidnapped a young man and killed him in the Orangi area.
A police inspector, Khurram Saeed, sustained injuries while his wife was shot dead when unidentified assailants shot at his car. The motive behind the attack was unknown.
Three suspects were held for an attempt on the life of Imamia Students' Organization's (a Shia Student Group) leader.
a woman, Safeeat Khatoon, was killed by her father on the pre-text of karo-kari in Wali Mohammad village.
The body of a man was found from Nayabad Lyari with a bullet in his head.

A tribal journalist, Nasrullah Afridi, was killed when a bomb fitted in his car exploded. The victim was 'not in the good books' of Lashkar-i-Islam and some people had hurled hand grenades at his house in Hayatabad in 2007. Afridi was a correspondent of Pakistan Television and the Urdu Daily Mashriq.
Indian forces did shelling along the Sialkot working boundary in Sucheetgarh sector, Chaprar, Bajwat, Charwa, Bajragarhi and Harpal Sectors on Thursday. However no casuality was reported.
A man was called out of his house and shot dead in Orangi Town. His political affiliation could not be known.
a man was shot dead by 2 unidentified assailants near the railway godowns.

A number of CD shops were damaged in an explosion at the Karim Manzil when an explosive device planted near the gate of a shop went off. The blast was heard far off and the pieces of the device were taken in by the police for investigation.
The bullet-ridden bodies of two policemen were found in an abandoned area. The two had been reported missing a couple of nights prior to this event.
The partially decomposed body of an unidentified man was found in Gulzar-i-Hijri.

A man shot dead his younger brother over a property issue in village 694-R, Kasrian. Reports said that the brother's father had given the three acre land to the younger brother, upon which the older brother shot dead the younger one.
A person was shot dead by unidentified assailant at Nila Gumbad cycle shop on Thursday.
Security personnel were conducting a search operation in Sangsilla area of Dera Bugti when some militants opened fire on them. The security forces retaliated killing one militant.
The body of a taxi driver, Dilwar, was found. His taxi was recovered from Banda Syedan village.

A headless and decomposed body of a woman was found in the storage tank. The police cannot ascertain the time of death as the body was really decomposed. There was no autopsy done on the body and it was sent straight to the morgue.
A bullet-riddled body of a woman was found with torture marks from behind Datanagar hillocks in Orangi Town.

Following the assassination of Maulana Yousuf Ludhianvi, the office of English Daily along with a branch of Muslim Commercial Bank were set on fire in the vicinity of Banori Town mosque on Thursday. The vehicles parked outside the office were also either damaged or set ablazed. Another  branch of a bank named Allied Bank of Pakistan at a distance of 50 yardswas looted.

A minor dispute between two student groups, both enjoying support of political parties in the ruling coalition, turning into an armed clash. The clash led to a suspension of activities on campus and spread panic in the area.
An MQM (Afaq) group member was killed ny unidentified attackers
Dil Mohammad was allegedly shot dead by 5 armed men over a land dispute.

Activists of the ANP attacked workers of a Sindhi nationalist party who were overseeing construction of a wall on plot. The cause behind the incident was an old land dispute between the two political groups. 1 person was killed while 4 were injured. Another clash took place between the two groups at the same spot later during the same day which led another member of the Sindhi party being killed. Intermittent firing was reported from the area after the clashes.

An exlosion took place at a government-run girls' school which caused damaged to the school building and houses nearby. Six month prior to the blast, the bomb disposal unit had defused a bomb at the same school.
Rally by around 50 PPP workers to mark International Women's Day resulted in scuffle with baton-wielding police when they tried to make their way to the Governor's House.
A youth was shot dead by 3 armed men over an alleged rivalry

During the fourth phase of local body elections, two men- belonging to the Raja Basharat  group- were injured in a clash with supporters of Awam Dost group outside the polling station. According to Raja Basharat, Raja Tariq Kiani- President of the Rawalpindi Chamber of Commerce and Industry- was responsible for the incident.

The school students of Katlang, resorted to public protest when asked to pay the newly imposed tuition fee. The provincial government had introduced fees in the higher and secondary schools which the students resented. They turned violent and started pelting stones on vehicles and the police party. They also severely damaged offices of Wapda and other buildings. Afterwards the also clashed with the police, who resorted to baton charge  and tear gas shelling. The angry students also brielfy held the resident magistrate, who was later allowed to go after negotiations.

The Pak-Afghan Defence Council called a strike in protest against the US-led attacks on Afghanistan. A protest procession of several hundred was passing the Nazimabad petrol pump when the police and Rangers lobbed teargas shells at them. According to the police, the miscreants were trying to damage the petrol pump. This led to a clash between the protesters and the police. The protesters fired at the police who returned the fire. During the clash, there was a loud explosion as well, but it was uncertain as to whether it was a firecracker or a bomb. At least two people were injured in the clash. According to the Nazim of Liaquatabad Town, Dr. Pervaiz Mahmood, the law enforcement agencies were too hard on the protesters.

A police van carrying some on trial prisoners came under indiscriminate fire from unknwon assailants. The firing left 6 people, including 4 policemen, dead. The other two victims were under-trial prisoners.

Muhammad Boota was shot dead in Kheeranwali village by Arshad Aziz and Sajjad, while his friend Muhammad Iqbal was shot at and injured when they were going home. The cause behind the murder is not known.
Militants blew up two schools, a basic health unit and three houses. However, no casulaties were reported.
Four militants were killed while two by standers were injured when a US drone strike hit a car in the Shahzadkot area of North Waziristan.

Old worker of Muslim League and prominent social worker- Rana Mohammad Hussain Chandial- was murdered by three young men. According to the report, \he had forbidden the accused of his misdeeds\" which the accused took as an insult and killed him."

a man killed his daughter and attempted to kills his wife and 2 other daughters for honour in Mughalpura. He alleged that his wife and daughters were not enjoyinga good repute in the area. The neighbours caught the accused and handed him over to the police.

Sub-inspector Rustam Khan, accompanied by four constables and some other people, showed up at a disputed sugarcane weighing scale, and opened fire with his official gun at Younas Khan who was the vice-president of MSF in Jhang district. Younas Khan died on the spot. The two had already had a heated exchange of words at a Panchayat, which was trying to settle a dispute over the possession of a sugarcane weighing scale.

The body of an unidentified man was found stuffed in a gunny bag near Bori Shah Mazaar. The victim appeared to be in his 40s, and had died two days ago. The motive behind the murder could not be ascertained.
Two policemen were shot dead by unknown assailants on jan Muhammad road
A Frontier Constabulary jawan, Samiullah, was killed after his vehicle was attacked by a rocket as him and 4 other FC men were on their way to Sui from Jaferabad District.
A Nato oil tanker was destroyed on Ring Road in Peshawar by militants. Some people had planted explosives on the rear end of the vehicle. After the blast, the tanker fell into a ravine.
Six people, including two women, were wounded in heavy firing in New Karachi.
An elderly man was chopped to pieces and his body was dumped in the Urdu bazaar area by unknown persons.
An unidentified person attacked a bakery with a grenade injuring the bakery owner and a customer.
A bullet-riddled body of a man was found near Sunny Civic centre in Korangi town.

A student was killed while another was injured in a clash between two rival student groups in the Allama Iqbal College Ground. A couple of students belonging to the People's Students Federation were sitting in the college lawns when members of the Anjuman-Talaba Islam came there and allegedly opened fire on them. Seven students had been named in the FIR.
Sakina, a 16-year old girl was gunned down by an unidentified person.

A large number of people, including shopkeepers and Nazims, held a demonstration in Khairpur Nathan Shah to protest against the tehsil municipal administration for not paying attention to the problems of the citizens. They blocked the Indus Highway and burnt tryes on the road to press their demands.
It was alleged that a sepoy of Khyber Rifles shot and killed a tribesman shah Hussein Afridi.
