an officer of the provencial agricultural department, Ayaz Bungash, was shot dead by four assailants near the Sariab Mills. The accused escaped. A police officer described it as a sectarian incident.
A man was axed to death by a father, and his accomplices, of a girl whom he allegedly had illicit relations with in Toba-Tek_Singh.
Security forces secured Tighak Banda and Gakhe Banda area. Two soldiers were injured during an exchange of fire in Pir Patai ridge.
A Christian woman was shot deadb y her husband on suspicion of having an affair.
one civilian was killed and 2 others were injured when militants fired 2 rockets at Bannu city.

Car of Maulana Sibghatullah, a pro-government cleric, was ambushed with gunfires at Laddah . The cleric wa associated with Taliban in the past but during the unrest in the agency he dissociated himself from the group and entered into an agreement with the government.
Three pesons were dead and 5 got injured in Indian shelling across LoC in neelum valley on Thursday
masked men opened fire on a barber's shop killing 2 men and Ishaq Khan who was the nephew of a tribal elder Mirazalam Khan who had been killed a while back.
A bomb blast occurred at Peshawar University Campus on Saturday. However no loss of life was reported.

Haji Asmatullah Khan Mehsood, president of the Sindh chapter of the ANP, claimed that the party president of central Karachi, Niaz Muhammad, was shot and injured by policemen. Allegedly, an SHO came to his house and requested him to advise his party workers to remain peaceful. After this, when Niaz Muhammad was leaving his house some policemen shot and injured him.

Supporters of the IJT and APMSO clashed and exchanged fire after they failed to resolve an issue surrounding a 'talent show' that was scheduled to be organized by the APMSO on campus. The police entered college premises and arrested 4 students.
In Khanpur Maher, 25 year old Mehran was shot dead by some unidentified armed men. Mehran's body was recovered from a nearby field.

Residents of Lallian were protesting against the non-availability of electricity in their town. Approximately 300 people blocked the road and the Levies opened fire on them. This resulted in several people being injured.
A Lahore-bound train was fired at, damaging the train and injuring the driver.

More than 2000 armed members of the Qaiserani tribe exchanged fire with FC personnel, causing injuries to several people from both sides. The clash came after the tribesmen had taken positions on the hills along the road leading the Dhodhak Oil and Gas Field and pressed for the acceptance of their demands, which included provision of jobs to the local tribemen, supply of natural gas to adjacent areas etc.
A dentist, Mohammed Iqbal, was riding on a motorcyle on his way home when he was shot and killed by unidentified armed men.
Following the stabbing of a trader, Muhammad Salim, in a mini-cinema, traders of scrap market observed a strike to protest the killing and demanded the closure of all mini-cinemas in the city.

At least nine people were killed and 41 others, including seven policemen, were injured when five rockets, fired by militants, hit heavily-populated parts of Bannu. At least five rockets, fired from different locations, hit two houses and a bookshop in the heart of the city. Police said that three rockets exploded, while two were defused. Most of the casualities occured in Chai bazaar, where people were conducting a rescue operation of a previous rocket attack when a rocket fell right in the middle of the crowd and exploded, killing 8 and injuring 40. The other rockets landed in Gohakhel locality and Rehamnia Kutubkhana.
1 child was killed and 14 people sustained injuries when security forces and militants exchanged fire after the militants attacked a security post in Tangoo Pul near Bajkatta village.
the city chief of the Shabab-i-Milli and worker of the Jamaat-i-Islami, Nazir Sajid were gunned down in an attack in Surjani Town.
2 people were killed and 2 were injured when the Rehman Dakait Group was attacked by the Arshad Pappu group.
Unidentified miscreants planted a bomb on the Kahan-Tartani road and blew it up while the vehicle of the security personnel was passing by. BLA claimed the responsibility of the attack.

The Indian Security Forces continued firing on Zafarwal, Charwa, Bajwat, Chaprar, Harpal, Sucheetgarh, Bajragarhi, Chhumb, Joriyan, Syedanwali, Jammu and Shakargarh sectors. As a result, the firing killed 4 animals, badly damaged 11 houses in Chhamb, Jorian and Bajwat sectors. The Chenab Rangers returned the fire.
Militants destroyed a girls school at Landi Kotal by planting an explosive device which detonated during the night. No one was reported killed or injured.
The Mansehra city police found a decomposed body of an unidentified man near Chikya road.
Armed men blew up a gas supply line, suspending supply from gas well No 74 field to the Sui purification plant.
Two boys were killed and three others were injured when unidentified men in a taxi opened fire in the Peerabad area in District West.
An activist of the Pakistan People's Party was shot dead in Surjani Town when two unknown gunmen opened fire on him.

Unidentified armed men dumped three bodies in Khajjir ground in the jurisdiction of Gulbahar police station. All three had their hands tied behind their backs and their political affiliation could not be known.
The joint incharge of Mutahida Qaumi Movement's unit no.38 was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in his shop.
Three women were going to the Fatwaal village with their parents when the Indian troops fired from across the LoC killing one of them and injuring two others.

A dispute arose at the central jail in Sahiwal when the jail employees tried to shift a prisoner to another block. The prisoners started rioting and pelting stones in anguish. A heavy police contingent reached the spot and fired tear gas on the prisoners. A prisoner died while 15 others sustained injuries when the police opened fire to quell the clash between prisoners and the jail staff. Follow up: 18 November Page 12: Two prisoners tortured to death in Kasur jail: Some prisoners were transferreed from Sahiwal to Kasur after the rioting incident. Now, two of the prisoners are tortured to death (Allegedly by the police) though no torture marks could be found on their bodies.
Unidentified armed men killed Imam Dino in his private residence. He is said to have been killed over karo-kari.

Some people lobbed a hand grenade on a police mobile, and the attack was followed by a heavy exchange of fire between militants and security forces. In the exchange of fire, a Mahsud tribesman was killed, and there were injuries to 7 other people.

Larkana and Shahdadkot observed shutter down strikes in protest against the deportation of the former prime minister Nawaz Sharif. Activists of the Sindh Tarraqi Pasand Party were arrested by the police when they were allegedly trying to force the shopkeepers to close their shops. The police baton charged them, injuring more than 6 people.
Following the strike call given by MQM steering committee, armed youths took to the streets and resorted to violence. A Hilux van was burnt in a school.
25-year-old Jamaluddin was shot dead while he was on his way home late at night.
25 armed tribesmen attacked a police station in Thatta and got away with four detenus on Monday who were arrested for homosexual assault.
A MQM (Altaf) activist who was also a dismissed constable was gunned down when unidentified men opened fire on him while he was outside a hotel in Liaquatabad.

a councillor-elect, Malik Ashraf, was beaten up when he tried to resist a kidnapping attempt by a rival candidate, Tahir, who is the son of a police inspector and his 10 accomplices. Soon after the incident the nazim-elect of union council Surgul and elders staged a demonstration infront of the house of the senior superintendent of police demanding a registration of the case.

A doctor was shot dead by militants from a banned organization in his clinic.The police belive it to be a sectarian kiling as the docotr was member of a peace committee and brokered peace in the area between Sunnis and Shias.

A 20 year old girl was electrocuted by her relatives on the order of a Punchayat in the name of honour in a village near Musafirkhana town. She had allegedly eloped with a village boy and moved to Karachi. Her parents brought her back  and reportedly electrocuted her the same night. The relatives claimed she committed suicide, however, the initial autopsy report suggested she had either been burnt by being electrocuted or boiling water or both.

Ansar Shah and his nephew Hasan Nawaz were invited to the city from Gujrat by their relatives. When they reached village Karooli five persons identified as Naeem Shah, Khalid Shah, Ayub Shah, Nazim Shah and Khurram Shah opened fire at them killing them on the spot. police have registered a case against the accused and the motive behid the killings is said to be old enmity.
Two men were shot dead while on their way back to Mingora. They were travelling in a cab when unknown armed men opened fire at them.
Two people were hurt in sporadic firing between two rival groups in Bilalabad near Banaras Colony. Both groups had used firearms indiscriminately for over half an hour.

Violence continued in different areas of Hyderabad during the strike called by nationalist parties in protest against restoration of the local government system. In the Qasimabad town area, three men were fired upon and injured while a police coaster and motorcycle were torched in the area.

A Drone strike on a residential compound killed local Taliban militants. Three different sources put the death toll at 6, 10 and 14 respectively. The area targeted was a stronghold of Taliban commander Hafiz Gul Bahadur.

The Mohammad Khan Kallay Government High School and the Latif Khan Kalay Government High School were blown up in Landi Kotal, damaging their boundary walls completely but the main buildings of both schools remained safe.
8 labourers were injured when troops shelled a marble factory in Qamber.
In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, angry mob demolished two Templesand burnt the effigy of Indian PM as the procession marched from Hyderia Chowk to Town Hall on Wednesday.
1 person was killed in a clash between two student groups in Hyderabad on Sunday.

Five rockets were fired on a private cement factory in Dasht area. Three rockets landed inside factory premises while two exploded in open area. A portion of factory was reportedly damaged after one of the rockets hit the factory's chimney. No casualty was however reported.

Four children sustained multiiple burns when some explosive substance stuffed in a can went off in Dhabeji.  They were playing in the workers colony in the mills area when they found the can and started playing with it.
After 3 suspected militants were killed by a drone strike, 3 more people who had gathered at the site to remove the bodies were killed by another drone attack.

At the women's polling station at Government Primary School (D branch), women polling agents of the candidates for the seat of Nazim clashed with each other. When the police tried to intervene, people threw bricks at them. The police retaliated with batons and tear gas shells and arrested 6 people. The police also allegedly injured 2 people during baton charging. SSP Sahiwal and the City Magistrate reached the spot and controlled the situaton.
At least 15 militants wre killed in clashes with the tribal volunteers and aerial attacks. 2 volunteers also lost their lives during the clashes.
A PPP activist, Shahid Hussain Rind, was killed and another was injured in the Gulistan I Jauhar area allegedly by MQM workers. Police has lodged an FIR against MQM.

Militar planes bombed militant targets, killing 14 militants and injuring 21. 11 hideouts were destroyed. Hafiz Saeed, a Taliban spokesman, dismissed the casualities claimed by the military and claimed that the number of militants killed was exaggerated. He accused troops of attacking civilians and destroying their houses.

An explosive device, planted by unidentified people in a gas cylinder in a populated area, was defused. The police said the cylinder was filled with dynamite and hidden underground on the bank of a canal on the Rawalpindi road. The police also seized 10 kilograms of explosives from the Indus Highway on the 9th of July 2007.
An aged industrial worker was killed by unknown men in Landhi on Tuesday. Police claimed that violence was executed on ethnic grounds.

some motorcyclists hurled bombs at a laundary shop and a grocery shop on the main Qasimabad road during a strike, on the on the call of the JSQM-A against the influx of IDPs into Sindh. However there was no serious damage.

Two persons were killed while another was injured in a clash between the Magsi and Jamali tribes when Magsi tribesmen attacked a village in the Gandhawa limits and resorted to insdiscriminate firing. The attack was repulsed by the Jamali tribesmen.
Naeem Khan, who worked at a tile shop, was killed when two men walked into the shop, fired shots at him and fled on their motorbike.

Militants attacked a police vehicle which led to an encounter between them and the police. 1 constable was killed and two others injured while 2 militants were also killed. Police also seized explosives from the assailants. Follow-up: Another report in the same newspaper titled \Four militants killed in Jamrud\" provides details of the incident and specifies the location as Mamokhwar. "

Dr. Tahir-ul-Qadri, Chairman of Pakistan Awami tehrik escaped an assassination bid when unidentified attackers sprayed his house with bullets and fled. He blames \prominent leaders of IJI\" for the attack."

Four people of a family were gunned down and three others injured when some armed men barged into their house and opened indiscriminate firing on the inmates of the house. The motivation behind the incident was not mentioned.
During a search operation, security forces were attacked by militants. In the encounter that followed, 3 militants were killed.

Police baton-charged scores of school and college students who were allegedly blocking traffic on the main Samundari-Rajana road and damaging buses in protest to a student getting injured in a road accident. About a dozen students were injured.
During a strike called by the Milli Yakjehti Council (MYC), activists resorted to shooting at public and private transport.
7 people were killed in polling related violence across Sindh. ; Follow-up: The report gives the details of the casualties.

At least 40 missiles landed and exploded in and around Sui town, no casualty was reported. The missiles were fired from Mohan Pat area, some 20 km from Sui gas field. Some rockets landed close to Sui gas plant, but the gas installation remained safe. Security forces retaliated and returned fire.
People protesting against prolonged power outages set fire to tyres as traffic remained blocked.
Random killings in Lyari take place while the police considers the violence as political. No clear details available.

A day of mourning was called by MQM in Karachi as the renewed violence continued, although not linked to the shut down. The body of young man was found stuffed in a gunny bag near Faqeer Mor in Qasbas Colony of Orangi. It has a note which stated \peace or war\"."
A villager, Khair Mohammad Chandio, clubbed his wife, Shahida, to death on the pretext of Karo-Kari. He surrendered himself to the Shahdadkot Police Station later.
The body of a woman was found burning in University grounds in front of Madrassatul Banat. Her throat had been slit open.
An activist of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (Haqiqi) was shot and killed in Shadman Colony of Malir.
Three security men were killed and six others were injured when around 59 militants stormed the check post at Qadirabad High School in Matni.
A married woman was stabbed to death by her brother.
Two soldiers were killed and two were injured when a convoy of the security forces was struck by a roadside bomb.

Angry youths burnt tyres at several roads in order to protest against the shortage of drinking water in the area for the last 15 days. This occurred during the strike called by the Shehri Action Committee.

A charged mob aatcked the police and pelted police vans with stones.The police tear-gassed the protesters to diperse them.The situation in the area was tense after an incident of cross-firing between Abid Raza and MPA Ghulam Raza Groups, a few days earlier.
Official sources also claimed that Indian forces were shelling villages in the Khuiratta and Nakyal sectors of Kotli district. No loss of life or damage to property was reported so far.

IJT activists clashed with PU security guards over the issue of the activists distributing pamphlets, which is not allowed on campus. The pamphlets were calling for the release of Dr. Aafia Siddiqui. A PU spokesman claimed that the security personnel had stopped the  activists from handing out pamphlets and the enraged activists attacked them. However, IJT claim that the security guards had been ordered by the vice-chancellor to thrash the activists and that they merely reacted.

As KESC workers continued protesting against their placement in a 'surplus pool', various incidents of violence were reported from the city. The general manager of IBC Gulistan-i-Jauhar was attacked outside his office but he managed to escape. The protesting workers denied the allegation that they had forcefully stopped people from working.

A Pakistan Coast Guard employee, Muhammad Riaz, was seriously injured in a blast in Hub town. Police said the powerful blast occurred near the PCG office. The explosive deviced was a locally-made time device. Azad Baloch, a spokeman for the defunct Balochistan Liberation Army, said his organization claimed responsibility for the blast.
A man was gunned down by unidentified gunmen near his house.

The casualties were a result of a Muslim-Christian clash over an eve teasing issue. Two christian youngsters teased the daughter of Mr. Khan who exchanged harsh words with them. They in result opened fire at him and he retaliated. All three sustained bullet injuries and Mr. Khan died. Many relatives of the deceased and other people in the nieghborhood gathered to protest the death and the demonstration turned violent where the protestors started attacking the houses of christians who attacked back and casulaties were reported on both sides. A large number of riot police was deployed to bring the situation under control.
A landmine planted by militants along a roadside exploded when security personnel were on routine patrol. Sepoy Ilyas was killed.
The body of a 'well built' man was found with multiple stab wounds.
Constable Sardar Zakir of the police was killed when unidentified armed men shot him while he was on duty at the Mauripur truck stand.

A man clubbed to death his sister when she came back home after eloping a week back. The girl's brother, Javed, objected to her entry in the house after her 'dishonourable' act, which prompted him to club her to death.

2 oil tankers were intercepted by unidentified armed men and fired at. One tanker was completely destroyed after it caught fire while the other was partially damaged. They were headed to Afghanistan to supply oil to Nato forces.
the body of an ANP activist was found under the Gulistan-i-Jauhar bridge at Abul Asar Hafeez Jallundhri Road, pumped full of bullets.
Two unidentified men shot dead a person outside the sessions court, Gujrat on Wednesday
the house of a Shia leader was badly damaged in a mystery blast in Muaza Kotla Bakar Shah. Ghulam Nabi Parhar and his family were not present at the time of the blast.

A remote-controlled bomb that was planted in a parked car was detonated when an army convoy was passing by. An army vehicle was destroyed and two other cars were damaged. 1 soldier lost his life while 15 people, including 7 security personnel, were injured. The Baloch Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the attack.
Two labourers fell victims to targeted attacks. Shabir Ahmed was killed outside his house while Muhammad Hassan was found dead in the same street.
One person was killed while three others sustained bullet injuries in  a clash  between two groups in the Kisana Kunjah area.

Following the death of Shameer Khan in police custody, allegedly due to police torture, residents of the area held a protest in front of the Luddan police station. Police opened fire at the mob after the latter allegedly pelted them with stones. Two protesters were shot and injured while 15 policemen also sustained injuries.

Five children were injured when a time bomb went off outside a private school in Pir Qala area. The bomb was planted at the main gate and went off 30 minutes before the closing hour of the school, which averted disaster.
Some unidentified men fired at the SSP's residence but fled as soon as the Frontier Constabulary retaliated.

a high profile, Darra Taliban Commander, Tariq, had asked the tribesmen of Mishtri tribe, three days ago, to expel Zahid and his desciples saying that  they were not real Taliban but criminals. the tribesmen failed to take action against the tribesmen because of fear. when Zahid ignored Tariq's warning to leave the area, Tariq seized him and his 8 other comrads in Danay Khla and shot them dead. they belonging to his rival group in Chapri Feroze Khel.

Approximately 30 outlaws, believed to be Bugti tribesmen, fired 12 rockets on the Bhitai Colony Police station and the Basket Police picket. They fled once the Rangers and FC retaliated. According to officials, 1 outlaw was killed but his accomplices took the body with them.

Militants attacked the headquarters of paramilitary forces in the Miramshah town, but no casualty was reported. The sources said that five rockets fired at the fort landed in adjoining areas. One rocket hit the hostel of a government school in the town and two others landed near the army camp.
The mutilated body of a woman was found, the police found its head a few yards away. Acording to the police the body bore severe torture marks.

scores of condemed prisoners incarcerated in the district jail held a demonstration against what they called 'maltreatment'. They also demanded that they be shifted from solitary confinement to barracks. The jail administration resorted to baton charge to compel them to return to their cells. Deputy jail superintendent Malik Farukh Sultan said that no prisoner went on strike.
Some houses, crops and 2 goats were killed due to Indian shelling in Sucheetgarh, Chaprar, Bajwat, Charwa, Bajragarhi, Harpal and Zafarwal Sectors on Sunday

Two brothers, Ramzan and Boota, allegedly killed their sister, Naseem Bibi. According to them, she was having illicit relations with a man from the locality and did not listen to their warnings against it. They strangled her with a dubatta and courted arrest.

PML-N workers were stopped by the police from entering Lahore to welcome Party President Mian Shahbaz Sharif. The local leaders were talking to the police when the police started arresting the activists. This resulted in the activists becoming violent and attacking the police, who responded by teargas shelling and baton-charging. The DPO and several other people sustained injuries. The Mandra police arrested 150 activists, including Sardar Mehtab and Iqbal Jhagra, and impounded 11 vehicles.
Militants used IEDs to blow up 3 government primary schools in Mamozai area.
some unidentified persons shot dead a truck driver, Aurang Zeb on National Highway near Karamabad.
50 suspected militants entered a school building, planted IEDs and blew up the school.
Six people were killed and 12 injured by Indian shelling and firing across LoC. The firing was reported to be very intense.

Hundreds of residents held a demonstration outisde the Tehsil Municipal Administrations office by smashing pitchers on the road, which resulted in a blockade, to protest over acute shortage of water in the city for a week. Police reached the situation and asked them to end the  blockade, however, the protesters claimed that gthe government needed to take notice of the problem.

In the hours leading upto the burial of Dr Imran Farooq, a senior MQM leader who was assassinated in London on 16-Sep-10, Karachi witnessed sporadic firing incidents and arson attacks. A minibus was set on fire at the given location
The body of a 16-year old was found in North Cantonment. It bore several marks of violence on the neck which suggested that he had been strangled to death.

7 people were killed and one was injured in a clash between two groups of Magsi Tribe in Khichi on Saturday. The reason behind was said to be the leadership of the Magsi Tribe between faction leader Yusuf Ali Khan Magsi and his nephew, Provincial Home Minister Zulfikar Ali Khan Magsi.
An employee of a multinational company was found dead in his office on Maratab Ali Road.
PDA Secretary General-Allama Mujtaba Hyder was shot dead by three unidentified assailants in a Mosque in F-11 Syedian Village on Monday.
A young man was killed and another was injured when unidentified men on motorcycles opened indiscrminate fire on a café where the two men were sitting.
Three armed men attacked a mosque with a hand grenade before opening indiscriminate fire at the people inside. 2 people were killed in the attack while at least 12 others were injured.
A remote controlled bomb was detonated inside a mosque when worshippers were leaving after Friday prayers. The blast damaged the mosque and killed at least 5 people while 30 others were injured.
4 persons of a familiy were killed and 1 was injured over a dispute of irrigation water, in Pakistan Korana  in Malakand, after an exchange of hot words.

Troops launched an offensive against militants after they were targetted by militants. The troops killed 2 militants and injured three others. They also destroyed several militants hideouts and defused a number of IEDs.

It was alleged that Maulana Bashir Ahmed Shad, provincial secretary of JUI (Sami Group), Abu Bakr, president of SSP Chishtian, Maulana Munir Ahmed Haqqani, secretary-general of SSP and 2 other people were behind the killing of Amer Raza and Maqsood Hussan, who were the sons of a commission agent. They were also accused of instigating people against a particular sect. The above claims were made in an IJP Press release following which the 5 accused were arrested.
Missiles fired by US Drones targeted a residential compound and car parked nearby, killing 6 militants.

Six militants and two lashkar men were killed in a clash over deployment of a Frontier Corps platoon in the area. Militants opened fire on tribesmen for welcoming the platoon, killing two volunteers, while six militants were killed in retaliation.
One person was injured in Barmoj village in Kotli as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.

Residents of Shershah town blocked the National Highway by burning tyres. They were protesting against the death of a man during a police raid.The police claim the man had a heart attack while getting arrested,however the people say that he was tortured to death by the police during the raid.
A lawyer, associated with the Pakistan Muslim League N's Lawyers Forum, was walking towards his home when unidentified men opened fire on him in Gulshan-i-Jamal, causing severe injuries.

Islamabad police resorted to baton-charge to prevent students, belonging to the IJT and the students wing of the JI ,from holding a peaceful demonstration outside the USIS centre against the US. 5 people, including 3 policemen were injured. The police also damaged the buses in which the student had arrived.
The house of a militant was blown up in the Bajaur Agency during an operation by the security forces.
A man was found stabbed to death in his hotel room on the Mall.

A man was killed, and eight other people, including DIG Shahid Nizam Durrani were injured when a bomb planted on a motorbike exploded outside the DIG's office in Quetta. Officials stated that the bomb was meant to target the DIG.

A suicide blast took place at the end of a demonstration against electricity loadshedding organized by the Jamaat-i-Islami. The JI's district naib amir and DSP Gulfat Hussain were among the dead. City police chief Liaqat Ali claimed that the DSP was the target of the attack but City Circle SP Imran Kishwar said that the target was the gathering itself.
Law enforcement agencies arrested 13 suspects and defused a large number of landmines from the along the Sindh - Balochistan border.
Some people fired from a car near Water Pump, Chowrangi. This resulted in injuries to 3 men travelling in a minibus.
a man axed his daughter and a man to death, as he suspected them of having illicit relations. He then surrendered to the police.

A rally led by Dr. Sarfraz Naeemia raised anti-American slogans, burnt the effigy of President Bush and showed solidarity with the Afghani government and Osama Bin Laden. The rally was also addressed by JUI and JI members.
a girl was gunned down by her cousin on suspicion of having an affair with a youth of the same village.
Two cows were killed and three houses damaged by Indian firing along the working boundary.

the younger brother of Mullah Wakeel Ahmed Mutawakkel, a former foreign minister of the Taliban Government in Afghanistan was killed on 3-jul-05, in an exchange of fire between two rival groups. Police sources say Jalil Ahmed was caught in a crossfire on Sariab road, where he suffered injuries. he was taken to the hospital where he died.

Two Taliban militants, armed with guns, entered a mosque and asked two elders to accompany them outside. When the two elders, identified as Israf Gul and Irab Gul, refused to oblige the militants beat them up before opening fire on them resulting in their deaths.
A clash between militants and security forces left 15 militants dead and 23 injured. Troops advanced to Meshti Mela and killed 5 militants.
Three rockets were fired upon police lines in Tank. Attackers fled when police returned fire.
One person was injured in the Mandhar village as the Indian shelling continued from across the LoC.
Four students were injured when unidentified gunmen fired at the hostel building and fled.

A 6-year-old girl was killed and nine others were injured when a bomb exploded in a tonga going from Chungi No-14 to the tomb of Hazrat Shah Rukn-i-Alam in Multan.  When the tonga reached near Aam Khas Bagh, a bomb blast destroyed the cart, but the driver and horse escaped unhurt.
Two passers-by were killed and a policeman was injured when armed men opened fire on the car of a police sub inspector at the CID in Korangi. It was alleged the SI Khosa was the target of the attack.
A ninth grade student was crushed to death by a speeding vehicle. Soon after, students went on a rampage and damaged multiple shops on their way to attacking a police station in Saddar.

According to reports form Islamabad, planes and helicopters heavily pounded militant positions in te Sam, Laddah, Makin and Kanigoram areas. Heavy bombing also caused wide spread damage to residential areas.
a grenade explosion occurred near the Cantonement Board Offices. Sialkot Police Chief said that the hand grenades were locally made and the motive behind the incident was to panic the public.
Following the assassination of Maulana Yousuf Ludhianvi, enlarged youths set Capri Cinema on fire on M.A Jinnah road.

Riaz Mohammad was riding a bicycle whe he was shot, his brothers-Javed and Aurangzeb- come to pick him up and the assailant fired on them too. Police registered a triple murder on the request of the father, Mohammad Iqbal.
some unknown armed persons shot dead one Soda of Ood tribe in his house. His wife was also injured. The murder was said to the be the result of an old feud.
A watchman of the hospital was found murdered in the premises. No further details were given.

Two suicide blasts within 3 minutes in a busy market area killed at least 50 people and injured 120. Among the victims, 8 soldiers were killed and another 12 injured. Most of the victims were civilian. The R.A. Bazaar is near sensitive military installation and offices. The TTP claimed responsibility for the attack. However, Lahore Commissioner Khusro Pervaiz claimed that India was behind the attacks. ; Follow-up: 3 people who had been wounded succumbed to their injuries on the 14th of March 2010. ; A man who suffered injuries in the blasts died at the General Hospital, taking the death toll upto 62. ; Another victim of the attacks who had sustained injures died the Combined Military Hospital.

Rizwana was found dead near the tracks with a single bullet wound to the head. Mohammad Ayaz, her husband, realised she was missing when he reached home in Chanesar Goth. Police could not ascertain the reason behind the murder.

A father of four was found shot dead in a plot near Shamkay Bhattian stop. 40-year old Muhammad Aslam of Hujra Shah Muqeem was, according to police speculation, kidnapped and then murdered. The family did not name anyone in the murder case.
Two men belonging to rival groups were killed in an exchange of fire while another was injured, in the Lachi area.
According to sources, three were killed and at least 27 people were injured in Indian firing from across the Line of Control in different villages of Neelum valley.

5 local leaders of PSF were injured when some armed asailants attacked them near Lohari Gate, when they were asked to remove some stickers from their chests by IJT men. When they refused, their rivals shot indiscriminately.

An explosive device went off in Tawakal market in Wana Bazaar during the opening of the bazaar after months of economic sanctions were lifted. Eyewitnesses report that a paramilitary soldier and a passer-by were injured in the explosion.
\Some\" people were injured in lathicharges and teargassing in Charsadda, including the SHO of Charsadda."

It was reported that there was a heavy exchange of fire between Indian and Pakistan troops at Siachen 'during the last few days', including a number of air violations by New Delhi in the area. But the exact incidents were not reported.

some unidentified person opened fire at Shah Alam market when people were returning home in the evening after the Ashura-i-Muharram procession. They also hurled empty bottle at the police party. They also damaged vehicles.1 man was injured. A student leader also reported that some people opened fire on them as a result of which 2 of his collegues were injured.

3 militants, that were signalled to stop by security personnel, opened fire at the latter. Retaliatory fire killed all three militants who were trying to infiltrate into Bayakan area from Shah Dheri. 1 of the security personnel was also injured.
Three tribesmen were killed while another was injured when armed men attacked a tractor trolley of Turi tribesmen in Munda area near the Afghan border in Kurram.

100s of youths protested the killing of Shahzad Raza by blocking the main road. The police resorted to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to disperse them. The police claim that the crowd refused to disperse and threw stones to which the police responded. During intermittent clashes between the two parties, 3 vehicles were set ablaze, passing vehicles were pelted with stones and there was exchange of fire as well.

Four people were killed while eight others were injured in an armed clash between the Sulemankhel and Seigi Tareen tribes in the Gulistan area of Qila Abdullah. The tribes had a previous dispute over the ownership of a tract of land.
The bullet riddled body of a 30-yearl old man was found. The reason behind the killing could not be ascertained.

After the police had vacated a plot that had been usurped by alleged lang-grabbers in the garb of flood-affected people, armed men showed up and opened fire at the police. In the clash that ensued, 4 policeman and 5 other people were injured. The office of a local builder was set on fire during the gun-battle. By the end of the clash the police had arrested 8 suspects. The police claimed that 'the land grabbers enjoyed political support' and that 'some leaders of a nationalist party have been found involved in staging the entire drama'.

Several shops in Pasni, Turbat and Mand were attacked and set on fire. In border town of Mand a customs office and a hostel were rensacked. Violent protests were also reported from Panjgur, Sibi, Mastung, Dera Murad Jamali, Usta Muhammad, Dera Allahyar and the industrial town of Hub.
a man, Jamal, was shot and killed by his rivals in the village of Jehanabad. The motive behind the murder is stated to be old rivalry between the two Afghan families.

The former Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and current candidate for the Lodhran district Nazim, Siddiq Khan Kanju, and his companions were outside a barber shop when three men got out of a car and shot at them. As a result, Kanju and one other person died and injured another.

Two powerful bomb blasts occurred in Quetta within moments of each other. The second blast occured in the backyard of a Hindu temple. There were no reports of casualties or major damage. The blast shattered windowpanes of the buildings near the explosion site.
A bomb exploded in Parachinar on Wednesday due to which a boy was injured.
three people were killed when gunmen opened fire on a Karachi bound trailer near Wadh Town in Khuzdar district.
Four people were killed in a clash between Wattoo and Chishti group over a piece of agricultural land on Monday

FC convoy was attacked by Baloch militants in Ganz Nallah area injuring 3 security personnel. Later, reinforcements arrived and FC attacked the militangts killing at least seven. BLA claimed the responsibility for the attack.

Tariq Aziz, an MQM worker carrying a head money one million rupees, died in an encounter with the police in Orangi. The police changed its story of the encounter three times, each time claiming that he was killed in 'self defence'. But the relatives of the deceased said that the police had arrested him in a raid on his house and then killed him a few hours later.
One person was killed by unknown assailants in Shakargarh on Thursday.
Five people were gunned down by their three rivals on a dispute of \adda\" posession."
Suspected militants entered the house of a pro-government tribal elder and vacated the inmates before planting an explosive device and blowing up the house. No casualties were reported.
Amir Iqbal- who was the main suspect in the killing of PPP leader Begum Rehana Sarwar- was shot dead by unidentified men. \nBegum Rehana Sarwar was killed 4 year ago on a property dispute in Defence
Miscreants fired a rocket on a governmetn slaughter house in Khar. No casualty was reported.
An SI(Syed Akhtar Hussain Zaidi) died while ASI(Shoaib Ahmad Soomro) received bullet injuries by unknown assailants chasing them near office of Sui Southern gas on Wednesday
A militant commander Anwar and his deputy Sadiq were killed during a clash with security forces. Both militants belonged to Odigram area.
Suspected militants fired rockets and machine guns into the army brigade headquarters. No damaged was reported. The forces guarding the brigade retaliated and this continued for a few hours.

8 policemen were injured when terrorists on motorbikes attacked 3 police posts with hand grenades. The first attack was when a grenade was hurled on a Rescue 15 post in Topawala Square on the Circular road. 6 policemen were injured.
1 man was killed and 9 others were injured when a bomb exploded at Badami Bagh Bus Stand. The explosion took place outside a New Khan's Sadiqabad-bound bus. The bus was also damaged.
Unidentified men shot dead an employee of the Agriculture Department. No further details given.
A roadside remote-controlled bomb was detonated as a security convoy was passing by. Lt-Col Mohammad Yousaf and 5 soldiers were killed while 2 other soldiers were injured.
A cracker exploded in a garbage can near the building.
Following the death of a student in an accident, hundreds of students kept Lahore-Sargodha road blocked for about an hour and pelted stones at cars and buses.

Two powerful blasts ripped through the busy Moon Market in Allama Iqbal Town claiming at least 45 lives. The blast also caused a massive fire in the market which destroyed several shops and vehicles and also knocked out the electricity supply. According to the police the first blast took place outside a bank and the other near a police station and both took place within a few second of each other. The commisioner blamed India for the blasts but the law minister said militants from Waziristan were behind the attack.
Following the rumor of an assassination attempt on the chief of the Sunni Tehrik in Pakpattan, a mini-bus was torched in Federal B area. The rumor turned out to be false.
In Nowshera, unidentified persons blew up an electricity tower.

Scattered incidents of violence were witnessed in Karachi on the fifth day of violence, when an armed clash between two 'ethnically' motivated groups took place leaving at least half a dozen wounded in Block 4 of Gulshan-i-Iqbal. The police intercepted and brought the situation under control.
Salesman Imran- a resident of Ghausia street, Ravi Road- was found dead in a sack in a park. His body was riddled with bullets and burnt. The family said that they had no enmity with anyone.

The body of a 28-year old man who was shot dead four days ago by some unidentified people was found in a drum near Wahdat Road. Family members of the victim said that he had no enmity with anyone. Police said the murder could have been carried out after a dispute.
Five people were killed and 21 others injured when unidentified gunmen fired at a food distribution (niaz) during the Zuljinnah procession of Moharram. The attackers could not be apprehended.
An explosion occurred near the office of the divisional superintendent of Railways. The explosion was caused by a locally-made bomb, and it could not be determined who was behind the attack.
A woman and her friend were killed in the name of honour according to the tribal 'traditions' by the woman's father and brother.
The bomb disposal squad managed to defuse a bomb planted near a venue where former chief minister Mohammad Akram Durrani was addressing a meeting.

Three CD shops, located in different markets of Matani Bazaar, were blown up and completely destroyed. Owners of the shops told the police that they had not received any prior letters or calls for the closure of their businesses. This is the fourth incident of attacks on CD and video shops in the city.

8 highly sensitive mines that had been planted along railway tracks were detected and defused by law enforcement agencies. This came after 2 bombs had exploded along railway tracks in the same area a couple of days ago.
A man died during shelling by Indian forces in Balakot village in Nakyal sector of Kotli district. Three other people were injured in the Goi village of Tatta Pani sector in the same district.
Armed motorcyclists shot and injured a padestrian, Malik Khizer Hayat.

Residents of Razaabad and family members of a teenager who drowned in a pond demonstrated against Wasa (Water and Sanitation Authority). The demonstrators blocked the main road, burnt tyres and broke the windows of more than a dozen vehicles. The Razaabad Police have registered a case against two people who had obtained a stay order against the removal of the pond.

Two groups, one from the Sher-i-Bengal Muslim League and the other from the Pakistani Bengali Action Committee, exchanged hot words over the possession of an office which led to an exchange of fire. This led to the death of two people. One of the deceased was a member of the Sher-i-Bengal Muslim League while the other was a passer-by. The police later arrested one person allegedly involved in the firing.
A group of youth made an attempt to set a KTC bus on fire in Burns Road Area on Tuesday.

As soon as news of the violence at an MQM procession in Karachi, where 2 people were killed, reached Hyderabad, angry youngsters took to the streets and pelted vehicles and shops with stones in addition to damaging public property and firing in the air. Later, a police contingent showed up and tried to bring the situation under control.
A man was shot and injured when unidentified men opened fire on him in Mehmoodabad.
The harvesting of seasonal crops was badly disrupted as Indian forces continued shelling on the Pakistani border villages across the LoC.
A man was killed and his wife amd daughter were injured when some people threw a hand grenade in their house while they were sleeping. The man was said to have no enemity with anyone.

A threatening call was received by FM 99's Producer News and Current Affairs, Ishfaq Joya, at his mobile phone. The caller introduced himself as an activist of the Anjuman Fidayan-i-Islam and said his Chief Abu Hureira had directed him to convey his message to the radio channel to leave Muzaffarabad to avoid any offence, as the activities of the channel, especially with \Save the Children\" programme were suspicious."
Unidentified gunmen attaked a bus of Attock cement factory killing three workers. The workers were returning to their homes in Karachi
Zahid Sanam, who was the vice chairman of Khanpur Zakat Committee, was gunned down at his front door allegedly by his opponents.
The decomposed body of an unidentified man was found in a manhole near a textile mill.
Two constables on a motorcycle were on their way to the Sindhi Hotel branch of the National Bank of Pakistan when they were intercepted and killed.
The bullet-riddled body of a militant commander, Nazir Khan, was found. Khan had been accused of attacks on government officials and installations.
The body of an unidentified young man was found from a house in Sector 14/B in Mochko. His hands and legs were tied and he had been strangled.

Police baton charged inmates at a prison after the prisoners had protested against the alleged 'excesses' of the jail administration. The baton charge left 18 inmates injured. The inmates also claimed that the jail authorities had demanded bribes from them and, upon their refusal to oblige, had tortured them.

Hundreds of residents of New Goth staged a rally against the civic authorities's failure to pump out drainage water from the area. The protestors burnt tyres and changed slogans against the Tehsil and District Nazims.  The Naib Nazim, Iqbal Dawood, rushed to the scene and ordered the water to be drained.
Muhammad Jan Ahmadzai-leader of Jamaat-i-Islami(Afghanistan) was gunned down  by unidentified person in Cherat Road, Pabbi on Thursday.
Security personnel destroyed houses of five militants in Shabaddin area of Charbagh. Three bodies were found in Kabal and Barikot tehsils of the district-two from Akhund Kalley and one from Nawagai.

Eight persons were killed when their rival party opened indiscriminate fire on them while they were being transported by the police. According to officials, the party had been taken into custody for allegedly killing the Ex-chariman union council.
A police party was attacked by a large number of men and women, who claimed that when the police raided their village and arrested two robbers, 'they did not observe the decency of the women folk'.

Unidentified assailants fired eight rockets at the convoy of security forces when it was passing through Tatrani area in Kohlu district. The troops returned fired forcing the attackers to flee. One soldier was injured in the exchange of fire.

Official sources said militants opened indiscriminate fire on security personnel in the hilly area of Sangsilla in the Dera Bugti district. The security forces immediately took positions. In the exchange of fire, security men Mazullah, Mohammad Qamar and Naeem were injured, who were taken to the military hospital.

two policemen and a civilian was killed and three others including two policement were injured in a clash over a disputed piece of land in Ranwati police area in Sukkur. A police team had gone to the disputed site allegedly to hand over possession to one of the parties when the group present their attacked them with rocket.
Two policemen were shot at and injured by four unidentified armed men in Green Town while they were on a routine patrol.

Unidentified persons opened fire indiscriminately on a jewellery shop in Ghotki, killing a 13-year-old boy and and injuring another person.  Police say the incident was caused by old enmity and the attackers intended to kill the proprietor of the shop, who escaped.

In the midst of a strike called by the MQM to protest against the 'extra judicial killing' of its workers in police custody, shooting incidents took place all over the city. A man was wounded in New Town.
The demolition squad of the Karachi Building Control Authority was attacked by a group involved in unauthorized construction on a privately owned land bearing survey No. 90-A, Khuldabad, Landhi.
In Korangi, Edhi volunteers found a bulet-riddled body near Mahal Cinema. His political affiliation could not be known.

Amanat, who was a Rescue 1122 constable, was shot while he was travelling on a van by another passenger on the same van. Other passengers managed to overpower the assailant, identified as Farhan, and handed him over to the police.
Two memebers of the ATI were shot dead in a clash between two factions of the student body over the reorganization of the group. The exchange of fire spread panic on the campus.
Prisoners in the Khairpur Jail staged a violent demonstration against non-provision of basic services.They pelted the police with stones.The police baron charged the protesters.
A man was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in his car.

The wave of 'ethnic' violence that affected Orangi town the previous day spread to other parts of the city when a man was on the rooftop of his house in the remit of Shahrah-i-Noor Jahan in North Nazimabad and was hit by a bullet. The police said he did not have political affiliation, however, the ANP spokesman claimed that he was the vice president of its Ward UC-2 in Orangi Town.
Cross-border firing by India in pooch district. Mohammad Rafique injured on Monday and Sofia received wounds on Tuesday.
Some miscreants tried to detonate two bombs on an oil pipeline carrying oil to Punjab from Sindh. One bomb exploded while the other was defused.

Several areas of Mohmand Agency were the site of a search operation by security forces as the offensive against militants in the region continued. Helicopter gunships were used to attack suspected militant hideouts. Several hideouts and 3 cars were destroyed in the operation.

a large number of textile workers staged a rally and blocked the traffic to protest low gas pressure, poor policy for textile mills, closure of second shift in mills and high tariffs of electricity and gas bills. They carried placards, shouted slogans and burnt tyres. police reached the spot, after negotiations the labourers dispersed.

Unknown armed men riding a motorcycle gunned down an afghan refugee identified as Molvi Yar Mohammad who was Pesh Imam in a mosque. The deceased had an enmity in Afghanistan which resulted in his assassination.

Four children were killed and seven people were injured when security forces pounded bases of Lashkar-i-Islam with shells and artillery gunfire. Tanks moved into the area and helicopters went into action.  Some people said that the people who's houses were damaged in the firing had no political affiliations, and that civilians were being caught up in the battle.
Two more persons were killed and two others were injured in a clash between two groups of the Bugti tribe in a village in Jaffarabad, Balochistan as part of the on-going clash between the two groups.

Members of the the Lahore Bar Association (LBA), after barring the entry of the Chief Justice into the Lahore High Court, marched towards PMG Chowk to continue pressing for the transfer of D&SJ Zawwar Ahmad Sheikh. After trying to convince them, in vain, to not violate Section 144, the police fired tear gas and shots into the air to disperse the mob but the lawyers retaliated by pelting the police with stones and damaging their vehicle, forcing the police back. Lawyers also thrashed some cameramen from private news channels, accusing them of 'supporting the LHC chief justice and provincial administration'.
shop of a faith healer was blown up by an unkown miscreant. 3 nearby shops were damaged as well as a rickshaw, however no casualties were reported.
A 35 year old man was found dead on Railway Road in the Naulakha area. He had an injury to his head.
A worker of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement was shot dead by two unidentified motorcyclists.
Jet fighters bombarded militant hideouts in different areas of Maond and Salarzai tehsils. However, no casualty was reported.
Teenager Imran was killed and 2 others were injured after they were attacked with knives by some people in Korangi.
Following a fresh wave of violence, Gullistan-i-Jauhar, Qasba Colony, Nazimabad, Lyari, Kharadar and Site Areas were paralyzed  by the incidents of intense fire by unknown men on Sunday.

Several people were injured when police resorted to baton-charge and tear gas shelling during an anti-encroachment campaign in Sialkot.  While shops were being demolished, a former MPA, Maulana Ghiasuddin, accompanied by several residents, wished to have a dialoque on the matter, however, the police began baton-charging and tear gas shelling. The Maulana and one of his colleague's were arrested and subjected to violence but later released. Shopkeepers went on strike in protest.
Four civilians were killed and four others were injured in Indian Shelling from across the LoC in Hajeera Sector in the Dea Sheir Khan village of the Rawalakot District.
A man's body was found tortured and shot dead in the Old City area. The police could not ascertain the motive behind the killing and the man's identity could not be established.

Seven camps of Taliban were destroyed and five militants were injured in the air strikes in Sultanzai, Feroze Khel, Bezote and Sam areas of Orakzai Agency. Heavy bombardment by the jetfighters two bunkers and underground ammunition dumps were also blown up in Bezote area of Orakzai Agency along Kohat district. Twelve militants were killed in the air strikes.

Jinnah', which is a local newspaper owned by property tycoon Malik Riaz, put up banners that questioned PML-N stalwart Chaudhry Nisar Ali Khan's income and property. Over 100 PML-N supporters arrived at the site and tried to pull down the banners which led to a brawl between supporters of both groups. The police, which was already present, tried to beat the rival sides back with batons while the latter threw stones and fired guns. Over a dozen people were arrested but no serious injuries were reported.
A school headmaster was shot dead allegedly by seven outlaws over a land dispute in karrianwala on Tuesday
Bullet riddled bodies of two Afghan nationals wre found inside a house. The reason behind the killing could not be known.

The heads of two rival groups were shot dead over old enemity in Berriwala village. Chaudhary Muhammad Sidiq Tarar was first killed by the rival party, after which, in retaliation, the leader of the rival party himself was shot dead by the relatives of the first victim.

Armed motorcyclsits opened fire at a car, killing one person on the spot and injuring 2 others. One of the two wounded victims succumbed to his injuries in the hospital. The police attributed the incident to old enmity between two tribes.
The SHO of Sariab Police station was killed along with two of his security guards when armed men attacked his vehicle while he was patrolling the Killi Shahnawaz area.

A man was injured when a bomb went off in front of the office of the hospitals' medical superintendent. The explosion damaged the windowpanes of a nearby offices and wards, and also a newly renovated resource centre for children. Noone claimed responsibility for the attack, but it was learnt that a former resident of the union of paramedic staff had developed differences with the hospital management over the renovation of the resource centre. It was learnt that the officials of the health department had expelled members of the union from resource centre where they had established an office without permission.
A bomb mounted on a bicycle exploded in a busy market killing one person and injuring at least 22 others.  This is the third bomb blast in Peshawar in the past four days.

The bullet-riddled body of a 32-year old man was found in a gunny bag  in the limits of the Bin Qasim police station, and a man was shot dead In his house in Peerabad. Awami National Party claimed that one of the victims was its worker, but the police said that the deaths were a result of personal enemity.
Four persons including two children were killed when the house of Saed was attacked with handgrenades by unknown assailants in the Hangu District. The attackers managed o escape from the scene

Militants killed Ghani, who was a member of a peace committee, for raising a voice against them. Militants had warned the armed lashkar of FR Kohat against supporting security forces against the Taliban.

A suicide bomber blew himself up inside the court of a senior judge in Quetta, killing 15 people and injuring 35 others. The provincial police officer said that attacks on government installations and personnel of law-enforcement agencies were a reaction to government's firm resolve to combat terrorism and sabotage activities in the country. Followup: Special police teams raided different places in Quetta and detained around 50 suspects, 25 of them Afghan nationals.  Followup: Police announced the arrest of an Afghan national involved in Quetta's suicide attack.

some members of a Deoband seminary, believed to now be activists of the now defunct Sipah-i-Sahaba objected to the holding of frequent Majlis in the Imambargah. They pelted the participants of the Majlis with stones and left 6 injured. In response some of the Majlis organisers resorted to aerial firing. it was the first incident of sectarian violence in 25 years.
A paramilitary soldier was killed in a clash between local Taliban and Arang tribesmen in Uthmankhel area. The tribesmen were asking the Taliban to vacate the checkposts of paramilitary troops.
Four people were killed and 10 others injured when Ghaibzai and Massyayzai tribes clashed against each other. The reason behind the clash was not mentioned in the report.
the Taliban took control of the city of Mingora and laid siege to a place which housed 46 security personnel. An official said that this was a violation of the Swat peace agreement.
2 people were shot at and injured by unknown assailants in Korangi on Sunday.
A 10 year old boy was injured in a landmine blast in the Dashat-i-Goran area of Dera Bugti. Police menawhile foiled attempts to blow up gas pipelines by defusing bombs.

Several workers of the Kissan Bachao Tehrik were injured when police resorted to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to control the situation of violence that arose when the workers  tried to halt vehicles and trains carrying supplies in various villages of the Silanwala tehsil. Three farmers sustained bullet injuries while several others were injured in the baton-charging in Chak 106-NB and surrounding areas. The farmers stopped a train near Ajnala and Chak Warrianchanwal, destroying milk adnd vegetables. They also pelted vehicles with stones that were driven by police. The Sargodha district magistrate narrated an incident on Sargodha road where over 150 people had blocked the road and beaten women and children of a bus, along with wasting milk of milkmen. To which the police resorted to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to disperse the crowd, however, the agitators pelted them with stones and began firing.

The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as a man was gunned down by armed men on a motorbike in Khuda ki Basti area. He was reportedly targeted due to his ethnic background as he did not belong to a political party.
The nose and lips of a man were chopped off by two men in Mouza Chanderwali as they had suspected that the man had relations with a woman from their tribe.
Two people were murdered in a village near Nawabshah following the custom of karo-kari.

A crime reporter of the Urdu daily ' Sang-i-Meel', who was also an activist of the Punjabi Pukhtoon Ittehad was kidnapped, and killed in Block 17 of the Federal B area. Witnesses reported that unidentified men dragged his out of the car and shot him several times with an AK-47 rifle.
As part of the violence on the second day of a two-day strike called by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM), protesters threw a 'cracker'  on the office of  ASP cantonment police station.
a former activist of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement-Haqiqi, Raees, was killed and two others were wounded when unidentified persons opened fire on them in Liaqatabad No.4 in the furniture market.

The Difah-i-Islam Mahaz, a 15-party Sunni Alliance held a protest rally to condemn the US-led war on Iraq when hundreds of activists marched towards Faisal Square and two constiuents of the alliance clashed over who would lead the demonstration. Three people were injured and the police did not intervene.
Asadullah Khan- resident of Shah Faisal Colony- was shot dead by unidentified armed men near the PAF base Faisal. He worked for Kashmir Press International.
A man was shot dead by two unidentified men near the Mari Shopping Centre.
Three rockets were fired on the house of Awami National Party leader Malik Ilyas in baghdada, near Punjab Regiment Centre. However, the rockets were misfired and hit nearcy houses.
An unidentified woman was gunned down in Orangi.
Karachi witnessed the bloodiest day of the recent wave of violence as a young man's bullet-riddled body was found from Qasba Colony during the on-going violence.
Hundreds of telephones were disconnected in Quetta after a cabinet housing phone utility equipment was blown up in Huda area.
The police defused a roadside bomb in Sambat area. No other detail was given.
an employee of the Punjab Civil Secretariat Muhammad Usman, a resident of Kacha Sanda,was gunned down by unidentified persons. He was the caretaker of the stationery store, S&GAD.
The body of an unidentified man was found under the Native's Jetty Bridge.
A police constable was gunned down outside his home in Rabbani Muhullah of Frontier Colony No.3.

MQM activist, Abdul Basit, was shot dead and his wife, Kiran was wounded when unidentified men on a motorbike opened fire right outside the former's house. Abdul Basit was a joint-incharge of the unit 9 of the MQM's organizational structure in Lyari Town.

As part of operations by Karachi Building Control Authority (KBCA), the KBCA squad came to raze an illegally constructed floors of a building in Bihar colony in Lyari town but were met with an angry mob that resisted and reportedly created a law and order situation. The KBCA squad had no option but to turn back.
A group of traders protested against the failure of the police to rid the area of crime.They burnt tyres and blocked the entrance of Hajipura police station.
Militants attacked the security forces checkpost in Spinal Raghzai area. While sources claim that 2 soldiers died in the attack, militants claim to have killed 5 soldiers.
Mirza Aftab Ahmed, a school teacher, was found shot dead. He had been shot several times and his body was riddled with bullets.

the people of the area, who were protesting against the firing of KDA  that injured a resident of Ziaul Haq Colony, lit a bonfire at Rashid Minhas road disrupting traffic between Gulshan Chowrangi and UBL Sprts Complex. following the firing the protesters dispersed and then remerged claiming that 2 residents had died. they pelted vehicles with stones and lit tyres on fire. they also damaged traffic signals and marriage halls located at Rashid Minhas road. the police fired tear-gas shells to disperse them. 5 miscreants were arrested for creating a law and order situation.
A bomb placed under a bridge on the Quetta-Taftan highway went off partially damaging the bridge. A spokesman for the Baloch Republican Army claimed responsibility for the attack.
One person was killed and nine others were seriously injured when a bomb went off in Pasrur town planted under the seat of the bicycle on Sunday. Authorities told that the bomb was Indian made

The Dera Bugti district chief of Jamaat-i-Islami, Amaanullah Bugti and two other men were killed and another was injured when their car was ambushed near Sui and armed men opened fire on them. The reason behind the killing was said to be an old tribal enmity.

A large number of lawyers and political and social activsts held a protest demonstration outside the Supreme  Court, demanding the reinstatement of Chief Justice Iftikhar Mohammad Chaudhary. The protesting lawyers beat two pro-government lawyers in the Supreme Court, and their colleagues outside the premise thrashed some persons allegedly belonging to an intelligence agency when they tried to creep into the protest rally wearing black coats.
Shabbir Ahmad killed his sister-in-law on suspicion of her bad character.
A body was found in the Badhber area which appeared to have been dumped there after being killed by suspected militants.
Taliban seiged a house in Dadukhel suspecting that some criminals were hiding in the house. In the ensuing shootout, three Talibans and four 'criminals' were killed.

Two rockets were fired from the Jandran mountains by terrorists and landed in an open space, causing no loss of life or any injuries. Officials claimed they were meant to target the FC checkpost but could not do so.
A jatoi tribesman was gunned down by the Mahar tribesmen because of previous disputes between the two tribes. Tension has mounted in the area since
Two armed men on a motorbike shot and killed Qari Abdul Mateen, who was a prayer leader, and his associate Hafiz Usman.

It was alleged by Aftab Ahmad Shaikh, the Deputy Governor of the MQM(A) Coordination Committee, that policemen in plain clothes had stopped MQM Coordination Committee member Begum M.G.Siddiqui and threatened her with 'dire consequences' if she didn't divulge certain information. This was reported in the context of the MQM(A)'s claim that the government and intelligence agencies were attempting to cruch the Mohajir community politically and economically.
Two bomb were defused from the Talaab Sheikh Maula Bux area of Sialkot.
armed tribesmen attacked FC post in Pathar Nullah. The rockets exploded in open areas, causing no casualty or damage. FC personnel retaliated and fired rockets on positions af assailants.

Two policemen were shot dead in the Model Colony, Malir after two culprits opened fire on them when they signalled the suspicious car to stop. Shafi Rind, Malir town police officer stated that terrorism could not be ruled out.
Two tribesmen were killed in an armed clash between two groups of the Daher tribe. The reason for the clash was not reported.
unidentified killers shot dead the private security guard of the Norwegian Embassy on 24-dec-06.
The bomb disposal squad defused a 10-Kg bomb planted at a girl's seminary, after locals informed the police about the presence of a suspicious container.

Students of the Sindh Punjabi Students Association attacked Sindhi students, injuring several of them. The JSTPSF claimed that when some of their members went to the college to settle the dispute they too were attacked by the SPSA.

A police constable was killed and three others were injured after an exchange of fire between two rival groups in the Satellite town area. Constable Abdullah was passing through the area along with other policemen when caught up in the cross fire. Policemen Mumtaz, Farman and Rehmatullah were injured in the incident.

Following the assassination of an activist of the MQM-H, other activists reached the district courts in Malir, ransacked a confectioner's shop and resorted to firing into the air, which left several people injured.  Incidents of firing were also reported from the areas of Saudabad, Khokhrapar and other parts of Malir.

Militants attacked the house of tribal elder Yar Akbar with rockets for allegedly spying for security forces and political administration.The army, that was deployed in the area, rushed to the spot and engaged the militants in battle, forcing the assailants to retreat.
A man was killed while four of his companions were wounded when their car was ambushed by unidentified  assailants in Shareefabad, Baldia Town.
Two people died while two others were injured in poll related clashes in Abbotabad.
Two explosions were heard from different parts of Quetta. However, the exactly location of the blasts could not be ascertained.
Violence re-erupted between the IJT and PSF as both groups exchanged fire in National College. 1 18-year-old boy was caught in the crossfire and received injuries.
A vehicle carrying personnel of the Sibi Scouts hit the landmine in Dera Bugti killing one security man and injuring four others. The vehicle was also completely destroyed.
In North Waziristan Agency, militants fired six rockets at a paramilitary base near Mirali town. No other detail was given.
Unidentified men shot dead a vegetable seller- Muhammad Rafiq, from Malakand in NWFP- standing next to his pushcart.
A group of militants attacked a patrolling party of security forces on the Palai-Katlang road. In retaliation the troops gunned down four militants in the exchange of fire.
Members of PSF and IJT exchanged fire on campus, causing damage to the car of a professor. The two groups have exchanged fire on several occasions during the last 3 days.
Two people were shot dead in Dak Ismail village in the Pabi area by their rivals on Tuesday.
A youth Muhammad Asif, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcylists when he was coming out of  his house in Chak Sada. No other information was given.
At least 7 Nato tankers were destroyed at a parking lot when a bomb planted on one of them exploded. The explosion caused a fire that engulfed and destroyed 6 other tankers.
Two men were gunned down outside a tea shop near Shabir Chowk in New Karachi when armed men on motorcycles opened fire on them, killing them on the spot.

A student activist, Syed Wasif Aziz, President of the United Student Front and a member of the central executive committee of the Jamaat-i-Islami, was shot dead by unknown people on motorcycles.  It is not known who was behind the attack or what their motives were.
Election day violence claimed the lives of 2 people during clashes between rival groups.
a man and a woman who had eloped were executed on a jirga's order in Kala Dhaka.

Police continued a crackdown on PPP workers and leaders in Punjab to deter them from making arragements for the reception of Asif Ali Zardari. Atleast 70 activists were arrested. Most of the arrests were made in Rawlapindi.
A student was killed after he stepped on an improvised explosive device outside a seminary in South Waziristan. Suspected militants had reportedly planted the device outside the seminary.

Following the assassination of senoir MQM member Farooq Baig that sparked anger among MQM workers, Karachi witnessed a number of arson attacks that the police claimed targeted mostly vehicles owned by 'people from a particular ethnic background'. A carpet showroom was set ablaze.
Three people were killed and as many injured in a tribal clah. Several people were arrested. No further details were given.
3 people were injured when unidentified persons opened fire in Sher Shah on Tuesday.
A man was shot dead in North Karachi.

Many PSF workers were said to have been injured in the second baton charge of the month of SP office premises. The PSF workers were protesting at alleged kidnappings of some Government Zamindar Science College students by local transporters.

15 civilians were killed and 12 others were injured during the shelling in Karo Dara. According to locals the security forces mistook a group of displaced people for militants and began shelling them. Police said only 4 people had been killed and 12 injured.

Two unidentified men knocked on the door of Ashraf's house in Qaimkhani colony and held him at knife point. They then barged into the house and slit the throat of his wife, Bushra Khatoon, and fled. The motive behind the murder could not be ascertained.
Two police constables, Mohammad Asif and Jamal Baig, were shot dead by unidentified people at a police picket.
A man and his wife fell victim to an old dispute over ownership of a plot of land. They were killed by their relatives.
The police found four bodies in a gunny bag with bearing torture marks.

For the second time in 12 hours, the Indian BSF resorted to shelling. The shelling lasted 2 hours and killed 1 villager in addition to injuring 15 people including 3 Rangers personnel. The Chenab Rangers retaliated by firing back.
Some unidentified armed assailants gunned down Mohammad BachalPhull, a driver of Agriculture Development Bank, and fled.
At least 50 people were injured, 40 of them lawyers, when fierce clashes broke out between the police and members of the legal fraternity at the Lahore High Court.
A man was killed in cross fire between two rival transporters' groups. The reason behind the clash was not reported.
Rafique had been living in orangi town whose bullet-riddled body was found in the same locality on Wednesday. The victim was former MQM activist.

2 people were killed and 20 were injured outside DC's office on Saturday when people of different political parties gathered and protested against the kidnapping of a girl allegedly by a Zamindar. Police opened fire and use teargas shells to disperse the crowd.
Militants fired a mortar shell that hit a checkpost manned by volunteers of a peace committee. 4 volunteers were injured in the attack.

Akbar ali shot dead his unmarried sister Jan Bibi and a man, Abdullah, in the pretext of karo-kari. Akbar Ali, surrendered before police along with the pistol he used in the crime. Abdullah's father lodged an FIR against the murder of his son however no one turned to lodge an FIR in connection with the female Jan Bibi.

Traffic on the Lahore-Multan Road remained suspended following a clash between two rival groups of the veterinary university. Reports suggested that the transporters' musclemen refused to let students get on the bus. The injured protesters were shifted to the hospital.
An explosive substance was hurled at the City Police Station on Thursday. However no loss of life was reported.
A young man was shot dead by unidentified gunmen.

The recent wave of political killings continued as gunbattles raged in Landhi and surrounding areas. An activist of the MQM was gunned down in Chishti Nagar in sector 11 1/2 of Orangi Town when armed men opened fire, killing him on the spot.
Shots fired by snipers hiding on a hill by the Islamabad Highway hit one of the cars used by PM Gillani. Two bullets hit one of the three cars used by the prime minister.
PMl-N workers protested against the arrest of party workers during the general strike the day before by burning tyres on the road.
Indian forces fired several mortars across the LoC. Details are not available.

militants killed a man they alleged was spying for the US forces stationed across the border in Afghanistan. Afghan national Imran Khan's body was found in the main bazaar of Razmak town. A notes was found on the body saying that he was spying for the US. he had been kidnapped from the area a few days ago.

following the supreme courts decision that Nawaz and Shahbaz Sharif were ineligibe to contest or hold public office, PML-N workers and leaders staged a protest in which they set tyres on fire. Security forces did not react to the incident.
An 'alleged' terrorist was injured in an encounter with the police in Gulbahar.
Dr. Qamar Hussain's car was attacked by armed motorcyclists. In the firing, Dr. Hussain was killed while his driver was injured. The Baloch Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the attack
Humayyon police recovered a beheaded body near the police station. The identity of the person could not be ascertained.

As the news of the murder of the Jeay Sindh activist's murder spread some youths in Khokhrapar pelted stones at passing vehicles and tried to block the roads by erecting barricades. police came and controlled theh situation.

Ten militants were killed and fourteen others were injured when helicopter gunships bombed militant hideouts during an operation by the security forces in Tarli area of the Kurram Agency. Two soldiers lost their lives and three others were injured.
Two explosive devices were recovered from separate areas in Mardan.

Following a dacoity at a shop, in which the shopkeeper was injured, shopkeepers of the area closed their businesses, blocked the main road, burnt tyres and chanted slogans against the police for their failure to provide security to the business community. Policemen rushed to the spot and assured the protesters that the criminals would be caught.

As part of the MQM protest day against the victimisation and arrest of its women workers, a total strike was observed throughout the troubled localities in Karachi. Incidents of heavy shooting were reported from the MQM dominated areas, however, no injury was reported.
Gas supply from 6 wells to the main Sui purification plant was suspended after a pipeline was blown up in Bugti colony of Dera Bugti.
security forces blew up the houses of Qari Shakeel, the vice chief of the Mohmand Taliban, his father-in-law and a suspected militant. Several other houses in the surrounding area were also damaged.
An Afghan refugee was shot dead by unidentified gunmen.
Two persons were shot dead and three seriously injured when two rival groups of village Lohyanwala.

12 people were killed and 50 others were injured when explosives stored in a house, which also had a seminary, exploded. The house was owned by Riaz Ahmad Kamboh, a religious teacher and reported to be an active member of a banned militant organization. there is no information on who is responsible for the attack.

PPP co-chairman Benazir Bhutto alleged that some people drove past her residence and opened fire at the house before fleeing. She also alleged that when she asked the police party standing outside to chase the cuplrits they 'refused to do so'.
The bullet-riddled body of Wakil Hussain, a PPP worker and member of the Salam group, was found in Orangi.
3 oil tankers were damaged in a blast.
A home-made device exploded on the Elementary road in Mastung. No casualty was reported but the windowpanes of some nearby houses were smashed.
Several civilians have been killed and injured in different areas of the tribal region during shelling by security forces from FC camp in Bhai Dag and Mohammad Gat.

Following the assassination of Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Nadeem of the Aalmi Tahaffuz-i-Khatam-i-Nabuat, as people took to the streets and started firing in the air. A large number of people, which included students of a seminary gathered at Patel Hospital where the body of the deceased was taken.
Three people were killed and two were injured when an improvised explosive device blasted outside a mosque when the people were coming out after the prayers.

Residents of Mandi Faizabad town blocked the Lahore-Jaranwala Road for 2 hours in order to protest against the growing incidents of theft and robbery in the area.
