They burnt tyres and chanted slogans against the police of \giving a free hand to outlaws\". They alleged that the SHO concerned refused to register cases. They also demanded that night patrolling be intensified."

A cricket match being played in Majra Kalan in Sambrial took a bloody turn when three unidentified people opened fire indiscriminately, killing four people and injuring nine. The accused left, shouting that they had avenged the murder of two relatives.

Five unknown gunmen robbed a man at Sarrafa Bazar at gunpoint around 3:30 pm and were confronted by a police party when they tried to escape through narrow alleys and roads of New Sarrafa Bazaar.  They opened fire on the police, creating panic and a stampede.  Two policemen and one betel leaf dealer were wounded in the firing.  Head Constable Zafar Iqbal succumbed to his wounds on the way to the hospital.
A low-intensity bomb blast damaged the railway tracks and suspended rail traffic from Karachi for a few hours.
A mysterious explosion caused panic in the cantonment area. The residents felt as if a bomb had exploded.
an IJT activist, Ahsan Ansari, was kidnapped and killed by unknown persons. His body was found in the airport area.
A bomb exploded 100 yards from the house of an MQM Senator and 500 metres from the headquarters of the MQM.3 people were killed and thirteen injured.
A man was killed in Orangi Extension.

A partially decomposed body was discovered from under the Jam Sadiq Ali bridge.The body had no injury marks however the right ear was chopped off. The body was identified as Gul Shah, a tanker driver who had arrived in Karachi on Dec 17 and had been missing since Dec 18.

Police defused 2 bombs that were left in a barber shop wrapped in gift packing. The barber noticed the gifts after two men left his shop, and called the police immediately. According to Model Town SP, the bombs were meant to be used somewhere else and someone left them in that area.
A rocket, which failed to explode hit the fields in Pakwa village near Peshawer. It was a russian-made rocket.
the body of an unidentified person was found in Isa Nagri.

The killing of a milkman by some kidnappers sparked a protest by the local people who blocked a road and burnt old tyres and chanted slogans against the government and police. They demanded the arrest of the accused. The protesters dispersed when the police assured them that the accused would be arrested soon.
security forces shelled suspected positions of militants in Kotkai, Serai Maule Khan and Barwand areas of South Waziristan in reaction to the attack on the checkpost on Jandola road.

Six people were shot dead at the Abul Fazil Abbas Imambargah in Pir Illahi Baksh Colony when unidentified men, armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols, entered the Imambargah and shot them dead while they were getting ready for their Fajr prayers. According to an eye-witness, the terrorists were seen leaving in a Suzuki Hi-roof and a motorcycle.
Two buses were burnt down.
A khasadar (tribal policeman) shot and killed a truck driver because he refused to pay him illegal tax at a checkpost on the Peshawar Torkham Road.
In Deh Balodai of Mehar taluka, unidentified attackers shot and killed Muharram Ali and fled after committing the murder.
Bakht Bibi was murdered by her brother who 'suspected her character'.

a tribal lashkar killed two Afghan nationals during a clash with a group of militants and set houses on fire that were owned by the Taliban and their supporters. Two fighters of the lashkar sustained injuries. Taliban sources have denied suffering any casualties. the fighting was triggered by a suicide attack in a mosque in Hayagay village.

Two personnel of the Pakistan Air Force and a child accompanying them were injured when a bomb exploded near their vehicle on Kohat Road. The police did not believe that the attack was intended to target the PAF personnel, and added that the bomb was planted on an under-construction shop, which went off while the vehicle was passing through. They said that three brothers had a dispute amongst themselves over the shop, but made no conclusive statement as to what they believed was the reason behind the blast.
Irfan Lahoti, a resident of Lyari, was found dead with torture and bullet marks all over his body.

As part of the on-going violence in Karachi, occupants of a car sprayed two members of the Jamat-i-Islami with bullets and then chased them as they were taken to the Abbasi Shaheed Hospital, opening fire on them again as a result injuring three pedestrians. The two died at the hospital as doctors ran for cover leaving the patients behind.
Helicopter gunships pounded three militant hideouts in Mirandi, Chinarak and Sangraba area of Kurram, killing twenty militants and injuring several others.
A policeman was shot dead, reportedly by militants, in Swat's Char Bagh area. It is believed that he was killed as a reaction to the action taken against the Lal Masjid by the government.

Four rockets were fired but all of them missed their target i.e. Pakistan Aereonautical Complex. One rocket landed on the roof of non-commissioned officer's mess, two hit airmen's residences and the fourth rocket exploded near the field in Qutba village.
Head Constable Jumma Khan was shot and killed by armed motorcyclists while he was on his way home.
A bomb was planted inside the house of Izzat Shah and when it blew up it damaged the house and a shop was burnt. There were no casualties.
An elderly person was shot dead in the outskirts of Charsadda by the military.
Mr Ghulam Abbas Robera, brother of MPA Shafqat Abbas Robera was gunned down by his rivals in Okara on Wednesday. One rival was also killed.
More than two dozen people were injured in Gujranwala when they were attacked by rivals.
Following the assassination of 2 ASWJ activists, enraged people resorted to aerial firing to force shopkeepers to close their businsses.
the two-day-old body of an unidentified man was found in an under-construction house in Gulshan-i-Millat, Korangi. The body bore marks of torture.
A woman was killed in the Hatli village of Nakyal Sector, Kotli, in Indian shelling from across the Line of Control. The Indians used machine-guns, mortar shells and medium artillery.

5 people were killed and 2 others were injured in a sectarian clash in Takht Hazara Village on Friday.Some people were leading campaign against Ahmedi's Baitul Zikr as a result of which Ahmedis clashed with them.
2 people were injured in a clash between the Chachar and Kalhoro tribes over a land dispute in Sohrab Chachar Village on Sunday

An unidentified man in his 30's was found dead at a commercial center in Liaquatabad. Torture and bullet wounds were visible on the body. The police believe that the man was kidnapped and subject to severe torture.
Militants fired 2 rockets at  the Kohat Cantonment. The rockets landed in Shiekhan, near a military installation, and Happy Valley, in the STC ground of the army, without causing any damage.
Roadside bomb blasted while the security personnel were going from Katcot to Khar.
Four people were killed and 15 others injured when security forces pounded residential areas in villages in North Waziristan.
A fifty year old man was killed in Mominabad.
Two blind rockets were fired into the cantonment area of Quetta. One landed and exploded in a house near Jinnah Ground on Tufail Road, damaging a wall and windows.

After the death of an under trial prisoner, a 5 hour clash ensued in the district jail. Angry prisoners held staff hostage and demanded immediate action against the death of the prisoner. Police had to resort to teargas shelling and aerial firing. Unofficial reports say 4 prisoners were killed and dozens injured.
An activist of MQM, Nooruddin, was kidnapped from his private residence and shot. His body was recovered from vehicle in a ground in K-Area.
Two persons were shot dead and 7 others were critically injured over a land dispute when a rival group opened indiscriminate fire upon the other.

A suicide bomber blew himself up near the a missionary school, opposite the Pakistan International Airlines office on the Mall Road. The bomber was on foot and detonated while fleeing from security personnel. SSP Ghulam Hussain stated that the militants who had been carrying out suicide attacks in the city belonged to the same group.
the police found the beheaded body of a man in a sack in Asif Town. The head was found at some distance.
One Latif was killed and two others injured when unidentified gunmen attacked their jeep and opened indiscriminate fire for unknown reasons.
Militants blew up a paramilitary vehicle by remote control.
A PPP activist was beaten up by a union council naib nazim near Railway road, Gujrat. Later, the union council naib nazim was also beaten up by the PPP supporters.
Six persons including five militants were killed in an exchange of fire over a property dispute.
The Chenab Rangers thwarted a major attempt by the Indian Security Forces to fence the Sialkot Working Boundary.

A mob killed a blasphemy accused after a local cleric had declared him an infidel. According to sources the accused had desecrated the holy quran following a quarrel with his wife. His uncle filed a blasphemy case on him but before the police could get to him a mob of around 400 people shot him dead.

As part of the violence on the second day of a two-day strike called by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM), protesters set on fire three vehicles and three people were reportedly injured in shooting in Latifabad.

A man allegedly killed a mother of four in the name of 'honour' in Harbanspura, Lahore, when he shot her dead over the issue of an extra-martial affair. He was later arrested on the complaint of the victims husband.

Nine people were killed and 13 others injured over an old anmity between the Ogahi and Teghani tribesmen in the Naparkot village. The Teghanis allegedly attacked the Ogahis in Naparkot vilage. The Ogahis retaliated and the exchange of fire continued for six hours.
According to locals, three persons were killed and three others were injured when a stray shell fell on the house of a resident of the Shamshah area in the Baizai tehsil of Mohmand.

After a brief encounter, the police arrested a 'key member of the Lashkar-i-Jhangvi in Karachi'. The police claim he had planned to attack the procession taken out on the 7th and 8th of Muharram. Arms, ammunition and suicide vests were recovered from him as well.
Militants planted improvised explosive devices inside the Government Higher Secondary School and Gobernment Primary School in Zaimdara which exploded, destroying the school buildings.
Six rockets were fired on FC check psot in Talngo area. Balochistan Liberation Army has claimed responsibility of the attack

Seven people were injured and a hotel was set on fire when two religious groups clashed over ownership of an old mosque. The owner of the land around the mosque had sold the property a year ago except the plot of the mosque. He had handed over the mosque to people of his own sect. Clashes began when a religious  leader along with other members of his sect came out of the mosque after prayers and were attacked by people belonging to the other sect. After the incident, baton-wielding youths asked the shops and traders to close down, and they took a procession out on the main highway.

Three men fired at the house of the Principal Municipal Degree College and ran away. The Principal was not at home at the time. The presumed target suspects that the IJT is responsible as he had refused their request to shut the university for an IJT procession earlier. The IJT had allegedly threatened him with 'consequences'.
Unknown people set fire to a mini bus of route KL while it was travelling.

Three activists of the PPP were gunned down and four others injured allegedly by firing of PML (N) workers. The PPP workers were going to congratulate PPP candidate  Abdullah Virk on his victory. The attackers fled after firing at them.

Shopkeepers Afzaal Butt and Afzaal Bhatti had an old dispute over a four marla piece of land. Afzaal Bhatti started construction of the boundary wall of the disputed plot. Knowing about the construction Afzaal Butt reached the site and attacked his rivals with a knife, killing Afzaal Bhatti and injuring another. Afzaal Butt was shot dead.
A man shot dead his mother, sister and former brother-in-law on suspicion of loose morals.
A man was gunned down in UP More in North Karachi. The motive behind the murder could not be known.
Kasur police recovered a dead body of a man from Raj Bah in the Changa Manga forest.
at least 12 rockets were fired on FC fort in Dera Bugti, damaging the fort's walls. No casualty was reported however.
The unidentified body of a man was found near Saggian bridge
JUI-F organised a rally on the call of the Pak-Afghan Defence Council against the US-led attack on Afghanistan. They burnt tyres and effigies of President Bush and chanted anti-American slogans.
troops pounded on remote village with artillery after militants fired rockets at security forces in Mir Ali area of North Waziristan. However, there was no immediate report of any casualty.
The body of an accountant was found with torture marks. The reason behind the killing is not known.

three armed men stormed into Government Primary school No3 in Bara Banda area and killed Ubaidullah, teacher, and Muhammad Hussain, son of Ghulam Muhammed. The accused had disputes with Ghulam Muhammed and wanted to settle them by killing his son.

Seven people had been so far reported killed in a clash between two tribes in Rojhan, Rajanpur district. Some armed men of the Sadvani tribe reportedly took away several cattle of the Umrani tribe. The infuriated Umranis opened fire on the Sadvani tribe's village, who returned fire.
Kahna police recovered the body of an unidentified man from a drain near Sua Asal, Kahna. According to the police, the body had some torture marks.
According to Malakand Levies officials five militants were killed in an exchange of fire with security forces in the Chinar Qalangai area in Malakand.
a man identified as Amir Muhammad Bugti was killed inlandmine blast when his tractor hit a landmine. Two other persons who were also in the tractor were injured.

Army Welfare Sugar Mill Workers Trade Union members were celebrating the restoration of their union by the Apex court when they tried to enter the mill but were stopped by the security guards, who apparently used batons and resorted to firing. Police and Rangers controlled the situation by firing tear-gas shells.

A woman was killed in the Chahal Khurd village, Qila Dedar Singh when her husband and villagers attacked her with stones and clubs, beating her to death because she had apparently opened up a brothel in the area.

Five suspected militants were killed when a US drone targeted a residential compound and a car in the Ghar Laley village of the Datakhel tehsil in North Waziristan.  A total of four missiles were fired in the strike. The area was considered to be a stronghold of the Taliban 'commander' Hafiz Gul Bahadur.
A policeman and a passer-by was killed and three constables were injured when unidentified armen men on a car opened fire on a police picket on Rashid Minhas Road.
A man was injured.
Three students of Polytechnic Institute, Khairpur (namely Mohammad Yousaf, Anis Abbass and Hasnein Raza) were allegedly attacked by Jeay Sindh activists.

The traders strike in Karor Lal Eisan (Leyyah) entered the fourth day of protest against the murder of PPP Shamshad Ali Khan. The protesters pelted law enforcers with stones. The police resorted to lathi-charge to disperse the protesters.
Two shops were set on fire.

Four tribal/separatist militants were killed as security forces used gunship helicopters to launch another operation in parts of Kohlu. Two members of security forces were also killed while an officer was killed. Security forces moved in Karmo-Wadh and Tatrani areas and used helicopter gunships for the attack.Azad Baloch claimed killing two FC men ina lanmine blast in Karmo Wadh area but official sources did not confirm the loss.

Tribal volunteers backed by security forces (Frontier Corp, Khasaddar force) demolished two residences of suspected militants by dynamite, in light of a previous agreement to provide security to the forces stationed inside the troubled region.
Police raided the house of an alleged murderer. A police constable was killed and another was seriously injured after an alleged murderer hurled hand grenades on them.
A man, Amir Shehzad, killed his father, sattar Ali, over a land dispute in Injra village. No other detail was given.

Abdul Aziz and Abdul Rasheed, who were the brothers of Abdul Navaid, were shot outside their house by members of a Lyari gang. The gang members came looking for Navaid, who was also a member of a rival Lyari gang, but after exchanging words with his brothers they shot them and fled. It is claimed that the incident was an attempt to take revenge by Navaid's rival gang members who are, \enjoying power these days due to their political clout in the area\". "

A group of PPP workers staged a demonstration in front of the parliament house to protest against the dissolution of National Assembly and dismissal of the Benazir Bhutto government. They raised slogans against President Farooq Leghari and set old tyres on fire. They dispersed after the police arrived.
Some incidents of firing and explosions were reported from different parts of the city of Nawabshah, but no loss of life or property was reported.

Later that same day, Shafeeq's supporters barged into the house of an MQM activist, Shaukat Lala, and shot him dead. While returning from Lala's house they spotted another MQM worker, Yaqoob Madda and opened fire on him as well.  A police official claimed the killings were the result of friction between criminal gangs having links with some political groups.

Other than the three targeted killings during the day, 4 people received bullet injuries in Landhi and Korangi. Since the report specifies that violence in Karachi on that day was for sectarian motives and due to factional fighting, the cause for these injuries is most probable one of the two reasons given. ; Follow-up: One of the people injured in Landhi, later identified as Sajid Ali, succumbed to his injuries on 07-Nov-94.

Two blasts blew up main pipelines of the Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited, which resulted in burn injuries to two people belonging to a nearby village, 50 sheep being burnt alive in the ensuing fire and damage to several nearby houses. ASP Chandio denies any evidence of sabotage, however, the SNGPL chief claimed that a bomb fuse was found and the watchmen had seen a projectile hit one of the pipeline causing a leak, which then later exploded.
A clash between protestors and the police took place at Chittian Hatian where some activists of the IJT pelted stones at the police and they retaliated with teargas shelling and baton charge.
A 50 year old woman was murdered on the the pretext of karo-kari. Police arrested two in connection to the murder.

A US drone targeted a vehicle, killing three Arab militants. However, local people claimed that no one was killed as the three Arabs had left the car before it was struck. Other sources claimed that the death toll was 4.
A 40 year old woman was killed by a stray bullet inside her house in Korangi.

An air hostess and her husband, traveling in their jeep, came under attack in block 2 of Kamran Chowrangi. The couple suffered multiple bullet wounds in the head and chest as armed men on a motorcycle opened fire on them, killing them on the spot.

A young boy, his mother and another family member were killed after an explosive device went off in the hands of the boy as he was playing with it in Neelum Valley. The bomb was believed to have been fired by Indian troops from across the LoC.
Two men shot dead the wife of their elder brother to claim ownership of 12 acres of land. No arrests were made.
A man, Ali Bakhsh Brohi, was murdered by unknown men in the Mouladad locality. According to officials the reason behind the killing was said to be an old feud.
A degree college for boys and a training institute was blown up. Taliban claimed responsibility for the event stating that the institutions were being used as military camps by security forces.

Mohammad Nazir, son of Said Rehman, resident of New Khankhel Koklian, was on his way home after offering Fajr prayers when he was shot dead by Waris Khan, son of Samandar Khan. They allegedly developed a rivalry over a Tablighi Jamaat issue

Mirza Suleman Baig, an affiliate of the Tehrik-i-Tahafaz-i-Pakistan tried to strangulate the counsel of Benzir Bhutto, Aitzaz Ahsan. He later confessed according to another report on the same page, that his real target was Benazir Bhutto.

Over 200 people from village Mureed protested against the release of 2 students from police custody. The students, who belonged to village Thoa Bahadur, had beaten up students from village Mureed and had been arrested by the police. The protesting villagers blocked the road, burnt tyres and chanted slogans against an adviser of Punjab Chief Minister who they alleged had gotten the students released. The City magistrate Chakwal reached the protest with a police contingent and assured the crowd that a case would be registered against the accused students, after which the protesters dispersed peacefully.
a young man was killed as a result of ethnic violence. In the past 24 hours 34 people had been killed as a result of ethnic violence. 50 miscreants have been arrested.
President of SQM-Hameed Asghar was intercepted allegedly by Usman and Muhammad Wasiqa while he was on his way to Khayaban-i-Sarwar on Wednesday
Anti-US demonstrations were held in Kurram Agency, headed by Maulana Amal Gul. A US flag and effigy of President Bush were burnt.
40 civilians including tribal elders were killed by a US drone strike in Nevi Adda Shega area on Thursday. There was a jirga in progress when the attack occurred

180 fishermen were on a fishing expedition when Indian force, believed to be naval personnel, allegedly attacked them. 176 fishermen and 30 boats were captured. 4 fishermen that managed to escape claimed that the incident took place in Pakistan's territorial waters.
Some masked men shot dead a government employee near Miramshah. No other information was given.
Allied Bank Vice-President Syed Amjad Ali was gunned down by unidentified gunmen on Ghazi Road, Factory Area.

Five people were killed and at least 10 others injured when they were attacked by their rivals while they were on their way to their hideout. It was learnt that the attackers had acted on a vengeful basis, and the two groups, that were both proclaimed offenders, had an old enmity between them. The police managed to arrest 3 of the proclaimed offenders, and recovered arms from their possession.
Nasrullah and his brother were attacked by armed men in a yellow cab. Both of them were shifted to the hospital where Nasrullah's brother succumbed to his injuries.
A man killed his mother after supecting her of having illicit relations. The police arrested the accused.
A worker of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement was shot earlier in the day. He succumbed to his injuries in the hospital.
Two personnel of the FC corps were injured in rocket attacks in the kohlu area. They also returned fire from where the rockets were launched.

Two deserters of the FC, who had joined the TTP were arrested and a 'ready-to-blow' suicide jacket, a pistol and FC uniforms were recovered from their possession. Police claim that the ex-FC men had planned a suicide attack on Pakistan Day (23rd March 2010). The arrest led to the capture of 3 more militants.
A blind rocket was fired at Quetta from the southern side of the city. It hit the house of a woman, wounding her slightly and damaging the house. No one claimed responsibility.

Dr Javed Ahmed Khan, an activists of the MQM, was shot dead by two armed motorcyclists outside his house. Dr Khan had recently been under pressure from both factions of the MQM to work for them and both factions have accused the other of being responsible for the killing.
A villager was injured as a result of Indian firing in Bajwat sector across the Line of Control.
A young woman's body was found stuffed in a gunny bag from an under-construction park in the remit of the Nazimabad police station.

Two MQM workers were killed and another was wounded in a raid in Ranchhore Lines. The police said that a party of the Crimes Investigation Agency (CIA) raided Shia Compound at Allah Mir Chowk and a shootout followed. In the encounter, Asif Khatri and Mohammad Hassan were killed and one other MQM worker was injured. Two MQM workers were also arrested.

Suspected militants killed a key Govt ally in the restive south waziristan tribal region. He had played a pivotal role in opening up the shakai valley the last bastion of foreign militants to the govt and also helped in striking a peace deal between the local militants and the army.

three tribesmen were killed and two others suffered injuries in a gunbattle between security forces and armed tribesmen in troubled district of Kohlu. Tribal sources claimed that security forces had suffered huge loses in the fighting. They claimed that at least six FC men were killed and three suffred injuries in the gunbattle.
On the second day of the strike called by the JSTPP, some miscreants resorted to aerial firing.
One person, Haider Zaman, was killed when unknown persons opened fire on him in the factory where he worked and shot him dead.
A sub-inspector deputed at the Anti car Lifting Cell was shot dead in Gulshan I Hadeed area by unidentified armed men in a car.
An unidentified man was tortured to death in Mowach Goth. The victim could not be identified.
Shabbar Shah, a Pir (a spiritual leader) was found brutally murdered inside his house. The reason for the killing was not specified.
The body of an unidentified man was found from outside the Liberty Plaza, Gulberg on Wednesday
Five people were wounded in a shooting incident at a Kashmiri Imambargah in Gulbahar area.

Parts of Liquatabad and Jamshed Quarters remained tense when angry protesters threw a cracker inside the residential quarters in protest of the death of an MQM activist in prison the day before. They claimed he had been severly tortured, however, the police stated he died of a \heart attack\". "
Ajab Gul was seriously injured when a minibus of National Coach Service was fired upon.

Ten policemen and six others were injured when a suicide bomber blew himself up after getting out of a car that was stopped for search on the Bund Road. At least four vehicles were damaged in the blast.
Two boys were killed in a firing incident by unknown people in Liaquatabad.
6 people were killed and 26 people were injured when security forces resorted to heavy fire and shelling after militants attacked an army base.

official sources said that after the landmine incident earlier in the day which claimed lives of three security personnel, nearly 40 tribesmen attacked Pirkoh gas field using heavy weapons, including rockets, against security forces. Security officers deployed in the area retaliated by returning fire and during the exchange of fire 12 tribesmen were killed. however Mr. Agha Shah Bugti, Spokesman of Bugti Tribe, claims that after the landmine incident, security forces raided the area and arrested 12 tribesmen. he said, \All 12 tribesmen were shot dead in custody by the FC men in reprisal for the killing of three security men in a landmine explosion.\""
The body of a police constable was found from Choona Depot in Liaquatabad. According to the polcie he had been kidnapped and tortured before being killed.
An \ethnic group\" blocked the road for two hours by burning tyres. They were protesting against the murder of Ghulam Mustafa, who was gunned down on Sunday."
A head constable of police was killed when unidentified men opened fire on a police picket.
2 women were killed in different parts of AJK by Indian cross firing.
A bullet-riddled body was found in Khuzdar; Follow up: The body was identified as one belonging to an activist of the BNM.
armed Pechuho tribesmen killed a girl and her lover on the pre-text of karo-kari.
A security guard at Safari Villas was shot dead by some persons.
Some people hurled a grenade into the house of Haji Musa. Haji Musa was killed while his son was injured.
A carpenter, Akbar, sustained bullet injuries when he was shot at by people in a white car.
A hand grenade was lobbed near a police checkpost. No causualties occurred.
A checkpost in Sarlara area was damaged when it was hit by rockets fired by militants. Two soldiers were injured in the incident.
A militant was killed during a search operation launched by security forces.
Brothers Noor and Mazhar opened fire  on Kizar Abbas and his father Ghulam Haider over a land dispute between the two parties.

A clash between the MSF and a rival students' alliance resulted in an exchange of fire at the Government College of Technology. The police tried to intervene but the students pelted stones on them as well as opened fire on them. The police arrested one student.
Armed militants blew up a gas pipeline in Pir Koh area, suspending gas supply to a number of areas

A rocket hit a 3 storey building in Quetta. Windows and glass of several other buildings were broken. No casualties were reported. This is the first time, since the last 10 months, that a densely populated area, close to a busy shopping area of the city has been targetted. the rocket was fired from an isolated place in the south of the city.
A powerful bomb explosion rocked the Kohlu township of Marri tribal agency.
Ghulam Qadir, a former secretary general of the PPP and his colleague were both gunned down  after being kidnapped in Orangi Town.
Unidentified motorcyclists shot dead a man on Mauripur Road. Police suspected that the killing was part of the fighting within rival gangs operating in Lyari.

Police constable, Asif, who was posted at the residence of a senior police officer on security duty, was gunned down by two men on a motorbike. The victim was on his way home from a shop when the incident took place.
Troops, backed by helicopter gunships targeted militant hideouts, destroying 3 compounds and killing 6 militants.
An old man was injured in Indian firing across LoC in Nakyal sector on Tuesday
A man was shot dead in Federal Capital area. Doctors and police who saw the body said the victim was subjected to severe torture.

Four armed men attacked the police escorting two under-trial prisoners at the district courts. The police returned fire and injured one of the assailants. They managed to arrest 2 while the other 2 escaped.
Three people inclduing a woman and an eight year old girl were killed when two rival tribes of Bugti and Jakhrani clashed over a land dispute in Mundrani village in Nasirabad.
Rana Muhammad Afzal, the president of the Anjuman-i-Fatwarian, was attacked and severly injured by Abdul Karim Qanungo and 40 accomplices who were armed with sophisticated weapons and rods.
3 people were killed and 18 others were injured in a rocket fired by unknown assailants near Sariab Railway crossing on Wednesday.

a large number of people staged a protest demonstration and blocked the Therhi railway Phatak against the demolition of shops, hotels and other structures on the road and its surrounding areas. They also burnt tyres on the Sukkur-Khairpur road.they raised slogans against the TMA Khairpur police. the police tried to convince the protesters to end their protest but failed.
Unidentified persons fired seven rockets on Kohlu township.
jet fighters bombed various militant infested areas in Panyali and Ambar tehsil. There have been no reports of casualties.
A brother shot his sister in the name of Honour. She was allegedly having illicit relations with another man.

Recovery of two decomposed bodies of minor girls- Hajra, 8, and Sassi Barejo, 5- who lived in Baricha-para and had gone missing on 20-Feb-04. A report was registered at the police station, however, according to residents the police had declined to register a case and were generally reluctant to search for the girls. Follow-up: Their bodies were found at a vetenary hospital that was under the use of the Gadap Police station. According to initial findings the girls were sexually abused, Hajra was axed to death and some parts of her abdomen were eaten by stray dogs while Sassi was shot in the head from behind. 3 policemen have been arrested for negligence murder, the fourth policeman is absconding. the government has compensated the families with Rs.200,000 each. Chief Minister, Sardar Ali Mohammad Mahar, has suspended all the officials-from SHO to constable- posted at Gadap at the time of the recovery of the girls. Follow-up: According to Syed Kamal Shah, police were not involved in the incident. He said that the girls had been taken to the house of Piral, where Zahid, Manzoor and Hanif had raped Hajra. They then axed her and shot Sassi in the head and dumped their bodies at the place next to the police station. He said that there was a dispute between the killers and the families of Hajra and Sassi. He also stated that the culprits wanted to divert the attention of the police away from the theft case the assailants were implicated it.

A woman was axed to death by her brother for pressuring him to give her 'dowry' on the insistence of her in-laws at laliyan village. She even complained of her in-laws torturing her to get the money. The brother fled right after killing her.

At least twelve militants were killed in two bomb blasts that took place in the Tharkho Khas and Tora Dara areas of Tirah valley that hit two vehicles carrying TTP militants. The first blast killed three while the second killed eight more. A passerby resportedly affiliated with Laskhar-i-Islam was also killed. According to sources, the area where the incident took place is inhabited by the Kukikhel tribe that has been resisting the Taliban militants and recently raised a lashkar of volunteers against the Taliban.
6 militants were killed in a clash between them and security forces in Kabal on Tuesday. 2 security personnel were also injured.
A private car was  burnt near UP Mor in North Karachi.
The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as a private car was torched within the remit of the Mobina Town police station.
A low intensity device exploded on a roadside, injuring two people.
Moosa Khan was killed and his three friends were injured when 3 men on a motorbike opened indiscriminate fire in the area.
A man was wounded in 'Sniper firing' in Orangi Extension.

Armed men, seeking revenge for an earlier murder, killed two brothers and injured the third brother when they opened indiscriminate fire on the victims house. The injured brother was the target of the attack, who escaped the scene in a wounded condition. According to police, the assailants were seeking revenge of a murder done by Nawaz, the injured brother, some years ago.

Activists of MQM-H burnt scores of US and Indian flags and effigies of the country's leaders to express their indignation over the policies of the two countries towards Pakistan. MQM-H sources claimed that their procession was attacked by the rival MQM (Altaf) group and also by the police who resorted to aerial fire in an attempt to disperse the activists.

Four students were injured when two student groups of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF) and the PSF clashed in the DHQ hospital. According to reports, the two groups had clashed previously at the Government College for Boys and were there for treatment when they began chanting slogans against each other and a clash ensued. The police and Frontier Constabilary had to be called in to control the situation.
Three people were injured in 'sniper firing' in Malir.
A police constable was stabbed and injured severely by unidentiied people in Ahmad Nager village. No motive behind the attack was mentioned in the report.
Residents of the Peoples Colony blocked the Faisalabad-Jaranwala road by burning tyres.  They were protesting against the WASA officials for failing to rectify the defectted sewage system.

At least 43 people were killed and 60 others injured when a suicide bomber blew himself up during a mourning procession for Moharram on M.A.Jinnah Road near the Light House area. The blast took place at the front of the procession where the security was tightest. According to a police officer, the bombing had taken place right between a police post and scouts' camp. As two scouts and a Rangers official lost their lives as well. As soon as the police reached the spot, they were greeted by angry processioners who pelted them with stones; Follow up: Taliban claimed reponsibility for the attack.
Former MQM-Haqiqi activist-Waqar Ahmed was shot dead by unknown assailants in Landhi on friday

Police intecepted two motorcyclists, alleged to be invovled in terrorist activities and told them to stop. The suspects started firing at the police which led to a shootout, resulting in both suspects getting killed. The suspects were identified as Dr. Umer Kundi and Adil. The were allegedly involved in the terrorist attacks on Manawan training centre, Rescue 15 in Lahore and the GHQ in Rawalpindi.
Eight rockets were fired at the Razmak Scouts fort. Three of them landed inside the camp, while five others missed their target and landed outside. No casualties or property damage was reported.
A man and a woman were clubbed to death by four relativs of the woman in Shah Jamal over suspicion of illicit relations.
6 people belonging to the Bugti tribe were injured when their vehicle hit a landmine on the roadside while they were on their way to Sui.
A man, with the help of an accomplice, threw acid on a recently married woman in Glotiyaan Kurd village of Daska tehsil for rejecting his proposal and marrying someone else.

Five officials of the Pakistan Mineral Department were kidnapped from the PMDC Colony in the Sorrange coalmines area. The Baloch Liberation Army's spokesman claimed responsibility for the kidnapping and threatened to kill them. He said the kidnapping was a reaction to the operation in Chamalang and Kohlu.
An unidentified woman, believed to be a factory worker, was tortured and killed in Orangi Town. The motive behind the killing could not be ascertained.
clash overa tribal dispute between rival groups.
Mohammad Baqar was shot dead by 5 accused over the distribution of water.
A remote controlled bomb went off killing 3 people and injuring 18 others in Dera Murad Jamali on Thursday.
Over a dozen armed tribesmen were killed in Peekal area of Dera Bugti when 5 vehicles of alleged miscreants came under attack during a gunbattle between security forces and armed militants.
A military convoy escaped a bomb blast while two shops were destroyed in the attack in the limits of the Matni police station in Sharikera village.
Muhammad Yameen, son of Phulwan Khan Babar, was shot dead by 4 armed men over a land dispute.
A young shopkeeper was gunned down in Sharifabad in the violence that followed two sectarian attacks on two Imambargahs early in the morning.

Rockets were fired on the paramilitary Scouts Camp in Wana, the region's head quarters. The rockets hit an empty building in the southern part of the camp and partially damaged it but did not cause any injury. The Scouts responded by firing medium-range artillery.
Mohammad Shabar was shot dead by two unidentified individuals. The reason for the murder was not specified.

It was reported that students were attacked in Liaquat Medical College, leaving 28 of them injured. No details given. ; Follow-up: It was claimed by NSSO that JSSF students attacked Punjabi students. This claim was made during a protest held by NSSO against the violence on campus. During the protest, some students also chanted slogans against Mohajir students and the MQM, claiming that the latter was responsible for 'uncertainty' in Sindh.
A US drone fired two missiles at a compound in Miramshah, North Waziristan, killing four suspected militants and injuring two others. A vehicle was also destroyed.
The bullet riddled body of a young man was found. The motive behindt he killing could not be ascertained.

Militants of an extremist group opened fire on the residents of Sakhi Colony due to which President of Working Committee Sikander Ali Soomro was injured on Monday. It is alleged that accused group used to run liquour, norcotics and gambling den.
a Security man received injuries in gunbattle with aremd tribesmen in Pir Koh area.
Some unidentified men opened fire, killing a man and injuring another near Kuladher. It was reported that the men had no enmity with anyone, and no possible reason was given behing the murder.

5 civilians were killed and 6 others were injured as a result of unprovoked firing in the Neelam Valley. A passenger bus was also damaged. They fired on every moving object in Athmuqam in the Neelam Valley.

As part of the violence due to MQM protests, a pitched gunbattle took place between law enforcement agencies and armed men at Holmstead Hall, which resulting in causing injuries to an unidentified miscreant who was later taken away by his comrades.

Firing by Indian troops along the Sialkot working boundary damaged nine more houses and damaged standing paddy crops. Rangers foiled two major Indian attempts at fencing in Chhumb, Joriyaan and Charwa sectors.

According to Peshawar SSP, Ijaz Khan, reserved policemen were traveling in a van when a bomb was detonated by remote control on the City Circular Road outside the Lahori Gate, killing five policemen and a boy while at least 24 others were injured.
Gunmen killed a man, Muhammad Bakhsh, and injured another.
Three children of a man were killed in Indian shelling the in Lanjot village of the Nakyal Sector in the southern border district when a mortar shell hit their house.

Seven militants were killed in clashes with security forces in Razmak area. One paramilitary soldier lost his life and nine others suffered injuries.  The clash erupted after militants fired 60 rockets at the main paramilitary camp in Razmak. Troops used heavy artillery and mortars to repulse the attack.  The Taliban have claimed responsibility for the attack. TTP spokesman claimed a different version of the event and said that the Taliban had killed several soldiers in the attack and captured a large quanity of weapons. He said that three militants were killed and two others injured.

A high school vice principal got seriously injured when he got caught in between a clash between two groups who were said to be rivals. The high school was closed due to the incident. It is not known why the two groups were rivals, or what they were fighting about.
two people were killed and a woman wounded when two rockets were fired at the house of Noor Gul in Miramshah.
Shabi Khel and Kekaray tribes clashed over the possesion of a hill.The clashed lasted 5 hours and took six lives.
Mohammad Hanif, a taxi-driver, was seriously injured when gunmen opened fire at him with a sub-machine gun.

Zia Alam, who was a senior PPP activist and also the lawyer of suspected assassin Ajmal Pahari, was shot dead by armed motorcyclists. It was claimed that the killing took place to 'harass' PPP activists.
A power transmission tower was damaged in a blast in Peshawar.

Some unidentified people shot at a Rangers van from a car bearing a government registration number. They fired indisciminantly and also tossed in a grenade. A police officer came over and started shooting as well but then the assailants sped away. According to the Jamshed town police officer, it was a targeted attack on a Ranger's picket.
During the strike called by religious parties against the US-led attack on Afghanistan, a person was injured in Baldia when miscreants opened fire.
The bodies of a woman and her son were found in F.B Industrial Area.According to police, they were beaten to death with a hard and blunt object.

A heavy contingent of police and Rangers conducted a siege-and-search operation in Orangi after receiving information that some 'harline MQM activists' were hiding in the area. During the operation the personnel allegedly beat up several men and forced all of them to sit in the open for several hours with blindfolds. This operation was part of the continuing search for the killers of Cheif Minister Syed Abdullah Shah's brother.
Indiscriminate firing by Indian troops from across the LoC killed one person.

One Abbas Ali Lund was killed in an armed clash between Bozdars and Lunds in village Ghoto Lund. The clash started over a piece of land. The local administration was trying to patch up the dispute through sardars to stop further bloodshed.
Imran, the owner of a tyre puncture shop, was targeted while he was inside his shop.

Two groups of Muslim Students' Federation and Peoples Students' Federation clashed with eachother.They used Kalashnikovs to fire at eachother.Seven people recived bullet injuries.;Follow-up:One injured person died of his injuries in the hospital.
armed tribesmen attacked FC post in Loti gas field area. The rockets exploded in open areas, causing no casualty or damage. FC personnel retaliated and fired rockets on positions af assailants.

Around 5:45 am, about one dozen PML women workers arrived in ones and twos at Platform No. 1 in the Karachi Cantonment Railway Station where the Shalimar Express train to Lahore was being prepped for departure.  Six women boarded the train engine and announced their intention to take control of the train.  The women reportedly chanted anti-government slogans and voiced their determination not to allow the wheels to move; two women activists also laid down on the tracks to block the train.  Two police teams came in and forcibly removed the women from the engine room and the tracks.  The women were physically grabbed by police officials led by ASI Farooq and pushed out.  As the women were taken to the exit of the station, they were joined by more protesters.  The police attempted to arrest them, but the enraged activists thwarted the attempt and left the station.  Later, three activists were captured from the car of a journalist and another protester was dragged into a police van by three policewomen.
A 30-year old man was gunned inside his shop.
PAI and PPP activists were harassed by the police as they were on their way to Lahore to join the rally. they were intercepted by the police, however they managed to flee as they were baton-charged.
A man was shot dead in Sabzi Mandi when unidentified men opened fire on him while he was getting out of his Pajero in the fruit market.
One person was gunned down by three unknown assailants at Rawal Town on Sunday

4 people were injured in sectarian clashes following the killing of Maulana Esarul Haq Qasmi when the ASS took out a procession in the main bazaar where a clash took place between 2 sectarian groups resulting in 2 ASS activists being injured. Later 2 activists of the Tehreek-i-Nifaz-i-Fiqah-i-Jafaria were severly beaten by activists of the ASS.
The office of the MQM was attacked by unidentifed gunmen with indiscrimnate firing. No casualties were reported
Sources reported that troops and militants exchanged fire in the Karwan Manza area but no casualties were reported. Military had targeted militants locations to flush them out.
Two people were killed on the pretext of Karo Kari. A man saw his wife with someone else and opened fire killing both of them.

Five security personnel were injured in a landmine explosion in Dera Bugti. Officials said that the landmine was planted in the Maro area of Dera Bugti and exploded when a vehicle of the FC Corps collided with it.

Unidentified militants planted explosives in a room of the Government Girls Higher Secondary School that went off and completely destroyed two rooms of the school. The explosion caused no loss of life.
Some youths tried to take over the Akbari Mosque, which resulted in an armed clash between the two groups. Several people were injured and the police arrested 12 people.
A man was killed and five others were injured when a bomb exploded in Sui town. According to AFP, the BLA claimed the responsibility for the attack.
Unidentified motorcyclists threw explosives into a polic mobile, thus injuring 4 policemen. The policemen were on their way to Saudabad from Jamshed Quarters.

Militants blew up six shrines in the area of Stori Khel. Stori Khel tribe, which is predominantly Shia, had raised a lashkar to fight the Taliban. Before the attack, the Taliban dug up the grave of a spiritual leader, Anwarul Haq, exhumed his body and desecrated his remains.
A person was shot dead by two unknown assailants in Samnabad area on Friday
A man was injured in Indian firing across LoC in Leepa valley on Monday

Saleem Bhandani, who was an activist of the MQM-H(Amir) and a worker of Unit-87 of Landhi Sector in the party's organizational sector, was found shot dead. He had been kidnapped earlier from Bandhani Colony.

An unidentified body was discovered on the Farooq Road, Siddiq Pura in the Badami Bagh area. The body bore torture marks and there was a cloth tied around the neck. A name was also inscribed across the wrist.

Unidentified men attacked the house of MQM-H leader Shakir Siddiqui and kidnapped two activists, the bullet-riddled bodies of whom were found a couple of hours later from the same area.  The cause is said to be the ongoing violence between MQM factions.
Unprovoked Indian firing from across the LoC injured one woman Naziran Bibi.
one person, Younas, was killed who found an explosive device and was carrying it in a bag when it exploded.
The decomposed body was recovered from fields near the shrine of Pir Munir Shah on Thursday
A couple was shot dead by the girl's father and cousin when they opened indiscriminate fire on them for marrying each other without consent.

A worker of the PPP, Shamsul Hasan, was ambushed at the parking lot of the Marine Drive and gunned down in an attack near his apartment in Clifton. Armed men took to the streets and resorted to aerial firing.
A man set his wife ablaze in over a dispute  about his wish to marry the second time.
A bridge was blown off by unidentified militants in Akkakhel locality on Monday
Three people were killed and 3 others injured when two groups, led by Ali Muhammad and Rehmat Virk respectively,  exchanged fire over an old land dispute.
Five troops were killed and sveral others were injured when three roadside bombs hit a convoy of security forces near Rashakai area.
A bomb planted by the wall of the house of Fraz Khan exploded.
Kotwali police found bodies of a young couple from an under contruction building on Vehari Road. The DSP was of the view that they were murdered because of their illicit relations.
an explosion took place in Kohlu, damaging windowpanes of a clinic and some nearby structures.
Two bodies of suspected militants of Lashkar-i-Islam were found from the Shen Drand area of Akakhel in Bara tehsil.
Militants had planted bombs in Governmnet Primary School for Boys, which exploded early in the morning
A Pakistan Steel bus was set on fire in the Al Falah society.
Two people killed Ahmad Ali over a property dispute.
A remote-controlled roadside bomb was used to target a police patrol van. 5 policemen were injured.

armed men of the Kharal group came to the out-house of Imtiaz Chadhar and opened indiscriminate fire killing 4 people. over a dozen people of the Kharal and the Chadhar groups had lost their lives due to a property dispute.

Militants kidnapped Nek Dar from Degan and beheaded him for supplying food to the security forces. The militants had earlier warned him not to provide food to the security forces, but Nek Dar had ignored their threats. His beheaded body was found in Degan with a chit on it warning that if anybody found violating the militants’ decisions would face the same treatment. Militants had warned locals not to supply food to the security forces in the region after they scrapped a peace deal with the government. Another tribesman, Gul Naib, was shot dead in the same area. Family sources said local militants had asked him to persuade his uncle to stop supplying food to the troops.

a suicide bomber blew up his vehicle near an FC checkpost in the outskirts of Darra Adamkhel killing 8 civilians, 2 security personnel and injuring 27 other people. Sources say that intelligence agencies have reported that Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan chief Baitullah Mehsud's commander Hakeemullah Mehsud had sent his bombers to Kohat last month to attack sensitive installations and one of them hit an army convoy in Hangu.
A shia activists was shot dead by three men from Sipah-i- Sahaba. The attackers managed to escape.
One student was injured in clash between APMSO and PSF. The policearrested the injured activist.
Indian forces did shelling across LoC in Leepa valley on Friday, however police reported no loss of life

nearly two dozen people were injured when Kashmiri refugees living on the official land near the prime minister's residence clashed with the staffers of a civic body attempting to remove some illegal constructions. The refugees later staged a protest.

Thousands of people from different areas of gathered and started marching towards Chashma raising slogans against the government and the loadshedding in the area. Police intercepted the procession at Watta Khel Chowk and used batons to stop them. Enraged protesters then began pelting the police with stones to which police had to use tear gas shells and aerial firing in order to bring the situation under control but failed and the protesters charged forcing police to take refuge as the seige continued for two hours. At least 20 protesters, and six policemen were injured.
Three security personnel were injured when a remote controlled bomb exploded while thei vehicle was passing by.
helicopter gunships pounded militants' hideouts in Qamber killing four militants.

A group of women blocking the Bannu-Kohat road and protesting against loadshedding were allegedly baton-charged and dragged onto the streets by the police in order to displace them. This infuriated the elders of the area, and a mob of armed enraged people burnt a checkpost of the Frontier Reserve Police and marched to the Banda Daud Shah police station. The police reportedly opened fire to disperse the advancing protesters, in which one person was killed and six others were injured. The protesters also returned fire, in which 3 policemen were injured.
Two brothers shot dead their cousin over a property dispute regarding the installation of a gate on their joint property.
A taxi driver, Gulab Khan, was shot and killed by armed motorcyclists while he was driving home.
A 25 year old man was killed and his body was found from the Railway tracks in Sharifabad.

Armed men on three vehicles opened fire at people who were playing sports and exercising in a ground, killing at least 6 and injuring another 10. Moments before the armed attack three rockets were fired from nearby mountains that landed in an open space. The Lashkar-i-Jhangvi claimed responsibility for the attack.

A bomb exploded in the Wanda area of D.I.Khan. After police and journalists reached the spot, another bomb blasted took place killing 4 policemen and a passer by. One jounalist was also injured in the second blast.
The office of an NGO was set of fire by unknown people in Swat. Two motorcyles parked outside the National Rural Support were also set on fire.
Militants clashed with security forces close to the Afghan border. No details given.
shops of the president of the Tribal Union of Journalists, Bajaur Unit,Mian Saeedur Rehman were destroyed in a rocket attack by unknown outlaws.
unidentified persons slaughtered a watchman.
A rocket was fired by unknown miscreants at the Commissioner's Office. No casualties were reported.

Two people were killed and four others were injured, including an Ex-MPA (Mohammad Aslam Midhiana), when a brother of the PML-MPA Shahnawaz Ranjha, opened fire on their car near Midh Ranjha. The Midhiana alleged that the brother, Rabnawaz Ranjha, had previously killed one of their group members as well.
A newly-wed couple was shot and killed by the bride's brothers on the pretext of 'honour' as they had contracted marriage without the consent of the girl's family.

Hundreds of people belonging to the Rajput community blocked the highway to protest against the police raiding their houses. A heavy police contingent reached the spot and opened aerial fire and tear-gas shelling without negotiating with the crowd. The crowd responded by pelting the police with stones, as a result of which 4 policemen received injuries. At least seven people were injured in this.
About a 1000 men, including members of the JI, participated in a rally to show their solidarity with Osama Bin Laden and to condemn the US. They blocked roads by burning tyres.
A housewife was shot dead by unknown assailants inside her house. The reason behind the killing is not known.
Two students were injured in a clash between two factions of the Muslim Students Federation (Q) and (N) over a minor issue on the campus of the Local Government College.

Police found the body of an unidentified man lying in the playfield in Gulbahar area. He had reportedly been hanged by unidentified men and a note was also recovered from his pocket which read \ All informers will meet the same fate\"."
Six dead bodies of murdered young men were brought to the hospital.

A young man was shot dead in Soldier Bazaar. The victim was identified as Tajuddin. The police could not determine whether he was hit by a stray bullet or if he was the target of an unknown assailant.
A cement dealer, Abdul Hameed, died when his Orangi Town shop was attacked by unidentified men.
troops came under attack near a government school for boys in the Elai village. The troops countered the attack and pounded Taliban positions with artillery. No casualty was reported.

A mother and her son was killed, while another one of hers sons got injured when six armed men barged into their house while they were sleeping and opened fire on them. It could not be known what the motive behind the attack was or who the perpetrators were.

An officer of the ISI, his subordinate and two tribesmen were killed while several others were wounded when some people opened fire on their vehicle after they were returning from a tribal jirga. The incident occurred after local political authorities and tribal elders signed an agreement not to harbour local and foreign militants. It was believed that some elements were unhappy with the agreement and wanted disturbances in the area. Followup: Political authorities detained 11 people on suspicion of their involvement in the killings of four people, including the two ISI officials in Bajaur.
a cement trader was shot dead at his outlet by three motorcyclists.

Three passerbys were injured when a bomb planted under a truck exploded in front of the Sariab police station. Reports said that the police had impounded the vehicle a few days ago. Two other cars were also damaged by the flying debris.
An Uzbek militant group Ansaarul Mohajireen has claimed to have killed a local Taliban commander Haji Hannan and his two companions in Darra Zenda area.

Five persons, including a woman, were gunned down in a village near Sibi when two armed men intercepted the groups pick-up and opened fire killing four family members and a nomad woman living in a nearby hut. According to officials the killing was due to an old dispute between the Selachi tribe.
Two rockets were fired by militants on the army Brigade HQ in Zari Noor Colony. The rockets were fired from unidentified locations and did not cause any casualties.

Hundreds of Afghan based terrorists attacked posts in Chitral, killing twenty-five security personnel. Twenty riaders were killed in retaliatory fire. Two border posts were taken over by the Afhgan militants.

Two unidentified assailants entered the clinic of Dr. Bakir Ali Naqvi, while he was with a patient, in Kot Lakpat and opened fire, injuring him while the patient remained unhurt. He was taken to the Lahore General Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. His relatives claimed he had no affiliations with any religious organisation and was cordial with all sects. Police stated that the nature of the killing was similar to those of sectarian nature in the past.
Cobra helicopters attacked the positions of militants in Shahnari, Haji Lawang, Ragha Dagg and Takht area killing 1 senior Al Qaeda operative and 17 others.

Wan Bachran police claimed to have arrested an alleged terrorist. Identified as Noor Muhammad, the police says he was on his way to Sargodha from Miramshahcarrying 10 hand-grenades and other arms and ammunition. He disclosed having plans to attack Shia gatherings at two Imambargahs in Sargodha.
Unidentified men killed a lawyer, Sultan Ahmed Rana, in his house and fled. The cause of the murder could not be ascertained as the family said that they had no enmity.

around 1000 demonstrators took to the streets and staged a protest against loadshedding, starting from Main Bazaar to the grid station. They chanted slogans against Lesco, burnt tyres, and later besieged a jgrid station and pelted stones and damaged 2 vehicles parked inside the grid station. they also ransacked the grid station.
A man was wounded in a shooting incident in Johrabad.
A roadside hotel in Phuleli was set ablaze.  No other details were reported, but the incident was included with reports of other violent incidents during the wheel-jam strike.
Four persons were seriously injured in an armed clash between two groups of the Baqalyn tribe over the ownership of a hill.

At least 2 people were killed and several injured in a clash between the sub-clans of Ali Sherzai over an old land dispute. They clans took arms after a jirga failed to resolve the issue which first started in 1895 when the British divided the area.

At least 10 people blocked the GT Road near Alam Chowk after setting old tyres on fire. They smashed window panes of various vehicles and chanted slogans against the government and the US strikes in Afghanistan.
Ghulam Haider was killed in Gulshan-i-Ghazi at his house by unidentified people.

more than 200 demonstrators, including villagers, lawyers, traders and activists of the PML-N blocked the main Gojra-Sumundri Road in protest against police for not releasing those detained in connection with the long march despite the Prime Minister's orders. the protest sparked after a delegation led by PMA Rao Kashif Raheem went to the police station and demanded the release of some detainees. the SHO allegedly misbehaved with the delegates and held them hostage inside the police station. the protesters blocked the road outside and chanted slogans. they also pelted the police with stones when they tried to disperse them. police held talks with the protesters later, convincing them to disperse.
Fourteen militants and six troops were killed while four others troops were injured during a search and clear operation in Lakki Ghundi.

A home-made explosive device, planted near a house on White road behind Governor's house went off creating panic in the area. Window panes of several houses were smashed by the powerful explosion. No loss of life or property damage was reported.

Six people were shot dead over an old enemity. The police claimed that two clans, Sehto and Paryo, had an old enemity, due to which these 6 people from the Sehto clan were killed. The motive seemed to be revenge killing,
The residents of Khai Road staged a protest demonstration against loadshedding and transparent crystal meters and blocked the road and burnt tyres.

An under-trial prisoner was injured when his rival fired on him near the district and session court. Mohammad Alamzeb was being brought to district and session court to appear before the court in a murder case when his rival Ibad Sher allegedly fired, causeing injury. the accused and his brother escaped after the incident.

Four Americans and their Pakistani driver, all employees of the Houstan based oil company, Union Texas Petroleum (UTP) were killed when their vehicle was ambushed by unidentified men in a Red Honda Civic who burst the tyres of the Nissan eight seater and resorted to indiscriminate firing and fled. All five men were killed on the spot. The attack came a day after the US embassy in Islamabad had issued a warning to all US national to be careful following sentencing in the Aimal Kansi case.

A gunbattle erupted in Kharadhar and Mithadar between supporters of Sunni Tehreek and the police.  The police attempted to disperse members of Sunni Tehreek who were observing the Chehlum of one of their members at Acchi Qabar in Mithadar and allegedly tried to raid its office.  An eyewitness said two plainclothes police officers even slapped an activist while telling them to obey the government ban on gatherings.  A constable was shot and seriously wounded; another was hit in the head with a stone.  Soon after, there was a heavy exchange of fire between masked youths and the police.  The police then fled from the scene and armed youths took over the area.  Masked men resorted to heavy firing, lit bonfires, and pelted stones at a Kharadhar traffic police kiosk.  A resident claimed the police lobbed tear-gass shells to disperse the protesters, and police claim they were fired upon when they attempted to raid the Sunni Tehreek office.  After two hours of chaos, the rangers were brought in to control the situation.  Police arrested at least 40 suspects for rioting and arson, but a resident told Dawn reporters that most of those arrested were spectators or pedestrians and that the masked men had fled.
a group of demonstrators attacked haf a dozen shops at the main Jinnah road after a protest rally held by the BSO. The mob dispersed after poice arrived at the scene.
Two shops were completely destroyed and 10 others were damaged partially when a bomb exploded in the Zainullah CD market in Charsadda. The police said the blast was carried out by unknown people.

Unidentified in a white car resorted to heavy firing near the MQM's headquarters in Azizabad and escaped. After a few minutes the same group reappeared near the Buturab Imambargah and resorted to firing before running away towards Ayesha Manzil.

Muhammad Shahid, 25, of Data Nagar in Badami Bagh, was on his way on Peco Road when he got hit by a stray bullet. The killer could not be identified, and it was reported that the deceased did not have any enemity with anyone.
Atleast 24  vehicles were torched by unidentified men in these areas.
Eight people were killed and ten others were injured when a bomb, planted in the rear end of a Sialkot bound bus, exploded when the bus reached near Jherol
A trader, his wife and niece were shot dead by 5 (Mohammad Khaliq and his sons) of their relatives over property disputes.
23 terrorists were killed in various areas of Malakand and Dir while 2 soldiers were killed and 12 others were injured.
The body of an unidentified man was found in Singhpura.

Indian security forces resumed intensified firing after a three-day lull on Pakistani border villages along the Sialkot working boundary. Nine more houses were damaged and paddy crops damaged in the incident. No casualty reported.
1 soldier was killed and 6 were injured in a gun battle with militants
One person was killed and another injured when they were attacked by unidentified gunmen.

A leader of the Sunni Tehreek was arrested to avert a sectarian clash. When The JUI leader came to inaugrate Jamia Usmani Farooq-i-Azam Mosque , The Sunni Tehreek leader claimed that it was a \sunni mosque\". There was an exchange of hot words and the police arrested the leader to avoid a mishap."
Four tribesmen were hurt when Levies forces opened fire on a group of protesters who were protesting against prolonged power cuts in the Mohmand area.
Two people were killed and another was injured in a clash between Shahlani and Buledi tribesmen. Details are not available.
A retired army Major Shafi Ghauri was found dead in his home in Gulshan-i-Iqbal on Saturday. He was strangulated
militants fired rockets at the Circuit House in Mingora, killing one soldier and injuring two others.

Following the killing of MQM worker Amir Yasin, angry party activists took to the streets and tried to force shopkeepers to close their shops but a police contingent showed up, prompting the activists to flee the scene. However, the police opened fire, killing 3 of the MQM workers that were attempting to flee. One other person was also killed.
A woman and her alleged paramour were shot dead by her uncle for having illicit relations. The killer later presented himself for arrest
Bhutto and Baloch tribesmen fight over the cable network business. A six year old boy and a young girl are killed in an armed clash.
Security forces opened fire on a car when it tried to overtake an army convoy, injuring six people, including a girl and a woman.
8 people were injured during an armed clash between two groups of the Banglani tribe. The clash was over grazing cattlehead.
Rockets were fired from an unknown place at Bara bazaar which injured a security official. Security forces retaliated by opening fire, killing three shopkeepers and injuring six others.

four people were killed in an exchange of fire between security forces and militants in Takhtaband. Helicopter gunships also targetted militant positions. 3 people were killed and 10 others were injured when mortar shells hit their houses in Shewar area of Matta tehsil.
A former member of District Council Narowal, Syed Afzal Shah was injured when two members of a rival group fired at him and fled.
Junaid Qureshi, an MQM activist, was shot dead by two men on a motorbike. The victim was sitting outside his house with his friends when the incident took place.
In Manghopir area, the bodies of two young men were found, both of whom were wearing shalwar and kameez and were trussed up. Police said they were tortured and later killed.

Police and FC raided a village after receiving information that militants were hiding there. When they reached the village, armed men opened fire on them leading to clash. 1 FC man and 1 'proclaimed offender' were killed and another FC man sustained injuries.
Two persons were killed and three others were injuredi in an exchange of fire between two rivals groups over the possession and cultivation of a piece of agricultural land.

The bodies of two Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan were found from the pavements in front of two adjacent Imambargahs in Muslim Town.  The two men bore marks of severe torture. They were said to be have been invovled in the murder of Dr. Ali Naqvi, a shia leader.
A young man was shot dead in his clothes godown by unidentified men.
Two unidentified armed people stabbed to death an industrialist Muhammad Akram and set his body on fire. No clue to the killers had been found so far.
tribesmen blew up a pipeline of the Pir Koh gas plant area causing suspension of gas supply to the plant.
Unidentified people attacked with a grenade the house in Nushki of Dr. Mohammad Tayyab, a deputy director in the live-stock department.
Two people were injured in heavy Indian shelling in the Munda Kali village from across the Line of Control.

After an incident where six of a 'Masih' family were butchered, around 300 protesters marched towards the Governor's house with the bodies to protest against the killings. Police intercepted them and resorted to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to disperse the crowd.
A decomposed body was found in an abandoned house. The vicitim' identity could not be established.
Salim Ansari was shot dead by an unidentified person. The reason behind the killing is not known.
a man slaughtered his wife and daughter over suspicion of loose morals in Faisal Town locality of Manawala, and then courted arrest.
Karim Dino Ujjan shot dead his wife, Safoora, and Asghar Ali (son of Bhale Dino Thebo) on suspicion of illicit relations between them. He was later arrested and confessed to the crime.
1 person was injured in Ward No 28, Gujrat during LB elections on Saturday.
a peasant, Khamiso Machi was killed while another, Arab Machi, was injured when they clashed over disputed graveyard land at village Haji Machi on Badin Sujawal Road.
Violent clashes amongst rival groups during local bodies elections left 36 people injured. The injured included political workers, election officers and policemen.
Akram Khan, a resident of Kausar Niazi Colony, was shot dead by armed motorcylsits.

A demonstration organised jointly by Muttahida Qaumi Movement and Jeay Sindh Qaumi Mahaz and led by former MPA Fareed Ahmed and Ali Hassan Chandio advocate at Market Chowk. The protesters blocked the M. A. Jinnah road and broke pitchers. They chanted slogans against the \Punjabi establishment\" and demanded Sindh's due share of water. When they reached outside the State Life building, they were baton charged by the police and 20 activists were arrested. "
following the killing of Qasim Ali Shah, Bagh Ali Shah along with his 4 accomplices shot dead Khair Ali Shah.

Two bombs went off in front of the Government Girls Higher Secondary School, destroying its main gate and damaging the power supply line. The nazim of the Gujrat union said that the school administration had received a letter about a month ago with the warning that if the students and staff did not observe purdah (veil), the school building would be blown up within 15 days.

A well-known Shia Zakir and employee of the Special Branch, Qaiser Mustafa, was shot and injured when two hooded motorcyclists opened fire on him while he was on his way home, near Yasir Hospital. According to officials, the attack was a continuation of the sectarian killings being carried out.

After the murder of Mir Mohammad- a Bhambhro tribesman allegedly killed by Lashari tribesmen during a clash between the Bhambhro and Lashari tribes over a land dispute- the police registered a case against 8 Lashari tribesmen. His uncle was also seriously injured.

Mohammad Hussain and his 5-year-old son were killed when armed men opened fire at the cab they were travelling in. Another person was injured in the firing. According to the police, the attack was based on sectarian motives. The victims belonged to the Hazara tribe.
Another clash between Bugti and Mazari Tribesmen left one person dead. The two tribes have been clashing for about 3 weeks.
Two time-bombs planted under police vehicles outside a police station exploded, destroying the vehicles and injuring 4 policemen.
Over a dozen people were injured when PML-N Youth Wing Workers and the PML-N National Guards clashed, using sticks, during a public meeting arranged in connection to observe a 'black day'.

Rana Safdar, a PPP worker, escaped an attempt on his life when three alleged attackers barged into his house and tried to strangle him but he managed to overpower them. The attackers however made good their escape.

Police baton-charged Sindh National Party activists who took out a protest procession here on Sunday against the Kalabagh dam and the greater Thal canal, injuring a number of protesters. The procession, led by SNP secretary-general Dilshad Bhutto, started from the Clock Tower and wanted to proceed towards the local press club but a heavy contingent of police reached at the scene and asked the protesters to disperse. When the activists refused to disperse, they were baton-charged. Two critically injured activists, Mir Ali and Lal Bux Bhambhro, were taken to the Sukkur Civil Hospital. Police also picked up at least 40 protesters, Dilshad Bhutto. Later, workers of the SNP, led by its president Ameer Bhambhro, surrounded the B-section police station and demanded release of the activists. After negotiations between SNP leaders and police authorities, the activists were released. No case was registered against any person.

Ashraf alias Qasai, who was associated with the Punjabi-Pakhtun Ittehad (PPI), was shot dead outside his home. The police later discovered that a dispute between two political groups was the reason behind the targeted killing, which was one of many that took place in Karachi that day.

On the day of the burial of assassinated MQM leader Dr Imran Farooq, a day of mourning was declared and Karachi witnessed sporadic incidents of violence. Two MQM workers were shot. The victims accused the Rangers of opening fire on them but the police claimed that they had not received any such report.
At least 22 people, including 5 women, were injured in an armed clash between two groups of the Malick tribesmen in Faiz Mohammad village.
A person was found dead in Al-Noor colony on Thursday
Two vehicles were set ablaze in the Azizabad area.
Armed motorcyclists shot dead Nawab Baloch and injured his friend Rasheed.
A bridge was blown up in Chak Ampur Road as the explosive device was planted underneath the bridge on Monday.
A bullet-ridden body of a man was found in a car in liaqatbad.
Police constable Latfullah Kalhoro died when unidentified armed men opened fire at him. No other detail was given.
A soldier of the Chenab Rangers was martyred in the mortar shelling by Indian troops in the Shakargark sector of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

A couple and their minor son was shot dead by four unidentified men in Bhimber. The gunmen barged into house of Maqbool and sprayed the family with bullets killing Maqbool, his wife and their son Salman. The motives behind the assassination could not be confirmed immediately.
Two people were killed when two groups of the the Lango tribe clashed.
Activists of the MQM and the ANP clashed over the issue of hoisting party flags in Korangi. Zahid Massih, a 12-year-old boy, was killed in the corssfire.
A gang of ofur unidentified gunmen opened indiscriminate fire killing the president of Pakistan's Peoples Party, Naudero and injuring a policeman.
A young man's charred body was found in Kasur Town, Malir with a bullet whole in his head.
Tauseef Mehmood, an ANP member, was gunned down by unidentified assailants on a motorbike. Akram Shah, also an ANP member who was with Mehmood at the time, was injured in the attack.
A rocket was fired at the Ghazi checkpost in Dera Bugti.  Balochistan Liberation Army has claimed rsponsibility of the attack.
A low-intensity bomb exploded at the arrival lounge of the Peshawar International Airport, but caused no casualty.
An unidentifed body of a young man was found. He was shot in the head

Twenty one people were killed and 50 others injured when four unknown assailants resorted to indiscriminate firing at a Fajr congregation at the Jamia Masjid Al-Khair in Mumtazabad locality. The assailants fled in a silver grey car.Last month a similar incident had occured at a Shia congregation. But the Punjab Chief Minister, Arif Nakai, said he did not believe that the firing was sectarian in nature, and said that it was an act of terrorism. Followup: One of the people injured in the Multan firing incident succumbed to his injuries.

After a public meeting addressed by local political and religious leaders, the protesters took out a procession in which they shouted slogans against the US, burnt an effigy of the US President, and marched towards the civil colony and attacked the gates of the city jail. The personnel fired shots to disperse the mob and ended up injuring 8 people.
A bullet-riddled body stuffed in a bag was found from the Killi Qambrani area.
