Four people were seriously injured when a bomb placed in a road roller that was being carried by a trailer to Kandahar, exploded when it got near a Frontier Corps Fort. It is not clear whether the bomb attack was intended for the Frontier Coprs Fort or for general terrorist agendas.
A van of Pakistan Steel Mills was set on fire.

Three MQM workers were killed in an encounter with the police. A police party, acting on some information, surrounded Rahim Shah Colony to arrest some wanted MQM terrorists. But the terrorists opened fire at the police, to which the police retaliated. 3 MQM workers were killed and a police inspector was injured. The MQM disputed the police claim and alleged that the three were killed in cold blood.
Some men of Shabab-i-Milli stormed into the hotel which was allegedly a torture cell of Police and beat several men in Gulshan Colony Factory Area on Thursday.

A former member of the district council, Khan Shuja Ahmad (younger brother of MPA of Mananwala, Khan Zia Ahmad Khan) was shot dead when five unidentified assailants opened fire on him on the district court premises.
security forces entered Akhorwal area, a stronghold of Taliban and exchaned fire with militants.6 militanst were arrested, one of them was injured.
An army soldier was killed and his father and sister-in-law were injured on the Dhoke area of Attock.

Aqai Sadiq Ganj, Director-General of the Iranian Cultural Centre, was shot dead by unidentified gunmen when he came to attend a farewell reception. Another Iranian student was injured. The police arrested one of the assailants when he was trying to escape.

The body of Abdul Wadood was found near Mehran Town with stab wounds. His family thought that Wadood was visiting friends but he did not come back the whole night. He had maried twice and was associated with Tableeghi Jamaat.

Scores of traders and shopkeepers staged a demonstration to protest against power outages that lasted for upto 20 hours. They blocked the main road and burnt tyres and pelted the police with stones when the latter tried to disperse them. The protest lasted for 6 hours. The leaders of the protest threatened to set ablaze Mepco offices if the issue was not resolved.

A land lord , Maula Baksh Keerio, was killed by unknown persons, and the weapons used in the attack were said to belong to the Sakarand Police station. The Brohi and the Keerio clans had been battling each other ever since the murder of a Brohi clan member by a Keerio clansmen. It was said that the chief of the Keerio clan had close and friendly ties with a key figure in the ruling Pakistan People's Party, and had been receiving aid to use against the Brohi clan. The Brohi claim alleged that the police tortured their women and took action against the clansmen, perhaps on the insistance of the Keerio clan.
A shoe vender, Zahid, was found dead in his rented room at Australia Chowk at Naulakha. Shahzad, Zahid's brother, said that he did not hear any gunshot and woke up to find his brother dead.
According to sources, local taliban killed a man and took two hostage on the Indua Highway in Darra Adamkhel agency.
A missile struck the house of Sher Zaman in Doug area killing one person and injuring two others.

Five traffic police personnel were injured when a bomb went off near the city traffic office. The policemen were going to the Gondlanwala Adda office when the blast occurred, which also damaged windowpanes of nearby houses.
Two bullet-riddled bodies, identified as those of Guldar Ali and Jalal Khan, were found with a note attached claiming that they were spying for the US.
Unknown assailants on a motorcyle killed two people who had come to Quetta from Mandi Bahauddin and were staying in a hotel in Satellite Town. The police dubbed the incident a terrorist act.

Thirteen persons attacked armed policemen in order to break the water course of a canal in Mirwah area, in which an official of irrigation department and two policemen were injured.  The attack did not deter the policemen, and the attackers fled after failing to break the water course of the canal.

Amjad Farooqi, a terrorist linked to Al Qaeda was killed in an encounter with the security forces when they raided a house on a tip-off. 3 other terrorist suspects were arrested according to the interior and information ministers. President Musharraf had named Amjad Farooqi as the lead suspect in being the mastermind behind carrying out the assassination plot on his convoy; Follow up: Security forces have detained over a dozen militants after the killing of Amjad Farooqi, from Sindh, Quetta, Peshawar, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi.

More than a dozen people were injured when residents were protesting against continued poor supply of gas when they tried to get into the regional office and were attacked by the staff armed with clubs and iron rods. Upon seeing this, protesters outside started pelting the office with stones, which caused the injuries. Later police were called and the mob dispersed.

A gas well of the Oil and Gas Development Corporation of Pakistan received damage when unknwon armed men fired rockets in Pir Koh area of Dera Bugti. A fire also broke out as a result of the blast but it was controlled after an hour's effort. It may also be recalled that around one dozen rocket firing incidents have been reported over the last two months in different gas fields of Dera Bugti.
A music show was underway at the marriage ceremony of an Afghan, at the Jalala refugee camp, when a bomb was lobbed at the gathering. At least 5 were killed and 35 injured.

Zahid Saeed, an activist of the PSF (People's Students Federation), was shot and killed by activsts of a rival faction within the PSF. The two groups have been fighting over the nomination of the new PSF president.

Two youths were injured when three motorcyclists resorted to firing in Phulleli area. The gangsters, who could not be identified, arrived at Hussain chowk and opened fire in which the two youngsters were injured.
A passerby was killed in an armed clash between two rival groups over a piece of land.
An explosion was reported from Mastung. No other detail was given.
During the long march by PDA protesters, Assistant Comissioner City and Magistrate raided the house and allegedly harassed the civilians in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
Area residents attacked a Wapda office during a protest rally to get electricity restored. However, the demands could not be met.

During a strike in interior Sindh that was called by AT,JSQM, STPP, JUI, JST and other nationalist parties to protest alleged irregularities in the ongoing house-count, members of Sindhiyani Tehrik took to the streets and burnt tyres to block traffic. Sindhiyani Tehrik is the women's wing of the Awami Tehrik
Some miscreants blew up a portion of a gas pipeline in Dera Bugti.

Twelve persons were injured as an explosive device went off at the Cantonment Railway Station. The device was planted by the subversive elements beneath or inside a washing machine which was kept at a bay between Paltform No 6 and 1.
Malik Madha Hussain,a TJP leader's house came under attck when unidentified gunmen opened fire and fled.Nobody was injured.
One person was injured in Mindarwal village as the Indian forces continued firing from across the Working Boundary.
1 person was killed and 3 were injured in a bomb blast in Circuit House on Tuesday. The bomb was planted under the sofa of the drawing room of the house.
two groups attacked each other when they opened fire with small firearms. As a result 3 men were killed. All three belonged to the Shakoor gang.

Seven miners were killed and four others were injured when their van came under indiscriminate fire by unidentified armed men. The attackers kidnapped three miners and sent a note with them which stated that the coalmines were the property of the Marri tribe and political administration should halt all work there. An official source said that there was a dispute between the Marri and the Luni tribes over ownership of the coalmines.
a person was injured by troops firing in Gwolarai.
Dr Anwar ul Islam was assassinated in Karimabad area of Karachi. The target killing of doctors continues in Karachi and Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) calls a strike to protest.
four persons killed when mortar shells hit their house in Qalagai.

A man was killed and a woman and minor boy were injured in Neelam Valley of Azad Kashmir in shelling by Indian forces across the Line Of Control. Officials reported that the firing began on Tuesday, 7th january, 2003, which resulted in the death of a man and injured two others in the village of Lawat. It came to a halt and began again the next day, this time targeting the villages in the upper belt.

In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, over 70 people were injured when police resorted to heavy tear-gas shelling to disperse the tens of thousands of demonstrators on Constitution Avenue on Tuesday.
The police severely beat up and arrrested scores of rights activists who tried to hold a mini marathon to highlight violence against women and for promoting enlightened moderation in society.
Militants killed two of the four men they had kidnapped on allegations of them being pro-government. The bodies of the two hostages were found with one of the bodies decapitated.

Two rival student groups, the IJT and the Inqilabi Council, had an armed clash that left 1 student dead and two others injured. The IJT allegedly started the firing. A dispute between the two groups had arisen a month ago but both parties had supposedly 'dropped their differences'.
During a strike called to protest against alleged police excesses and widespread violence in Karachi, a WAPDA school bus was set on fire.

a pro-government tribal elder, Malak Stana Gul. was gunned down when armed men intercepted his vehicle and opened fire on him on the Laghari highway. He had received threats from militants previously due to his pro-government stance.

Four of the MQM activists, who the government claimed had kidnapped and killed four army and police personnel earlier, died during a Ranger's siege and search operation in Gharibabad and its adjoining areas. Mystery shrouded the death of the four MQM activists, as the Rangers did not allow newsmen to visit the area, and the family members of one of the deceased claimed that the victim was in the Rangers custody for the last 22 days.
Mushtaq was on his way home when an unidentified person opened fire at him killing him on the spot. The family said he had no enmity.
a MQM worker was shot dead by his friend after an exchange of hot words, who fled after the incident.

Three rockets exploded one after the other in Quetta. All three rockets were 107 MM Russian-made and were fired by some unknown person(s) from the north-west of the city. The third rocket hit a house in the Christian Colony at Kansi Road. No one was hurt.

Five pedestrians, including a woman, were wounded when activists of the MQM (H) allegedly opened fire at a police picket.  Police claimed that activists of the Haqiqi fired at the police party in Bismillah, however, they missed and hit pedestrians.

Two Uzbek militants were said to be killed while attempting to plant a mine aimed at killing Ibrahim Khan, Senior Vice president of the Makin Peace Committee. This apparently was the third attempt on the life of Ibrahim Khan who had been instrumental in nabbing of the two uzbek militants and handing them over to the authorities some time back.

The district coordinator of Tawana Pakistan Project, Mohammad Qaiser Anis, accused special assistant to chief minister and leader of Muttahida Qaumi Movement, Murtaza Memon, and his men of attacking the office and manhandling the staff. Mr Anis told Dawn that police, understandably under pressure, were dilly-dallying on registering FIR against Mr Memon and his men, and demanded protection for his staff. He said that he received a phone call from somebody who claimed to be leader of MQM, Murtaza Memon, and threatened they would not allow him to work if he hired anybody without his recommendation. Minutes afterwards, Mr Memon in a vehicle (GS-7304) along with four armed men barged into his office, used abusive language and manhandled the staff. They also ransacked the office and threw out office record.
A Station House Officer of the Police was shot dead by unidentified attackers, who managed to escape. Thereason behind the killing is not known.
A police check point at Durand Gate came under attack by militants, killing one paramiltary soldier and injuring another. Soon after that, an armoured personnel carrier was also attacked.

After the death of a youth during a surgery and the death of his mother from 'shock', relatives of the victims and residents of the area blocked the Lahore Road in protest against the private hospital. Some protesters entered the hospital and set the building and some equipment on fire. The police reached the hospital and brought the situation under control. The doctor incharge of the the surgery, denies negligence or malpractice and claims that the victims died of a cardiac arrest.
Maulana Zia-ur-Rehman-Patron-in-Chief of Sipah-i-Sahaba and other ulemas narrowly escaped unhurt when some assailants opened fire on them in Multan Cantonment Area on Monday
A medical store in Saddar was set on fire.
a woman, Uzma, was shot dead while her sister, Siddiqa, injured by their cousins, Navid, Qasim, Goga and Bashir over an agricultural land dispute in Civil Lines area.
Four people were killed and ten others injured in an armed clash between Mohammad Hussain and Sher Mohammad groups. Both the groups have a history of armed clashes.
2 police constables were injured when armed men opened fire at a police mobile van.
Arbab Sethar was axed to death in Mirani Mohallah by unknown assailants.
Secuirty forces claimed to have killed 5 foreign militants in Maidan when troops fired mortar shells on a vehicle carrying militants.

Clashes between the military and militants continued for a second day running and the military pounded their positions and used air strikes to target “enemy positions”. The military lost another 25 soldiers and the chief of the Inter Services Public Relations put the toll on the militants’ side at 60.
A trainee police constable was shot dead in Saeedabad. He had been kidnapped earlier.

a pakistani national was killed and 2 others were injured when Iranian border guards opened fire on three people who had crossed into Iranian territory without legal documents, along the Pakistan-Iran border.
Two people were killed and two others wounded in an armed clash between to clans of the Magsi tribe.

A suspected militant was killed in an exchange of fire with the police when the latter were chasing them after receiving a tip-off. The 2 other men in the car were arrested. A huge cache of weapons and explosives was recovered from the car.

2 security personnel were killed when militants attacked a security post. Six paramilitray troops were reported missing. 15 militants were killed when security personnel pounded their houses in in Spinki Tangi area retaliation. A stray shell hit a house in Qandaharo area of Safi tehsil, killing two civilians. the shelling has also affected the telephone system in the area.
A prominent social worker and a former councilor of Baghdadi, Abdul Qadir alias Qadir  Councillor, was shot dead. The motive behind the killing was said to be personal enmity.

Two rockets hit Quetta creating panic in the area. The first hit an under construction house in Killi Shabu while the other was near the office of the Inspector General Prisoner Balochistan. Both blasts did damage property.
Ethnic Violence' in Karachi continued for the 3rd consecutive day as the unidentified body of a middle-aged man was found with marks of severe torture on it.
Villagers of Shad Mohammad claimed that a police party raided the village at the behest of some influential landlords and arrested 10 people who were locked up and continuously tortured for 5 days.

Security forces destroyed two arms shops and two music outlets selling jihadi songs. Lashkar-i-Islam had earlier imposed a complete ban on the sale of all types of music cassettes and CDs throughout Bara tehsil.
6 militants and were killed in fighting in various areas of Swat. 4 security men were injured.
2 bottles exploded at the Kumharan Chowk when a Tazai procession was passing through, causing panic.
A police constable was gunned down by dacoits at Mubarak Lakhan police check post situated in the Andal Sundrani police limits in Ghotki. The reason for murder could not be ascertained.
A clash between PPP and IJI supporters at a polling station left 2 PPP workers, Muhammad Farooq and Muhammad Sharif, injured.
A body of a man was found stuffed in a gunny bag in Barafwali Gali near the Old Haji camp. The body bore strangulation marks on the neck.
Nine persons were injured when a bomb exploded in a Karachi bound bus near the Liberty market chowk in hyderabad.
Qazzafi, shot dead his mother, Ms. Khalida and her alleged lover, Abdul Sattar Mirbahar, in Saddar Mohalla and then surrendered himself to the police.
Houses of three suspected militants were demolished in Kabal area as troops continued their offensive in different parts of Swat. Security forces also defused a bomb placed by a road.

two brothers, Khalid Khan and Shahid Khan, were gunned down allegedl by their brother-in-law, Rahim. They were having a monetary dispute with him who attacked them when they were returning home and injured them. They died before they could be shifted to hospital. police registered a case against the accused, who managed to escape.
Chairman Town Committee, Jati Haji, Pir Mohammad Mirbahr, was beaten up by 2 unidentified men as he tried to remove an encroachment on a commercial plot in Jati Town.
Two brothers were seriously injured when eight men opened fire on them on the District court premises in Sahiwal.

Two anti-tank mines and detonators, batteries and a clock were found in a burning car parked outside a branch of the Askari Bank. An official of the bomb disposal squad said that the car (registration number Sindh-AEG 622) had been laden with anit-tank mines hooked to batteries, detonator and a time device. It is believed that the assailants planned to blow up the car, but the bomb disposal squad managed to defuse it.
Indian forces did shelling in Sucheetgarh, Chaprar, Bajwat, Charwa, Harpal and Shakargarh Sectors on Sunday. However no loss was reported.
A bomb planted on a bike exploded near a canteen wall in the catonment area. Pieces from the explosion injured people within a 500 yard radius, while the canteen and surrounding shops were damaged.
Three armed villagers shot dead a woman and injured three others of a rival group over a land dispute.

After an attempt on the life of a senior ANP leader, violence broke out in Banaras, Qasba Colony and parts of Orangi Town, which reverberated with gunfire. At least seven people were killed while twelve others were injured in different incidents of firing and armed attacks in the areas of Liaquatabad, Orangi Town and Qasba Mor.
two militants were killed in an air strike in Orakzai.
A truck, on its way to Muzaffarabad came under machine-gun fire by Indian forces from across the LoC. Two occupants of the truck were injured.
a bridge on the Peshawar-Torkham Highway was damaged when an explosive device beneath it went off wounding a security personnel.
A high intensity bomb plantd on a road in Charwa sector near the Indian border was defused by the Sialkot bomb defusal squad on Monday. Authorities said that the bomb was Indian made.
A net café in Bannu was destroyed and 4 customers were injured in a bomb blast.
A farmer, Abdul Sattar Lakhiar, was shot dead by armed men while he was working in his fields in the Fareed Lakhiar village, near Radhan Town.

As part of the violence on the second day of a two-day strike called by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM), protesters blocked the road and attacked a Rangers Wagon, in which a sepoy was killed while another was injured. Rangers retaliated and laid seige to Khata Chowk, and pitched battles were fought between the protesters and law enforcement agencies. Three people were killed by stray bullets while eight others were injured.
Four security personnel were seriously injured after they stepped on a powerful landmine while patrolling the area.

Flood affected IDPs from Kando Wah village of Mehar taluka, took out a procession from a relief camp and were marching towards the press club to protest against shortage of relief goods. They were near the house of Senior Minister Pir Mazharul Haq when unidentified men on motorbikes, who were holding clubs, attacked them. 9 protesters were injured.
A watchman was found murdered in Shadbagh on Wednesday by unknown men.
Unidentified gunmen opened fire on a street vendor and a passer-by in Orangi Town, killing him on the spot while injuring the passer-by.

Unidentified persons gunned down two personnel of a security agency in ASC Colony. The deceased, identified as Intikhab Alam and Amir Hamza were said to be informers of a secret agency, and were sitting in a park when they were attacked by unknown people.

Four people were killed and 12 others, 5 of them policemen, were injured in clashes between the police and a large crowd protesting against the Sindh government's decision for making Shahdadkot a new district instead of Qambar. According to the DPO the unruly mob attacked the Qambar police station and police had to use tear-gas, batons and aerial firing in retaliation.He stated that the protesters held an on-duty policeman hostage and ransacked the Qambar police station along with the TPO's office. Tehsil nazim accused the police of firing upon protesters. He claimed having witnessed the whole thing. According to independent sources, the clash ensued when the protesting crowd got word that two people of the area had been arrested by the police. The mob marched to the police station and the clash ensued. The tehsil nazim also accused the police of having barged into a meeting at the tehsil office and breaking window-panes and office furniture. DIG Mohammad Ramzan stated that an inquiry would be held into the matter. 50 people were taken into custody.

A young man was gunned down in Orangi Town when unidentified men opened fire on him in a street. The victim was a prayer leader of a local mosque. The police claimed it was too early to term it as a sectarian killing.
One person of the Jatoi tribe was killed and another injured when a group of people from the Maher village attacked the Nazar Jatoi village. The cause of the attack was stated to be land dispute.
a man gunned down his married sister allegedly in the name of honour after a heated argument.
A bomb planted on the wall of the Government Polite High School went off in Mastung, damaging the wall and windowpanes of nearby houses. No casualty was reported.

Three employees of the City Development Centre and Municipal Department were freed by the security forces after an armed encounter with kidnappers in which one captor was killed. Five people had been kidnapped earlier by unknown people in what was believed to be a ransom case. In bid to free them, security forces launched an operation in the area and encountered the kidnappers in a shootout near Sakhi Pul area, in which one injured kidnapper was also arrested. Two of the kidnapped were still held hostage.
The body of a young man was found dumped in the roadside in Korangi on Tuesday. There were torture marks on his body
Militants destroyed a vacant check post about 24 km from Khar using an explosive device. Nobody had so far claimed responsibility of the attack.
One policeman was injured in a clash between students of Polytechnic Institute Sargodha and police in Sargodha on Saturday.
A woman was shot and wounded by a stray bullet in her home.
Three militants were injured when security forces pounded militant hideouts in the Haleemzai tehsil of Mohmand Agency.
one Khasadar was killed when tribesmen fired on a peace jirga. Following this clashes erupted in the evening. The jirga was trying to broker a ceasefire
A bullet riddled body of a policeman was found in a desolate place. The reason behind the killing could not be ascertained.

A man, suspected to be a militant by witnesses, was killed in a blast outside a video shop. Police believed that the man was trying to plant a bomb outside the video shop when it went off prematurely.  Officials suspected the hand of radicals in the incident, who, in recent months, had distributed pamphlets warning music shops to close down.

A  violent day of mourning was observed by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement upon the death of their leader Chaudry Altaf Hussain and a constable was shot dead in Orangi Town in the midst of on-going violence.

a strike was observed in Balochistan against the killing of the three Baloch leaders.in turbat protesters became violent when law-enforcement personnel tried to disperse them. They threw stones at security men and burnt down two bank branches in a commercial area.

At least 12 people were killed and 30 others were injured when a suicide bomber blew up his explosive laden vehicle near a checkpost on the Pishtakhara intersection after a police man stopped him from entering the intersection.
Syed Ramazan Shah was found dead in his rented house. He was killed with an ice pick and the room was ransacked. The motive behind the crime was not known.
A man was killed and several others were injured in an armed clash between the Ajmal Dogar group and the Afzal Chadher group over a previous land dispute.
Unidentified persons snatched a Land Cruiser jee and later it was set on fire at the Nishan-i-Haider Chowk in Orangi.

An anonymous caller warned the police of a bomb planted at the district courts. The police, who searched the premises and foung nothing, termed it a hoax. However, the caller was successful in spreading panic amongst the lawyers and litgants.

Following a tip-off that militant commander Wahid Jalal was present at his den, district police conducted a raid which led to a severe exchange of fire. Following the exchange the militant commander and 22 other suspects were arrested.
Two armed men on a motorbike opened fire on policemen, killing one and injuring another. Head constable Abdul Wahid  was killed and constable Nasurullah was injured.
Two men of rival groups were killed in a clash that took place at Chak 184 GB in Toba Tek Singh, over an old tribal enmity that reportedly started during independence.
A journalist of the Express new channel, Muhammad Ibrahim Khan, was shot dead while he was going to his village.

The bodies of four policemen killed by kidnappers were found by Nasirabad police. A spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Army had informed journalists that the group had killed four more policemen who had been kidnapped along with other police personnel and labourers from Chattar area. The BRA gave a deadline of 48 hours to the government to release detained Baloch leaders and workers and threatend to kill more policemen if the demand was not met.
A member of TJP was gunned down by three armed assailants in Chishtian town on Friday
three hours after the blast in Khyber Bazaar, hand grenades were hurled at a police post in Wazirbagh.
Traders staged a demonstration against the killing of a trader by armed men in Quetta due to which they were lathi charged and teargassed by the police on Thursday.
Two armed men on a motorbike shot and killed Roedad Khan, area leader of the ANP while he was sitting with a friend outside a general store. His friend also sustained bullet injuries.

A remote controlled bomb was detonated at a development site in Arabi Tela where an international construction company was carrying out work. Machinary at the site was damaged but no loss of life was reported.
A bus of route 4-J (JA-1105) was set ablaze in front of Kharadar Police Station.
Khalid Khan, who was associated with the ANP, was shot and killed by armed motorcyclists while he was sitting outside with his friends.

The Rangers were attacked by armed men which led to a clash in which one of the assailants was killed an assistant sub-inspector was wounded. 3 suspects were detained as well. The Jafria Alliance Pakistan (JAP) and Majlis-i-Wahdat-i-Muslimeen claimed that it was the Rangers that initiated the violence by attacking the mourners returning from a funeral. The youths involved in the clash belonged to the Shia sect.
A white Suzuki blew up near the Novelty cinema on Nishter Road. According to officials a 200 gram explosive device was planted in the rear. No casualty was reported.
a man killed his mother and neighbour on the pre-text of karo-kari. He opened fire on them as his mother was talking to the neighbour at the door of her house.
The occupants of a Suzuki car opened indiscriminate firing in Unit No: 8, 9, 11. They also hurled firecrackers in Timber Market and Gahushala area. No one was injured or arrested.
Two people were shot down in the Kabal tehsil of Swat district. One of the dead was a prayer leader well known to be an anti-Taliban.
Zar Din of Mehmand Agency had a land dispute with one of his relatives, Ghaffar Khan, who then shot Zar Din dead in his house in Satellite Town.
An electricity pylon was blown up in Dagorak area of Charbagh causing disruption in power supply.
Syed Abbas was gunned down while he was standing at a bus stop. (See note)
A student affiliated with a religious organization was shot dead and his lawyer injured whne unidentified gunmen barged into his lawyer's chamber.

Four rockets were fired into Sui. One hit and destroyed the tower that supplies drinking water to the Sui Gas installations. Another hit the iron grill of the Pakistan Petroleum Limited, causing some damage to the office building. Two rockets hit a field and no casualties were reported. A senior official of the Sui administration stated that they did not have any idea as to the identity of the attackers.

A 30 year old woman and her 32 year old brother-in-law were shot dead  allegedly by the former's husband at a family function. The family claimed that the murders were a result of a long-standing monetary dispute while the police suspected an 'honour killing' case.
Sunni Tehrik (ST) called for a country-wide strike. Mohammad Ali was seriously wouned when unidentified people fired on a minibus in Korangi.

A second clash occurred here in one day. This time, an exchange of fire between PPP and MQM activists was reported. However, the TPO denied occurrence of this incident. This incident took place during the by-elections for 3 NA seats and 1 PA seat.

militants blew up 14 shops, most of them CD centres in a series of explosions at three main markets of Hakeemabad. The first blast occoured in Qurban Khan Plaza. The second blast took place at Fawad market. The third took place in Nowsherwan Market. Unidentified masked men coordinated this series of blasts.

Two students, who were on their way to school, were killed when unidentified men opened indiscriminate fire on them. The incident took place next to a Levies checkpost but the security personnel did not chase the assailants who fled.
Two men killed their 60 year old mother on the pretext of karo-kari in Kokrani village of Larkana. Later one of them stated that she was innocent. The main reason for killing her could not be known.
Mudassir Ahmed, who was associated with the Ahl-i-Sunnat Wal Jamaat (Formerly known as SSP), was targeted on 08-Aug-10. The incident was not reported before this paper.
The body of a worker bearing injury mrks from a sharp weapon, was found.
A protest demonstration was staged  by the traders of Beadon road against increasing dacoities. They blocked the road by burning tyres etc.
One person was injured in the Chahi village as the Indian shelling continued from across the LoC.
A boy was killed and several others were injured in a clash between Frontier Constabulary personnel deployed at United Nations Commision for Refugees Thuthi Saidan in Islamabad on Thursday
An unidentified body was found in New Karachi.

A gas pipeline was blown up from two places near Kashmore by unknown sabotuers. Their intentions for doing so were not known. A gas pipeline of Loti gas field was also targetted, along with a water pipeline supplying water to Uch gas field.
Three children were injured when a bomb in the shape of a toy exploded, according to the Home Department.
A man belonging to the Mahar tribe was killed in the Moli Dino village as part of the on-going dispute between the Mahar and Jatoi tribes.
Several journalists were attacked when armed men disguised at KESC officials entered the Karachi Press Club, thrashed them around and fled.

One person was shot dead and three others injured in an exchange of fire between two rival groups in village Kurralki Minara. Hafiz and Sadiq group had an old enmity over a piece of land. Hafiz, along with three accomplices, attacked Sadiq's house, who retaliated.
tribesmen fired nine rockets at FC checkpost in Dera Bugti Area. No loss of property or casualties were reported however.

Two activists o MQM suffered bullet injuries whereas offices of the sindh peoples students federation and two union council niab nazims were torched and ransacked as violence erupted in the wake of the custodial death of a man.

A mob on Empire road attacked the anti-encroachment staff of Larkana Municipal Corporation while they were demolishing illegal constructions. An anti-encroachment inspector, Gul Muhammad Gaad, was injured in the attack. The angry mob comprised mostly of shop keepers who burnt tyres and pelted stones at the anti-encroachment staff.

militants killed a man after accusing him of spying for the US forces in Afghanistan. The body of afghan national, Jalendhar was found. A note was found on his bullet riddled body which said that he was spying for Americans and asked people to let the body remain there till 2pm.
A young boy, Muhammad Hussain, allegedly murdered his sister, Hamida Bibi, on 'suspicion of illicit relations with another man'.
Sources said that two militants identified as Aziz and Bacha were injured during exchange of fire with security forces in the Daggar area of Buner.
Taliban attacked three army vehicles near Wana bazaar. 2 soldiers were killed while 7 others were injured.
militanst fired three rockets at a security post, however the rockets missed the target. One of the rockets landed near a basic health unit and the second at a governmnet high school building.
A local leader of PML N, Deedar Ghangro, was killed in Ratodero by unidentified gunmen who stopped his car in Bappar Mohallah.
following the killing of the baloch nationalist leaders violence continued in Balochistan. Six people were injured in a grenade attack.
Bashir Ahmed Shah, a resident of Larkana was found with a bullet injury in a stolen car. He later died in the hospital. The reason behind the killing is not known.
Some militants, allegedly belonging to the Bugti tribe, severely beat up personnel of Levies , who were on a patrol duty in the area.They also snatched their weapons and fled.
scores of youth appeared in groups in Aath Chowk and confronted with police. They blocked roads, lit bonfires and pelted police and private vehicles with stones.
In an armed clash at a polling station in Sohawa, 6 people were injured and were taken to the District Hospital.

enraged members of the JSQM damaged several cars and set 6 vehicles on fire in the wake of the death of their collegue in an attack on a JSQM rally. The official car of the district naib nazim Zafar Rajput was fired upon and a bus of Lakhra fire house was completely burnt. in Thatta they blocked the National Highway, torched tyres and pelted stones at passing vehicles.

A convoy on its way to kashmore was attacked by armed attackers. They opened indiscriminate fire and a bomb planted on the side of the road also exploded, blowing up one vehicle. The FC forces retaliated but the attackers escaped.
An automobile was set ablaze in a clash between two student groups in Tilak Incline on Sunday.
Militants blew up a dispensary in Khadi village, destroying the building completely.
A person was shot dead by unidentified men in banana orchard in Tando Muhammad Khan on Monday.

At least 20 people, including five policemen, were injured in a clash between National Students Federation supporters and the city police.  Police said that NSF activists attacked the city police station and damaged public property. Their reasons for attacking the police station were not stated.
A student was injured when rival student groups exchanged fire at the Murray College, Sialkot.

A suspected Al Qaeda operative was killed and his two accomplices were captured in an operation at Bhatti Colony in Lahore. The operation was launched by an intelligence agency when they surrounded a house in the colony. The inmates hurled hand grenades and opened fire and the Pakistan Elite Force had to be called. Exchange of fire continued for two hours. Two Elite force officials and two agency personnel were injured.

Enraged people set the MQM's unit office and a shop on fire, along with three vehicles and disrupted traffic in protest over the killings that had taken place in a clash between the Sunni Tehreek and MQM on 9th November, 2004.
A person was shot down by unknown assailants in Ranchhore Lines on Wednesday. Although his family denied, but police claimed that he had political affiliation.
An angry mob attacked a police station in Pak Colony area after a bullet riddled body of a boy arrived at the hospital.
IJT activists held protest demonstrations in front of several mosques against the US attacks on Afghanistan. They burnt effigies of President Gen Musharraf and US President Bush.
Iqbal, a farmer, was on his way to his village on a motorbike when two armed men opened fire at him. He died on the spot.
A rangers's official was killed in an encounter between the rangers and outlaws belonging to the Bugti areas.
tribesmen fired several rockets at FC checkpost in Karmo-Wadh area. One FC personnel was killed in the attack . Blochistan Liberation Army has claimed responsibility of the attack.
The Malakand Levies baton charged a student procession to protest against the imposition of emergency by Musharraf.

A car bomb exploded in a market, killing 10 people and injuring 26 others. It was claimed that the intended target was the nearby Badbher Police Station but the terrorists could not reach it which is why the bomb exploded in the middle of the market, destroying 10 shops and a restaurant and causing damage to 7 other shops. ; Follow-up: Police claimed that they had found evidence that 4 Taliban commanders were responsible for planning the blast.
A military vehicle hit a roadside bomb near the Brigade Headquarters killing four soldiers and injuring three others.

A remote-controlled IED placed on a main road was detonated when a car, containing two elders (Malik Zahirullah and Malik Mohibullah) and 4 'volunteers', was passing by. The two elders were killed while the volunteers were injured. The two elders had played a big role in raising the Salarzai Qaumi Lashkar which helped security forces fight militants.
In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, angry mob led by JUI MPA attacked the Hindu Temple in Loralai and set it ablaze on Tuesday.
A policeman was shot dead by five armed assailants in Khairpur Nathan Shah on Monday

A member of the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan attempted to throw a hand grenade at a convoy of the security forces near Sheikhan Pul but was intercepted and shot dead by the troops. A chit was found on him which had instructions about an attack on the security forces.

Three persons were injured when a powerful bomb went off at Madina Photo Studio in the Dhok Elahi Baksh Area. The photo studio owner lost his leg and two other boys sustained multiple injuries as well. According to the owner, three men in their forties had come to get their photograph taken and left a polythene bag in the shop, excusing themselves to get a shave before the picture. As soon as they left the bomb went off, bringin the building down. Police termed it an act of terrorism.
seven tribes men were injured when their vehicle hit an explosive device planted on the road.
12 militants and 2 security forces personnel were killed in a clash when militants attacked a base of security forces.
At several places in Lahore city, PML workers pelted stones and damaged seven vehicles as part of the wheel-jam strike.
Two persons were wounded in the Nabibaksh area when an explosive device went off.
Villagers killed six members of a militant group in Dara Shalbandi in Buner.
Following the assassination of Raza Haider, a police vehicle was attacked leaving 3 policemen injured.
A woman was killed while three others were injured due to Indian shelling along LoC on Friday
An elderly woman and a young boy were killed and three others were injured in the Mera village in bhimber as the Indian shelling from across the LoC continued.
A vegetable vendor was wounded by 'sniper firing' at Hali Road vegetable market. Some sources claim he was injured in firing by the police.
Militants were firing mortar shells at an army camp in Khyber when one shell landed in a house, killing a little girl and injuring 3 others.
A bomb exploded and injured two children. No further details were given.

Bashir Malah, an employee of the Highway Department, Sargodha, hacked his sister to death before setting her dead body on fire. The reason for the incident is stated to be the woman's decision to marry someone against the will of her parents and her brother about 7 years ago.
A sub-inspector of the CIA police was shot dead near Dehli Muslim Hotel in North Nazimabad while he was on his way to his office in a taxi.

Unidentified men attacked the Ajmer Nagri police station by firing three rockets from nearby residential areas. According to the police a portion of the roof of a nearby mosque was damaged and a constable was injured.
A 50-year old man was injured in firing by unidentified people.

Border Military Police and some local politicians are suspected of creating trouble for a foreign based company which is constructing a canal. The Central China Power Group International company's tanker hit a landmine injuring the driver and his helper.
4 people were killed and 5 were injured when Indian forces fired on villagers in the Athmuquam area.
The body of an unidentified woman was found in a drain. The body was tied up with ropes and bore marks of violence.
a girls' high school was blown up, damaging the building. No casualties were reported.

in another incident on the day of protests/riots against Nawab Akbar Bugti's killing. Police constable Haq Nawaz was killed after unidentified men opened fire at him near Sariab police station. Sabir Ali, a cameraman was beaten up by protesters who snatched his camera and mobile in Sariab Area.
The bullet riddled body of an unidentified young man was recovered from a forest near village Khandowa.
Rockets were fired from Fazil Chal hills in Kohlu which exploded near a camp of the Frontier Corps. No casualty or losses were reported

Police went on a state of high alert after three power pylons of the Water and Power Development Authority were blown up in different parts of Gadap town. Police sources said that two more bombs had been placed at the foot of another tower, about four kilometres away. These bombs did not go off.
Two policemen and two prisoners were killed and 2 policemen were injured when a police vehicle carrying 5 prisoners was ambushed by assailants. One of the prisoners escaped with the assailants.

Angry demonstrators encircled the CIA office to protest against the the CIA for allegedly torturing Allah Dita to death. The police resorted to 'mild' baton charge and tear gas in order to disperse the mob.
Armed men shot Gul Hassan Makrani to death in Makrani Oara.
A teenage girl was axed to death by her uncle in lal Pitafi village on the pre text of karo-kari.
1 person was murdered by unidentified men in Chak No 261 RB on Monday.
It was reported that 3 explosions and rocket blasts left 3 people dead and 4 injured. The deceased included two Afghan refugees. No details of the blasts are given.
The body of an unidentified middle aged man was found in Iqbal Park. The body had marks of violence on it which suggested that the man could have been strangled.
An unidentified body was found from Mominabad.

Six powerful blasts rocked different areas of Bara tehsil. Officials insisted that the explosions were aimed at creating harassment in the area but local people said they had found letters at blast sites “heralding” the arrival of the Taliban in Bara. The letter said the local Taliban had no enmity with any individual or a religious organisation, but warned of strong resistance if anybody tried to harass or arrest them. It said the blasts were a warning to people in Bara who had shed the blood of Pakistani and Afghan “mujahideen”. The explosions, however, caused no damage to life and property.
Muhammad Saleem was stabbed to death by his four brothers over a property dispute. No arrests were made.
Abdul Sattar, Ishaque, and Alam Kapri allegedly attacked and wounded Allah Bukhsh
armed men gunned down a traffic police head constable, Nazar Hayat, in Sariab area.

A jirga was being held in Battan Sharif Kalley in the remote Tirah valley to resolve a land dispute. However, the two rival groups opened fire on each other killing eight persons and injuring eight others.

Indian forces used light and heavy machine guns to fire on villages in the Sialkot working boundary's Chhumb, Jooriyan, Bajwat, Chaprar, Jammu, Saamba, Akhnoor and Zafarwal-Shakargarh-Narowal sectors.
Sources stated that militants planted explosives at the building of a primary school for boys in Tatan area. The building was completely destroyed in the explosion.  No casualty was reported.
A policeman was shot dead on airport road in Quetta. BLA has claimed the responsibility of the assassination.
A bomb explosion caused damage to the outer wall of a recently established checkpost at Charwazai, however, the Khasadars posted there remained unuhrt.
The brother of an outlaw was flogged on the orders of the Bara peace committee for his alleged involvement in an attack on its naib amir
Some unidentitifed men shot at Ghulam Abbas, injuring him and escaped. He later died due to his wounds.
A bomb exploded in University Town area on Wednesday due to which one person was injured and caused damage to two Suzuki pick-ups.
A person was shot dead by unidentified assailants in Federal.B.Area on Friday.
Two armoured vehicles of Nato were damaged when a group of people set a trailer transporting them tp Afghanistan on fire at maripur truck terminal.

Wapda's two main electricity poles were badly damaged in two  bomb blasts. The blasts took place near to the Chenab Rangers' post called Patoli and also damaged it as well as a couple of acres of standing wheat crop.
A man was killed by two people for an unspecified reason. The police rrested the accused men.
four people were injured when a mortar shell hit their house.
A terrorist plot foiled after two indigeniously made bombs are found at the roadside in Tajpura area, Lahore.

A car suicide attack tore through a crowded area surrounded by banks, shops and a wedding hall. The suicide bomber, sitting inside the vehicle, first hurled a hand grenade and then detonated himself and the car. The explosive material used is estimated to be around 100 Kg.  The target of the attacl was assumed to be an Askari Bank branch, operated by Army Welfare Trust. Followup: the death toll of the blast rose to 12 as two of the injured passed away.

Five persons, including 2 security persons, were killed and a number of others injured as a result of exchange of fire between Mohmand Rifles and the tribesmen in Meerokhel village. The Mohmand Rifles were conducting a search operation to clean up the area off arms and amunition. The tribesmen retaliated on grounds that their village did not fall under the Pakistani administration, and hence the security personnel had no right to conduct raids there.
Four militants were killed and ten others were injured in an air attack on Taliban hideouts in the villages of Mishto mela, Ghunda Mela and Ghiljo. Two camps were also destroyed.
Two motorcyclists were shot dead by armed persons in Alif Katcho on Saturday
An unidentified man was gunned down. No further details given.
Two rockets were fired in Kohlu that could not reach their target.
three soldiers were injured when a military truck was hit by an explosive device in Soor Bagh area.

A mother and her daughter were killed by Muhammad Khan Khoso, relative of the deceased. The murderer killed Parveen on suspicion of her having illicit relations with a man who was presently in jail. Parveen's mother was also shot dead when she tried to save her.

A suicide bomber, who was allegedly making his way towards a security convoy, exploded prematurely near a bus terminal killing at least 5 people and injuring 58. 7 vehicles and 12 shops were destroyed. ; Follow-up: One of the people injured succumbed to his injurise on 15-Jul-10.
The body of a young man was found, in an isolated place, with gunshot wounds to the head and chest.

Syed Mohsin Abbas, who was the brother of slain PML-N MNA and of a former district naib nazim, was killed when he stopped at a petrol pump and assailants in another car opened fire. Former councillor Mirza Mohammad Aslam, who was accompanying Mohsin Abbas, was also killed along with two other people who were at the petrol pump.
Unidentified gunmen opened fire on a GTS bus between Herichand and Umarze villages, killing two and injuring eight others.
A Head Constable was killed and three others injured in firing form a moving vehicle.
A coaster full MQM (altaf) activists was hijacked allegedly by memebers of MQM (Haqiqi). They beat up the passengers, after which the attackers fled.
The main railway line linking quetta to the rest of the country was blown up by a powerful local made bomb. The railway service was affected for several hours until the track was repaired.

Two persons were killed and five suffered injuries in fierce clashes between Magsi and Jamali tribesmen. Tribesmen killed were identified as Haji Khan Magsi and Ali Baksh. Firing continued till late night.
3 men were killed and 8 others were injured in a clash between two groups of tribesmen, the Rind and Lahri, at the cattle market.
A man was killed and two others were injured when a tractor hit a landmine in the Chamalang area.

At least two people were injured in a clash between All Pakistan Muttahida Student Organization and Islami Jamiat Talba in University of Karachi. Ranger deployed at University of Karachi resorted to light baton-charge and use of tear-gas to control the students.
A man was injured by Indian firing across LoC.

Following recent pitched pattles between a group of Arab militants and local tribesmen, about 5000 tribesmen attacked the Arabs, forcing them to flee to neighbouring Afghanistan. Mohammad Abdullah Arrefai, who was the leader of the militants, was killed while 10 militants and 4 women were captured. The two groups have been clashing recently. (See Note)
Khurshid Khan, a prominent landlord of the area was killed by three men from his village over an irrigation water dispute.
a man and a woman were killed on the pre-text of karo-kari in the Arbab Shaikh village, Gambat taluka. The father of the deceased woman lodged a FIR against Sardaruddin Shaikh.

Two armed motorcyclists went to a shop and asked the employees to pull the shutters down. When the motorcyclists were told that the shopowner was away and that the employees could not close the shop they opened indiscriminate fire, damaging shops and a pick-up.

The Pak-Afghan Defence Council called a strike in protest against the US-led attacks on Afghanistan. Protesters gathered from localities such as Jalalabad, Aurangabad, and  Nazimabad No. 3, they burnt tyres and clashed with the police and Rangers. The law enforcement agencies were trying to disperse the crowd and prevent them from heading towards the Nazimabad petrol pump intersection. They lobbed teargas shells, fired in the air, and chased the protesters in the streets. There were four people wounded.

One person was killed and three injured when security personnel(khasaadars) opened fire on protesters protesting against power loadshedding.In protest tribal women, blocked the Jamrud road and burnt tyres.
A person was killed and another was injured when unknown assailants opened fire on two motorcyclists in Gilgit on Monday. Authorities claimed that attack was sectarian(Between Shias and Sunnis).
An activist of a banned sectarian organisation (Sipah I Sahaba) was shot dead by unknown assailants in Clifton, Karachi.
Mubarak Afridi, a resident of Karachi, was found dead in his hotel room. He had been living there since 20-May.

The Afghan militia threw over 4 mortors at the Tora Bara Security checkpost that landed 200 metres from the checkpost. They also were firing at the checkpost, but there have been no reports about the loss of life or property.
3 security personnel were injured in a landmine explosion along a road while they were on patrol.
Abdul Latif Shahwani, who was a district office-bearer of the BNP-M, and another BNP party worker were attacked and killed by armed motorcyclists. The BNP-M termed it a targeted killing.
5 militants were killed in a clash between them and security forces in Swat on Sunday.

A group of students attacked the Nusratul Islam High School and broke its window panes and doors. Later the students hurled stones and bricks on the shops that were open. Police resorted to mild baton charge to disperse then. The incident occurred when there were mass protests throughout the city condemning the terrorist attack on a mosque which claimed 21 lives.

At least 10 people, including two women, were injured in a clash between two groups of people. Reports said Christian residents of the village wanted to hold a ceremony outside the church, which a group of 30 people, led by Irshad Fouji and Abdul Jabbar, allegedly tried to stop. Upon the organizers' refusal to stop the preparations, the group of people attacked the Christians, injuring 10 of them. The police allegedly tried not to file a report against the perpetrators because they were of influential backgrounds,
According to Agha Sher Ali, resident of Ali Raza Bagh, his son was shot dead in a vacant plot near their house. He denied it was due to a personal enmity.
A military convoy came under fire in jandola. No more details available.
The dead body of a man was found in Lytton Road area on Tuesday
Shamoon, a barber by profession, shot his two sisters at their home for 'honour'.
A person was shot dead by unknown assailant within the jurisdiction of secretariat police station on Saturday
a girl was shot dead by her brother, Manzoor Ahmed Sandrello, in Ali Sanderlo village in Moro. The girl wanted to marry a boy of her choice.

Militant groups of Lashkar-i-Islam and Ansaarul Islam braced for a showdown and fortified their positions in Sedak area. Both groups established their positions and gathered supporters to prepare for a possible encounter. It was also learnt that the Zakakhel tribe has announced raising an armed band of 200 men to support Lashkar against its opponents in Tirah.
The body of an unidentified youth was found.

Jewellers Association Faisalabad organized a demonstration, where they blocked the main road and burnt tyres to protest against the police's failure to arrest the robbers who looted gold worth Rs 48 million from a jeweller.
Two workers of the SSP were murdered when unidentified men opened fire on them in Gilmala village while they were on their way back from a Qul ceremony.

A young man was shot dead in Bantwa Nagar, Liaquatabad by unknown persons.  SSP central stated that the motive behind the killing could not be known as the deceased political affiliation could not be established.
4 Rangers personnel were kidnapped and killed by unknown assailants. (See Note)

An activist of Mohajir Qaumi Movement who was an MQM-H sector in charge of Model Colony, Yameen Sikandar -resident of Mohammadi Colony, Khokhrapar. According to the autopsy, he had suffered internal injuries and had rope marks around his wrists.
Iqbal Nabil Khan was found dead in his house. His head had been hit with a sharp weapon. He was the driver of a coach
Boota Masih was stabbed to death by four people, inlcuding two women. Further details not given.
2 passers by were injured when a bomb planted outside a PTCL office in Kalat went off. 2 people were injured and slight damage to the building and other structures was reported.
Unknown miscreants planted an improvised explosive device at the door of Burhan CD shop. After the blast, the shop was partially damaged and the window panes of the nearby shops were damaged.
The bullet-riddled body of a militant commander in the Kalam area of Swat was found.

a bomb exploded at the clinic of Dr. Farooq Haider, the Chairman of his faction of Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front, in Rawalpindi Cantonment killing 10 and injuring 30 others. Dr. Haider held held the Indian Intelligence Agency RAW responsible.; three Indian agents have been arrested for the bombing.

During the second phase of the operation Brekhna (lightening), security forces, backed by helicpoter gunships, warplanes and artillery pounded militant hideouts in Suran Darra, Musakhel, Bahadar Kalley, Matai, Shinwari, and Ghalingar areas of Bezai and Safi tehsils. Administration officials said that 50 militants were killed and several others injured as air strikes destroyed hideouts. Four security personnel were killed and several injured during clashes with militants.

a security personnel was killed and four personnel were injured when an FC vehicle patrolling the area around a gas installation hit an anti-tank landmine. The Baloch Republican Army claimed responsibility for the incident.
A clash between Lakhan tribe and Wallan tribe left 3 Lakhan tribesmen dead and 1 injured. The clash was the result of a dispute over the possession of some agricultural land.

4 missiles fired by US drones targeted a vehicle and a compound, kiling 12 militants. 9 militants were Afghan while the rest were Pakistani. Among the dead was an 'important militant commander' from Khost province of Aghanistan.
A man was arrested with a TT pistol after a police party came under a firing attack. No further details were given.

As part of the on-going protests against the Islamiat curricula for primary and secondary schools in Gilgit, hundreds of primary and secondary school students staged protest rallies on the third consecutive day and created hurdles and burnt tyres on roads. No loss of life or injury was reported. 16 students were reportedly arrested.
TTP militants blew up the only telephone exchange in Darra Adamkhel, suspending all PTCl phoneline connections in the area.

A coal mine blast left 5 miners dead and another 6 injured. The labourers were busy in their routine excavation work when the blast took place. It was mentioned that the mine holder, Jan Ali, was issued a warning a day earlier to stop work at the mine but he did not comply.
2 person were killed and 3 were injured when the rivals belonging to Zardari tribe opened fir on them in Nawabshah Taluka on Thursday.

Twenty-sxi pilgrims were killed while another eight were injured when armed men intercepted their bus on its way to Taftan. They ordered them to disembark, lined them up, checked their ID cards and opened fire. Most of the dead belonged to the Hazara tribe. Soon after, armed men killed three other people who were in an ambulance on their way to take the injured to Quetta. The Banned outfit Lashkar-i-Jhangvi claimed resposibility for the attacks.
A girls school buiding was blown up in Tangi village, Salarzai.
The bomb disposal squad diffused 9 grenades planted by militants under a bridge that is frequently used by police and the general public.
Three persons allegedly shot and killed a doctor at his home.

some relatives of SSP Mehr Zafar Abbas Luck, tried to occupy land on Rakh Branch Canal where a new wagon stand is being constructed by the Faisalabad Municipal Corporation on Irrigation Deparment Land. The PRO of FMC pulled down the structure raised by the relatives of the SSP. this land grabbing incident was taking place between two political families of the Punjab.

One, Daim Langarial was allegedly shot dead by Zafar, resident of Chak No. 58/KB over an old land dispute when the 2 groups exchanged fire. Noor Mohammad was killed in the crossfire and 2 other people were injured.

One paramilitary soldier was killed and three others wounded when a bomb exploded near the Banda Post. The soldiers were fetching water from a nearby spring when the bomb went off. The Gul Bahadar Group, which has alliance with the group of Baitullah Mehsud, claimed responsibility for the attack.
Video cassettes and CDs were set on fire in a campaign against obscenity in the Karkhano Bazaar. The government officials ordered police officials to confiscate all such materials and destroye them.

Students belonging to PSF held a violent protest aginst the desecration of Babri Mosque in India by Hindu militants. When they tried to enter the court premises the police baton charged them and arrested the injured workers.

Two shops allegedly dealing with narcotics were destroyed and four others partially damaged in an explosion at a market in Salarzai tehsil. The two shopkeepers whos shops were blown up had received threats earlier to wind up their businese.
Around 3000 enraged labourers of contruction companies burnt offices, injured 15 officials and later threw traffic out of gear because they hadn't received their salaries.
A low-intensity explosive device was planted and detonated on the boundary wall of Shezan Factory. Two people suffered minor injuries.

A roadside remote-controlled bomb planted in a garbage dump was detonated when a school bus was passing by. The bus was damaged, 1 teenage boy was killed while 5 other people, including the bus driver, were injured. The TTP claimed responsibility for the blast.
Three persons were injured when a cracker went off in Fun Land in the Clifton area of Karachi.
Two soldiers of Frontier Corps were injured when their vehicle hit a landmine in Kahan tehsil of Kohly district.

at least 4 people were killed and more than 13 others were injured when a group of unidentified men opened indiscriminate fire near Lal Masjid in Jhang. The police moved in and arrested more than 50 people belonging to different sects.

7 students were injured in Sindh Agriculture University Tandojam on thursday in a clash between Sindh Taraqqi Pasand students Federation, Sindh People's Student Federation and Baloch Students Organisation(Hayee Group) and Pashtoon Students Organisation as they were protesting against the VC of the university
Militants fired two rockets at FC Kotal checkpost near Darra. The security forces retaliated and targetted the militant hideouts in Darra Adamkhel. No casualty was reported from either side.

Prisoners in the district jail started protesting when an inmate, Muhammad Alam Lund, suffering from acute renal pain was refused medical aid. The prisoners first all refused to have breakfast, and when the jail superintendent, Mr. Sadat Ali, approached, they attacked him and other jailers with pitchers and bottles. The law enforcement agencies resorted to heavy teargas shelling. The situation was finally under control when Muhammad Alam was taken to the hospital.
Pro-Taliban militants ambushed the vehicles of the top officials in Mir Ali area, killing a guard and injuring two others.
A young man was found dead. Sammasatta police said an arm was found chopped.
strike observed to condemn the arrest of political party activists. The police opened fire on them.

An old woman, Attiya, was allegedly shot dead by accused Tariq, who wanted to kill her son Attiq. He suspected that Attiq had provided information about him to the police. When the Tariq could not find Attiq, he killed his mother instead. It could not be determined from the report whether the accused had any political affiliations or not.
An unidentified body with a bullet wound to the head was found in a parked taxi.

local police resorted to baton-charge to disperse a group of farmers who were protesting against the closure of the Sarwala Distributory. It started from Dhobi Gat and terminated at Katchery Bazaar, where the protesters were baton-charged by the police.

An injured man was shot dead in the DHQ hospital by his rivals over a land dispute. He had been attacked earlier but had narrowly escaped and was only left injured, some ten days back. However, the rivals came to his surgical ward and shot him.
A vehicle of the Frontier Corps was destroyed in a powerful landmine explosion in PirKoh gas field area of Dera Bugti.
Gas supply to power and fertilizer plants in Punjab and Khyber-Paktunkhawa (NWFP) was suspended following a blast in main pipelines in Shahwali area of Rajanpur. The blast damaged a 30-inch piepline.

The chief of Punjab Muslim Students' Federation, Rana Imtiaz was shot and injured in a targetted attack by five men who later escaped. He was shot in the college premises during a function to mark the death anniversary of a slaim MSF leader.

Taliban militants clashed with security forces during a join army and paramilitary search operation in Kohat. 17 militants were killed while one security man was injured. Arms, explosives and 8 suicide vests were also seized .
Vice president of PML-J PP-198, Bao Farzand Ali was shot and killed by unidentified armed men. His friend Sultan Ahmed was also killed in the firing while another friend was injured.

Two American diplomats working at the US consulate in Karachi were killed and another was wounded when their vehicle was came under attack by two unidentified men in a taxi, armed with AK-47 rifles who opened indiscriminate fire on each side of the vehicle, killing one man on the spot while injuring two others, one of whom later succumbed to her injuries. According to officials, it was an act of terrorism most probably carried out by the drug mafia to keep foreign investors away.
a man, Pathan Mazari, shot dead his wife and her alleged paramour in Ghulam Qadir Mazari village
A US drone fired missiles at a house, killing 7 militants.
Armed men kidnapped 7 people of Masoori clan, including 2 women, after intercepting their vehicle. An enmity between the two clans resulted in their kidnapping.

Suspected militants fired four rockets from an unknown location which landed in agricultural farms and a drain in the limits of the Badbher police station. A police official said that the militants had tried to hit the Shahab Khel police post but missed the target and the rocket landed away from the post. He said the rocket was probably fired from Khyber Agency where security forces had launched an operation against criminals.

Three people were killed in seperate incidents of shooting by unknown armed men. The police claim that the victims were fired at indiscriminately but the PPP claims that they were all party 'sympathizers' and were thus targeted.
A bomb exploded on election day in a congested area. One person was injured.

A clash near Banoo town in the mirpur batoro tehsil between the supporters of PPP's and PPP-SB's candidates resulted in injuries to 19 persons. The incidnet occurred right after voting was closed and ten of the Chang tribe and nine of the Palija tribe were injured.

At least 20 students and a policeman were injured in a clash between  police and the Islami Jamiat Talaba during a demostration by the students for their movement for restoration of their rights. The students refused to disperse and used brickbats and the police were forced to resort 'lathi-charge' to control the situation.
A man was injured in a shooting incident in Brigade area.
At least 12 suspected militants were killed when security forces backed by gunship helicopters and planes attacked the Taliban bunkers.

2 policemen and 9 \terrorists\" were killed in a joint operation by Police and Eagle Squad against suspected terrorists. The Operation continued for many hours and there was an exchange of heavy gunfire. The police cordoned off a large area. "
A man was killed outside the Sindhi Hotel in Liaquatabad.

Dozens of Jaranwala bar association members, led by president Shahbaz Haider, took out a rally and burnt tyres on the road before smashing the windows of the DDOR's office. They were demanding the immediate transfer of the DDOR. They claim that they had been protesting for 2 weeks but nobody had paid heed to the issue.

Riots broke out as protesters assembled in the Mohammad Gat area, the entry of Bajaur Agency, for a demonstration against the air strike on a seminary in Bajaur. Protesters ransacked public property, damaged a grid station and an under construction Khasadar post.
Rangers arrested two of the JSQM workers durng a protest demonstration against the arrest of the JSQM leader by the police. The police had to resort to baton-charge to bring the crowd under control.
A man was kidnapped and killed in Orangi.

A clash between two student groups left Pervez Siddiqi, Jamal Leghari and Zulfiqar Leghari injured. Some students also resorted to aerial firing which spread panic in the area. However, police rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control.
gunmen shot a man dead in Kani Kot village when he was returning home with his wife.

Mustafa Mari, leader of SPSF(SB) was killed in an encounter in Qasimabad on Monday. Groups activists claimed that it was a fake encounter, however police claims exactly opposite to it.  As the original incident was not reported, details have been taken from this article.

Hundreds of Anjuman Talba-e-Islam (ATI) and Sunni Tehrik (ST) activists took to Bainazir Bhutto Road to protest the killing of a religious scholar Maulana Dr Sarafaraz Ahmed Naeemi in a suicide bomb blast. The protesters chanted slogans and set tyres on fire. The rally was led by Shabab-i-Islami Ameer Maulana Mufti Hanif Qureshi.
fierce clash took place in Charbagh and Kabal triggering a massive exodus. Security forces used mortar, artillery and helicopter gunships to attack militant hideouts.

Enraged students of the University of Peshwar ransacked a post office and smashed windowpanes of campus buildings in protest against hours long load-shedding. The police on campus resorted to teargas shelling to subdue the angry students.
Zafar Bharwana of Makhina village shot dead Kazim Bharwana of the same village over a land dispute.
A bullet-riddled body of an unidentified man was found in Jamshed Quarters.
The body of a young man was found bearing torture marks. Police has taken the body into custody.
A Taliban 'commander' Alamgir, and his father were killed in an exchange of fire with the security forces operating in the area.
A man was gunned down when three unidentified men opened fire on him in the limits of Garhi Kapoora police station in Mardan.
A security forces led operation in Kabal tehsil of Swat led to at least 6 people killed and 40 injured.

The son of Sindh IGP Ziaul Hassan, Zohair Zia, escaped an attempt on his life when some five armed men attacked him when he was present at a public gathering in connection to his election campaign. One of the attackers was caught, who turned out to be a guard of Zohair Zia's opponent, MPA Amanat (full name was unreadable in the report).
Two labourers were killed and four others were injured when unidentified men attacked a camp of the road construction company. The area was cordoned off and some suspects had been picked up.

Family members of Sheikh Sadiq shot at the family members of Rahat Gul when they were constructing a house adjacent to Sheikh Sadiq's residence.  According to some people, the two families have a property dispute.
unidentified persons planted an improvised explosive device at Zakir babershop, destroying the shop completely. A few adjoining shops were also partially damaged.

The students of Lal Masjid reportedly misbehaved with journalists and tried to snatch their cameras. The students adopted the harsh behavior with the journalists for providing live-coverage of the clash between the Lal Masjid brigade and the government.
bike riders killed one Ghulam Sadiq with bullets in the ongoing spate of target killings.
A union council naib nazim sustained a bullet injury when some PPP activists allegedly opened fire on him.
Helicopter gunships targeted militant hideouts, killing 25 militants and injuring another 18. An explosive-laden vehicle was also destroyed in the shelling.
Aijaz Ali was shot dead by two brothers, Mir Mohammad and Jalal
The body of a 30-year-old man with bruises on his face was found in a manhole in Jubilee Town.

A crucial supply line for the US and Nato forces was disrupted when a bridge on the Peshawar-Torkham road was blown up. The blast damaged the bridge and it collapsed when a trailer loaded with cement was crossing it.
One child suffered injuries when a shell struck a compound in Bazikhel village. No other detail was given.

a man was killed and 2 others were injured in a clash between two groups, one led by a property dealer Nisar and the other by union council naib Nazim Chaudhry Nadeem Abbas over a property dispute. Police reached the scene and arrested over a dozen people.

Armed men attacked a passenger coach, injuring one person identified as Kashif. ; Follow-up: It was reported that 3 other people had also been injured in this attack and that Kashif succumbed to his injuries in the hospital.
Another youngster was found shot dead near Shah Faisal Naddi Road. His body bore multiple bullet wounds in the chest.
a soldier was killed and 5 soldiers and three militanst were injured in an exchange of fire with militants when paramilitary soldiers who were building a checkpost were attacked on the Datakhel road.
Activists of the PADC damaged a cinema \hoarding\" on the Mall during the strike against the US-led attack on Afghanistan."
A security guard was found dead in Ittefaq Town, Hanjerwala.

Madrassa students and their supporters stopped a train near Shahdan Lond Railway Station by placing boulders on the railway track. The police reached the area with reinforcements and the local officials began negotiations with protestors to remove hurdles. When negotiations failed the protestors pelted the police with stones, the police reacted with teargas shelling and eventually opened fire as well, killing three protestors. Later the mob went on a rampage, setting fire to a number of official vehicles and 'kidnapped' some police officials- 4 according to the police-  after thrashing them. Earlier in the day madrassa students blocked the inter-provincial Indus Highway. During this time a prisoners-van carrying religious leaders arrested during a midnight crackdown ahead of the strike was passing through and was intercepted by the mob. It reportedly managed to set free a number of ulema and thereafter set the van on fire. ; Follow-Up: Local Hizbul Mujahideen Nazim Junaid Akhwan, who had sustained serious bullet wounds in police firing on Nov 9 succumbed to injuries and died on Nov 10 raising the death toll to 4.
A railway line was blown up near Musa Colony, which lead to a suspension of rail traffic.

A local leader of Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan was shot and injured by a rival party when he was kidnapped from the Yateem Khana bus stop, tortured, shot and thrown near the Hanjerwal police station in critical condition; Follow up: Two unidentified men shot and killed the injured SSP activist who was recovering from an earlier attempt on his life. They entered the hospital ward and opened fire on him, killing him on the spot, and fled.
Militants attacked an army's security camp with four rockets, injuring 1 soldier.

A man claiming to be the spokesperson of BLA said that his organisation had carried out attacks on security forces in various parts of Kohlu districts killing 6 soldiers and injuring several others. The government sources have not verified this information.
The decomposed body of a 40 year old man was recovered from a drain. According to the police, 4 bullet wounds were found on the body.
A tirbal Lashkar attacked militants which led to an exchange of fire. 3 lashkar volunteers died while 8 others were injured.
In clashes with militants five lashkar volunteers and four levy officials were killed in the Chamjana area. 29 militants were also killed in the clash.

Residents of Karampur Town and nearby localities held a demonstration against prolonged outages and thrashed two Mepco officials at a local cotton factory. The demonstrators alleged that the two linemen had disconnected the power supply to 'oblige a local cotton factory owner'. The executive engineer of Mepco intervened to rescue the linemen and ordered the restoration of power supply to the area.
Unidentified people set fire to the factory and fled. No casualties were reported but thebuilding was damaged.
A man was killed and a woman was injured in the kahuta sector as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.

A body was found near the Kundal post of Bajwat. A huge bag of explosives was found near the body.; Follow-up: An Indian terrorist entered Pakistan through the Bajwat sectors' border village, and was carrying 6 high intensity bombs. One of the bombs exploded and killed the person.
Baghali Jatoi shot dead his mother-in-law-Musammat Aminat- on suspicion of her character and fled.

There were sporadic incidents of violence reported in various areas and at least 3 people were injured when they were fired on. This incident occurred during the strike by MMA against the killings of its workers during the by-elections.
the TNFJ carried out a procession on Al-Quds day. Members of a particular sect raised slogans calling the processionists infidels and stoned them. 4 students were critically injured.

Malik Sabil Khan, who was an anti-Taliban tribal elder, was found shot dead after he had been kidnapped earlier in the week. 3 elders from the same area who were against militants were also killed on the same day that Sabil Khan was kidnapped.
A person was found murdered in Rohri on Tuesday. He had been missing for two days. There were torture marks on his body and his head was also chopped off.
A dead body of a man was found bearing marks of violence.
A man was wounded in 'sniper firing' in Landhi, Karachi.

Protesters- led by Muttahida's Abdul Sattar Ansari and Zafar Rajput and JSQM's Sikandar Soomro and Saleem Sayal- moved towards the KPC, which was the planned venue for the hunger-strike. However, they were stopped by LEA personnel in civilian clothing and were roughened up and bundled into police vans and sent away. Some 25 activists were arrested, including 5 women. According to MQM, they arrested protesters were joined by three dozen women and three dozen elders and the LEA resorted to highhandedness and torture.
Two people were shot dead and four others were injured in an exchange of fire between two rival groups over a land dispute.

Following the strike call given by MQM steering committee, armed youths took to the streets and resorted to violence. Protesters stopped a Zeal Pak Cement Factory staff bus and set it on fire. The driver managed to escape.
