Tension gripped Baldia Town after the identification of the decomposed dead body. MQM activists were attacked as a rival group claimed the victim belonged to their group and blamed the MQM for his murder. Several shops were set on fire by Shafeeq's supporters in Dilawar Mohalla.

Residents of an area in Gharibabad took to the streets to protest against the anti-encroachment government team who planned on demolishing some structures said to be in the way of the Lyari Expressway. The protesters burnt tyres and chanted slogans but the police did not intervene with any force. They did manage to curb the tension before it escalated into violence.

Two suicide bombings in quick succession at the Abdullah Shah Ghazi shrine left over 8 people dead and over 60 injured. The first bomb was detonated at the main entrance of the shrine followed by a blast within a 100 yards near the stairs where people take their shoes off. ; Follow-up: A person injured at the shrine succumbed to his injuries.
Militants attacked security posts with heavy weapons which led to an hour-long exchange of fire between militants and security forces. Eventually, security forces managed to push militants back.
A grenade hurled by militants exploded near railway tracks in the eastern bypass area. No other information was given.
As part of the violence on the second day of a two-day strike called by the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM), protesters set a vehicle on fire in phuleli.

The body of an MQM Altaf activist was brought to the JPMC after he was shot dead in Malir City.  The details of the case were not reported, but this incident was more than likely connected to the violence between the two groups in Landhi, Korangi, and Malir.

Security forces and militants exchanged fire in the South Waziristan tribal region; Follow up: Clashes between security forces and militants continued in the south waziristan region for a second cosecutive day. Along with firing artillery shells the PAF jets made several sorties on the areas.
A 22 year old man identified as Shahzaza was stabbed in Khayabane-i-Roomi in Clifton. The motive behind the attack was not mentioned.

Following the death of Ishaq Bacchu in a clash between two communities in Lyari, armed protesters took to the streets and forced shopkeepers to pull their shutters down. A group of protesters set ablaze two restaurants, a bus, a truck and two motorcycles.
Three unidentified masked men opened fire at the car of Malik Rashid Ahmed, former Chairman of the Municipal Committee Ahmadpur Sharqia and leader of the Opposition in Municipal Committee.
A proclaimed offender was killed in an encounter with the law enforcement agents in Madina Colony in a raid by the police. Three of his companions managed to escape.

The residents of American Quarters, Hazara Colony, Bohri Compound, Irani Colony and others protested against the shortage of water supply to their area for the last few days. They blocked the main Fateh Chowk and burnt a garbage containter. The SDM of Latifabad rushed to the spot and held negotiations. The result was that the supply would be restored  by 9:30pm and the residents would clear their water dues within the next two days. The protest lasted 30 minutes.
a man axed to death his younger sister on suspicion of her having illicit relations in Sanda area.

outages-ridden people wanted to move towards the Faislabad Electric Supply Company Office when the police stopped them. They got infuriated and pelted the police with stones as a result of which 5 constables were injured. The police resorted to baton-charge which resluted in 7 protesters being injured. The police also arrested 5 protesters.

Police arrested 27 Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) activists for violating section 144 that prohibits processions on Mall road Lahore. The protest was held to mark the anniversary of 1999 military takeover of government. To disperse the protesters, police used batons which left eight activists injured. as the protesters did not disperse, they were beaten up and dragged by the policemen before being herded up into official vans.
Two people, Haji Qasim Magsi and Aftab Ahmed Mallah, were shot dead by 4 gunmen on motorcycles.
A government primary school for girls was blown up by unidentified armed men.

An enraged crowd of flood affected IDPs staged a demonstration and pelted cars, shops and offices with stones to protest against the non-payment of cash for celebrating Eid that the Government had promised it would provide. The mob tried to move towards Clock Tower chowk but were stopped by a heavy contingent of police.

in a firing spree a 5-month pregnant mid-wife of the eye department of the hospital was killed and 3 others were injured when the Deputy Medical Superintendent of the hospital Dr. Shah Beg Chandio along with his associates opened fire on the protesters. the paramedical staff of the CMCH took out a procession at the hospital as their demands had been turned down.

Sporadic firing, stoning and stabbing was reported from Latifabad during the curfew break between 4 - 5 PM. Aftab Nizammi and Noor Mohammad were killed in the crossfire while Abid Hussain and an unidenified person were stabbed to death.
Unidentified armed persons killed a man in indiscriminate firing in Dubber area; the reason for the killing was unknown.
terrorists opened fire at Lal Qila, but suffered heavy casualties when troops fired back.
Sharif Chattar, Principal of Givernment Degree College was attacked by a former student in a bid to kill him. He escaped after injuring the Principal.

A violent clash occurred between the protesters and the police in which the protesters attacked the police by pelting them with stones. The police resorted with teargas shelling to disperse the crowd. Aqaldeen and Riffatullah were injured.

Six armed men entered the house of Nawabzada Nasrullah, President of Paksitan Democratic Party and tried to make their way to the Nawabzada's room. They were stopped by some party workers and then they fled. Nawabzada Nasrullah has expressed his ignorance about the motive of the assailants, who have been identified.

Two tribesmen were killed while five others were injured, including the SHO of Kuchlak Police station during a violent demonstration held by the Maahtarzai tribesmen over the arrest of one of their men, when a clash between the police and the tribesmen. Five rockets were fired on the police and a APC was completely destroyed. Twenty-six suspects were arrested.
A strike was observed in interior Sindh towns on the call of JSQM against the construction of the Kalabagh dam and greater Thal canal project. A local passenger bus was set on fire.
Muhammad Javed shot dead his grandfather, Fateh Muhammad and his brother Muhammad Ramzan besides injuring three women over a land disput in Khateeb colony

The Indian Security Forces continued firing on Zafarwal, Charwa, Bajwat, Chaprar, Harpal, Sucheetgarh, Bajragarhi and Shakargarh sectors. As a result, a villager- Muhammad Husain of Bajwat Sector- was killed in the courtyard of his house by stray bullets fired by the Indian Forces. The firing also killed 2 animals, badly damaged 6 houses and several tractors as well as distrupted the sowing of paddy crop. The Chenab Rangers returned the fire after which the Imdian forced fled to their bunkers.

25 militants attacked Nato oil tankers with sophisticated weapons and used timed explosive devices to blow them up. 13 oil tankers were blown up while 4 people were killed and 6 were left injured. The police claimed that they exchanged fire with the militants and recovered explosives and grenades that they had left behind.
An ice seller, Ghulam Shabbir Butt, was shot dead. According to the police, the motive behind the incident is unknown.
One person was killed in Khorian village as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.
Akbar Hameed was shot dead by armed men on a motorbike.

Twenty members of the Chandio clan attacked four members of the Mari clan over an old agricultural land dispute. The armed men opened indiscriminate fire on the car of the Mari clan. They also stole Rs. 12,000 and 2 licensed shotguns.

Syed Muslim Hasan Rizvi, an activist of Sipah-i-Muhammad, was shot dead in Model Town-B area. The deceased was the elder brother of Ghazanfar Rizvi, vice president of the Punjab Tehrik-i- Jafria. It was claimed by the relatives of the deceased and eye witnesses that the target of the attack was Ghazanfar Rizvi, and that the killers mistook Syed Muslim Hasan Rizvi for him as they resembled each other.
Faizullah, an SSP worker, was killed and another man was injured when they were attacked by unknown assailants.
Two members of a family were shot dead while three others were injured by their rivals over an old enmity in Botala Sharam Singh village on Sunday.
A man and a woman were killed by a cousin of the woman on the pre text of karo-kari. The relatives of the woman protested and alleged that the killings occurred to take over  the woman's property.

Two people were killed and three injured in an armed clash between Malik Dinkhel and Qamberkhel clans of the Afridi tribe. The clash started over a road being constructed by the Deenkhel clan which crossed Qamberkhel territory.
An activist of the banned Sipah-i-Sahaba was gunned down outside a shop by unknown assailants, one of whom was wearing a burqa (veil).
A shootout between Fida Joggi and Shahzad gangs resulted in a death of a woman. Both these gangs are involved in drug dealing.
PPP leader Amir Hamza Bugti was gunned down by unidentified assailants near Sui on Thursday. Five others were injured out of which his bodyguard succumbed to injuries on Friday
2 personnel of the Levies Force were kidnapped and a checkpost was destroyed near the Pakistan-Afghanistan border. No group had taken responsibility for the incident.

A bomb planted on a vehicle was detonated, killing all 5 occupants of the car. A Taliban spokesman in the area, Hafiz Saeed, criticized the blast and said that stern action would be taken against those responsible.

two activists from a militant organization from Bara had forcibly stopped some vehicles on the main Jamrud-Landi Kotal road. When it was reported, the police rushed to the area and aerial fired to scare them. They retaliated  with firing. One militant was caught while the others took refuge in nearby houses.
Ten people were injured in an armed clash between two groups over cattle grazing in the paddy crop.
security forces backed by artillery and helicopter gunships attacked militants' hideouts in Gujar Kalay Amnavi, Sabonae and Yakh Tangi Top areas of Shangla.
As part of the on-going MQM strike, of the At least five vehicles were set on fire in New Karachi, North Nazimabad, Korangi and Liaquatabad.
A man was shot dead by seven people over a land dispute in Nowshera Virkan. The deceased was identified as Muhammad Sarwar.
Three policemen were killed and another was injured when two dozen Taliban, armed with rocket launchers and automatic weapons, attacked a checkpost on Chakisar road in Karora area of Shangla.

Military helicopters launched an offensive after reports about a fierce gunfight between two factions of a banned militant organisation in Tirah valley. Four persons, including a key militant commander, were killed in the attack when gunships and artillery were used to pound militant areas of Sandana, Nari Baba and Nangrosa.
The decomposed body of a boy was found. According to the doctors, the boy had been hanged.
A man was shot dead and another injured when unknown assailants opened fire at a roadside hotel.
Following the killing of ANP activist Paras Khan, unknown people resorted to firing, injuring 2 people.

On the day of mourning announced by the MQM after 2 people were killed in a clash between police and MQM workers the day before, MQM workers took to the streets and lit bonfires and damaged property in addition to clashing with police at various places. The report on the incidents of the day claims that 30 people were wounded but the report itself only accounts for 20 of those. ; Another report in the same newspaper claims that 35 buses, mini-buses and yellow cabs were damaged or completely destroyed by the protesters.
Six people were killed in a clash between two groups in Jaranwala when they used axes and clubs against each other over an irrigation water dispute.

The renewed wave of targetted killings that began a couple of days ago with gun attacks in Malir and Landhi spread to Lyari as two young men were killed while another was injured when unknown men opened fire on them on Jamila Street.

Paramilitary forces subdued the pro-Afghan tribesmen after intense gunbattle in the Anargi area in the Mohmand tribal region, which left three rebels dead and four wounded. Pakistani forces used armoured personnel carriers, heavy artillery, machine guns, rockets and helicopters. Security officials alleged that militiamen of the Jalalabad Corps commander, Malik Hazrat Ali, were involved in actively fighting with Pakistani forces.

A heavy gun-fire battle between the warring Bugti and Mazari tribes continued when rocket fire was exchanged on the Punjab-Balochistan border. The exchange of fire resulted in damaging two main gas pipeline in the region, which caused supply to be halted. There was no respite to the battle till the next day and law enforcement was reluctant to defuse the tension.
Ten militants and two tribal elders were killed in Gutkai and Bandarae areas of Bajaur region.
3 people of a family were killed by unknown men in Shahdara area on Tuesday
A security personnel was killed and his six of his colleagues were injured in a clash that took place between troops and militants after militants opened fire on them from the Yousaf Talab area.
A minor girl was killed and another injured when a bomb went off in a house in Orangi Town. The bomb was locally made and was placed in a tobacco box.
A Levies checkpoint in Dori area was destroyed when an explosive device went off near it.
An elected councillor, Basharat, along with 4 accomplices shot dead Aslam Masih and Ashraf Masih in order to take revenge over an altercation that cropped up during the May 31 elections.
Three people were killed and several others were wounded in a bomb blat at a mosque in hangu. Details not available.
A man was shot dead by unidentified men in C-1 area of Liaquatabad.
A young man was found dumped in Baldia Town with critical. He later succumbed to his injuries.
Zeeshan, an MQM worker, was killed and his cousin, Rehan was tortured by unknown men who had kidnapped them earlier. The victims were residents of Orangi town.
Indian troops targeted Neelam valley villages, killing one person and injuring two others according to official sources.

A fresh wave of violence erupted in reaction to  senior minister, Dr. Zulfikar Mirza's statements against the Urdu-speaking community and MQM chief. During intermittent firing incidents, a young woman was shot and killed in the Husainabad area.
A man was killed while another was injured by rivals over an old enmity in the nearby locality of Safdarabad on Thursday

Three persons were killed and two others were injured when the Marfani, Brohi and Bhaiyo tribes clashed in the Dhaimki Wand village of Jacobabad as part of the on-going dispute between the Marfaniand Brohi tribes.
Unprovoked firing by Indian troops from across the LoC killed one elderly man in Battal village.

Two members of an extremist group shot dead Fariduddin Mohajir, a worker of MQM along with two other people. The accused were arrested and arms recovered from them. ; Follow-up: Another injured worker died in the hospital and the report mentions that the attackers belonged to a nationalist/ethnic group.

Pro-Taliban militants in FATA beheaded an Afghan national for allegedly spying for the US-led forces in Afghanistan. A note was also found on the body which said 'whoever spies for the Americans will meet the same fate'. The victim was identified as Sarwar Khan, a livestock trader originally from Afghanistan's Kunar province who was living in Bajaur with his family.

The Pakistan Muslim League in charge media centre, Ali Mohammad Sahto, has said that the PPP government had committed hooliganism by torching the PML media centre. He said that the henchmen of the ruling party  blocked the main gate of the centre with a view to stopping the party activities.

A group of 'dacoits' attacked a vehicle in which a family was taking a deceased person for burial in Waziristan. The dacoits took away the son of the deceased and his relative who were later found shot dead in Army Forest. It was alleged that this was a part of a wave of atrocities let loose against the Pakhtoons in Sindh.
A police sup-inspector's body was found from behind Raja Petrol Pump, Malir. He had been kidnapped earlier.
A person was gunned down by four armed assailants in Tando Allahyar on Saturday.
a FC checkpost came under militants attack in Datakhel area resulting in one soldier, Kamal Bhittani, killed and another injured.

A man was killed in Malir, when unidentified men entered his house and murdered him in a similar way another murder had taken place in the same vicinity where the assaialnts had stabbed the victim several times and slit his throat. The deceased's affiliation could not be ascertained.
A bomb that was planted in a hotel in Khyber Bazaar was defused by the authorities on Wednesday.

Six labourers were killed and 44 others injured when a bomb placed under the seat of a bicycle exploded.; Follow-up: According to sources, it was an Indian made plastic time bomb. According to the Nazim, the people caught a suspect trying to escape and handed him over to the police.

Residents of Orangi Town took out a procession to protest the death of a Mason and against the alleged excesses of the 'land mafia' when they gathered at the offices of Orangi Town's Nazim with the Mason's body. They chanted slogans against the Nazim and lit several bonfires. The police arrived and brought the situation under control after reassuring them that an impartial inquiry would be constituted.

7 people were injured when a suicide bomber rammed his explosive laden jeep into an empty trailer returning from Afghanistan, on the main Peshawar-Torkham highway. His jeep was destroyed while the trailer overturned and fell off the road. A Taliban spokesperson claimed responsibility for the attack and threatened more attacks on the Nato supply route unless the government halted military operations in the area.
Saboteurs blew up a power supply pylon of the Sibi-Harnai transmission line, disrupting electricity supply to a large area in the Harnai tehsil.
According to Maqsoodan Bibi (mother of Rubina Bibi), Rubina was stabbed to death by her husband, Akram, as he had started doubting her character. He had previously beaten her up as well.
One person was killed and another injured when unidentified men sprayed them with bullets and fled.
Ghulam Qasim was axed to death by three people over the suspicion that the deceased had illicit relations with a woman relative of one of the accused.

The Tehsil Municipal Administraion launched an operation to wind up encroachments by vendors, shopkeepers traders etc. One of the traders retaliated by throwing acid on the TMA officials, injuring three. Following this a sit-in was staged the next day to protest over the anti-encroachment operations by the TMA.
at least 100 rocket were fired on the Ibrahimzai village near Hangu. The NWFP (KP) government has ordered a judicial inquiry into the incident.
A person of Rind Trobe was shot dead by armed men of rival Unnar tribe in Sakrand on Monday.
Shaukat Usman, a police constable who was deployed at the Presidency, was shot dead while he was on his way home.

The National Assembly witnessed pandemonium and a number of unruly scenes.  A number of politicians used indecent, unparliamentary language and Khwaja Asif and Raja Nader Pervaiz even began fighting with other treasury members.  After the scuffle, opposition member Ms. Tehmina Daultana rushed at Prime Minister Bhutto and attempted to throw glass bangles at her.  She was stopped by deputy opposition leader Gohar Ayub.  There were several other disturbances before the opposition walked out of the House just as the Speaker was about to give the ruling on the question of the opposition MNA's detention.
a man was shot dead and his 2 daughters were injured when their rival Mehrban attacked them in their house. The motive behind the killing was said to be a property dispute.
A group of armed men shot dead two people on the pretext of Karo-kari in Baboo Jakhrani village.
Some unidentfied men fired a rocket at a village and later fired on the Kurram militia. No loss of life was reported.

The applicants for police jobs protested on the National Highway bypass after their interviews were cancelled once again. They demanded that the government should not postpone their interviews again and again. The protestors pelted stones on the police who then fired in the air and lobbed teargas shells injuring 5 protestors.
Two people were found dead on the railway track
Allah Ditta was shot dead by three unidentified assailants for unknown reasons.
Five persons were killed and 22 were injured in a bomb blast in the main bazaar of Torkham on Tuesday

On the last day of the 7 day demonstration across Dir, Swat, Buner and Malakand Division, paramilitary troops opened fire on demonstrators in Buner which led to an armed clash, in which 10 people were killed and several others were injured. The demonstration was part of the movement, led by the TNS, for the implimentation of Shariah Law in Malakand Division. (See Note) ; Follow-up: A follow-up report estimates the number of people injured to be at least two dozen.

Students of the Nishtar Medical College, blocked the road and burnt tyres to protest against he removal of kiosks from Nishtar Road. The group later dispersed when informed about the Government's anti-encroachment drive.

2 madressah students were killed and 28 other people were injured when unidentified motorcyclists hurled a grenade inside a mosque when Fajr prayers were ending. The blast also damaged the mosque. The Imam of the mosque claimed that the attack was, \hatched by members of a particular sect\". ; Follow-up: The death toll rose to 3 as Muhammad Sharif, a clerk by profession, succumbed to his injuries. "
A powerful explosion occurred near the Post Office chowk in Khuzdar. No other information was given.
One person was injured when three rockets fired from Murdar mountain hit city areas on Tuesday

Unidentified attackers opened fire on a Sunni religious seminary and fled. No casualties were reported. Allam Rizvi, the head of the institution blamed the Adiviser to Punjab Chief Minister for the attack.
Three women were gunned down by two men from their village allegedly foe developing illicit relations with other men.
ASI Mohammad Naseem posted at Liaquatbagh police station on intelligence duty was ambushed by unknown assailants when he was on his way home. Five other persons were also injured in the attack.

At least five people were injured when attackers riding a motorcyle hurled a hand grenade at the house of a police officer on Sariab Road. The house belonged to Pir Jan, a deputy superintendent of the Mastung police.
The body of an elderly man was recovered from the Lahore canal in the Mughalpura area on Wednesday

A group of students protesting against the occupation of school land allegedly by the area assistant commissioner Muhammad Aslam Kalayar, were baton charged by the police. The protesting students were also joined by the area people when the talks between the administration and agitating students failed. More than a dozen people were injured when the police lobbed tear gas shells and baton charged the protesters in order to bring the situation under control.
A hand grenade was hurled at the house of Chief Minister Jam Mir Mohammad Yousuf. It exploded at the roof of the house and shattered windowpanes but no one was hurt as there was no one living there.
Helicopter gunships shelled a village.
A 48 year old unidentified man was gunned down in Nazimabad. Police found a written note on the body stating his name.
A watchman was murdered by unknown men at Alam Chowk By-pass on Tuesday
Abdul Majeed Mughul, a retired school teacher, was killed when unknown armed men on a motorbike opened fire at a bus stand.
Ahmed Chachar was injured in an exchange of fire between Chachars and Shaikhs
Unidentified men shot and killed two workers of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement.

A fresh wave of violence erupted in reaction to  senior minister, Dr. Zulfikar Mirza's statements against the Urdu-speaking community and MQM chief. A young man was shot dead by unknown persons near A-One Chowk within the remit of the Shah Faisal Colony police station.
Two girls and a woman belonging to the same family died when they stepped on an explosive device.
12 armed men opened fire at the house of Rahib Shar, killing him on the spot and injuring his wife.
A young woman was found shot dead near Malir river.

Al Barry, president of one of the leading cellular phone companies in Pakistan claimed that an he had escaped an attempt on his life on 14-Jan-03 when returning from work he had heard a gun shot and had ignored it and later found a big dent at the rear end of the car. Which the police confirmed came from a bullet later on.

At least ten suspected militants were killed and several others were injured in an exchange of fire with the security forces during a search operation in Baz Garha. Independent sources claimed that only one person had been killed and another injured.

A 41-year old MQM activist died after a brief gunbattle between two rival groups in Orangi Town. The victim was identified as Syed Haider Ali, who was a clerk in the House Building Finance Corporation and was also an office-bearer of its labour union. The police registered a case against MQM men for attacking an killing Haider Ali.

Supporters of Lashkar-i-Islam and Ansaarul Islam enaged in yet another intense gun battle in the Tirah area, with the two groups giving conflicting figured about casualties. According to offiical sources, four people had been injured. Maulana Mustamin, a supporter of Ansarul Islam, said that five people had been killed while three of his supporters were injured in fighting between the two groups. The Lashkar-i-Islam denied the claims and said that none of its supporters had been killed or injured. The fighting restarted when some armed activists of Lashkar-i-Islam attacked two bunkers of their rival groupm after which a fierce gun battle ensued. The Ansaar sources said the fighting had lasted 13 hours. The conflict between Ansaarul Islam and Lashkar-i-Islam had claimed at last 200 lives in the past year and a half.

Buildings of the government's agriculture office, a police station and two houses were destroyed in intense shelling by the Indian troops from across the LoC in the Athmuqam town, the tehsil headquarters of Neelam Valley.
4 suspected terrorists were killed in a clash between two militant groups in which both sides used heavy weapons.

Shooting incidents that started on Friday night in Korangi continued through Saturday in various parts of Karachi. 2 people were killed and 21 others, including 2 policemen were injured. Korangi was the worst hit by the latest wave of violence. It was also reported that activists of MQM and MQM-H traded fire as well.
Supply of gas to Kalat was suspended after a main pipeline was blown up on the RCD highway.
An IED was used to attack a tanker carrying water for security forces. In reaction, security forces conducted search operations in Hangu and Orakzai which led to the arrest of 9 militants.
A man shot an 18 year old girl over a marriage dispute. He wanted to take her as his bride and upon being refused by her father, he shot her.

Following the PIA management's decision to hand over some air routes to Turkish Airlines, a group of PIA employees arrived at the airport, some of them carrying sticks and batons. They prevented other PIA employees from working and scuffled with some passengers and airport staff members. They also damaged some property and when the riot police failed to handle the situation the Rangers had to called in. According to Sohail Baloch, convener of the protesting employees, 'outsiders' had been sent by certain politicians to disturb the otherwise peaceful strike. He also claimed that some PIA staffers were injured during the day. The strike had been called by a joint action committee of various PIA worker's unions.

Due to the 'atta' (flour) crisis people turned to violence and blocked the main G.T. Road in NWFP, and pelted the passing vehicles with stones, causing a severe traffic jam. Hundreds of vehicles were stranded on both sides and the road was opened after many hours. Thousands of protesters beiseiged flour mills since morning and did not allow the movement of flour out of the premises. While several trucks of flour were looted at a number of places.

District Attorney Abdul Baqi Achakzai was injured in an incident of firing in the Chaman Housing Society. Official sources say that Mr. Achakzai was injured by a bullet fired by by his guard. They said the gumman had picked a quarrel with someone and Mr. Achakzai went to reslove it and was injured.
A person was shot dead by unknown men in Chakiwara on Friday.

A mininus was set ablaze by unknown militants at Baloch Colony flyover crossing on Friday. Karachi was gripped with violence following a strike called by certain political parties against the power crises and in support of striking workers of the KESC.
Police reocvered bodies of two young brothers who were tortured and later killed by unidentified men in Korangi.
A MQM worker was found dead in Korangi. Doctors who examined his body claimed he had been severely tortured and then shot.
A person was killed when unknown militants planted a bomb on the road to target volunterrs of Adezai Qaumi Lashker in Matani area on Wednesday.
In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, angry mob pelted the Hindus Waqf property with stones in D.G Khan on Tuesday.
A suicide bomber rammed an explosive ladden car into an army check post in Jandola, wounding six troops. The soldiers were establishing a check point on Wana-Tank road

On the second consecutive day, Afghan army resorted to firing over Balochistan border near Chaman without any provocation. Afghan artillery launched medium-gun rockets which landed near Saeed Chauji in Balochistan. Pakistan Border Security Forces were forced to go into action against Afghan artillery.
A man was shot and killed when unidentified men opened fire on him in North Nazimabad while he was on his way to teach the Quran in Block H in Khawaja Ajmer Nagri.
Three people were injured when a tractor trolley hit a landmine in the Mazari Goth area. Mazari Goth is an area which was a battle field for rival Mazari and Bugti tribes of Bloch origin.

Several women protestors of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement gathered in front of the Kaarachi Press club and marched towards the Governor's House against the sealing of MQM-H headquarters in Landhi and a crackdown on the party leadership. The police women and the women protestors clashed and several were injured in the ensuing violence.

The bullet-riddled body of a income tax office superintendent was recovered from a minor distributary 9/L near Chak 95/9-L. Relatives and colleagues of the victim allege the involvement of the headconstable with whom the victim was last seen and accused the police of protecting the headconstable.
An activist of the Moahajir Qaumi Movement was shot dead by unidentifed gunmen.
A man was shot dead by unidentified gunmen.Two passers-by were injured too.
Unidentified men opened fire on an Al-Rehman coach, killing the driver on the spot. Later, they torched the coach and fled.
Two villagers were killed and five others injured when rival groups clashed over a disputed piece of land. No arrests were made.
Militants blew up three power pylons, disrupting electricity supply to seven villages of Sheikhan tribe.
Talal bin Hadi and a friend were sitting when 2 men on a motorcycle opened fire on them. They killed Talal and injured the other. The SSP said that it might be a terrorist activity.
The decomposing body of a woman was found on the bank of a nullah. The police claimed that she was killed 2 days ago and her body was thrown next to the nullah.
A young man was shot dead by two unidentified young motorcyclists near Murad Eye Hospital on G.T. Road.

Waqar Kiani, a journalist with The Guardian, was beaten up by policemen, allegedly in connection to his appearance on a TV show recently. Mr. Kiani alleged that 4 people in police uniforms, who came in a police van,  stopped him then started beating him before leaving the scene.

A body of a woman, who worked as a managing editor for the Sindhi weekly \Jhalak\", was found with three bullet wounds in the head, shoulder and hand, with her legs and arms tied. She was believed to have been raped before being shot dead."

Residents of Bhedian Kalan village, led by UC naib nazim Muhammad Yahya, blocked the main road by torching tyres to protest against the alleged torture of 5 people by Sutlej Rangers. They dispersed after PML-N MNA Sheikh Waseem Ahmed assured them that action would be taken against those responsible.
Two minibuses were set on fire in unit No. 1-1/2 of Korangi.
Two young men were found shot dead in a graveyard in Baldia Town. Both were clad in shalwar kameez and were tied up with three gunshot wounds each.

PML-N activists wer roughed up by police while holding a protest against the disqualification of the Sharif brothers. Police resorted to baton charging the workers and arresting many of them. They were later released when the PML-N workers blocked the roads and demanded their immediate release.
A sub-inspector was killed and his son was injured when two unidentified men on a motorcycle opened fire on their vehicle. The motive behind the killing could not be ascertained.

Two rockets were fired into Quetta Cantonment. The first landed in near a military police check post near police lines on a traffic island on Gulistan road. The second rocket exploded near an ordinance depot on Ordinance Road. According to the Inspector General Police, \certain elements from Afghanistan were responsible for the attacks\". He also stated that there was no fixed target after examining the rocket launching device. There was no loss of life or property damage."

Syed Liaquat Hussain Nayyar Zaidi, who was the founding president of Pasban-i-Aza, was shot and killed by armed motorcyclists while he was waiting in his car at a level train crossing. He was accompanied by his nephew who remained unhurt. The victim had set up the Pasban-i-Aza which was an organization dedicated to religious activities.

During the fourth phase of local body elections, in Bangash Colony, supporters of rival candidates attacked each others with stones and sticks. Each group accused the other of of using unfair means. Police used batons to disperse them.
The headline claims that seven people were killed but the details account for only five of them.
Adeel suspected that his sister, Iram, had developed 'relations' with a man from the area. He killed her for 'honour'.

3 gunmen pulled up to a roadside restaurant in a car and fired multiple shots at some people sitting there, killing 2 and injuring 1. The restaurant was adjacent to an ANP unit office and frequented by ANP members and the victims of the attack were ANP workers.
a heavy exchange of fire between security forces and tribesmen was reported in the Sangsilla area in Dera Bugti. However no casualties were reported.
A milkman was killed and his relative was wounded when unidentified people opened fire at his Paksitan Chowk shop.
6 people were injured in a clash between the supporters of Awam Dost and Awam Ittehad Panels in Union council Chanesar-1.

Dozens of students were injured in a clash between students mainly (PSF lead) by its leader and the police on Friday at Peshawar University Campus. The reason of the clash was the decision taken by VC of the university that university would not open in spring vacations. Police fired rubber bullets, teargas shells and batoncharged the students.
Two bridges wee destroyed by unknown militants in Akkakhel locality on Friday. As the original incident was not reported, so details are being taken from this article.
Security forces, backed by gunship helicopters pounded various hideouts of the militants with heavy artillery. A man was killed while several others were wounded.
A man was shot dead in the Kot Mir Mohammad village, allegedly over a land dispute. No case was registered.
Double murder of a couple in the name of Honour.
A trader belonging to the Hazara tribe was shot and killed while he was sitting at his shop.

The Serena Hotel, that was housing foreign delegates including Afghanistan Vice President Karim Khalili, received a call from Afghanistan urging the staff to evacuate the hotel as it was going to be blown up. After a thorough security search the hotel was declared safe. The hotel's security officer, Wajahat Hussain, claimed that it was a 'routine drill' but no other official could corroborate the claim.
Unidentified assailants shot dead an expatriate, Muhammad Asif, in Sialkot Saddar.
one man was killed an 2 others were injured when a landmine exploded as a tractor trolley hit it.
MSF's divisional president Mohammad Fiaz Qadri was taken from his home and shot in nearby fields by unidentified men. Eye witnesses told that they danced around his body and fled.

Two ethnic groups clashed over an old dispute, which led to one of the groups launching an armed attack on the other. The victims were from a newly-formed group called the Punjab Front. The police showed up after the event had already transpired and fired shots in the air to disperse some people who had gathered to protest.
A partially decomposed body of a teenage boy was found in the hills of North Karachi. The police stated that his throat had been slit and there were marks of torture on his body.
An agriculturist, Baggu Masih, was shot dead by his neighbours over a property dispute. According to his son, the neighbours wanted him to vacate his house and upon refusal, they shot him.
A Shalobar tribesman was killed and one other injured when a hand grenade exploded in a trench. This seems to be an extension of the ongoing conflict between Ansarul Islam and Lashkar-i-Islam.

Unidentified men opened fire outside Masjid-o-Madressah Darul Uloom Rehmania, injuring 3 and killing 4. They assailants then went to Madressah Khalid bin Abdulaziz and opened fire there, leaving four people injured. A senior police official stated that the firing appeared to be sectarian motivated but the involvement of a foreign hand could not be ruled out.

Two meeting between two groups, who had an ongoing land dispute, met  to resolve the issue but the meeting turned violent. 3 people sustained bullet wounds and 2 of them later succumbed to their injuries. The STP (Sindh Tarraqqi Pasand Party) claimed that the deceased were its members and that they died while resisting a land-grabbing bid. However, the police denied that that STP had made any such claims.

A strike, called by the Save River Committee, was held in order to protest the acute shortage of water in Sindh. During the strike, many protesters burnt tyres and pelted vehicles with stones in Shikarpur, Garhi Yaseen and Jacobabad. Hundreds blocked Indus Highway between Jahania and Shikarpur.

Participants of a funeral procession of two men of Iranian decent, who were killed previously, forced shopekeepers in Lea market to close down their shops. They started pelting moving and parked vehicles with stones in the Karadar area and Lea Market; they lit bonfires in the old city area and damaged an eating house of the Al-Khair Hotel. Tehy also tried to put an oil tanker on fire near Khagzai bazaar but failed upon intervention by the police. Two buses carrying the processionists were detained and would be released upon taking undertakiings according to police reports.
one person was killed and another was injured as a result of unprovocative firing by the Indian troops on the civil population of two border villages of Azad Kashmir.
A ten year old girl was killed in Dhamala village as the Indian forces continued firing from across the Working Boundary.

After the incident involving the death of the SHO due to a dispute over toll taxes, the police officials got angry and damaged a number of vehicles parked at the municipal bus stand and trashed the office of Feroze Khan, the president of the Wagon Owners Association. Many drivers and office bearers of different transporter bodies have been rounded up. Follow-up: According to the VP of Pakistan Yellow Cab Federation, more than 100 vehicles were damaged and the police and FC officials also damaged the offices of Blue Line and Dolphin Coach services due to which transporters have suffered a loss of Rs. 15 million. Accoding to unconfirmed reports, a person of Kohinstani ethnic group was allegedly involved in the firing incident.

Three people were killed and two others were injured when armed group of Ansarul Islam attacked compound of Lashkar-i-Islam. Three lashkar men were killed and two injjured were Ansarul Islam men. Ansarul Islam alleged that the bunker was used by the Lashkar men for shelling their center in the locality.

Worshippers belonging to the Ahl-e-Sunnat and Ahl-e-Hadith had an argument over a religious issue which led to a scuffle. This led to an exchange of fire as both groups brought out weapons. 7 people were injured.
A local farmer, Mehmand, was shot dead by two armed men on his way home over a property dispute. The police have registered a case against Ghulam Ali and Javel Iqbal.
Four armed men killed three brothers and gunned down their grandfather near Drigh village on Friday on the pretext of karo-kari. There was an old enmity between the murderers and the victims.
Two soldiers were injured in an attack on a security checkpoint.

Two local leaders of the Sindh People's Student Federation were killed and an activist of the Jeay Sindh Taraqqi Pasand Party was wounded in a clash between the two groups when both exchanged fire at a hotel in Sukkur after a heated argument took place.
The strife-hit areas of Karachi witnessed renewed violence, as a man was killed while friend was injured when armed men targeted them in Shesha Gali of Bhora Pir area.
Mohammad Nawaz axed to death his wife, after accusing her of having a bad character.
Taliban attacked  a security checkpost in Tiazra in South Waziristan. The security forces retaliated killing 11 Taliban and injuring 20 others.
Two missiles fired by a US drone hit a house in Miramshah Bazaar, killing 6 suspected militants and injuring another 2. According to AFP,  3 of the killed militants belonged to the Haqqani Network.
Two tribesmen were killed and two were injured in a clash between two groups of the Kakar tribe in Majak.
Indian border security forces and Pakistani guards traded fire twice across the borderline near Sialkot's working boundary in the area which distinguishes it from the International border.
An unmanned US drone crashed near in the rice fields of Juma Khan village. Officials claimed the plane was on a routine surveillance mission and crashed due to a technical fault.
At least 4 people were killed and 11 were injured by unidentifed assailants in Azimpura, Green Town, Golden Town, Shah Faisal Colony and adjoining localities on Monday.

At least seven people were killed and 18 others injured in firing by unknown gunmen in main Bazaar. The motive behind the seemingly terrorist action was not known.  The gunmen arrived at the market and opened indiscriminate fire at the people. They managed to escape after committing the massacre. Followup: One of the injured in the Shorkot incident succumbed to her injuries, raising the death toll to 8.
Indian troops targeted Zero point, in Neelum valley, by shelling which hit a passenger bus injuring five persons on board.
US drone fired six missiles in the Doga area of Dattakhel and killed six suspected militants. However, according to locals, the men were tribesmen and had nothing to do with the military.

The body of an unidentified man was found in steel box left unattended in Kotlakhpat-Baba Farid Colony on Thursday. Police said that middle aged man and women came in a car who hired a van for bringing the steelbox, but due to potholes on kathchajail,the driver refused. The middle aged couple flee from the scene. Later it was found that the body was poisoned to death

As a result of the assassination of JSQM activist Lal Buksh Noorani, activists of JSQM demonstrated outside Mehrabpur Police Station and some protesters attacked some shops and set ablaze a welding shop on Saturday.
Badhber police with the help of the bomb disposal squad defused a home-made bomb in the fields of Mashugagar village.

The decapitated bodies of Malik Dost Mohammad and Malik Umer were found. The two tribal elders were kidnapped from Sheraki area of Darra Adamkhel a few days prior to their bodies being found. The TTP had warned the elders of the area to not allow food and water to be supplied to security personnel at checkposts but the warning was ignored.
5 children were killed in a bombexplosion in Khan Mahi Village on Monday. The device was a booby trap that exploded when children picked it up thinking it was a toy.
Syed Shahanshah Hussain, a former student leader and a city lawyer was shot dead by unidentified gunmen while he was going to Sadar in a taxi. The reason behind the killnig is not known.

A renowned trader, Syed Inayat Ali Kazmi was killed by his nephew insdie the ward of the hsopital where he was admitted. The accused slit open his uncle's throat. The nephew was arrested but the reason behind the killing could not be ascertained.
The body of a 35-year old was found near the stadium in Korangi No. 5. It bore torture marks and had been stuffed in a gunny bag.

Suspected militants blew up Khobai Educational Academy, a private high school, in Khobai area of Sabqadar. They had planted improvised devices which went off one after the other, destroying the school building, and damaging a mosque and houses in the vicinity.

An angry mob burnt a minibus and set a few hotels on fire after the driver of a bus, after hitting a small girl, exchanged rude words with the child's mother. The infuriated mob (some taking advantage of the situation) set hotels on fire too.

3 people were killed and 6 others wounded when troops fired artillery rounds near Sadda when some combatants refused to vacate their positions. This attack was in relation to the violence that was occuring in the area between two rival groups that had claimed a number of lives.

Students of the Government Islamia College Civil Lines torched three buses and damaged 15 others after their college fellow aws killed by a bus on Lower Mall. The police reached the spot but to no avail. The protesters finally dispersed when a senior police officer assured them that a morder case would be registered against the driver and bus company owner.
Saifullah Siddique, a Haqiqi worker, was shot dead near Gole market in Nazimabad.
At least 11 people were killed and 60 were injured when the angry protesters were trying to demolish a Hindu Temple near Jamia Khairul Madaras on Tuesday.
A man was killed while two others sustained injuries when four people attacked them with clubs at Jatoi town in muzaffargarh district on Wednesday

An armed clash between two student groups, one of which was PkSF, left 6 people injured including 3 passer-bys and a policeman. Following a clash between two student groups, an injured member of the PkSF was taken to Liaquat National Hospital where he was allegedly denied 'proper treatment'. This led to the hospital being attacked by armed youths who ransacked the building and fired shots in the air to force the suspension of several services including the emergency unit. A later report implies that the other group involved was the APMSO (\10 more killed as 'ethnic violence' continues in Karachi\", Dawn, 16-Jun-11, page 2)"
At least one person was killed and three were injured in Indian shelling along LoC in Tarroti Village on Tuesday
Bullet-riddled bodies of two militants were found from the Zor Mandi area, Batkhela.

In an attack on the People's Peace Committee's office, 2 activists were gunned down by members of the Ghaffar Zikri gang which led to a series of scattered incidents of violence. Other than the two PPC activists, 5 other people were killed and 7 were injured. A heavy contingent of police and Rangers took about 12 hours after the clashes started to move into the area. Follow-up: Intermittent firing continued over night and through the next day. During the night rockets were fired at Ali Muhammad Mohalla and Band Mohalla and firing became intense again in the following afternoon. 2 more people, Aqeel son of Faqir Mohammad and Nasir son of Rafi, were killed and one injured person, Shahid alias Dhobi, from the previous day succumbed to his injuries.
A prominent PML leader, Abdul Aziz Qureshi, was killed when unidentified armed men opened fire on him as soon as he opened the door to his house in Bagh Hayat Ali Shah, and fled on motorcycles.
The Jagirani tribesmen killed two members of the Jatoi clan to avenge the killing of a woman by the Jatois.
Saeed Akhtar, a local cloth merchant, was shot and killed by unidentified people. The assailants knocked on his door and opened fire as soon as he answered it.

Mukhtar, Rafaqat and Akhtar opened fire on Naveed, Asif and Irfan as they were going to the house of Aslam. Naveed died on the spot, and according to his father, the accused had forcefully occupied their land and he along with the village elders requested the them to hand over the land. The Chhanga Manga police have registered a case and arrested the accused.
A woman was injured in Indian firing across the LoC
An alleged 'terrorist' in a shoot out with the police when a gang of terrorists were asked to stop for checking near Piyala Hotel, Federal B Area.
A woman in her 20s was axed to death by her uncle, Faiz Bakhsh. It was alleged that she had developed 'illicit relations' with someone.
A militant was killed in an encounter while he was trying to sneak into Buner district.

Unprovoked Indian shelling on the Tchowar, Thokhmus and Pyone villages in the Chorbat valley, Shyoke sector near the Line of Control caused damage to standing crops and fruit trees in the villages. However, no casualties were reported.
the mother and wife of an accountant of the Sihala Police Office CollegeNazeer Omer, were killed at their houes by unknown assailants in Dhoke Chaudhrian.
2 people were killed and 2 were injured when unidentified armed persons attacked on PKMAP Office on Club Road on Saturday.

A student of Islamia College, belonging to the MSF, was stabbed to death by a student belonging to the PSF (along with accomplices) after the two had had a heated conversation in which the PSF member had threatened to teach the deceased a lesson after college hours.
Heavy shooting was reported near the Schon Circle in Clifton, Phase 6, however, the police did not confirm this report.
A man wa shot dead by unidentified men in Madina Colony of Korangi.
two brothers belonging to the Dareshak family were shot dead while in their car by unidentified assailants. One man was also injured.

high explosives with timer were planted on a bicycle parked in front of a small restaurant on Sariab road exploded destroying the restaurant three other shops and half a dozen pushcarts. A police had calimed five deaths in the blast however the hospital sources confirmed four deaths. only one the body has been identified as Sharkal Khan Pirkani.
Two people were injured after being hit by splinters of a shell fired by the Indian forces across the LoC.

A 30 year old MQM worker was shot dead by unknown assailants near the KDA flats in Karachi. The police chased the attackers and fired on them injuring the two attackers. According to the Police, the attackers belonged to the PPP youth wing.
the bullet-riddled body of an alleged US spy, Sher Nawab, was found in Mirali.

Police recovered parts of a young man's body from a drain in Gulshan-i-Iqbal. One sack containing parts of the body was stuck in the drain and another sack- with the remaining body parts- was found a few meters away. Later, a head of a man was found in the street near Sabzazar's fruit market.
Hawaldar of Swabi police was shot dead by unidentified attackers in Kalu Khan, Swabi.
A bullet riddled body of a teenage boy was found in the graveyard.The reason behind the killing could not be ascertained.

An explosion outside an Imambargah left 6 people injured. However, the target of the blast Syed Muhammad Taqi Naqvi, central Vice-President of the Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan (TJP), escaped unhurt. Naqvi was on his way to the Imambargah for a meeting in connection with Yaum-i-Ali when the bomb exploded.
Masked assailants entered a grocery shop in Misgaran bazaar and opened indiscriminate fire killing three Shia persons.
Paras Khan, an ANP activist, was shot and killed by two men on a motorbike while he was standing outside a shop.
Fahmeed Khan, of Gondlanwala, was going to his dera on his cycle when some armed unidentified men opened fire on him and killed him. The motive behind the incident could not be ascertained.
Militants attacked security forces in the Palai area of Malakand after which a clash ensued which left five militants dead.
Two groups of the Panhwar tribe clashed over an old enmity. 10 people, including a woman, were injured.
A mother of eight children was strangled to death by her son over her alleged illicit relations with a man in village Kasoki.
12 militants overpowered the watchman at a school and then planted explosives. The explosion destroyed the school building.
A man was found dead in Gulberg. He had reportedly been kidnapped the night before.
A young man, Abdul Rehman, was stabbed to death during a clash. No further details given.
Waseem, in charge of the Edhi ambulance service at Jinnah Postgraduate medical Centre was kidnapped and tortured by armed suspects.
1 person was killed and 6 SSP men were injured in a sudden attack by a group of rivals in Shorkot on Monday.

security froces thwarted an attempt by militants to destroy their base in Peochar valley, a stronghold of the Tehrik-i-Taliban Swat chief Maulana Fazlullah. MaJ-Gen Athar Abbas said that at least 21 of the militants who had attacked the base were killed. 8 secuirty personnel were injured in the clash.
A paramilitary checkpoint near Miramshah was attacked by militants in which 3 soldiers were injured.
Nusrat Ali and Rashid Malik were on their way back from a 'religious gathering' when they were intercepted by 4 armed motorcyclists and shot dead.

During a protest demonstration by the Christain community agains the Shantinagar incident of 6-Feb-97, police dispersed protesters in the Mehmoodabad area who had disrupted traffic and tried to set vehicles on fire.

Security forces clashed with militants in Zakarkhel village, killing 3 Uzbeks and one tribesman. An official said that the militants opened fire first, after which the security forces targetted a militants stronghold with heavy machine guns. The gun battle took place when talks between tribal elders and militants hiding in the house failed.
An explosive device planted under a truck was defused by the police.
In Mustafaabad, former councillor Hafizullah along with his 10 supporters were arrested for injuring the supporters of his opponent.
Four persons were killed while twenty-seven others were injured when a  2kg bomb, planted under a 'parapet' adjacent to a vegetable shop in a vegetable market in Peshawar, exploded.

police intercepted a bus on Sargodha Road and arrested two alleged terrorists, Ahmad Saeed and Mukhtar Ahmad. Two hand grenades and explosives were found in their possession. Sources claimed that those arrested were on their way to commit some sabotage activity on the eve of Shab-i-Barat in the city.

unidentified miscreants resorted to indiscriminate firing in the Wadhat Colony and Polytechnic College areas. The Sindh Punjabi Students Association accused the sepratists elements living in Wadhat Colony of firing.
Two youths, Azhar Abbas and another, were wounded when they were attacked in 5-C area. Azhar died later in the hospital.

A procession coming from Khudadad Colony was stopped by personnel of law enforcement agencies which resulted in a clash between the law-enforcers and the people in the procession. Protesters threw brickbats on the neon signs besides the gate of Quaid-i-Azam's mausoleum. They also stormed into the mausoleum and \ransacked benches\" and damaged a few cars parked inside the mausoleum. The police resorted to baton charging and teargas shelling to control the situation . The people then gathered at Naumaish Chowk and ransacked the traffic police checkpost. "

Police said riaz suspected his niece to be having illicit relations with her neighbor. He with his two accomplices first went to his nieces house killing her and injuring her sister and then went to her nieghbour's house killing another person and injuring three others. The condition of the injured is stated to be critical.

One was killed and nine others injured when a low intensity time bomb exploded in a minibus near Jama Cloth Market. The device weighed 300 grams and was fitted with a 15 minute timer and was placed under the seat which was above the fuel tank.
1 person was injured in Indian shelling along LoC in Digwar Village on Tuesday.

Karachi witnessed the bloodiest day of the recent wave of violence as a trader was killed and six others were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire on a group of people in Qasba Colony No.2 during the on-going violence.

around 200 PML-N activists were outside Nawaz Sharif's residence. The police had blocked the two exit points from his residence by placing buses there. The marchers damages three buses placed to stop them from marching further. The policemen ran for their lives and took shelter in the residential quarters. the police said that they were not willing to stop the protesters as they were doing supporting the right cause.
A villager was killed and his mother was seriously injured in shelling by Indian troops on Sialkot's Working Boundary of Charwa sector.
Military jetfighters bombed suspected militant hideouts. Locals claimed that 2 people were killed and 7 injured.
An owner of a bakery and a milkman were killed when unidentified men on a motorcycle opened fire on them while they were chatting at the Bakery in Gulberg. The motive of could not be known.

At least 10 people were killed and 14 others injured when Namdar and Takia groups exchanged fire over a business dispute. The groups had clashed two times before as well, one of the instances being when Lashkar Islami leader Mangal Bagh visited the area.

A suicide bomber blew himself up in Khar upong being challenged by security forces. He had sneaked into Khar from Sara Meena and when security personnel had surrounded him, he detonated himself. No one was hurt in the explosion.
security forces pounded militant hideouts in Tor Chappar and adjoining areas of Darra Adamkhel. No loss of life or property was reported from any side.

Security forces launched an operation in Manzari Chena, Athamkhel and Zorh Kallay of Baizai Tehsil. Two volunteers and a soldier were killed in the clashes with militants while twelve security personnel and five volunteers were injured in a mine blast and clashes. The security forces defused several bombs in Shanikhel and Dobakhel areas.

A dispute that started with a cheating incident spiralled into open violence between PSF (People's Student Federation) and the ISO (Imamia Student Organization). Students of one group stormed into an examination room in the sociology department and thrashed a student of the other group, leaving him with bruises and fractures. A faculty member who tried to intervene was also injured. Even though the Rangers personnel deployed at the site were informed of the incident they took no action. A former KU student was also beaten up near the administration block.
a PPP activist Riaz Ali was shot dead by 2 men in Orangi Town. Two suspects were named, by the victim's father, in the FIR.

Some students reportedly belonging to the Islami Jamiat Tulaba (IJT) thrashed a boy and girl for sitting together on campus. The IJT, however, denied doing so, and claimed that they had only warned them of sitting together and not thrashed them.

Some unidnetified men resorted to indiscriminate firing in the congested locality. Panic spread in the area and a young boy was injured as a result. The gunmen escaped after a few minutes. Police believe they were angry college students or members of a student organisation.
A labourer was found dead outside his house in Nazimabad on Saturday. He also had wound on his body.
A police head constable was shot and wounded by unidentified assailants near the Lea Market Chowk while he was on his way on a motorcycle.

A former president of the Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan Vehari, Liaquat Ali Gujjar, was shot dead when 2 motorcylists blocked the road and opened fire on him on the Multan road. The police raided several houses in Thingi Colony and Chak 95/WB and took people into custody.
A woman was killed by her brother for having illicit relations with a man from her village.
A man was killed and three people were injured when a tractor trolley hit a landmine in Sui.
Unidentified armed men opened fire on Malang Mangrio polling station killing one and injuring 2 others.
Two people were killed and four others were wounded when unidentified people entered the Al Falah mosque in Liaquatabad and opened fire on the people present.
A man was killed and three others injured in a clash between two rival groups in Langah village.
Violent mob attacked the residence of Col.Anwer, DOHA Secretary and ransacked it. One of the vehicles parked inside the house was also set ablaze
Fresh clases between security forces and militants put the military in an advantageous position as they seized higher ground.
Militants fired 12 rockets on Monrah security camp in Dattakhel. However, no loss of life or property was reported.

Khair Muhammad alias Foto Dayo- a resident of the village Nandha Bossan- was shot dead by five armed men. As the police heard the shots, they reached the area and chased the killers. They caught Ghulam Ali, Nek Muhammad, and Imdad (all Dayo clan). Two escaped.

Microwave station of Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation Limited (PTCL) was damged in an attack. The assailants fired scores of rounds of automatic weapons hitting different parts of the building. Levies personnel deployed in the area rushed to the place and returned fire. the exchange of fire continued for a hour after which the assailants fled away.

As part of the ongoing dispute between the two rival student groups, Islami Jamiat Talaba (IJT) and the All Pakistan Mohajir Students Organisation (APMSO), clashes took place at the Arts and Science campuses of the Federal Urdu University of Science, where  both sides indulged in fist fights and later used clubs, empty bottles, stones etc. Sources expressed that the continuing clashes between the two groups had evovled into a power struggle and now aimed to invovle the local governments to maintain the law and order situations in the colleges and universities.
In reaction to the demolition of Babri Mosque in Ayodhya, angry mob burnt the effigies of Indian Prime Minister and other Hindu leaders in Renala Khurd on Tuesday.

Approximately 12 armed youths attacked the provincial office of the PPP. They held the inmates at gunpoint, damaged property. According to Kissan Wing President, the assailants were from PML (N) youth wing and the MSF.
Militants attacked security forces with remote controlled devices resulting in three injured soldiers.

An activist of the MQM-H (Afaq Ahmed led faction) was found shot dead in a playground in Malir. He had been shot in the head and chest. The police stated it to be too early to term it a political killing.

A 28 year old shopkeeper reportedly drowned in the lake of Minar-i-Pakistan under mysterious circumstances. He had gone to his shop but did not return. Later, his body was found which bore marks of violence.
Pakistani gunship helicopters targeted militant hideouts along the the border between North and South Waziristan, killing 3 suspected militants and injuring 8 others.
A time-device attached to the rear end of an oil tanker exploded, setting the tanker on fire. The tanker was on its way to Afghanistan. The driver and the cleaner of the truck were arrested.
Chenab Rangers found a 1.5kg bomb (that was made in Pakistan) planted beneath an electricity pole. The bomb disposal squad was called from Sialkot and defused the bomb.
A police constable was shot dead near Palm Street, Usmanabad. According to reports, unidentified people kidnapped him and his bullet-riddled body was later found behind an Imambargah.
5 people were killed and minimum of 45 prisoners were injured in a riot in Central Jail Gujranwala on Thursday.
3 houses of suspected militants were demolished.

PML(N) MNA Shaikh Tahir Rasheed alleged that Muslim Leaguers, including himself, were baton-charged by the police under orders of the Punjab Governor Chaudhry Mohammad Altaf. He claimed that the policemen had openly admitted to the orders having been given. This allegation was made in an application submitted to Multan SSP and SHO Cantonment police station.
According to a Press briefing by Karachi commissioner, as part of the on-going violence, one person was killed and another was injured in District West.
Indian shelling across the Line of Control. Details are not available.
It was reported that on 08-Jun-94 Indian forces opened fire on their Pakistani counterparts across the LoC, killing Captain Abdul Kaleem Dar of the Baloch Regiment.
Two women were murdered by five armed persons on the pretext of Karo-kari in Manga Mandi Area on Saturday.
During a strike called by the Milli Yakjehti Council (MYC), police baton charged and tear-gassed MYC workers who were allegedly damaging buses and blocking roads. As many as 15 workers were arrested.
military expanded its operation in Bajaur. Security forces claimed killing 10 militants in attacks by gunships and heavy artillery.

A large number of residents of the American Quarters smashed windowpanes of an engine of Faisalabad-bound Super Express near Shahbaz hospital on Wednesday to protest against non-availability of water in their area. The protesters only dispersed after XEN Bashir Awan assured them that the water supply will reach the area soon.
A young man was found shot dead in Korangi No. 3 1/2. He bore a single bullet wound to the head.
A youth suffered serious wounds in a landmine blast in Kotli Syed Mir village in the Chaprar sector.
Indian forces continued shelling on the Pakistani border villages across the LoC.
An unidentified person was killed and his bosy dumped in the cotton fields.
A boy was injured in the Ghantarbala village of Nakyal Sector, Kotli, in Indian shelling from across the Line of Control. The Indians used machine-guns, mortar shells and medium artillery.
Yasin Khan Pathan was injured when some explosive materials planted in his air conditioner blew up, damaging the whole room. The police could not ascertain the cause behind the incident.
2 ST men, Mohammad Ali Qadri and Merajuddin, were gunned down by unidentified men in Karachi's Eastern neighbourhood of Korangi Industrial area.
Security forces demolished the houses of Sakhi Jan and Rafeel Khan who were leaders of Lashkar-i-Islam.
Fazal Husain and Amir Hussain had a land dispute which led to the two parties exchanging fire. 3 people were killed in the exchange.
A landlord, Muhammad Bashir of Datay Wali, was shot dead by unknown assailants who then fled the scene.
A man was killed in the village of Juran when he came under the fire of the Indian security forces from across the LoC.

As claimed in the condemnation statement of Chief Organiser of National People's Party, S.M Zafar, There was a Scud missile fired from Afghanistan and it exploded in Wah. No other details are available. ; Follow-up : The Foreign Office has condemend the attack and lodged a protest. The report also mentions the date and location of the attack.
A body of an unidentified boy was found on the street in Madina Colony.
Gangsters' barged into the house of Murad Ali Domki and opened fire, killing Murad Ali and injuring his wife.
Unidentified assailants shot dead Feroz Hussain Shaha- the former TJP President of Tank- and Maqbool Hussain Shah as they were heading to Shorkot. The assailants threw their bodies in the fields.
Unidentified arsonists set a KESC van on fire in Buffer Zone.
A police officer, SHO Farid Barach of Panjpai area and his son were injured when unknown persons hurled a hand grenade at their house.
An unidentified boy was shot dead by unidentified assailants.
Arif Massih, a vendor, alleged that ASI Rafique of the Muslim Town police station took him to the police station and tortured him after the vendor refused to pay the ASI 'monthly'. (See note)
A man and his three sons shot a man dead and injured his wife over a land dispute.

Occupants of a yellow-cab opened fire at a police party when the latter signalled the former to stop for a 'snap check'. An ASI was killed while a constable was injured. One of the assailants was also injured when the police fired back.
A youth, identified as Mujeeb of Adezai area was shot dead by unidentified people. Report claims that he was a 'security personnel'.
Two men were shot dead by unidentified men on a motorcycle near Mastung Cadet College. This attack reportedly came five adays after the education minister was shot dead.

The police raided the house of Hashim Brohi, looted the house and taken Mehmooda and her brother Rajab Brohi. The police kept them at the Civil Lines police post in illegal confinement over several days. According to Mehmooda, she was gang raped there. There is an FIR registered against ASI Israr Ahmed Khoso, constable Iqbal Shah and two unidentified constables. ASI Khoso and constable Shah have been suspended
13 militants were killed when secuirty forces pounded their hideouts in Babra, Charmang, Hashim and Cheenar areas of Nawagai subdivision.

militants fired 5 rockets at Shahgai and Ali Masjid forts, situated on the main Peshawar-Torkham highway. Sources say that at least 2 hit the Shahgai and Ali Masjid forts while another hit a near by hilltop in Lala Cheena locality. No damage was caused to any of the forts. the security forces resorted to indiscriminate firing. the forts were jointly occupied by the Pakistan Army and the Khyber Rifles. local militants had threatened to carry out attacks on government and military installations if the suppy of fuel and military hardware to Nato forces in Afghanistan was not stopped.

Two bomb blasts in quick succession at a main market left at least 32 people dead while at least 90 were injured. The first blast was small in comparison and drew a rescue workers, police and journalists to the spot after which a second explosion tool place. Among the victims were 6 injured journalists, 2 of which later succumbed to their injuries. The attack took place across the street from the offices of the top political agent for Khyber. Housing for army soldiers was also in the vicinity of the blast. ; Follow-up: The final injury count was reported to be 108, while the death toll rose to 40 as 8 people succumbed to their injuries.

Ten people were injured when an explosive device went off in the busiest trading centre of Sargodha. The bomb, which was placed under a crate, exploded at around 5:50 pm.  The blast was described as an act of terrorism.
unknown assailants gunned down a senior journalist
2 members of the MQM,Yaqoob and Muhammad Shahid, were gunned down by 4 unidentified attackers on motorcycles in Mohajir Camp, Baldia locality. The fleeing attackers fired into the air.
Militants attacked a checkpost in Pat Feeder area of Nasirabad. At least eight rockets were fired but none of them hit the target.

3 video and Cd shops were blown up in Mattani Bazaar. According to the police, improvised explosive devices were used. Moreover,t he shopkeepers had received warning letters from unknown people asking them to stop video and CD businesses in that area.

About 15,000 people, displaced by floods, surrounded the district coordinator's office and protested against the shortage of food, shelter and potable water. They set ablaze tyres and pelted vehicles with stones. In an attempt to pacify them, government and police officials arranged for 3 pick-ups loaded with flour but the collection and distribution of flour led to a fistfight and the police resorted to aerial fire to disperse the mob. Three women were injured.
A bomb planted on a motorbike exploded near a bus stand. Police couldn’t decipher whether the boy killed was a terrorist or not.

Rival sectarian groups exchanged fire in different parts of Kurram Agency for the fourth day in a row. The report claims that the total number of people killed in the four days was 200, but the inidividual incidents when added up puts the number killed to a total of around 40.  The incident has been coded as a report earlier titled: \Curfew in Parachinar after sectarian clashes; Sectarian riots escalate in Kurram Agency; Pitched battles continue in Kurram; truce not in sight\". The dates of the report are from 11-Sep- 1996 to 13- Sep -1996. Followup: It was later reported that the number of people killed that was reported, which was 200, was an unofficial number, and had been taken from local and independant sources. However, official sources put the number of people killed in the clashes to 103."

As the strike called by Joint Action Committee of PIA employees continued, Airport Security Force attacked PIA emplyees with batons in an attempt to prevent them from entering the airport. Several people, including women and media personnel, were injured and 5 of the injured had to be taken to the hospital.

At least six people were killed and five others injured in fresh clashes between militants of the banned Lashkar-i-Islam and Ansarul Islam groups in the remote Tirah valley of Khyber Agency.  Armed supporters of the two organizations traded heavy gunfire to gain control of the Kukikhel area. Lashkar spokesman Zar Khan said they had regained control of Ghulam Ali, Zmarai, Souk, Garhai and Sandapal hills. However, Ansaar spokesman Haji Mobin refuted the claim and said the Lashkar's attack was repulsed.
The caretaker of an Imambargah was killed and his gardner was injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on them outside an Imambargah in Orangi Town.

Doctors and other health professionals from various private clinics and government hospitals received unaddressed envelopes with bullets in them, death threats and extortion demands. This alarmed the medical community as in the past Karachi has witnessed widespread targeted killing of doctors.
Unidentified men attacked an auto workshop with a grenade, killing one person and injuring another 3.
a passerby was killed and 4 others were injured in an exchange of fire between two rival groupss at Chak 187-GB near Rajana. They had an old enmity over a property dispute.

Heavy fighting between security forces and tribesmen erupted. A government official claimed a militant was injured during the clash. Agha Shahid accused the security forces of attacking the tribesmen. He told that there was no casualties on tribesmen's side.
A boy was killed and three others injured when two groups exchanged fired on an unknown issue in Kohat.Of the three injured, two were women who got caught in the crossfire.
Akbar Raza, a resident of Malir Saudabad, was killed by unidentified people who threw his dead body in Darakhshan Colony.

The Indian Security Forces continued firing on Zafarwal, Charwa, Bajwat, Chaprar, Harpal, Sucheetgarh, Bajragarhi and Shakargarh sectors. As a result, the firing killed 1 donkey, badly damaged some houses as well as distrupted the sowing of paddy crop. The Chenab Rangers returned the fire.
a 'suicide vehicle' which was going to Saidu Sharif, was spotted by security forces and destroyed after an exchange of fire.

Almost all religious and jihadi organisations took out a protest procession in Gujranwala against the US and its allies for attacking Afghanistan. The protesters burnt an effigy of US President Bush. The protest was attended by JUI, JI, PML-N, SSP, Jamiat Ahle Hadith, Jamaat Ahle Sunnat, traders and lawyers.

Police and Rangers conducted a search operation in Shanti Nagar after two rival gangs had clashed repeatedly for a few days. In the clash that took place between law-enforcement personnel and the gang members, 5 suspects were killed while 4 were arrested. Significantly, Kalu Karrant, who was the front man of notorious Lyari gangster Ghaffar Zikri, was also killed.
Two people were killed in Charhoi village in Kotli as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.
Militants attacked a police station in Rahimabad. An exchange of fire between militants and police which continued till Sunday morning.

Atleast four persons were killed and several others injured in clash between the Nazir Choliani and Nawab Choliani groups of the Choliani tribe over a land dispute,when a serious gun battle took place for five hours near Karampur. The two groups had reportedly been involved in the dispute for the past many months.

Maulana Idrees Chinioti, a religious leader and brother of Maulana Ilyas Chinioti (MPA of the ruling  party) escaped a murder attempt while he was returning from Chak 45-JB when four to five men opened fire on his vehicle, killing the driver and injuring Maulvi Mukhtar.

one person was killed and many others injured when a bomb exploded in a tonga near Naz cinema.; Mazhar Husain, injured in the bomb blast died. He is the fourth person to have lost his life in the blast.
4 armed persons shot dead two men in Bokan Morr on Wednesday.
2 people were injured when unidentified assailants opened fire on a minibus on Saturday.
following the killing of the baloch nationalist leaders violence erupted in Balochistan. The bodies of Ghulam Mohammad Baloch, Lala, and Sher Mohammad Baloch were found.

Hakim Said , chancellor of the Hamdard University, philantropist and a leading practitioner of alternative medicine (Hakim) was shot dead along with his two aides. The attackers could not be identified. The Hakim was a well known figure in Pakistan.

Hundreds of residents of Khanqah Dogran set a police station on fire. They had earlier ransacked the police station to show their protest against their inclusion into the new district of Nankana Sahib.
3 people were found killed in the city of Karachi. The report does not provide any details of the killings.
Eleven persons were injured in an armed clash between two groups of the Burro clan over a minor dispute

An elder of the Raisani tribe, Hajir Noor Muhammad Raisani, was gunned down while his two grandsons were injured, when unknown armed men opened fire on them while they were sleeping in the backyard of their house located in the village of Haji Shahar.
