Militants blew up a servant quarter near the Government High School. The school building itself had already been destroyed by militants.
Three people were killed while five others were injured over a land dispute in Unga village of Soan Sakesar Jauharabad.
Haji Mohammad Bux was beaten to death in his house allegedly by four unidentified men who used to frequent his house.

A minubus was burnt after the funeral procession of a man that had died in a previous clash between two religious groups on 23-05-03. After attending the funeral prayers people gathered at the mosque marched on the main road as a procession and lit a bonfire along with setting a minibus ablaze. They claimed they had wanted to take the deceased's body to the Chief Minister's House but were not allowed to do so by the law enforcement agencies.

Sabit Hussain and Muhammad Rizwan, labourers and residents of Rato Dero, were shot and killed by unknown men on a motorbike while they were sitting outside a restaurant. In protest against the killing, some miscreants set the nearby Akram Ghazi Hotel on fire.
2 people were killed and 12 were injured in a bomb blast in Lorry Adda on Sunday. Authorities claimed that it was a time-bomb of 1.5 kg
A woman presiding officer of UC No. 8, Multan City, was beaten up along with other polling staff by the male supporters of a candidate at the Kumharanwala polling station.

Sindh University turned into a battle ground when two groups of students belonging to the SPSF and SPSF-Shaheed Bhutto clashes at the Information Technology department over the appointment of a monitor for the IT department. Both groups resorted to aerial firing which led to fear and harassment. No injuries were reported.
An employee of UET was gunned down by unknown assailants in Harbanspura on Thursday

A powerful explosion on the Karachi-bound Chenab Express left 2 people injured and 1 dead. One of the injured victims later succumbed to this injuries. The victims were railway workers and members of a trade union, PREM.
Reportedly, a eunuch was found dead in Model Town G Block.
Two bullet riddled bodies were found in an abandoned car.

Shopkeepers and traders protested against the prolonged electricity breakdown. The protest got violent when the electricity still wasn't restored. The protesters blocked Superhighway, intercepted a truck and 2 cars and set them on fire, set 2 bank branches on fire, and attacked the police. The police called for reinforcements and used batons and teargas shells to control the mob. A police officer said that they did not arrest anyone as it was a protest against a utility service.
A police official, ASI Mohammad Saleem was shot dead in his home. The police say that he had a dispute over a plot with some people, who might be behind the killing.

At least four people were killed and as many injured when clashes erupted between supporters of militant commander Maulvi Nazir and his rival Noor Islam, who was backing foreign militants in different areas.  The fighting began when the Nazir group tried to dislodge foreigners from a government school in Gawakha area.
The decomposed body of a 35-year old man was found in the fields near Mayo Colony, Factory area in Lahore.

Police found the bullet-riddled body of an ex-army man in Orangi Extension from the Talibul Maula Colony. Sources stated that workers of the PPP, MQM and the Haqiqi had taken positions on roof tops in their respective areas and were intermittently firing shots at their rival parties.
the caretaker of an Imambargah was killed by armed men in a busy market.
Two tribesmen were injured in an exchange of fire with militants in the Stori Khel area.
Maulana Mohammad Yousaf Ali, a prominent leader of ASSP, was shot dead by unidentified assassins.
a woman Bashiran bibi was killed and another was injured during a shootout between two rival groups . The police has arrested 4 people.
A woman was shot dead by her husband as he suspected her character.
Militants fired three rockets on paramilitary camps which led to a three hour long exchange of fire between the militants and security forces
Many houses and crops were damaged due to Indian shelling along LoC in Sucheetgarh, Chaprar, Bajwat, Charwa, Bajragarhi, Harpal and Zafarwal Sectors on Wednesday.
Three children were killed in an explosion believed to be of a landmine in a field in Toba Qasimwala.

2 men on a motorbike opened fire at a group of people who were in the waiting room of a transport company. 4 people were killed and 2 were injured. The victims had illegally entered from Iran an hour before the firing took place. They claimed to be Iranian nationals but their ID cards showed that they belonged to Lahore and Faisalabad in Punjab. The town's administrator Mohammad Rafiq termed it a 'target killing'. ; Follow-up: It was claimed that the assailants targeted 'Punjabi settlers' and those visiting Balochistan.
Two Afghan nationals, Abdul Rauf and Badaruddin, were shot at by two men on a motorbike. Abdul Rauf was killed while Badaruddin was injured.
Hub SHO Aziz Hayat Baloch was gunned down by unknown assailants when he was in his vehicle AFH 412 near Juma Khan Hotel.

Hafiz Muhammad Asif, a prayer leader, was thrashed by two members of a rival sect over a 'secarian' issue. The victim claimed that Nadeem and Usman were provoked when he recited 'salat-o-salam' before and after the call player.
Security forces fired on a speeding car near Chashma Bridge on the Miramshah-Bannu road.
An unidentified body was found.

At least 4 vehicles and tyres were set on fire. Miscreants also blocked several main roads. In North Karachi sector 5-B/3, a stationary bus of route 4-J was set ablaze. In New Karachi, near the terminus of route 4-K, miscreants torched 2 buses. This occured on the day of the protest called by Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan, even though SSP retracted the protest call late night on Friday (2-Mar-01). According to the police, no arrests were made. According to sources near to the police, more than 3 dozen SSP activists were arrested. According to SSP sources, 50 activists were held by the police.

A roadside remote-controlled bomb was detonated when a passenger vehicle was passing by. 7 people including a Khasadar were injured. Taliban have recently attacked local tribesman as the latter had raised a lashkar against them.

Some unidentified persons resorted to indiscriminate firing with automatic weapons on Raees Hotel in Unit No. 10, Latifabad, killing two people and injuring another seriously. The possible motives behind the incident were not mentioned.
A worker of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement-Haqiqi (Amir Khan group), Syed Mohammad Haider, was killed. The police said it may have been due to personal enmity.

Dr. Syed Haider Abbas was intercepted by two men on a motorbike while he was driviing home. He was told to step out of the car and was shot when he tried to speed away. No valuables were taken which is why robbery was ruled out by the police. It is stated that he was targeted.

a group of infuriated people attacked the Wasa team when it visited Kashmir Road of Ghulam Muhammadabad to distribute water supply and sewerage bills. The residents protested against the Wasa for its failure to rectify the sewerage system and potable water supply. Later, they tortures officials Daleer and Anwar forcing them to leave the area.
The bullet riddled body of a 30 year old man was found with a chit on it saying 'American face the same fate'.

A woman, working for the Kurram Levies Force, was killed along with five other members of her family in an attack on her house in Toot Kass village in Hangu. According to sources, they were gunned down by militants while her minor son was injured.
A girl, Huma, was stabbed to death by her uncle and cousin for honour.

A tribal lashkar launched an operation against militants in which 3 militants were killed and 2 were injured. The operation was launched as a response to the killing of a tribal elder and two of his family members in an explosion on 04-Jul-10.
At least nine students wee injured when two groups belonging to Islami Jamiat Tulaba and All Pakistan Muttahida Students' Organisation clashed In S.M. law College in Karachi due to unknown reasons.

Hideouts of the Lashkar-i-Islami in Narai Baba, Sandana, Nangrosa, Ghulam Ali, Nakai and Sra Vela areas of Tirah Valley were targeted by military jet fighters, killing at least 50 people, non-combatant civilians among them. Khyber Agency's political agent Shafeerullah claimed that the death toll was 42 with 15 injured. The bombing of Sra Vela was strongly condemned by Kokikhel elders who claimed that most of the dead were innocent tribesmen. ; Follow-up: The death toll of the bombing had increased to 81 ; Follow-up: The residents of Sera Vella (spelt Sra Vela in the original report) claimed that their village, inhabited by Kokokhel Tribe, was a 'militant-free' area and the casualties from this area were all civilian. ; Follow-up: Chief of the Army Staff Gen. Ashfaq Parvez Kiyani apologized to the Kukikhel tribe for the loss of civilian life in the operation. The military had earlier claimed that all those killed were militants.
An unidentified body was found from Pak Colony under the Dhobi Ghat bridge. The body bore torture marks besides a gunshot wound.

Militants fired several rockets at the paramilitary base in Miramshah. One of the rockets hit the air strip near the base, but caused no damage or casualties. Three rockets were fired at the Saidgai checkpoint in the region.
Three people were killed when assailants in a car fired at bystanders outside a shopping mall.

Farmers from nearby villages protested the shortage of irrigation water, alleging that irrigation department staff had made an 'underhand' deal with agriculturalists and increased their supply for 4L Canal, depriving the farmers of 10 villages at the tail-end of the canal system.
A woman was killed and her husband and brother-in-law injured following an alleged dispute over property in Lassi Goth. The police could not be reached for details of the incident.
A powerful explosion rocked Kohlu township. However, no casualty or loss was reported.
Armed men attacked two people standing outside their house killing them both on the spot. One of the victims worked for the army.
Ethnic Violence' in Karachi continued for the 3rd consecutive day as a police mobile of SITE-A police station was attacked by armed men, leaving a police constable, Javed Shah, injured.

Three people were shot dead by uidentified gunmen in the court premises. The attackers reportedly wanted to target the Special Prosecuter but when they could not, they opened indiscriminate fire in a courtroom.

Security forces combating militants in the South Waziristan region moved into the hometown of the late Taliban chief Baitullah Mehsud and blew up his house amid clashes with militants which resulted in the killing of 24 terrorists while one was captured.
A mob carrying wooden sticks and pieces of rocks forced shopkeepers to close their businesses in light of the death of Allama Ali Sher Hyderi.
Two bullet-riddled bodies of Afghan nationals were recovered from a well. The victims were identified as Abdul Malik, resident of Ghamkol camp Merozai and Zaafran, resident of Ghamkol camp number 3.
A levy official of Orakzai Agency, Subedar Tajdar Ali, was killed by unknown armed men inside his house.
in UC Hala, Baho Khan Pathan, UC Sekhat and Saeedabad city 10 people were injured in clashes.

Police baton-charged and tear-gassed about 5000 powerloom labourers who were demonstrating for a pay raise. The protesters pelted the police with stones after the latter tried to stop them from proceeding to Clock Tower Chowk. The police then resorted to aerial fire. The protesters also tried to set a weaving factory on fire but were intercepted by factory guards. The resulting scuffle left 4 labourers injured. The call for the protest strike was given by Labour Quami Movement who also alleged that scores of labourers were injured and over a 100 were arrested by the police. The police denied the claim. The protesters dispersed after the DCO assured them that their demands would be met.
Two bullet-riddled bodies of two labourers were found in a desolate place in Turbat.

Suspected militants gunned down ANP's local leader of Swat Mukhtar Ali Khan and his associate Sardar Ali. The chief of Pakistan Tehrik I Insaaf's Swat chapter, Fazal hakeem, was also seriously injured in the attack.

Razia Bibi, who had been staying at her sister's place was fonud dead with two bullet wounds to the head. Police suspected that she had been shot by her sister, Ayesha and the latter's husband for 'honour' but Ayesha claims that her sister was killed as a result of a gun-cleaning accident.
Some unidentified gunmen made a murderous attack on the life of Muhammad Akram, an IJT activist.
Wakil Ahmed was talking to two men outside his house when a third person fired shots at him. All three men fled after the killing.
One person was shot dead.
An old man, Naseer Ahmed, was stabbed to death under mysterious conditions in a local hotel. No other detail was given.

Residents of the area protested against the police for giving the nephew of a DSP preferential treatment. They blocked the Ferozepur road and pelted stones at the police. The police responded with teargas shells and batons.

Two people were shot dead by unidentified people. The deceased, Anwar of Pindi Bhago and Sarwar of Mundeke Bairian, had taken away a mare of a local political figure from his dera. They took it to a farm house. A group of unknown people came the next day and shot them both dead.
Irfan, a 22-year-old resident of Manzoor Colony, was found shot dead inside a garbage dump.
Following a clash between militants and military personnel, a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into the gate of the Jansi post, killing at least 6 security personnel and injuring 15.
Unknown armed men shot at and injured a member of the Mahar tribe.
A woman was burnt when her second husband and his son threw acid on her over what she claimed sale of property at Maqbool Colony, Baghdad Road.
Unknown gunmen shot and killed a man identified as Muhammad Ibrahim

A checkpost manned by volunteers of Baizai Peace Committee was attacked by about 30 militants. The volunteers also responded and in the clash that ensued, 2 militants were killed and 5 were injured while 4 volunteers were killed and 1 was kidnapped.
A bullet-riddled body of a 35 year old man was found from Sector 13-A of Orangi Town.

Armed men on a motorbike opened fire at people standing outside a shop. As a result Faryal Khan was killed and another man was injured. This and other incidents of firing - aerial firing- were part of the violence that took place in Karachi following the sucide attack on Abdullah Shah Ghazi shrine.
Militants blew up the house of Ali Akbar, a volunteer of a local peace committee

Thousands of tribesmen staged protest demonstrations in several areas. They were addressed by the leaders of Tehrik-i-Taliban of the Agency. The speakers stated that all the ativities of the US government were anti-Islam and that the tribesmen would fight for Islam and the Taliban if the US government did not desist from striking against Afghanistan. They already set up recruitment centers so that the youth could register for Jihad.
A vendor was shot dead in Al-Flah Society on suspicion of being a police informer.
An unidentified body was found form the canal. The police is investigating.
It was alleged that an IJI candidate, Mian Mehmud Ahmed, tried to stop polling when his defeat became imminent which led to a clash between PPP and IJI supporters in which 6 people were injured.
a guard of Sunni Tehrik Chief Sarwar Chaudry was shot dead by unknown persons in Malir. The body of Irshad Qadri was found near Bagh-i-Malir, ehre his vehicle was also found parked.

At least eleven were injured during a clash between rival groups of students belonging to the PSF at Bahauddin University. They made use of arms and batons against each other. Apparently two female students of one groups were tortured by the rival group.

local militants known as Taliban killed 2 extortionists and hung their bodies on plyons near Zakim Hospital. They were both Afghan refugees, who were members of the Hakim group that had attacked the Taliban some time back.

a group of militants ambushed an army vehicle in Aligrama and killed three security personnel on the spot. The security forces cordoned off the area and imposed a curfew. They also targetted hideouts of suuspected militants with artillery fire. A number of houses were also destroyed.
A 45 year old woman died and 5 others received critical injuries as Indian troops shelled villages along the LoC in Kel sector.

Unidentified 'miscreants' broke into the post office and set it on fire after stealing certificates, bonds, postal orders and Khas certificates worth Rs 1 million. The post office records were completely destroyed. (see note)
Six tribesmen were killed and 30 injured in an armed clash between two Mengal clans over distrubution of land. The clash was reported to be very intense.
The body of an unidentified young man was found stuffed in a gunny bag near Natha Khan bridge.
A rocket fired from an unknown location damaged a house. No further details given.

Helicopters hovering over a military convoy fired on vehicles parked near a restaurant in Mirali tehsil, killing two people and injuring one. Maj-Gen Waheed said they military only targetted vehicles that were approach to attack the convoy.
A group of militants attacked a checkpost in the Baidmani area of Baizai tehsil in Mohmand, using heavy weapons. Security forces returned fire, killing four militants (two of them Afghans).
An Assistant sub inspector of the police and a nephew of a provincial minister were shot dead by unidentified gunmen in their house.
2 youngsters were found shot dead in Landhi on Thursday. However police claimed that they were criminals and probably died after a clash with some gangsters.
In PF-20, Mardan, a PML-N candidate escaped an attempt on his life when he was coming back after casting his vote.

In a clash between Pathans and Punjabis at Chowk sarwar shaheed area on Saturday, one person was killed and around a dozen were injured. The clash started as some pathans beated 2 punjabis as a result of which large number of Punjabis gathered in the heart of town and blocked the road

In response to SNA's call a small group of Jeay Sindh students federation tried to disrupt traffic and normal life on Rohri-Sukkur road near District Jail to press their demands for the release of Jeay Sindh detenus in October incident., but failed to gain momentum. Some of them pelted stones at the police and also attempted to obstruct a railway track. They also burnt tyres on busy roads and corners of old Sukkur.

A pull Dengro police post team raided a house to arrest some 'wanted  men'. However, the Langrana police was not informed of the raid. During the raid, the inmates of the house attacked and beat up the policemen. A case has been registered, with no arrest so far.

An explosion occurred on the rooftop of the Rehmani hotel in Gwadar. Two unidentified assailants came to the hotel and ordered tea but left without taking it. Soon after the explosion occurred. According to reports it was a locally made cracker-like device.
An 18-year old student was shot dead outside his house by unidentified gunmen.

Two militants were killed and four others injured during a clash with security forces in Charmang area of Bajaur tribal region.  A group of militants had attacked a checkpost and security retaliated, after which a heavy exchange of fire ensued. The hideouts of militants were also destroyed in the search operation in the area.
Noor Mustafa, who was the watchman at House# 436/A in Buffer Zone, was shot dead by armed motorcyclists.
Abdul Sattar, after exchanging harsh words with Nusrat Bibi (his step mother), opened fire on her and killed her over a property issue.

Fierce clashes broke out between police and people of Johi, Wahi Paudhi in Dadu district. Police had arrested a teacher of the Wahi Pandhi High School and detained a local journalist when the latter tried to enquire about the reason for the arrest of the first. Police also arrested 18 other people, prompting a wave of anger among the people. The people staged a sit in in front of the police station, which turned ugly when the police started baton charging them to disperse them. The protesters then clashed with the police in which at least 10 people were injured.

During a protest rally organized jointly by the IJT and the ISO to protest the increase in tuition fee by the government, a violent mob tried to break into the Government High School for Boys. The police intervened and baton-charged the protesters, arrested several of them in the process.

a bomb exploded near the Scouts post in Chukiatan. A missile planted near the post did not fire.there were no casualties and the post(Qila) was not damaged. Police said they had no information about any blast.
A police constable was kidnapped in Allahabad area of Charbagh.
Three people were killed and four others were injured in the Indian shelling on the Neelum valley.
A powerful bomb exploded near a police checkpoint of Shaikhan Chowk on Saturday injuring 5 persons. Bombs was planted on a bicycle.
Forty Malik Dinkhel tribesmen demolished the house of a tribal elder for giving a verdict against his own tribe in a previous property dispute.
Two brothers shot dead their sister in Sukkur as they 'suspected her character'.

Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front had planned a demonstration in front of Dyal Singh Mansion office in order to press for the release of its leaders and workers arrested in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and to condemn the rejection of its candidates nomination in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly. They started the rally but as they turned on Queen's road, the police that was accomplying them baton charged them and forced them to disperse. They also arrested 8 people.
The headless body of Ambel Khan was found in Akkakhel. Residents said he had been kidnapped by some gunmen from the locality.
Two unidentified men broke into the house of Advocate Muhammad Iqbal and shot him dead.
An activist of the People's Party was gunned down near Gulshan-i-Maymar of the Super Highway.
Six civilians were killed when an American missile landed in Pakistani territory during a strike at Al-Qaeda hideouts in Afghanistan.
Indian troops lobbed at least five mortar shells in Bandala village of Samahni sector injuring one person.
As a result of the verdict of supreme court annulling the appointment of Justice (Retd) Deedar Shah as NAB chairman, a bus was set ablaze in Ranchore Lines area on Thursday.
A man was shot dead allegedly by five people over a land dispute, when he was fired upon in his sleep by five armed men in Chak 24, Pattoki.
Riaz Mohammad Solangi was shot dead by Haider Sonagi and Qaiser Solangi in village Naseer Solangi.
Heavy indian shellin across the LoC injured two people in Athmuqam and Lala on Tuesday. Several buildings got damaged as a result of shelling
Naila, wife of Faiz Muhammad Sethar, was shot dead by ber brother-in-law, Jinsar Sethar, in the name of Karo-kari.

According to Pir Binyamin Rizvi, the police is arresting PML activists before the arrival of party president, Shahbaz Sharif, in order to prevent a reception for him. He stated that police raided Dewan Mushtaq's house in order to arrest him.
security forces destroyed 6 camps of militant Marri tribesmen in different areas of Kohlu. They also arrested men from Jhabar.
Ghulam Qadir was killed in Liaquat Colony during curfew break.

Two rockets were fired into Quetta Cantonment. The first landed in an open area near Chaman Housing Scheme and disrupted the electricity supply. The second rocket exploded in the backyard of a small house owned by Bushra- a teacher at Federal Government Public School- near Combined Military Hospital after an interval of 10 minutes. The rockets damaged window panes of houses in both localities. There were no injuries.
The body of a 22 year old man was found from Orangi town. His political affiliation could not be known.
A young man was shot dead in the Jalalabad area of Pak Colony by unknown persons. He was reportedly said to belong to a notorious Haji Laloo group.
Two men were wounded in a 'sniping incident' in Quaidabad.
Nine militants were killed and five militants were injured during a search operation in different areas of the Kurram region.
Gas supply to parts of Quetta was suspended after some saboteurs blew up a portion of the pipeline in the Sariab area.

Clashes between the Bugti and Mazari tribesmen have continued for more than 20 years. In recent incidents of violence, Bugtis kidnapped two Mazari tribesmen while the Mazaris kidnapped three Bugti tribesmen.

After the murder of one of their gang members- Mohammad Iqbal alias Babu Dakait- earlier in the day, the gang members of Rehman Dakait allegedly killed Abdul Malik of Babu Dakait's group near Baloch Hall. Later, his house was set ablaze.

Rafiqullah, who was later identified as an activist of MQM, was killed and two others, also MQM activists, were injured when unknown persons opened fire on them in Baldia town. Police said the incident coincided with the funeral procession of Rehman Baloch which was passing through the area when the inicident occured.

Ghous Bakhsh Langah shot dead his sister and his relative on the pre-text of karo-kari. Ali Gohar Langah, father of the deceased boy said that it was not a karo-kari case, both the deceased had been called to the house to settle domestic issues when they were gunned down.
Security forces killed three militants in the Bara tehsil of Khyber Agency during a search operation in the Gurguri and adjoining areas.
two soldiers were injured when terrorists opened fire at Soko Kandao, near Malam Jabba.
District General Secretary of JUI-F, Hafiz Ehtisham, was gunned down in Panjgur when armed men opened fire on him and fled.
An activist of MQM, Muhammad Shakil Patel, was shot dead. The assailants escaped.

2 missiles were fired from the Kotaki refugee camp onto the private residence of tribal elder, Malik Mohammad Rehman. 1 missile badly damaged the house, while the other did not explode. The elder stated that he had no enmity with anyone but did exchange harsh words with refugees a few days ago. Police arrested 2 people.
Two groups exchanged hot words over the issue of appointing an Imam for the Jamia Masjid Rodi. They opened fire on each other and 13 persons sustained injuries.
Unknown assailants shot and killed a young man and fled.

An activist of the MQM (H) was gunned down and another was kidnapped in G-36 Landi area, by unknown armed persons who managed to flee after killing. Haqiqi men claimed that the rival faction of MQM was behind the incident.

The local Taliban blew four shops of cosmetics in the Bilitang bazaar, 16 km east of Kohat city. Police claimed that the Taliban had planted four improvised explosive devices in front of the shops. Furthermore, the business of CD and video shops has already been closed in the area following threats from Taliban.
An unidentified man was stabbed to death by two assailants. The reasons behind the attack were unknown.

An ethnic clash broke out between Mohajirs and Pathans when the Municipal Staff razed a hotel owned by a Pathan, as part of the anti-encroachment drive. The hotel owner claimed he was vicitmised because of his ethnicity and the Mohajirs got enraged. In the ensuing shootout one person was killed and six were injured.
A constable was shot dead by three attackers in his house. The police did not give any reason behind the attack, but claimed to have arrested one of the suspects.

a boy was killed and three other people were injured when a bomb exploded in Nushki which had been planted on a power pylon 200 yards away from the fort of Chagai Malitia, a wing of the FC, on the mess road. The walls of a house were also destroyed as were the windows of many houses.
Air strikes conducted by the Pakistan Military destroyed 3 TTP hideouts and killed 5 militants.

Relatives of Tariq Mehmood, a trader who was bludgeoned to death after a minor road accident by the other party, by placing the victims body on the road, burning tyres and pelting policemen with stones. They also tried to attack a TV correspondent for 'wrong reporting'. The assailants in the original killing were reported to be '2 lawyers and their accomplices'.

A pregnant woman was killed and three others of the same family were injured when seven armed men entered a house of a landlord in Chiyanwala village and opened fire on them. The incident is said to be because of a rivalry between two groups in the area.
the body of Gollu, a tribesman who had been killed by militants for being a 'spy' was found in the town of Wana.

In the Samar bagh village of Lower Dir, at least twenty-six people were killed while another sixty-five were injured when a young suicide bomber blew himself up during funeral prayers as he was standing in one of the rear rows. The funeral was attended by the Mishwani tribe who had been raising anti-Taliban lashkars.
Three unknown assailants, armed with sophisticated weapons, entered the railway godown and set it on fire.
One policeman was killed and eight were injured when the police mobile hit a bomb in Dobai Ada are in Mardan.
A partially decomposed body of Haleema Bibi was recovered from Kalri Nullah. It appeared that the woman was beaten up and dumped into the drain.

Indian forces opened 'unprovoked' firing on Pakistani positions along the border near Sialkot. Pakistani Rangers retaliated with fire. A spokesman for Indian border guards claims that they were provoked by terrorists who were attempting to illegally cross the border.
An exchange of fire took place between two 'warring' rival groups. One person was killed and when the police tried to intervene a constable was also shot dead.
10 days ago, a UC chairman Malik-Gulzar Awan was shot at and injured by unidentified assailants when he was on his to Isha prayers.
two retired army personnel were killed in Gilgit.
Militants blew up a girls' primary school. A girls' highschool was also blown up in the same area that day.
Hangu's Mohall station area was tense after three bullet-riddled bodies were found following clashes between rival sects.
Unknown armed men on motorcycles killed a bus driver of the Mahar Tribe.

Irshad Ahmad Khan, audit officer of Allied Bank was on his way home to Batala Colony when some unidentified people opened fire on his car. His brother-in-law was the additional secretary Sohail Saqlain.

after imposing a curfew in Bannu forces began shelling militant hideouts in Bannu. 70 to 80 militants were killed in Janikhel area of Bannu Frontier Region. The house of a local Taliban commander was destroyed in the fighting. 5 vehicles, an explosive laden vehicle among them, were destroyed. 39 suspected Taliban were arrested.

a clash took place in Chak 4/14-L between two parties where two persons, Bacha Khan and Gulab Khan were killed while others sustained serious injuries. The police have arrested 8 people from both parties.
An \irate mob\" took away a vehicle from its driver and set it on fire. No further details given. "
A senior official of the Balochistan food department was killed and his son injured when unidentified men opened fire on them in Tin Town on Kasi Road. Another passer-by was also injured .

Abdul Majeed Gujjar, an ex-student of UET said to have links with the Muslim Students Federation (MSF) died of his wounds that were inflicted upon him on 17th May 1996. According to reports, MSF workers, including Abdul Majeed Gujjar and Khurshid Ghani, raided the house of Rana Muzaffar on UET campus with the police to recover some items which were lost when PSF workers ransacked a room owned by Khurshid Ghani of MSF. When they arrived at the house, they were fired upon by assailants from the inside, which killed Abdul Majeed Gujjar and injured Khurshid.
Unidentified persons attacked a toll-tax post and injured two people in Old Bahawalpur Road on Sunday

Armed men on a motorbike opened fire at a group of friends sitting outside at a market, killing one and injuring 3 others. 2 of the injured vitims were associated with PPP-SB. The incident seemed to be a result of some dispute between two political groups in the area.
Pattoki police found the body of an unidentified young man in the Pattoki College.
Unidentified men riding a car fired at security forces, injuring a paramilitary soldier. Security forces had also diffused two missiles near Saidgi area

Mohammad Busksh was on his way home on his motorcycle when armed men shot and killed him before fleeing the scene. ; A later report titled \Murdered\" (dawn, 26-Feb-94, Page 4) claims that the victim's name was Mohammad Bux. "
A device planted near a girls' school in Mastung's Hindu Mohalla exploded, damaging the boundary wall and the gate of the school and shattering windowpanes of nearby buildings.

Troops from India and Pakistan exchanged heavy fire along the Line of Control (LoC). Pakistani troops fired over 2000 rounds on Indian troops from South Charva post in Sambah sector. They did so in retaliation to unprovoked firing on Pakistani troops by Indian Border Security Force.
2 people were injured due to Indian shelling along LoC in Shah Kot Salkhala Village on Thursday
Four labourers were injured when some unidentified people attacked them with sticks and lathis while they were asleep in the labour camps.
In union council 1 and 3 and Mitro and 90/W.B areas, rival candidates fought and as a result, many of them were wounded. Later, the army and the police controlled the situation.

Islampura residents blocked the main road and burnt tyres to protest the arrest of prayer leader Muhammad Imran by Islampura police. It was alleged that the prayer leader was arrested for misuse of loudspeaker. The protesters dispersed when the prayer leader was released and they were assured that action would be taken against the policemen responsible for the arrest.
the security forces killed three militants in the house of Maulana Shad Mohammad, a hardcore taliban leader, in Khan Abad area of Maidan. Sources say that the house was destroyed.
Some unidentified men shot dead a billiards club owner, Sher Afzal, as he was at a PCO making a call. He was also a telephone cards contractor.

Following the incidents of Kharadar and Gullistan-i-Jauhar, a fresh wave of violence erupted in Karachi as a result of which an activist of MQM was gunned down by unknown assailants in Ranchore Lines Area on Sunday
A bus was set ablaze by protesters.

It was alleged that 4 PML workers, identified as Aurangzeb Tunio, Khalid hussain Tunio, Ashraf Malik and Syed Jaffar Shah, were arrested by the police and were being beaten up at the police station at the behest of local PPP men. This was claimed by Mazhar Ali Magsi, chief organizer of the Shahdadkot PML.
A boy was killed and another person was injured in Indian shelling along LoC in Nakyal Sector on Monday.
Eight people were injured in a clash between two groups of Gadahi tribe in Khairpur Nathan Shah.

2 people, including a policeman, were injured when some armed men led by a Jamiat Tulba-i-Islam leader, Maulana Zubair Bhatti, tried to take control of the central Eidgah by opening fire on its legal occupants. The police reached the spot and 1 was injured in the crossfire. Maulana Zubair had illegally occupied Eidgah to build a seminay, but the cort had decided in favour of the legal occupants.
A leader of the Imamia jirga, Ghulam Hussain Toori, was going to his workplace when unidentified men opened fire killing him on the spot. A passer by was also injured.

Two young activists of the ASWJ were going somewhere on a motorbike when armed motorcyclists intercepted them. Shoaib was shot and killed on the spot while his friend, Mustafa, was chased and then fired at in Sector-G. Mustafa received bullet injuries along with 2 bystanders who were also wounded. Shoaib was the third ASWJ member targeted in December 2010.

Two powerful bomb blasts occurred in Quetta within moments of each other. The first blast occured in a small street of the Jamiat-Ray road. There were no reports of casualties or major damage. The blast shattered windowpanes of the buildings near the explosion site.
at least 19 rockets were fired on FC checkpost in Chashma, Loti, Pir Koh and Sangsilla areas of Dera Bugti. However no casualties were reported in the attack.
A bullet-riddled body of a young man was found near Rupali Homes in Surjani Town. The victim had been shot twice and his face had been burnt by acid beyond recognition.

one labourer was killed and another 7 were injured in a grenade attack on a house by a group of armed men in Gharibabad area. Some suspects were arrested. The Baloch Republican Army spokesperson, Sarbaz Baloch claimed responsibility for the attack. official sources say that a Bugti tribesman was injured in the explosion.
three people were killed in an exchange of fire, following an attack by a group of Bugti tribesmen on a house in Mir Hasan village near Dera Murad Jamali.
An unidentified person was shot at and injured. No further details were given.

A security guard and a driver were found strangled to death from separate rooms in a welfare organization office run by a retired army officer in Garden Town. The bodies bore torture marks. The retired army officer claimed that a four-wheeler, two computers and a TV set were also missing from the building.
An MQM worker was shot dead by two gunmen on a motorcycle and fled
Five people were killed and six others were injured when a missile, allegedly fired by a US drone, hit a suspected militants compound in Dandi Darpakhel.

the Principal of Commerce College, Quetta, Prof Mirza Amanat Ali Baig, was killed when men on motorbikes opened indiscriminate fire on him. The students of the college boycotted their classes and held a demonstration infront of the hospital demanding the immediate arrest of the killers.

According to ISPR, the security forces engaged militants in Piochar , north of Matta,  and areas between Charbagh and Khawazakhela. Wireless communication intercepted by security forces revealed that the militants had suffered heavy losses.
Abdul Jabbar, a bus conductor by profession, was kidnapped on his way home and was severely tortured. His body was thrown at Chandani Chowk in Orangi.
The office of a customs clearing agent was paritally damaged in a bomb blast while another bomb discovered at the same office was defused.
A PAF official was killed after he sustained a bullet woud in Khokhrapar No.3, as part of the renewed violence in Karachi.

In the aftermath of an incident where two brothers were killed over a land dispute, heirs and residents of the village blocked the Sialkot Bypass road and burnt tyres to protest the killings. They chanted slogans against the police as two policemen were allgegedly invovled in the murders. They, later, dispersed peacefully upon the assurance from the DPO Saud Aziz that the accused would be arrested within 24 hours. Arrop police claimed to have arrested the constable allegedly invovled in the killing but his accomplice, Ghulam Mustafa, was still at large.

The police have claimed to have taken into custody a girl suspected to be a suicide bomber. A police officer, Khadim Hussain Bhatti, informed the police that a girl had entered his house with suspected gadgetry. The police arrested the girl, who identified herself and Nabeela Bibi, about 18, with a shopping bag containing a remote control and a bomb-shaped bottle full of wires. A bomb disposal squad checked the bottle and said there was no incendiary device in it.
Following a fresh wave of violence, a truck and a bus were torched by unknown militants in Safora Goth on Sunday.
In village Talwar, Abdul Hameed was killed by unknown people.
A US drone fired 4 missiles at a militant compound, destroying the compound and killing 4 militants.

11 people were injured during a clash between the supporters of former PPP minister Hamid Saeed Kazmi and PML-N MNA Rana Mehmoodul Hassan as the supporters of Hamid Saeed Kazmi were protesting against his arrest at Bahawalpur Bypass on Sunday.
A landmine was planted to blow up the rangers vehicle. However, the device exploded after the vehicle had passed. However, two Sindh Rangers personnel got injured.
An MQM activist was axed to death allegedly by activists of a rival party.
A tehsildar and three Levies personnel were kidnapped from Nawagai. Militants in Mohmand agency claimed the responsibility.
The Ismailkhel checkpost was attacked with rockets and missiles, which killed one soldier and left two others injured.
Three men were killed and another was injured when gunmen on mortorbikes opened fire on them.
One person was injured in Nagdar village of Neelum valley as the Indian forces continued firing from across the LoC.
As part of the on-going violence in Karachi, at least four people were injured in shooting incidents in Ditrict Central.
As violence in Karachi continued for a fourth consecutive day, armed men set over a dozen vehicles on fire, paralysing several parts of the city.

The tribal lashkar burnt down the house ouf Sher Khan as he tried to stop the drummers from beating the drums while accompanying the tribal lashkar (as per tribal custom). The lashkar decided that he is liable to punishment as he interfered with the lashkar.
President of the Hindu Panchayat, Larkana and his driver were assaulted and kidnapped by five armed men.

As a result of the verdict of supreme court annulling the appointment of Justice (Retd) Deedar Shah as NAB chairman, violence broke out in Karachi as a result of which several roadside stalls were set ablaze near Al-Asif Square and PIB Colony on Friday.

A former PML MPA, Chaudary Sarwar Booch, was ambushed by 3 people. He was travelling with 4 bodyguards in 3 cars, and managed to escape unharmed. However, 2 guards were killed and 1 was injured in the attack.
Rockets were fired at an FC post in Panjoo Chakrani near sui. No casualties were reported.
A blast caused damage to the building of district and sessions court on Shershah suri Road. The police were not sure of how the blast was caused.
A Rangers vehicle hit a landmine on Sui road killing one Rangers personnel and injuring three others. Details n.a.
at least 7 people were injured and three official vehicles were damaged while trying to defuse a remote controlled IED.
helicopter gunships shelled an office of militants and destroyed a large quantity of weapons.

A Hesco lineman was beaten up in a clash between the Hesco staff in Luqman and the residents of the Serai Ghanwar Khan Mohalla over the installation of electric meters. Following the attack the chairman of the Hesco union informed that the Hesco staff had suspended work and demanded that the police register a case against the accused.
A suicide bomber blew an explosive laden car near a police station in Mardan killing  a sub inspector and two other people. 37 people including 22 policemen were also injured.
Military planes targerted militant hideouts, destroying 7 of them and killing 18 militants. 12 militants were also wounded.

Twenty five people were injured when pro-Zahir Shah and anti-monarchy groups of the Afghan Mujahideen and refugees clashes during a big rally at Nishat Mills on Charsadda Road. Clashes and skirmishes erupted when a former minister of Zahir Shah and Daud government Azizullah Wasifi suggested that the war should end after the Societ troops withdrawal. Incidents of exchange of fire were  reported as people turned down the suggestion of giving up armed struggle.

A bomb placed under a cart exploded in the fruit market, injuring 30 people. According to an explosives expert, the bomb weighed 1.5kg and had an intensity of 250/H.E. The bomb also damaged a pickup van standing near the cart as well as window panes of nearby windows. According to Nasir Khan Durrani, there were no casualties and no arrests have been made in connection to the blast.
Some unidentified people killed an employee of a honey farm in Sarban area.

A trader was kidnapped which caused a violent protest. The villagers gathered on the Thehri bridge and pelted vehicles with stones, burnt tyres, put a firebrigade truck on fire, smashed its windscreen and lights; the driver was injured. The police arrived and baton charged the villagers, injuring 5.
A tribal elder was shot dead in Inayar Kalley reportedly for being pro-governemnt.

Armed men struck at Gulistan-i-Jauher which led to heavy crossfire in the area, resulting the death of a pedestrian. Another body was taken to the casualty unit of Jinnah Postgraduate medical from the same area. Intense firing left 5 people wounded as well.
6 people were killed in a clash between two tribes-Khankhel and Astrand tribes over a piece of land in D.G Khan on Thursday.
Three people including two brothers were killed, and another was injured when unidentified men attacked Jamil Brothers Autos in Siddiq Plaza in the Buffer zone.

According to sources, militants planted a bomb outside the residence of the member of the Mamond Peace Committee, Malik Gul Rehman in the Gat Agra area and exploded as soon as the pro-government tribal elder came out of his house.
A person was killed by unknown assailants on Thursday in Hub chowk
A primary school for girls was blown up in the Koz Qalla area of Manglor
Militants attacked a paramilitary checkpost by firing rockets. This prompted the security forces to retaliate with artillery shelling which then resulted in local casualties.
A mine explosion damaged a FC water tanker.
Haji Isjaq was shot and wounded in Bengali Para in Korangi when he refused to give donation to members of a group.
Two women were critically injured when a mortar shell hit a house in the Sipah area.
A young girl was killed by her father after he saw her with a man.

It was reported that firing on a mosque in Shehr Sultan left 6 people dead and several others injured. The police claimed to have unearthed the group responsible which was stated to be a militant organization composed of former SSP activists who had decided to wage a \crusade\" against the Shia sect. (See Note)"

About 200 'miscreants' allegedly broke into the city office of the PPP and damaged everything inside. They broke the doors, smashed the signboards and glasses of picture frames and raised slogans against the PPP.

According to officials, forty militants and one security man had been killed in clashes that took place between the militants and the security forces, and that the Mohmand area was cleared of militants after the three day long operation.

Followin the stabbing of a motorcyclist, Ramzan, violence erupted in the Orangi area with two rival groups exchanging fire. Scores were people were injured in the clashes that took place in different sectors of Orangi town.  ; Follow-up: A statement given by the MQM chief Altaf Hussain indicates that the clashing rivals were ethnic groups.

Armed men of the Khoso tribe opened fire on a paddy shop in Qazi Ahmed, killing 7 people and injuring 3. After protesting against the failure of the police to provide security, a group of enraged Jataoi tribesmen attacked the village of Ghazi Hassan Khoso and killed a man identified as Qurban Khoso. The clash was the result of an old dispute between the two tribes which also claimed 3 lives in December 2009.
A man who had recently returned from England was found strangled in his house in Shadbagh. The tenant of the house claimed that two boys went to visit the victim on Dec 25.
Two rival religious groups clashed over the possesion of a mosque. Two people were injured.

The Sindh Professors and Lecturers Association (SPLA) had taken out a rally to demand an increase in pay-scales and hiring of new teachers but were intercepted by the police who prevented them from marching towards the CM's House. A brief baton-charge was witnessed which was followed by a scuffle with the police. 12 protesters were taken into police custody but were released later.
troops foiled an attempt by militants to launch a rocket attack by hitting the suspected location with artillery and mortar shells killing three militants and injuring 5.
Pakhtun Khan and Miran Jan, who had come from Kohistan to collect funds for seminary students in Kohistan, were found killed.
One person was injured in indian shelling across LoC in Samahni sector on Wednesday
A local leader of Awami national party, Dilasa Khan, was shot dead by unknown motorcyclists at his retaurant in Karachi. His son escaped the assassination attempt.

an FC personnel was killed and five others including a civilian was injured when two landmines exploded in Kahan Town. A landmine blast injured a civilian. Paramilitary troops rushed to the site and recued the man but the vehicle carrying the FC personnel struck another landmine when it was on its way to the nearby hospital. Meanwhile the Baloch Liberation Army(BLA) and Baloch Liberation Fron (BLF) claimed responsibility for the attack through its joint spokeman Azad Baloch.

At least five  persons were killed while another thirty three were injured when a bomb attached to a motorbike was detonated by remote control in a commercial area at Nishtarabad Chowk along the GT Road. According to the police, the main target of the blast was a CD music centre in the area.

angry protesters took out a procession as they wanted the  government to relax the curfew and allow the Ashura to pass through the regular route. the armed men blocked the main Kohat-Parachinar Highway and began their march towards Hangu. They marched into Hangu to take out Ashura procession by force amid curfew in the city. The army fired mortars near the Orakzai Agency headquarters when they tries to enter Hangu city.

Six students were injured in a clash between two rival groups of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF) at the Government Polytechnical College, Lahore. According to the police over a dozen armed students belonging to one group of MSF tried to take control of the hostel and upon resistance from the other group, a clash ensued in which firing with automatic weapons  resulted in damage to the building as well. They claimed that it was the second clash to take over the Yaqoob Hostel. Two students were taken into custody.
Two men were gunned down outside a hospital. No further details given.

The Additional Advocate General of Punjab, Arif Bhinder, and six other people were gunned down by Zahid and his accomplices, belonged to a rival political group. The motive behind the killing was said to be a political rivalry between Mr. Bhinder and Zahid alias Zahdu, residents of Khokar village, Badami Bagh. The attacker, Zahid, was also killed in the exchange of fire. Followup: The death toll of the attack rose to 8 Followup: 2 people were arrested in connection to the Bhinder murder.
A teenager was shot dead in Orangi  and the motive behind the killing could not be known.

Police contingents trying to restore traffic on various blocked roads faced fierce firing near Jamiatul Maaraf al Sharia. The police suspected the JUI to be involved in the firing and raided the JUI madrassa later that day. The police resorted to aerial firing and teargas shelling inside the madrassa. Students were severely beaten and four were reported injured. The police further confiscated 3 motorcycles, 3 bicycles, more than Rs. 550,000 and gold and silver ornaments collected as donations for Afghans.

Police fired teargas shells and dispersed an angry mob of young people who went on rampage smashing the windowpanes of shops and windscreens of passing vehicles. They were protesting against an explosion  which took place at Abal Chowk, which has caused no injury to anyone, nor had it damaged property.

Rehan Umer Farooqi, a former MQM MNA, was shot and killed when he tried to resist a kidnapping attempt by unidentified people. The incident took place when Farooqi had gone to visit the family of Wasim Ahmed, another former MQM MNA. The victim was originally part of the MQM but latter left it for the MQM-H. Interestingly, the Malir Extension police watered down the crime scene, leaving no trace of blood or any evidence.
In the after math of Benazir Bhutto's death, angry PPP protesters chanted slogans against the government in rallies all over and burnt tyres in protest which terminated at V Chowk.
a FC soldier was killed in a landmine blast near Mullah Baksh village in Nasirabad district.

Some unidentified armed men attacked the house of Mr. Ghulam Mustafa Jatoi (Leader of the Combined Opposition in the National Assembly). They fired 'indiscinimantly' and threw brickbats, injuring the guard.
A woman was gunned down by three unknown persons over a karo kari dispute 15 years after her 'indictment'.

according to official sources, three security personnel were killed and three others injured in a remote-controlled landmine explosion. They were returning after distributing ration to the soldiers when their vehicle was blown up by the blast.
A landmine blast killed a tribesman in Dera Bugti

saboteurs five powerful bombs on the Quetta Zahida line between the Sheikh Wasal and Galangur railway stations four of exploded destroying the tracks at two places. BLA claimed responsibility fo rthe railway track blasts.
The Army was called out to control the situation as protester's burnt the  district court and the magistrate's office.
Militants attacked military troops to which the latter responded with heavy artillery fire, killing 10 militants. 1 soldier was injured in the initial attack.

As KESC workers continued protesting against their placement in a 'surplus pool', various incidents of violence were reported from the city. Armed masked men attacked three assistant executive engineers outside the latter's office to stop them from working. The protesting workers denied the allegation that they had forcefully stopped people from working.
Two men were gunned down in an encounter with the police in Goth Ali Akbar Shah when they tried to flee.

The house of two alleged killers was set on fire by angry protesters in Block G/1 in Johar Town when they pelted stones, destroyed valuables and burned the house down. No one was reported to be injured as the alleged killers had escaped before.

A woman, Bashiran Bibi, and er daughter-in-law, Rehana Bibi, were found butchered in their house. Rehana Bibi was going to go to Saudi Arabia soon and according to the other family members, they had no enmity with anyone. The police could not ascertain the motive behind the murders.
Unidentified armed people attacked the military personnel on Matta Ronyal road. Tehrik I Taliban Pakistan claimed the responsbility for the attack.
The body of an unidentified man was found floating in the Indus river near the Ghazi Barotha barrage.

a police party led bySHO Riaz Khan was on patrol on the Indus Highway when a group of armed men opened indiscriminate firing on their vehicle. The SHO and his bodyguard was killed while another policeman was injured. The SHO had been receiving threats from different criminal gangs, politicians and the Taliban.

Persistent water and power shortage led to a protest by residents of Zaman Town who took to the streets and attacked water hydrants. The police were there to intercept the protesters and later called Rangers for backup. In one of the multiple attempts to damage hydrants some shots were fired which led to one young man getting injured and later succumbing to those injuries. The police and Rangers denied having fired the shots, but residents of the area blamed the police for the firing and returned later to demonstrate violently against the police. A passenger bus was set on fire near Matkay Wali Pulya. A fire tender rushed to the spot was unable to do its job as people kept pelting it with stones.

Ahmad Ali was shot dead by his armed rivals in the Shahdara town. The deceased owned some agricultural land in the area that was repeatedly trespassed on by tractor trollies owned by the accused, Mohammad Riaz. The 2 parties had often quarreled over this in the past.
A young man's body was found wrapped in a sheet in the parking lot of the Jinnah Post Graduate Medical Centre. He had reportedly been strangled and there were no torture marks on his body.

A clash took place between law enforcement agencies and demonstrators. local administration, with the help of Frontier corps was able to remove the barricades that had been setup. the protesters regrouped around the main highway. some shots were fired in the air, causing injury to FC personnel. FC responded by firing shots.
The Sui administration defused three rockets from a gas field. Details are not available.
As the protesters were protesting in Khurrianwala Chowk against the release of Raymond Davis, police resorted to baton-charge injuring two men on Wednesday.
FC was ordered to take action against the Tori and Banghash militant tribesmen who had been fighting for several days now in the Kurram region. 15 to 20 militants were killed by the Fc troops.

The beheaded body of a Khasadar was found in Bara tehsil of Khyber tribal region. The headless body of Shah Ahmad alias Shanak was found in Speen Qabar Chowk. The deceased was kidnapped from his house by unidentified gunmen. Nobody claimed responsibility for the attack.

Syed Ejaz Hussain came to the Imambargah during Maghrib prayers and detonated the bomb in the second rakat. Everyone ran out, 4 worshippers were injured and the bomber died. Acting District Nazim Raja Javed Ikhlas promised a revision on the security arrangements in mosques for Muharram.; Follow-up: According to Mr. Hayat, the suicide bomber was Muzaffar-ur-Rehman. He was trained in Afghanistan and belonged to a miltant group.
The situation in Lyari remained tense as protests continued against the house arrest of Benazir Bhutto. Protestors burnt tyres and threw stones at vehicles while the police fired tear gas shells.

Two rival rallies were planned in connection to the deposition of the Chief Justice of Pakistan, and it was feared that the showdown would degenerate into a violent 'show of strength'. Already, incidents of firing had been reported from different areas of the city, and a man was gunned down. No detail of any incident was given, but it seems to be the precursor of a larger blast of violence that the city would soon experience.

Markets and shops were closed and protest demonstrations were held in Rajo Khanani town against the desecration of the Holy Quran on the previous day allegedly by a 25 year old man. Angry mobs took to the streets and besieged a police station, in which they forced the police to arrest the accused.
A rocket fired by militants from a nearby hilltop hit a mosque in Landi Kotal, damaging its boundary wall. Another rocket was defused by the khasadars from the place where the first one was fired.
4 persons were killed and 8 others were injured in an indiscriminate firing by a religious group in Old Jhang city.

A powerful bomb blast badly damaged two classrooms and an office of the Government Middle Boys School Kachi Maand, in Sialkot working boundary. No casualty was reported as no one was on the school premises at the time of the explosion. According to officials, the Indian-made time bomb, weighing 5kg, was placed beneath school walls and was meant to target the students but due to some technical fault the explosive device exploded earlier at 3:05am. A civil defence official confirmed that another identical time bomb was also found on the premises which was defused 5 minutes before its scheduled time.

two people, Kora Khan Domki and Shaho Domki, were shot dead in Bakhtairabad area of Nasirabad. they had gone to attend a jirga to help decide a dispute with their rivals. The deceased had refused to accept the decision on the jirga. They were killed on their way home
Two unknown motorcyclists gunned down Iqbal Hussain Butt, a former PPP councillor near his house in sector 34-L, Korangi.
Three unidentified gunmen opened fire at one Afzal Bajwa. He died later in the hospital. The reason behind the murder is not known.
militant hideouts in Tor Chappar and Shni Kalay were bombed by security forces.
Mohammad Sajid, 18,  received injuried in Liaquatabad.

A drone strike on the residence of Karim Khan killed 5 and injured 2. Karim Khan, who used to work for a newspaper, had allegedly developed ties with militant organizations, representatives of which would frequent his house. ; Follow-up: The two injured later succumbed to their injures, taking the death toll upto 7. One of the victims was a top militant leader, Haji Mohammad Umar.
Police sources said some people opened fire on FC personnel in the Sarona area of Wadh. However no casualties were reported.
Protests were held at Aath Chowk and other places where enraged youth burnt old tyres.
following the killing of the baloch nationalist leaders violence erupted in Balochistan.a mob set on fire an under construction building.
5 militants were killed in an exchange of fire with the security forces in Matta Tehsil on Friday.

An eight member gang attacked the Korangi residence of milk-seller Deen Muhammad. The armed men first took the family hostage, then had the Deen Muhammad and his sons stand in a line against the wall, and sprayed them with bullets. Initially the police described the incident as terrorism, suspecting that the five were killed on the suspicion of being police informers. But later, a senior police officer said that they were investigating other aspects of the murder too.
The trussed-up body of a leader of the Baloch Republican Army (a seperatist militant outfit), Saleem Afshani, was found in Lea Market.
An unidentified body was found near White Hall with his hands tied behind his back.
two people were killed in an exchange of fire in Gulzar-i-Hijri when a chowkidar Gulshan-i-Maimar was attacked by 4 men.
Four members of the Mehar clan were injured when they were attacked with clubs and daggers by their rivals.
Mohammad Hussain was injured in firing near Landhi police station.
The body of an unidentified man was found. There was an injury mark around his neck.
Unknown men fired 2 rockets at the Sui Airport and damaged a portion of the runway. The first landed on the runway and the second exploded near the airport but did not damage it.
The house of PPP Gujrat President , Ashraf Deuna was attacked by rivals with 30 rockets. Mr. Deuna and his family escaped unhurt.

Feroze Ahmad, a local MQM activist, lodged a complaint with the Garden Police, claiming that a number of PPP activists, led by Ramzan Baloch, fired at the MQM office and tried to ransack it. They came in two vehicles and allegedly opened fire at the MQM Office.
The body of young man was found with multiple bullet wounds.
Militants blew up a gas pipeline in the Dasht area suspending gas supply to Quetta.

The Lahore chapter of Shabab-i-Milli, Pakistan, held a demonstration against the rising level of obscenity in Pakistani films.  The increasing obscenity was termed 'a conspiracy to pollute the minds of Pakistani youth'.  Some Shabab-i-Milli activists reportedly entered the building of Central Film Censor Board and ransacked the office of its chairman.
Armed men on a motorcycle opened fire at a hair salon, killing two employees of the saloon. The police claim that the employees were targeted.
A stray bullet hit a person in Orangi town injuring him. (This event occured on the election day)
Unidentified men threw a body on the main road near Jinnah Postgraduate medical centre. Its hands and legs were tied.

As part of the military operation in Orakzai that started on 10-Apr-10, security forces used heavy artillery and helicopters to target militants in Shereen Dera, killing 11 and capturing 5. Clashes also took place in Sangara and Saam areas where a further 12 militants were killed and 4 captured. 4 Militant hideouts were also destroyed.

Protesters who were demonstrating agaisnt the failure of the police to arrest the murderers of a brick-kiln worker, were baton charged by the police. Eight people were arrested and two policemen were injured.
Aijaz Ahmed, a councillor of the Municipal Corporation of Lahore was shot dead by seven gunmen. His family alleges that Muhammad Asghar, his political rival, was behind the assasination.

Dr. Syed Jafar Raza  was standing outside his ENT General Clinic when some unidentified men on a bike came and opened fire on him, killing him instantly. A senior police offical stated that it was too early to tell but there might be sectarian motives behind the killing.
A young man, Zahid Ali, was shot dead in Mominabad. According to the alleged killer, Munna, fled.
The wave of 'ethnic' violence that affected Orangi town the previous day spread to other parts of the city when two watchmen were gunned down in front of Madni Masjid in the Garden area.

A clash took place between workers of two student political organizations, the SPSF -student wing of the PPP - and SPSF(SB) - student wing of the PPP(SB). However exact details are difficult to ascertain given the contradictory nature of competing claims made by the parties involved. Ghinwa Bhutto, chairperson of the PPP-SB, claimed that SPSF members opened fire at her car and convoy which led to the clash. The Sindh Law Minister and president of the PPP's Larkana chapter claimed that SPSF(SB) students manhandled PPP workers and attacked the car of SPSF leader Sohrab Marri. DPO Irfan Baloch claimed that it was a clash between workers of the two student political parties after an SPSF-SB activist had fired in the air.

Amid a fresh bout of war between 'criminal gangs'-supported by political parties-operating in Lyari after five young men of the area were found dead. Before protests over the killing broke out, armed men on motorcycles arrived at Bheempura, Salaar Compound and Hindu Para area, throwing hand grenades and firing rockets, which led to the death of three people, including a 10 year old boy and 16 year old girl.
A person was shot dead by unknown assailants in Nishtar Colony on Sunday

Two groups of students affiliated with different political parties clashed on campus, causing injuries to 2 students. The Jeay Sindh Students Federation claimed that accusations of teasing female students were at the heart of the clash. However this version was disputed by other students who were injured in the clash. A fact finding committee was setup to determine the cause of the clash. Though no arrests were made, 17 students were nominated in the FIR. The nominated students belonged to JSSF, Sf-SB and Asgheria Students Organization.
a 132 KV power supply pylon was blown up in the Barkhan area, disrupting power supply to Barkhan and Kohlu area.
Six civilians were killed in Shah Dheri area of Swat due to mortar shells.
PML workers in Kasur took out a procession under the leadership of VP Mian Khurshid Mahmood Kasuri and pelted stones at open shops to force the owners to close them.
A low intensity explosion took place on a railway track in Mehrabpur. Pamphlets found at the blast site contained the name of The Sindhudesh Liberation Army (SLA).

Around 1,200 clients affected by the lawyers' strike took out a protest rally against lawyers, attacked the bar office, ransacked its furniture and thrashed some of the lawyers as well. They demanded of the lawyers to either reimburse their fees or call off their strike and appear in courts. The protesters dispersed after an assurance given by the DPO that the action would be taken against lawyers if they submitted written applications.
Zulfiqar Masih was on his way home when armed men on a motorbike shot him. He died on the spot. Police claim that it was a targeted killing.

An amulet giver was gunned down in his house in Wahdat Colony area when an unidentified person opened fire on him. He suffered a bullet wound in the head and succumbed to his injuries while on his way to the hospital. It was not immediately clear whether the killing was a terrorist act.
Workers of PPP and IJI ransacked the offices of PML and IJI. Thiswas alleged by provincial general secretary of PML, Haji Mohammad Javed.

Dozens of contractual employees of the National Programme for Improvement of Watercourses (NPIW), marched towards the Sindh Chief Minister's house to protest against the non-regularisation of their jobs. Despite the government's assurance, nearly 3000 jobs have not been regularised. They were intercepted by the police who baton-charged them and fired tear gas shells. NPIW leaders claim that more than 12 people were arrested but the Police have denied that claim.
The partially decomposed bpdy of a woman was found in her house in PIB Colony. Her hands were tied and although the house was ransacked, no valuables were taken. She lived alone.
An unidentified man was wounded in Korangi.
A shopkeeper was gunned down by two armed motorcyclists in Quaidabad on Saturday.
Mohammad Ali, a 32-year-old man, was purchasing fruit when two men on a motorbike shot and injured him before fleeing.
Security forces demolished the houses of two militant commanders, Bacha Munir and Maqbol
Two people were arrested with an Indian made time bomb. They planned on planting it in the Shakrgarh civil court. Their affiliation to any group/organization could not be ascertained.

Hundreds of villagers blocked the National Highway for 3 hours in order to protest against the excesses of the police in Khanpur Maher town, Ghotki. The protesters burnt tyres and demanded that action be taken against the police officers that extort money from the public. The police baton charged the protesters but they refused to budge until the Khanpur police release a villager, Atta Muhammad, who had been arrested on false charges.

Infuriated locals blocked the highway and chanted slogans against the police and the officials of the forest department. The protest was the result of an incident in which a speeding pickup loaded with smuggled timber colliding with another pickup. According to eyewitnesses the driver of the pickup unloaded the smuggled timber in a nearby saw machine and made good his escape. It is also mentioned in the report that speedy vehicles of timber smugglers have injured a number of people in the past including school children.

Gunmen attacked a passenger van, killing a policeman Arshad Mehmood, and injuring 3 other people. A local official suspected that the attack was orchestrated by a local criminal group whose leader, Balo Mian, had been killed in a police encounter recently.
Ayub Butt alias Ayub Commander, who was a local leader of the PPP, was shot dead by armed men who opened fire on his car after ambushing it.
US and NATO airplanes, while chasing Taliban from Afghanistan, crossed over into Pakistan airspace. They stayed in Pakistan for about 30 minutes and fired missiles at suspected militant positions.
2 people were injured when armed men opened fire at a group of people that was on its way to the mosque for morning prayers. The injured victims were identified as Intikhab Alam and Muhammad Ali.

Abdul Wahab Jamali allegedly shot dead his wife, Zarina, and cousin, Shahnawaz Jamali on the pretext of Karo-kari. His father, Mohammad Ali, registered an FIR against the accused claiming the victims were innocent.

Gunmen of a Zehri Tribe elder were travelling on a pick-up when unidentified people ambushed them and opened fire. 6 gunmen and a bystander were killed. Levies Force personnel rushed to the spot and took the injured to the hospital and were later deployed in the area to prevent clashes between rival tribesmen.

At least 4 policemen and 5 students were injured in a clash between the police and students during a demonstration held by the students over the increase in university hostel prices. During the protest some students tried entering the administrative block and upon resistance by the police they pelted them with stones, smashes window panes and damaged some officials' vehicles. Police had to resort to baton-charge and tear gas to disperse the crowd. The students claimed that 15 of them had been injured. 20 students were taken into custody.
An unidentified bullet riddled body was found from Mehmoodabad area.

A curfew was imposed in Parachinar after three people were killed in heavy fighting amongst two religious groups. The two groups were aggravated when one of the took down the flag of the other during an Eid Milad un Nabi procession in the area. The incident sparked anger and violence in the area, which led to to the death of three people and injuries to 18. An ambulance carrying some injured people was also attacked in a continuation of the said attacks ; Followup: The number killed in the sectarian clash between the two religious groups grew to be 40 in the 2 days of fighting, while the number injured came out to be 70. Strict curfew had been imposed in the area, and the military and paramilitary forces were brought in to bring the situation under control
Bakhtra Gul of Khost province (Afghanistan) was found dead and a not was found along with his body stating that he was involved in spying for the US.
A 13 year old boy was stabbed to death by some unidentified murderers.
A mild intensity bomb exploded near the High Court. No loss of life or property was reported.
A watchman was shot dead by unidentified persons in Orangi Extension on Friday.

Sub-Inspector Nabi Buksh of the police was killed when armed motorcyclists opened fire at him. The BLA claimed responsibility for the attack. This was the 3rd targeted killing of a policeman in Balochistan in the last few days.
Law enforcement agencies demolisehd 50 houses belonging to outlaws in the tribal areas as a sweep up operation by blowing them up with dynamite, bulldozing them or setting them on fire.

4 Elite Force personnel and a secret agency officer and 2 others were injured when suspected terrorists hurled a hand grenade at them during a raid in Hajiabad. 2 medical college students, who had provided the police with information about the terrorists, were among those injured injured. the terrorists escaped on motorcycles.

Oil tanker drivers were protesting against the \partial attitude\" of the management of the PSO Terminal. There then was a clash betweent the police and the protesting drivers. This resulted in injuries to five drivers. "
The only girls' college in Orakzai tribal region was destroyed when militants planted and detonated explosive devices.
Raja Beckers, a resident of Malir Cantt, was targeted and killed by two men on a motorbike as he was getting off a rickshaw.
Five people were killed in Sector F-5 in New Karachi.
Three students of Karachi University were killed and 10 others were injured in clashes between Islami Jamiat Tulaba and All Pakistan Mohajir Students Organisation.
Nazir Gul was killed. According to his son, he left the house at night and didn't come back. His body was found the next day.

Violence continued in Hyderabad and Latifabad for a second consecutive day when the Wapda office in Affandi town was set ablaze but the fire was brought under control quickly causing partial damage to the building.

Two lawyers were stabbed by unidentified persons. One of them was the Principal of the Law college and he along with his friend were attacked with daggers inside his office. The attackers managed to escape.
Five gunmen, opened fire at people in a medical store, below the Imamia mosque. Two people were killed and five injured in this sectarian attack.
A child was killed and his parents were injured as security forces opened fire on them during the curfew near Miranshah on Monday.
three girls were killed when they stepped on an anti-personnel mine planted near a water-tanker where they were playing.
Unidentified gunmen shot dead the care taker of an Imambargh while he was on his way there.
a home made explosive device had been planted at the back of the building of a girls school. The building was partially damaged in the explosion.
at least four rockets were fired at a checkpost of the Frontiers Corps in Kahan Town. However, no damage or casualty was reported.
1 policeman was killed when militants attacked the Mamokhwara checkpost in Hangu. Security personnel manning the post returned fire and killed six attackers.

Unidentified armed men of Jeha tribe opened fire on Aziz alias Usman Kehar and killed him on the spot. The Jeha and Kehar tribes were at odds for the past one and a half year over a dispute involving a woman.

Two men were found shot dead at a desolate place in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. According to SHO, the unknown persons had brought the victims to Block 3 and fired a volley of bullets on them. The police could not ascertain the motive behind the killing as the two, reportedly, did not have any political affiliation, however, it was termed a targeted killing.
the body of Afzal Khan, a resident of Osmanikhel Garhai in the Dargai Tehsil was found, hung with a pole along the Dargai river.
Policemen and some protestors were injured when a protest rally was prevented from marching to the WAPDA office by the police

Police resorted to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to disperse violent demonstrators who had gathered to protest against the inability of the police to arrest the killers of a shopkeeper, despite knowing who the culprit was. A case was later registered against the accused and the SHO was transferred on public demand.
A teenager was stopped by volunteers outside a mosque when he detonated his suicide vest. He was apparently headed towards the shura that was convening inside the mosque at the time.
A person was stabbed to death in Liaqatabad by unknown men on Monday

1 person was killed and 5 were injured during a clash between two groups of the Lund tribe. Both groups exchanged hot words over a theft which turned into an armed clash. Police arrested 6 people from both sides.
abandoned police post was blown up.

A rally was organised by the Brailvi sect against the destruction of banners and posters by the Deobandi sect the day before. During the rally the protesters stated pelting the Khairul madaris with stones upon which the Frontier Constabulary, deployed to control law and order, resorted to aerial firing to calm the crowd. Later some youths tried to enter the Madaris and started pelting the FC personnel with stones, injuring two. The FC men then opened fire on the crowd, killing one boy and injuring three others. However, the FC men deny opening fire on the crowd.
Ghulamoo Janwari was shot dead by seven armed men over the distribution of a piece of land near a old cinema.
Two men on a motorbike hurled two hand-grenades on the Saudi Consulate, causing damage to property. No injuries of deaths were reported.
A Frontier Corps soldier was killed and another seriously injured when tribesmen opened fire on them. No other information was given.
A bomb exploded injuring one person.

According to the North Nazimabad police, some persons wearing masks in a Toyota Corolla opened fire an injured Salman Shamsi and Sadaqat. The police stated that the occupants of the car seemed to be Iranians by appearance.
two persons were killed and 5 others were injured, in an armed clash between people belonging to the Chandio and Chachar communities over sharing of irrigation water, in village Ghuneja Pull.

about 125 men were rounded up in Multan when they tried to hold a rally procession and damage the property. Punjab Government has imposed a ban on rallies after incident of widespread violence in rallies in the city on Feb,14.
